In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

Let $H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$ be an ordered $n$-qubit register, let
$\rho\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ be a density operator, and let $M\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$
be a Hermitian Pauli observable with $M^2=I$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ define

$$P_b:=\frac{I+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b),\qquad \mathcal I_b(\rho):=P_b\rho P_b.$$

The outcome $b$ has probability $p_b$. Its conditional density operator is
$\rho_b:=\mathcal I_b(\rho)/p_b$ when $p_b>0$; it is $\bot$ (no assigned
conditional density operator) when $p_b=0$.
The branch map $\mathcal I_b$ is the projective measurement instrument for the
$(-1)^b$ eigenspace of $M$. A non-Hermitian phase-aware Pauli is outside this
definition. For $n\ge1$, Hermiticity of $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ means
$k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod2$; in particular $Y=iXZ$ is admitted. For $n=0$,
the admitted observables are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$.

The hypotheses and meanings of density operator, Pauli observable, projective
measurement, POVM outcome law, and instrument are the cited suppliers. The
local projector calculation is [[lem-qc-pauli-measurement-projectors]].

Let $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ be a pure stabilizer state density operator,
and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli observable that anticommutes with one of its
stabilizer generators. Then
$\operatorname{Tr}(P_0\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_1\rho)=1/2$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\rangle$ be a stabilizer
subgroup whose displayed generators have linearly independent binary labels
and fix a unit vector $\psi$ on $n$ qubits. Let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable anticommuting with $g_1$. For either outcome $b\in\{0,1\}$, define
$g'_1=(-1)^bM$ and, for $j>1$, set $g'_j=g_jg_1$ if $g_j$ anticommutes with
$M$, and $g'_j=g_j$ otherwise. Then the updated rows generate a rank-$n$
stabilizer subgroup for the normalized post-measurement state
$P_b|\psi\rangle/\|P_b|\psi\rangle\|$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ put
$P_b=(I_H+(-1)^bM)/2$ and $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$. If $p_b=0$,
then $P_b\rho P_b=0$. The outcome has probability zero and, under the
conditional-state convention, has no normalized conditional state.

derivations.claim: The initial generator $Z$ fixes $|0\rangle$, and it anticommutes with $X$ by [F1]. Hence [F3] gives $p_0=p_1=1/2$ for the first measurement.

Directly, $P_0|0\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/2$ and $P_1|0\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/2$. Each vector has squared norm $1/2$, so normalization gives $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $|-\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$. By [F4], their stabilizers are $+X$ and $-X$, respectively.

Measuring $X$ again on either state is deterministic: $|+\rangle$ lies in $P_0H_1$ and $|-\rangle$ lies in $P_1H_1$. The opposite projector annihilates the state, so its branch has probability zero and no normalized conditional state by [F5].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Let $F$ be a field, let $m,n,p\in\mathbb N$, and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and
$B=(b_{jk})\in M_{n\times p}(F)$. Their **matrix product** is the matrix
$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

$$(AB)_{ik}:=\sum_{j\in n}a_{ij}b_{jk}.$$

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,
it is the empty sum, so $AB$ is the zero matrix of shape $m$ by $p$.

The **identity matrix** $I_n\in M_n(F)$ has entry $1$ when $i=j$ and entry $0$
when $i\ne j$. In particular, $I_0$ is the unique empty matrix in $M_0(F)$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

derivations.claim: For $s=(-1)^b$, $P_b^\dagger=P_b$ because $M^\dagger=M$, and $P_b^2=(I_H+2sM+M^2)/4=(I_H+sM)/2=P_b$ by the distributive and identity laws for matrix multiplication. Thus both $P_b$ are self-adjoint idempotents.
Direct multiplication gives $P_0+P_1=I$ and $P_0P_1=(I-M^2)/4=0=P_1P_0$. Hence their ranges are orthogonal and sum to the full register.

Put $Q_b=P_b\rho P_b$. For every vector $v$, $\langle Q_bv,v\rangle=\langle \rho P_bv,P_bv\rangle\ge0$, using the root-linear-first inner-product convention and $P_b^\dagger=P_b$. Therefore $Q_b$ is positive semidefinite.

By cyclicity [F3] and $P_b^2=P_b$, $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_b\rho P_b) =\operatorname{Tr}(Q_b)$. In the orthonormal eigenbasis supplied by [F4], the diagonal entries of $Q_b$ are nonnegative; [F3] and [F5] therefore give $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(Q_b)\ge0$. Linearity of the finite diagonal sum and $P_0+P_1=I$ give $p_0+p_1=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=1$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ set

$$P_b:=\frac{I_H+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b).$$

Then $P_0,P_1$ are complementary orthogonal projections and
$p_0,p_1\ge0$, with $p_0+p_1=1$.

For every natural $n$, the map
$\operatorname{tr}:M_n(F)\to F$ is linear:

$$\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\lambda A)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(A).$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

derivations.claim: Set $Q_b=P_b\rho P_b$. By [F2], $Q_b$ is nonnegative and has trace $p_b$. Since $p_b>0$, the scalar $1/p_b$ is positive. Hence, for every $v$, $\langle (Q_b/p_b)v,v\rangle=(1/p_b)\langle Q_bv,v\rangle\ge0$.
By [F3] and [F2], $\operatorname{Tr}(Q_b/p_b)=p_b^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(Q_b)=1$. Thus $Q_b/p_b$ is a density operator by [F4].
The conditional state in [F1] is exactly $Q_b/p_b$, so it is the density operator established in step 2.1.

citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ set

$$P_b:=\frac{I_H+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b).$$

Then $P_0,P_1$ are complementary orthogonal projections and
$p_0,p_1\ge0$, with $p_0+p_1=1$.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and write $\mathcal L(H)$ and $\mathcal L(K)$ for their vector spaces of complex-linear endomorphisms with pointwise operations ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]], [[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]]). Let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. For each integer $r\ge1$, put $R=\mathbb C^r$ with its standard ordered register basis ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). Write an operator $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$ in its unique $r\times r$ block form $X=[X_{ij}]$ with $X_{ij}\in\mathcal L(H)$, and define $\Phi^{(r)}(X)$ to have blocks $[\Phi(X_{ij})]$ on $K\otimes R$. Lemma [[lem-qc-finite-ancilla-amplification-is-block-map]] proves that this block rule defines a linear map on the full operator space for every finite $r$. For $r=1$, the extension is $\Phi$ under the canonical unitary identifications $x\mapsto x\otimes e_0$ and $y\mapsto y\otimes e_0$ proved in that lemma.

The map $\Phi$ is **completely positive** if, for every finite $r\ge1$, $\Phi^{(r)}$ sends every nonnegative operator on $H\otimes R$ to a nonnegative operator on $K\otimes R$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]). The quantifier includes $r=1$; complete positivity therefore implies positivity. No Kraus, Choi, or Stinespring characterization is part of this definition.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces, let $r\ge1$, and let $R=\mathbb C^r$ have its standard ordered orthonormal basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{r-1})$. For every $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes R)$ there is a unique family $X_{ij}\in\mathcal L(H)$ such that

$$X(x\otimes e_j)=\sum_{i<r}X_{ij}x\otimes e_i\qquad(x\in H,\ j<r).$$

For every complex-linear $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$, there is a unique operator $\Phi^{(r)}(X)\in\mathcal L(K\otimes R)$ satisfying

$$\Phi^{(r)}(X)(y\otimes e_j)=\sum_{i<r}\Phi(X_{ij})y\otimes e_i\qquad(y\in K,\ j<r).$$

Thus the block rule $[X_{ij}]\mapsto[\Phi(X_{ij})]$ defines a well-defined linear map on the full operator space. At $r=1$, it is $\Phi$ under the canonical unitary identifications $x\mapsto x\otimes e_0$ and $y\mapsto y\otimes e_0$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The operator $T$ is **non-negative** when $T$ is
self-adjoint in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle\ge 0$$

for every $v\in V$.

The operator $T$ is **positive** when $T$ is self-adjoint and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle>0$$

for every nonzero $v\in V$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, let $K$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space, and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite instrument** from $H$ to $K$ is a family of complex-linear maps $\mathcal I_a:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$, one for each $a\in\Omega$, such that each $\mathcal I_a$ is completely positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and

$$\sum_{a\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative with trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), define the outcome weight $p_a(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}_K(\mathcal I_a(\rho))$. The **conditional state** for outcome $a$ is

$$\rho_a:=\begin{cases}\mathcal I_a(\rho)/p_a(\rho),&p_a(\rho)>0,\\[2pt]\bot,&p_a(\rho)=0.\end{cases}$$

Here $\bot$ is a symbol meaning that no conditional density operator is assigned; it is not a state. Positivity and normalization of the outcome weights, and density of every positive-probability conditional state, are proved in [[thm-qc-instrument-outcome-law-normalizes]] and [[thm-qc-instrument-conditional-state-is-density]].

derivations.claim: Each $\mathcal I_b$ is complex-linear because matrix multiplication distributes over finite sums and scalars: $P_b(aX+cY)P_b=aP_bXP_b+cP_bYP_b$.

Fix $r\ge1$, take an orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j<r}$ of the ancilla, and write $X=[X_{ij}]$ for a nonnegative operator on $H\otimes\mathbb C^r$. Self-adjointness of $X$ by [F6] gives $X_{ij}^\dagger=X_{ji}$: for $\xi,\eta\in H$, $\langle X_{ij}\xi,\eta\rangle =\langle X(\xi\otimes e_j),\eta\otimes e_i\rangle =\langle \xi\otimes e_j,X(\eta\otimes e_i)\rangle =\langle \xi,X_{ji}\eta\rangle$ by the product pairing [F5]. Consequently the blocks $P_bX_{ij}P_b$ satisfy the same adjoint relation, so $\mathcal I_b^{(r)}(X)$ is self-adjoint.

For every operator $X$, cyclicity [F7] and idempotence [F2] give $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal I_0(X))+\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal I_1(X)) =\operatorname{Tr}(XP_0)+\operatorname{Tr}(XP_1) =\operatorname{Tr}(X(P_0+P_1))=\operatorname{Tr}(X)$. For a density operator $\rho$, the same calculation gives $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal I_b(\rho))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$, the branch trace.

Write $v=\sum_{j<r}v_j\otimes e_j$ and $w=\sum_{j<r}P_bv_j\otimes e_j$. By [F4] and the product pairing [F5], $\langle\mathcal I_b^{(r)}(X)v,v\rangle =\sum_{i,j<r}\langle P_bX_{ij}P_bv_j,v_i\rangle =\sum_{i,j<r}\langle X_{ij}P_bv_j,P_bv_i\rangle =\langle Xw,w\rangle\ge0$. Thus the ampliation preserves nonnegative operators. Since $r$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal I_b$ is completely positive by [F3].
The two maps are completely positive by step 2.1 and their total output trace equals the input trace by step 1.3. They therefore form a finite instrument by [F8].
By the branch-weight clause of [F8], the outcome weight on $\rho$ is $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal I_b(\rho))$. Step 1.3 identifies this with $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$.

For an ordered register of $n$ qubits, a **stabilizer subgroup** is an abelian
subgroup $S$ of the Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators such that
$-I\notin S$. The binary label of a phase-aware Pauli $P(k,x,z)$ is
$(x,z)\in\mathbb F_2^{2n}$. Define the **rank** of $S$ by

$$\operatorname{rank}(S):=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{span} \{(x,z):P(k,x,z)\in S\}.$$

The binary label convention and commutation form are supplied by the cited
Pauli items. [[lem-qc-stabilizer-subgroup-label-space-and-order]] proves that
this label span is isotropic, its dimension is independent of any generating
set, and $|S|=2^{\operatorname{rank}(S)}$. Matrix multiplication gives the
phase-aware Pauli group operation by
[[thm-qc-pauli-product-and-adjoint]]. For $n=0$, the Pauli group is the
empty-register convention of [[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]].

Let $Z_n$ be the scalar center of $\mathcal P_n$. Define $P\sim Q$ when $P^{-1}Q\in Z_n$, and let $Q_n$ be the set of equivalence classes $[P]=PZ_n$. The proposed coset product is $[P][Q]=[PQ]$. The quotient theorem verifies this product is well-defined and proves that the assignment

$$\lambda:Q_n\longrightarrow V_n:=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n,\qquad [P(k,x,z)]\longmapsto(x,z)$$

is a group isomorphism to the additive group of $V_n$. A binary label deliberately forgets the scalar phase.

The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.
For $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z\in\mathcal P_n$, the operator is Hermitian exactly when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$. In that case $P(k,x,z)^2=I$.

A **finite field** is a field whose underlying set is finite. Its **order** is its finite cardinality, written $|F|$.

Once existence and uniqueness are proved, $\mathbb F_q$ denotes a field of order $q$ up to isomorphism. The notation does not assert that the field is the quotient ring $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$.

For every prime $p$, the operations of addition and multiplication on
$\mathbb Z/p$ make it a field ([[def-field]]).

Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, and let $V$ be a $d$-dimensional
$F$-vector space. Then

$$\lvert V\rvert=q^d.$$

The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

This supplies the empty-register case when an item uses Pauli notation whose
general positive-wire convention is stated separately.

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

This supplies the empty-register case when an item uses Pauli notation whose
general positive-wire convention is stated separately.

derivations.claim: If $n=0$, then $S=\{I\}$: a subgroup contains $I$ and its only other possible Hermitian scalar Pauli is $-I$, which is excluded. Thus $\lambda|_S$ is injective, its image is the zero subspace of dimension $0$, this dimension is independent of any generating list, and $|S|=1=2^0$.

Assume now $n\ge1$. The identity of $S$ has zero label. If $P,Q\in S$, then $PQ\in S$ and $\lambda(PQ)=\lambda(P)+\lambda(Q)$ by [F3]. Thus $L=\lambda(S)$ contains zero and is closed under addition; over $\mathbb F_2$, closure under the only scalars $0,1$ follows, so $L$ is a subspace.

Suppose $P,Q\in S$ have the same label. By the homomorphism in [F3], $\lambda(P^{-1}Q)=0$, so $P^{-1}Q$ is a scalar Pauli. Since Hermitian Paulis square to $I$ by [F5], $P^{-1}=P$; as $P,Q$ commute and are Hermitian, $P^{-1}Q=PQ$ is Hermitian. The phase criterion [F5] then makes this scalar equal to $I$ or $-I$. The latter is excluded by [F1], hence $P=Q$ and $\lambda|_S$ is injective.

For $n\ge1$, any two labels in $L$ come from commuting elements of the abelian group $S$, so [F4] gives symplectic pairing zero. Bilinearity then makes every pair in their span pair to zero; hence $L$ is isotropic. The image $L$ is defined from $S$ alone, so its dimension is unchanged by replacing one generating list of $S$ by another.

For $n\ge1$, the map $\lambda|_S:S\to L$ is onto by the definition of $L$ and injective by step 1.3, so it is a bijection of finite sets by [F8]. If $r=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L$, [F6] and [F7] give $|L|=2^r$. Therefore $|S|=|L|=2^r$, as claimed.
Step 1.1 proves the claim for $n=0$, and step 1.2 and step 1.3 and step 2.1 and step 2.2 prove it for $n\ge1$. These cases exhaust all $n\ge0$.

On $V_n=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n$, with coordinate order $(x,z)$, define

$$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over $F$, with $V$
finite-dimensional. Then

$$\dim_F V=\operatorname{nullity}T+\operatorname{rank}T.$$

Equivalently,

$$\dim_F V=\dim_F(\ker T)+\dim_F(\operatorname{im}T).$$

Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$ ([[def-vector-space]]) that is
finite-dimensional with $\dim_F V = n$ ([[def-dimension]]), and let $U$ be a
linear subspace of $V$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). Then

1. $U$ is finite-dimensional over $F$ and $\dim_F U \le n$;
2. $\dim_F U = n$ **if and only if** $U = V$;
3. **Extension, with no choice principle.** Every linearly independent
   $A_0 \subseteq U$ is contained in a basis of $U$: there is a basis $B$ of $U$
   with $A_0 \subseteq B \subseteq U$. Claim 1 is the case $A_0 = \varnothing$.
   Since $V$ is itself a linear subspace of $V$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]), claim 3
   applies with $V$ in place of $U$, and hence to **any** finite-dimensional
   vector space over $F$ in place of the pair $(V, U)$.

**Nothing above uses a choice principle**, and claim 3 in particular is the
finite-dimensional substitute for the Zorn-based extension theorem stated earlier
on this page. In finite dimension the extension terminates on its own, because
[[cor-independent-set-is-no-larger-than-a-finite-spanning-set]] bounds the size
of an independent set and [[thm-well-ordering-principle]] then supplies a largest
one; no selection is made anywhere.

**Finiteness is essential in claim 2.** Without it the equality case fails: the
companion page exhibits a
proper linear subspace of an infinite-dimensional space whose basis is
equinumerous with a basis of the whole space.

derivations.claim: If $n=0$, then $V=L=L^\perp=\{0\}$ and $r=0$, so $\dim L^\perp=0=2n-r$, $r\le n$, and $L^\perp=L$. Hence the result holds.

Assume now $n\ge1$. If $v=(x,z)\in V$ pairs to zero with every vector, pairing with $(e_j,0)$ and $(0,e_j)$ gives $z_j=x_j=0$ for every $j$. More generally, for any linear functional $\phi$ on $V$, set $a_j=\phi(e_j,0)$ and $b_j=\phi(0,e_j)$. Then $v=(b,a)$ satisfies $\omega(v,(x',z'))=b\cdot z'+a\cdot x'=\phi(x',z')$ by linearity. Thus $v\mapsto\omega(v,\cdot)$ is both injective and onto.

Put $r=\dim L$ and choose a basis $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$ of $L$. Extend it to a basis of $V$ using [F3]. For any $y\in\mathbb F_2^r$, define a linear functional on this basis by $\phi(\ell_j)=y_j$ and by zero on the added basis vectors. Step 1.2 supplies $v\in V$ with $\omega(v,\cdot)=\phi$, so $T:V\to\mathbb F_2^r$, $T(v)=(\omega(v,\ell_j))_{j=1}^r$, is onto. Its kernel is $L^\perp$, and [F2] gives $\dim L^\perp=2n-r$. This includes $r=0$, where both the basis and $\mathbb F_2^r$ are empty or zero-dimensional.

For $n\ge1$, isotropy gives $L\subseteq L^\perp$. Comparing dimensions with step 2.1 gives $r\le2n-r$, hence $r\le n$. If $r=n$, both subspaces have dimension $n$, so [F3] gives $L=L^\perp$. This argument uses only finite basis extension and no choice principle.
Step 1.1 proves the result for $n=0$, and step 1.2 and step 2.1 and step 3.1 prove it for $n\ge1$. These cases exhaust all dimensions in the Statement.

citations.quote:
For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

This supplies the empty-register case when an item uses Pauli notation whose
general positive-wire convention is stated separately.

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

For $n\ge0$, $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and $k\in\mathbb Z/4$, write
$P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$, with the fixed tensor order and
$X^x=\bigotimes_{j<n}X^{x_j}$, $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j<n}Z^{z_j}$. A **row**
$(k,x,z)$ is Hermitian when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$; it stores the exact
Pauli phase as well as its binary label $(x,z)$.

For $n=0$, use the scalar Pauli convention of
[[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]]; the generator list is empty.

A **generator tableau** is an ordered list of $n$ Hermitian rows whose Pauli
operators commute, have linearly independent labels, and generate a subgroup
not containing $-I$. It represents the unique common $+1$ ray when the rows
stabilize a pure state. An **extended tableau** also stores Hermitian
destabilizer rows $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ and stabilizer rows $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ with

$$\omega(d_i,s_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad \omega(d_i,d_j)=0,\quad \omega(s_i,s_j)=0.$$

The exact phase and symplectic conventions are those of the cited Pauli
suppliers. The generator-only simulator uses the $s_j$ rows; the extended
pairing is retained as a second representation invariant.

On $V_n=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n$, with coordinate order $(x,z)$, define

$$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

For the matrices $X,Y,Z$ of [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], each is self-adjoint and unitary, and $X^2=Y^2=Z^2=I$. Distinct Pauli matrices anticommute. For $j,k\in\{x,y,z\}$,
$$\sigma_j\sigma_k=\delta_{jk}I+i\sum_{\ell\in\{x,y,z\}}\epsilon_{jk\ell}\sigma_\ell,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\sigma_j\sigma_k)=2\delta_{jk}.$$
Here $\sigma_x=X,\sigma_y=Y,\sigma_z=Z$, $\delta_{jk}=1$ when $j=k$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\epsilon$ is the alternating symbol with $\epsilon_{xyz}=1$. Also $\operatorname{tr}(I)=2$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_j)=0$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

derivations.claim: For each $0\le j<n$, the Pauli $Z_{j+1}$ acts on factor $j$ by [F9], and [F7] gives $Z_{j+1}|x\rangle=(-1)^{x_j}|x\rangle$. Thus $s_{j+1}=(-1)^{x_j}Z_{j+1}$ fixes $|x\rangle$; the vector is normalized by [F4].

For $0\le i,j<n$, the labels of $s_{j+1}$ are $(0,e_j)$ and of $d_{i+1}=X_{i+1}$ are $(e_i,0)$. Therefore $\omega(d_{i+1},s_{j+1})=e_i\cdot e_j=\delta_{ij}$, which is the required pairing $\delta_{i+1,j+1}$; pairings within either family vanish by [F5]. By [F8], the stabilizer rows commute. The $s_{j+1}$ labels are independent, so no nonempty product has zero label; by [F6] the generated group therefore excludes $-I$. For $n=0$, the empty row families generate $\{I\}$ by [F3], and all pairing and independence conditions hold vacuously.

citations.quote:
Let $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the ordered qubit register with computational basis
$(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and use the ordered two-factor register
$Q_2\otimes Q_2$ from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. Define the
four **Bell vectors** by

$$|\Phi^+\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle+|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Phi^-\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle-|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^+\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle+|10\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^-\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle-|10\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$$

The ordered label convention is
$|00\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^+\rangle$,
$|01\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^+\rangle$,
$|10\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^-\rangle$, and
$|11\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^-\rangle$. Thus the first label is the phase/sign
bit and the second is the bit-flip bit. The next theorem verifies that these
vectors form an orthonormal basis and gives the corresponding preparation and
decoding maps.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces. In orthonormal bases $\mathcal E=(e_j)$ of $V$ and $\mathcal F=(f_i)$ of $W$,

$$[T^*]_{\mathcal E\leftarrow\mathcal F}=\overline{[T]_{\mathcal F\leftarrow\mathcal E}}^{\mathsf T}.$$

Over $\mathbb R$ this is the transpose. The statement includes zero-sized bases.

derivations.claim: The matrix in [F2] gives $H|a\rangle=(|0\rangle+(-1)^a|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ for each bit $a$. By [F6], $(H\otimes I)|ab\rangle=(|0,b\rangle+(-1)^a|1,b\rangle)/\sqrt2$.

From [F3], applying CNOT twice fixes every basis vector because $(t\oplus a)\oplus a=t$. Its matrix permutes the orthonormal basis [F4], so its inverse is its transpose and equals itself. The matrix of $H\otimes I$ in [F4] is real symmetric and its square is the identity by [F2]. Thus both factors are self-adjoint involutions, and direct composition gives $(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}B=I=B(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}$.

Apply the control-first action in [F3] to the two terms of step 1.1. The control-zero term is fixed, while the control-one term changes its target from $b$ to $b\oplus1$. Therefore $B|ab\rangle=(|0,b\rangle+(-1)^a|1,b\oplus1\rangle)/\sqrt2$.

Substituting $00,01,10,11$ into step 2.1 gives $\Phi^+,\Psi^+,\Phi^-,\Psi^-$ in that order, exactly as defined in [F1]. Each has norm one because it is a signed sum of two distinct orthonormal computational basis vectors from [F5], divided by $\sqrt2$. The inner product of $\Phi^+$ with $\Phi^-$ and of $\Psi^+$ with $\Psi^-$ is $(1-1)/2=0$; cross-pair inner products are zero because their computational supports are disjoint.
The four vectors in step 3.1 are an orthonormal set of four vectors in the four-dimensional space whose product basis is listed in [F4]; hence they are an orthonormal basis.

In matrices, $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$, so conjugating and transposing this finite sum gives $(AB)^\dagger=B^\dagger A^\dagger$. By [F7]–[F8] this is the adjoint product rule in the register pairing. Since both factors in [F6] and [F3] are self-adjoint by step 1.2, $B^\dagger=(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}$. Applying CNOT sends the four Bell vectors to $\frac{|0\rangle+|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|0\rangle$, $\frac{|0\rangle+|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|1\rangle$, $\frac{|0\rangle-|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|0\rangle$, and $\frac{|0\rangle-|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|1\rangle$, respectively. By the matrix in [F2], $H$ sends the first factors in these expressions to $|0\rangle,|0\rangle,|1\rangle,|1\rangle$, respectively, so the reverse sequence recovers $00,01,10,11$.

The **teleportation procedure** has input a normalized qubit vector $|\psi\rangle_A\in Q_2$ and a preshared resource $|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}$, with Alice holding wires $A,B$ and Bob holding $C$. The wire order is $A,B,C$. It uses $|\Phi^+\rangle$ from [[def-qc-bell-basis]], CNOT with $A$ control and $B$ target from [[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], the Hadamard $H$ from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]], the Pauli matrices from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], and the finite projective measurement convention of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]].

1. Alice applies $\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$ and then $H_A$, so the combined operator is $V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, with the rightmost gate applied first.
2. Alice measures $A,B$ in their ordered computational basis and records the pair $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$, in that wire order.
3. Alice sends the two classical bits $a,b$ to Bob.
4. Bob applies $X_C^b$ and then $Z_C^a$, whose operator product is $Z_C^aX_C^b$.

The output is the corrected state on Bob's wire $C$. The shared Bell pair is an
input resource; its preparation and physical realization are outside this
procedure. A zero-probability measurement label has no conditional state and
is assigned no branch output; the normalized-input hypotheses here are later
shown to make all four labels positive.

Let $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the ordered qubit register with computational basis
$(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and use the ordered two-factor register
$Q_2\otimes Q_2$ from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. Define the
four **Bell vectors** by

$$|\Phi^+\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle+|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Phi^-\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle-|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^+\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle+|10\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^-\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle-|10\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$$

The ordered label convention is
$|00\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^+\rangle$,
$|01\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^+\rangle$,
$|10\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^-\rangle$, and
$|11\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^-\rangle$. Thus the first label is the phase/sign
bit and the second is the bit-flip bit. The next theorem verifies that these
vectors form an orthonormal basis and gives the corresponding preparation and
decoding maps.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

derivations.claim: By [F2], the initial vector is $2^{-1/2}(\alpha|000\rangle+\alpha|011\rangle+\beta|100\rangle+\beta|111\rangle)$ in wire order $A,B,C$.

Applying [F4] to the four basis vectors gives $2^{-1/2}(\alpha|000\rangle+\alpha|011\rangle+\beta|110\rangle+\beta|101\rangle)$ after CNOT: the first two terms have control bit $0$ and are fixed, while the last two have control bit $1$ and their target bits flip.

By [F3] and [F6], $H_A$ sends each first-wire $|0\rangle$ to $(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and each $|1\rangle$ to $(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$. Regrouping the resulting eight terms by the first two wires gives $\frac12\bigl(|00\rangle(\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle)+|01\rangle(\alpha|1\rangle+\beta|0\rangle)+|10\rangle(\alpha|0\rangle-\beta|1\rangle)+|11\rangle(\alpha|1\rangle-\beta|0\rangle)\bigr)$.

The four receiver vectors in step 3.1 are respectively $|\psi\rangle$, $X|\psi\rangle$, $Z|\psi\rangle$, and $XZ|\psi\rangle$ by the actions in [F5]. These are exactly $X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$ for labels $00,01,10,11$, so step 3.1 is the sum in the Statement.

citations.quote:
For arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$, put
$|\psi\rangle=\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle$ and
$V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, in wire order
$A,B,C$. Then

$$V_{AB}(|\psi\rangle_A\otimes|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC})=\frac12\sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes X_C^bZ_C^a|\psi\rangle_C.$$

No normalization assumption on $|\psi\rangle$ is needed for this vector
identity.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

derivations.claim: For each $(a,b)$, let $P_{ab}$ be the diagonal projection onto the two basis vectors $|ab0\rangle,|ab1\rangle$ of the ordered three-wire register. These four projections are self-adjoint idempotents, their ranges are pairwise orthogonal, and their sum is the identity because the eight orthonormal computational basis vectors from [F8] are partitioned by their first two bits. Hence they form a projective measurement as in [F2].

Write the post-gate vector in [F1] as $\Omega=\sum_i c_i e_i$ in the orthonormal basis [F4]. For the matrix $\rho$ with entries $\rho_{ij}=c_i\overline{c_j}$, self-adjointness is immediate; for any coordinate vector $z$, $\langle\rho z,z\rangle=|\sum_j z_j\overline{c_j}|^2\ge0$. The matrix [F6] sends $(\alpha,\beta)$ to $(\beta,\alpha)$ under $X$ and to $(\alpha,-\beta)$ under $Z$, so each preserves $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2$ and every $X^bZ^a$ preserves norm. The branch vectors in [F1] have orthogonal $AB$ labels, hence $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=\sum_i|c_i|^2=\|\Omega\|^2=\|\psi\|^2=1$ by [A1] and [F7]. Thus $\rho$ is a density operator by [F9], since the preceding calculation establishes nonnegativity and trace one.

By [F2] and [F7], the probability weight of label $(a,b)$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{ab})=|c_{ab0}|^2+|c_{ab1}|^2$, the sum of the two diagonal entries selected by $P_{ab}$. The branch vector in [F1] has these two coefficients equal to those of $\frac12X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$, so this sum is $\frac14\|X^bZ^a\psi\|^2$.

The matrices in [F6] are unitary: direct multiplication gives $X^*X=I$ and $Z^*Z=I$. Hence $\|X^bZ^a\psi\|^2=\|\psi\|^2=1$, so every weight in step 2.1 is $1/4$. By [F3] these are the outcome probabilities, and the four weights sum to one.

citations.quote:
The **dense-coding procedure** takes classical input bits $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ and
a preshared pair $|\Phi^+\rangle_{AB}$, with Alice holding $A$ and Bob holding
$B$. The local convention is that $a$ is the phase bit and $b$ the flip bit.

1. Alice applies $X_A^b$ and then $Z_A^a$, so the encoding operator is $Z_A^aX_A^b$.
2. Alice sends the single qubit $A$ to Bob.
3. Bob applies $\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, then $H_A$, and measures the ordered register $A,B$ in the computational basis.
4. Bob outputs the ordered pair of measured bits.

If a surrounding measurement model assigns an outcome zero weight, no
conditional state is assigned for that outcome. The four decoded output
weights in the correctness theorem are positive/deterministic as computed
there.

The Bell resource, Pauli matrices, Hadamard, CNOT wire order, and projective
measurement use the conventions of [[def-qc-bell-basis]],
[[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]],
[[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], and
[[def-qc-projective-measurement]]. No optimality claim is part of this
procedure.

Let $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the ordered qubit register with computational basis
$(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and use the ordered two-factor register
$Q_2\otimes Q_2$ from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. Define the
four **Bell vectors** by

$$|\Phi^+\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle+|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Phi^-\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle-|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^+\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle+|10\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^-\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle-|10\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$$

The ordered label convention is
$|00\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^+\rangle$,
$|01\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^+\rangle$,
$|10\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^-\rangle$, and
$|11\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^-\rangle$. Thus the first label is the phase/sign
bit and the second is the bit-flip bit. The next theorem verifies that these
vectors form an orthonormal basis and gives the corresponding preparation and
decoding maps.

On the ordered two-qubit register, let
$B:=\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}(H\otimes I)$, where operator products act
right-to-left. For $a,b\in\{0,1\}$,

$$B|ab\rangle=\frac{|0,b\rangle+(-1)^a|1,b\mathbin\oplus1\rangle}{\sqrt2}=(I\otimes X^b)(Z^a\otimes I)|\Phi^+\rangle.$$

In the label order $00,01,10,11$, these are respectively
$|\Phi^+\rangle,|\Psi^+\rangle,|\Phi^-\rangle,|\Psi^-\rangle$. They form an
orthonormal basis of $Q_2\otimes Q_2$, and
$B^\dagger=(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}$ maps those four vectors
back to their labels.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

derivations.claim: Applying $Z_A^aX_A^b$ to $|\Phi^+\rangle=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and using [F4] gives the four cases: $00\mapsto\Phi^+$, $01\mapsto\Psi^+$, $10\mapsto\Phi^-$, and $11\mapsto\Psi^-$. In the last case, $Z_A X_A|00\rangle=-|10\rangle$ and $Z_A X_A|11\rangle=|01\rangle$, so the state is exactly $\Psi^-$ in the chosen convention.

For $x\in\{0,1\}$, [F4] gives $Z^a|x\rangle=(-1)^{ax}|x\rangle$. Expanding the left side and then substituting $y=x\oplus b$ gives $(Z^aX^b\otimes I)|\Phi^+\rangle=2^{-1/2}\sum_x(-1)^{a(x\oplus b)}|x\oplus b,x\rangle=2^{-1/2}\sum_y(-1)^{ay}|y,y\oplus b\rangle=(I\otimes X^bZ^a)|\Phi^+\rangle$. The same matrices give $XZ=-ZX$, hence $X^bZ^a=(-1)^{ab}Z^aX^b$. The scalar $\lambda=(-1)^{ab}$ leaves the rank-one projector unchanged because $(\lambda v)(\lambda v)^*=|\lambda|^2vv^*=vv^*$; it changes no projective outcome weight, while the direct four-case vectors in step 1.1 fix the exact label phase.

By [F3], the four encoded vectors in step 1.1 are $B|ab\rangle$, and $B^\dagger$ sends each to $|ab\rangle$. The output projectors are the orthogonal basis projections in [F8]. The rank-one matrix of $|ab\rangle$ has a single diagonal entry $1$ at label $(a,b)$, so its quadratic form is nonnegative and its trace is one by [F7]; it is a density operator by [F9]. Then [F5] and [F7] give weight one at $(a,b)$ and zero at the other labels. By [F6] this is a deterministic output law.

The procedure [F1] begins with one shared pair, sends only wire $A$ once, and outputs the two input bits at Bob's measurement. Its instructions contain at most two conditional Pauli gate occurrences for Alice's encoding, one CNOT and one Hadamard for Bob, and two final measured wires. Thus it achieves the stated resource exchange for this procedure; no optimality statement is used.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

For arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$, put
$|\psi\rangle=\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle$ and
$V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, in wire order

$$V_{AB}(|\psi\rangle_A\otimes|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC})=\frac12\sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes X_C^bZ_C^a|\psi\rangle_C.$$

No normalization assumption on $|\psi\rangle$ is needed for this vector
identity.

For every qubit vector $|\psi\rangle$ and bits $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, the
teleportation branch byproduct is $X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$, and the prescribed
correction returns it exactly:

$$Z^aX^bX^bZ^a|\psi\rangle=|\psi\rangle.$$

The operator order is part of the statement; no Pauli factors are commuted.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator and $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ a finite projective measurement on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. Put $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$. If $p_a>0$, then

$$\rho_a:=\frac{P_a\rho P_a}{p_a}$$

is a density operator whose image $\operatorname{im}(\rho_a):=\{\rho_a x:x\in H\}$ is contained in $\operatorname{im}(P_a)$ ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]). This statement assigns a conditional state only on positive-probability branches.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

derivations.claim: For any instance of the theorem, choose an ordered orthonormal basis $\mathcal E_R=(e_j)_{j<d}$ of $R$ using [F11]. This supplies the reference-factor basis required by [F1]; together with the qubit computational bases, it gives product bases for the initial order $A,R,B,C$ and the stated global order $A,B,C,R$. Write $|\Psi\rangle_{AR}=\sum_{j<d}|\psi_j\rangle_A\otimes e_j$, where $|\psi_j\rangle=\alpha_j|0\rangle+\beta_j|1\rangle$. The canonical wire permutation in [F1] sends the initial vector to $\sum_j|\psi_j\rangle_A\otimes|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}\otimes e_j$. By [F3], for each (not necessarily normalized) qubit vector $|\psi_j\rangle$, the pre-measurement gates give $\frac12\sum_{a,b}|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes X^bZ^a|\psi_j\rangle_C$. Tensoring these identities with $e_j$ using [F2] and summing yields $$|\Omega\rangle_{ABCR}=\frac12\sum_{a,b}|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes (X^bZ^a\otimes I_R)|\Psi\rangle_{CR}.$$

Define $P_{ab}$ on $A,B,C,R$ as the diagonal projection onto product-basis vectors whose first two bits are $ab$. These four projections form a PVM because they partition the product basis from step 1.1; that product basis is orthonormal by [F1] and [F10]. Write $|\Omega\rangle=\sum_i c_i e_i$ in this basis and define $\rho_{ij}=c_i\overline{c_j}$. This rank-one matrix is self-adjoint and has nonnegative quadratic form $\langle\rho z,z\rangle=|\sum_j z_j\overline{c_j}|^2$. For each label, write $|\chi_{ab}\rangle=(X^bZ^a\otimes I_R)|\Psi\rangle$. The product inner product and the chosen basis of $R$ give $$\|\chi_{ab}\|^2=\sum_{j<d}\|X^bZ^a|\psi_j\rangle\|^2=\sum_{j<d}\|\psi_j\|^2=\|\Psi\|^2=1,$$ since [F9] shows that $X$ and $Z$ each preserve the qubit norm. The four $AB$ labels in step 1.1 are orthogonal, so $\|\Omega\|^2=\frac14\sum_{a,b}\|\chi_{ab}\|^2=1$. Thus [F8] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=\sum_i|c_i|^2=1$, and $\rho$ is a density operator by [F12]. The weight $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{ab})$ is the sum of the diagonal entries selected by $P_{ab}$, equal to $\|P_{ab}|\Omega\rangle\|^2=\frac14$; by [F6] these weights are probabilities.

Applying $P_{ab}$ to step 1.1 gives $\frac12|ab\rangle\otimes|\chi_{ab}\rangle$. Since $\|\chi_{ab}\|=1$ by step 2.1, this projected vector has norm $1/2$ and its normalized branch vector is exactly $|ab\rangle\otimes|\chi_{ab}\rangle$. Equivalently, [F7] gives conditional density $|ab\rangle\langle ab|_{AB}\otimes|\chi_{ab}\rangle\langle\chi_{ab}|_{CR}$ after division by the outcome weight $1/4$. Thus the conditional vector on $C\otimes R$ before Bob's correction is $|\chi_{ab}\rangle$.

Bob's correction acts on the $C$ factor as $Z^aX^b$. By [F2] and [F4], on every elementary tensor $x_C\otimes r_R$ its composition with $X^bZ^a\otimes I_R$ is $x_C\otimes r_R$; elementary tensors span by [F1], so it fixes the whole joint vector $|\Psi\rangle_{CR}$. The corrected normalized branch vector is therefore $|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes|\Psi\rangle_{CR}$, whose $C\otimes R$ factor is exactly the original input vector for every label.

The **teleportation procedure** has input a normalized qubit vector $|\psi\rangle_A\in Q_2$ and a preshared resource $|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}$, with Alice holding wires $A,B$ and Bob holding $C$. The wire order is $A,B,C$. It uses $|\Phi^+\rangle$ from [[def-qc-bell-basis]], CNOT with $A$ control and $B$ target from [[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], the Hadamard $H$ from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]], the Pauli matrices from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], and the finite projective measurement convention of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]].

1. Alice applies $\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$ and then $H_A$, so the combined operator is $V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, with the rightmost gate applied first.
2. Alice measures $A,B$ in their ordered computational basis and records the pair $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$, in that wire order.
3. Alice sends the two classical bits $a,b$ to Bob.
4. Bob applies $X_C^b$ and then $Z_C^a$, whose operator product is $Z_C^aX_C^b$.

The output is the corrected state on Bob's wire $C$. The shared Bell pair is an
input resource; its preparation and physical realization are outside this
procedure. A zero-probability measurement label has no conditional state and
is assigned no branch output; the normalized-input hypotheses here are later
shown to make all four labels positive.

For every normalized input qubit vector $|\psi\rangle$, the projective
measurement of the first two wires after the pre-measurement gates in
[[alg-qc-teleportation]] has
$\Pr[(a,b)]=1/4$ for each $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$.

For every qubit vector $|\psi\rangle$ and bits $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, the
teleportation branch byproduct is $X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$, and the prescribed
correction returns it exactly:

$$Z^aX^bX^bZ^a|\psi\rangle=|\psi\rangle.$$

The operator order is part of the statement; no Pauli factors are commuted.

Let $R$ be any finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$|\Psi\rangle_{AR}$ be any normalized vector on $Q_2\otimes R$, with no
product-state assumption. Run teleportation on $A$ using a shared
$|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}$, keeping the global wire order $A,B,C,R$ and applying
the canonical ordered tensor identifications. For every measured label $(a,b)$,
the corrected joint vector on $C\otimes R$ is exactly
$|\Psi\rangle_{CR}$, with $A$ relabelled as the output wire $C$.

For the procedure [[alg-qc-teleportation]], define a protocol-specific resource
record with separate coordinates as follows. A **shared-pair use** is one
initial Bell pair supplied as an input resource; its preparation is excluded.
A **classical communication bit** is one bit sent from Alice to Bob; the record
contains two. A **transmitted qubit** is a qubit sent during the protocol after
the shared pair is available; the record contains zero. A **measurement-record
bit** is one of the two ordered computational-basis outcomes measured by Alice;
the record contains two such bits. A **local gate occurrence** is counted by
the size convention of [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]], namely as one
gate occurrence in the declared circuit: Alice uses one CNOT and one Hadamard,
and Bob uses at most two conditional Pauli gate occurrences, $X^b$ and $Z^a$.
The pair preparation is not included among those gate occurrences. This record
counts the stated procedure only; it asserts no optimality or physical
realization.

For arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$, put
$|\psi\rangle=\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle$ and
$V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, in wire order
$A,B,C$. Then

$$V_{AB}(|\psi\rangle_A\otimes|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC})=\frac12\sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes X_C^bZ_C^a|\psi\rangle_C.$$

No normalization assumption on $|\psi\rangle$ is needed for this vector
identity.

derivations.claim: By [F2], each of the four possible labels has probability $1/4$, so every branch has positive probability and the conditional branch is defined. The Bell expansion [F6] identifies its receiver vector as $X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$.
