A **finite probability space** is a pair $(\Omega,w)$ consisting of a finite set $\Omega$ and a function $w:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ such that $w(\omega)\ge0$ for every $\omega\in\Omega$ and
$$\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}w(\omega)=1.$$
The elements of $\Omega$ are **outcomes**. Every subset $A\subseteq\Omega$ is an **event**, and its probability is
$$\mathbb P(A):=\sum_{\omega\in A}w(\omega).$$

An outcome of weight zero remains an outcome. Thus an event can be nonempty and still have probability zero.

For an integer $d\ge2$, use the relative $d\times d$ square patch with $n=2d^2$ data edges. Let $E$ be a set of actual $Z$-error edges and let $R$ be any minimum-cardinality correction satisfying $\partial_1R=\partial_1E$ (the same perfect syndrome). Recovery fails logically when $E\triangle R\notin\operatorname{im}\partial_2$. In that case $E\triangle R$ contains a self-avoiding primal path $P$ joining the left and right rough boundaries. Writing $\ell=|P|$, one has $d\le\ell\le n$ and $|P\cap E|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.

For the relative $d\times d$ square patch of
[[def-qc-square-planar-surface-code]], the code encodes one logical qubit and
has stabilizer distance $d$. Every nontrivial Z logical class contains a
rough-to-rough path of length at least $d$, and a straight row attains $d$.
Every nontrivial X logical class contains a top-to-bottom dual path of length
at least $d+1$. For each $\ell\ge1$, the number of self-avoiding
rough-to-rough paths of length $\ell$ is at most $(d+1)3^\ell$.

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, let $I$ be an index
set, and let $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of classes of events
$\mathcal C_i\subseteq\mathcal F$.

The family $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$ is **independent** when for every natural
number $n\ge1$, every choice of distinct indices $i_0,\dots,i_{n-1}\in I$, and
every choice of events $A_k\in\mathcal C_{i_k}$, one has

$$\mathbb P\left(\bigcap_{k<n}A_k\right)=\prod_{k<n}\mathbb P(A_k).$$

Thus independence is a finite-subfamily condition. In particular, the empty
family and every one-member family are independent.

For every finite family of events $A_0,\ldots,A_{n-1}$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i<n}A_i\right)\le\sum_{i<n}\mathbb P(A_i).$$
For $n=0$ both sides are $0$.

derivations.claim: Fix a candidate path $P$ of length $\ell$. A logical failure witness on it requires at least $k=\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ actual errors by [F2]. If at least $k$ of its $\ell$ edges are faulty, some $k$-subset is entirely faulty. There are at most $\binom\ell k\le2^\ell$ such subsets; by [F4] each has probability $\epsilon^k\le\epsilon^{\ell/2}$ for $\epsilon\in[0,1]$. The union bound [F5] gives $\mathbb P(P\text{ is a failure witness})\le2^\ell\epsilon^{\ell/2}$.

There are at most $(d+1)3^\ell$ candidate paths of length $\ell$ by [F3]. By [F2], every logical failure lies in the union of witness events for paths with $d\le\ell\le n$. The finite union bound [F5] and step 1.1 therefore give $P_{\mathrm{logical}}\le\sum_{\ell=d}^{n}(d+1)3^\ell 2^\ell\epsilon^{\ell/2}=(d+1)\sum_{\ell=d}^{n}(36\epsilon)^{\ell/2}$.

If $\epsilon<1/36$, set $r=6\sqrt{\epsilon}<1$. The finite sum is at most $\sum_{\ell=d}^{\infty}r^\ell=r^d/(1-r)$, so $P_{\mathrm{logical}}\le\frac{d+1}{1-6\sqrt{\epsilon}}(6\sqrt{\epsilon})^d$. The denominator is a fixed positive constant for fixed $\epsilon<1/36$, while $d+1$ is polynomial in $d$; hence the bound decays exponentially up to a polynomial prefactor.

Let $C$ be a finite channel-location schedule as in [[def-qc-finite-channel-location-schedule]], with finite ordered location set $L(C)$. A location is a supplied gate, preparation, measurement, reset, or explicitly scheduled idle channel with declared support $S_\ell$. The model does not create idle locations that the schedule did not declare.

Fix $\eta\in[0,1]$. A fault pattern is a subset $F\subseteq L(C)$. Its probability is
$$
\mathbb P(F)=\eta^{|F|}(1-\eta)^{|L(C)\setminus F|},
$$
where integer powers use the empty-product convention $x^0=1$, including at $x=0$. Thus each location faults with probability $\eta$, and the event classes generated by the fault/no-fault indicator at each location form an independent family in the sense of [[def-independent-families-of-event-classes]]. Conditional on $F$, each $\ell\in F$ replaces only the ideal operation at $\ell$ by an arbitrary CPTP map supported on $S_\ell$; all other locations apply their ideal channels. A replacement map may depend on the full pattern, but it acts only at its own location. Faults at measurement and reset locations are represented by channels on their declared quantum and classical registers.

This definition is the independent, local fault model: location indicators are independent, and each fault map acts at its own scheduled location.

Fix an integer $q\ge1$ and a recursively replaced gadget family with disjoint child rectangles as in [[def-qc-fault-location-path-and-rectangle]]. A level-zero rectangle is good exactly when its elementary location is fault-free, and is bad otherwise. Recursively, a level-$(r+1)$ rectangle is $q$-good exactly when at most $q$ of its level-$r$ child rectangles are bad; it is $q$-bad otherwise.

The implication from $q$-goodness to the ideal reference-preserving logical action is a property that must be proved from the gadget contracts in [[def-qc-ft-gadget-and-proper-code-contract]]. The definition of good and bad rectangles alone does not prove that implication. For each parent, the number of children is at most $a$, and their underlying elementary-location sets are pairwise disjoint.

In the independent local fault model, events determined by pairwise disjoint finite sets of location fault indicators are mutually independent. In particular, bad-rectangle events determined only by the faults in pairwise disjoint child rectangles are independent.

derivations.claim: Fix a level-$(r+1)$ rectangle. If it is bad, then some $(q+1)$-subset $J$ of its children consists entirely of bad level-$r$ rectangles. There are at most $A=\binom{a}{q+1}$ such subsets.

For each fixed $J$, its child-bad events depend on pairwise disjoint location sets, so they are independent by [F3]. Each has probability at most $p_r$; hence the probability that every child in $J$ is bad is at most $p_r^{q+1}$. Since the indicator of a finite union is at most the sum of its event indicators, summing probabilities over the at most $A$ choices of $J$ proves $p_{r+1}\le A p_r^{q+1}$.

Set $\theta=A^{1/q}\eta$. The asserted closed form holds at $r=0$, since $A^{-1/q}\theta=\eta$. If it holds at $r$, then $p_{r+1}\le A(A^{-1/q}\theta^{(q+1)^r})^{q+1}=A^{-1/q}\theta^{(q+1)^{r+1}}$, because $1-(q+1)/q=-1/q$. Induction proves the formula for every $r$.
The condition $A\eta^q<1$ is equivalent to $0\le\theta<1$. For $A\ge1$ and $q+1>1$, the exponent $(q+1)^r$ tends to infinity, so the closed-form upper bound tends to zero.

Consider one block of $m$ tensor factors $H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_m$, its code subspace $Q$, and an arbitrary finite reference system $R$. For an integer $s\ge0$, let $\mathcal E_s$ be the complex linear span of all operators on the block supported on at most $s$ physical coordinates, with support and weight as in [[def-qc-local-operator-support-and-weight]].

A density operator $\rho$ on the block and $R$ is $s$-deviated from a code-supported density operator $\sigma$ if there is a CPTP map $\mathcal N$ on the block with a finite Kraus family $K_1,\ldots,K_t\in\mathcal E_s$ such that $\rho=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\sigma)=\sum_{j=1}^t(K_j\otimes I_R)\sigma(K_j^\dagger\otimes I_R)$ and $\sum_{j=1}^tK_j^\dagger K_j=I$.
Here $\sigma$ is **code-supported** when its joint support is contained in $Q\otimes R$. The reference factor is retained in the identity above. Equality of reduced states outside a coordinate set is not the definition of deviation here.

For a finite family of live blocks indexed by $B$, use the joint error space $\mathcal E_s^{B}:=\operatorname{span}\{\bigotimes_{b\in B}A_b: A_b\text{ is supported on at most }s\text{ coordinates of block }b\}$. Joint $s$-deviation means the same Kraus formula with a single CPTP map on all live blocks, every Kraus operator in $\mathcal E_s^B$, and identity on the external reference alone. The ideal joint state is supported in $\bigotimes_{b\in B}Q_b\otimes R$. This includes the original one-block definition when $|B|=1$. The joint error map need not factor across blocks: a faulty multi-block gate can correlate their errors. Other live data blocks are part of the data system, not part of the unchanged external reference. Statements about deviation per block in a multi-block computation use this joint convention.

There is also a weaker **encoded instrument error-sector relation**, which does not require a CPTP extension to the whole physical input space. Fix the joint encoding $V_B=\bigotimes_{b\in B}V_b$. An $s$-supported encoded instrument is a finite family of completely positive branch maps from the joint logical register to the physical register, with Kraus operators

$$A_{\beta j}=E_{\beta j}V_B,\qquad E_{\beta j}\in\mathcal E_s^B,\qquad\sum_{\beta,j}A_{\beta j}^*A_{\beta j}=I_{H_L}.$$

Thus its full instrument is trace preserving on the admitted encoded input domain. A branch retains its actual subnormalized probability; neither it nor its normalized conditional output is required to extend to a full-space CPTP error map. With an ideal logical unitary $g$, replace $V_B$ in this formula by $V_Bg$. For other ideal logical instruments, state the analogous Kraus identities and output registers explicitly. Every equality is tensored with identity on an arbitrary finite external reference. With auxiliary fault memory $M$, allow coefficients on $M$, that is Kraus sums $\sum_a(E_aV_B)\otimes M_a$, and impose the full instrument's trace-preservation identity on $H_L\otimes M$. Memory output may change; after its trace, the logical/reference channel is the one required by the declared decoded-recovery identity.

A correcting gadget states the stronger input-sector/output-sector operator identity it needs: on every admitted incoming error term $EV_B$, its branch Kraus maps are sums of $E'V_Bg$ with the prescribed output support budget. Coefficients may depend on the incoming error term and on retained branch/memory registers, but not act on the logical factor. Linearity covers coherent incoming errors and correlated blocks. This is the sector convention for noisy correcting instruments. The earlier full-space CPTP deviation relation remains a sufficient, stronger relation; it is not redefined to mean this weaker encoded relation.

For an integer $\ell\ge1$, **literal support-propagation spread** applies to a specified unitary circuit segment: conjugating a fault operator supported on $S$ through the remaining fault-free unitary gates produces an operator supported on at most $\ell|S|$ output coordinates per block. For several faults, expand the finite Kraus families and take the union of their propagated supports. This gives the sum of the individual support bounds. The bound must account for all input blocks of a multi-block gate.

For a correcting, preparing or measuring gadget, an **effective spread budget** is instead part of an explicit input-sector/output-sector contract. The gadget declares its admitted joint error sectors, allowed fault supports, ideal logical channel or instrument, and joint residual-error sector for each allowed fault count. The required identities compare its decoded output with that ideal logical channel or instrument on every admitted input, with an arbitrary finite external reference. Measurement identities are identities of the subnormalized branch maps, not equations obtained by ignoring their probabilities. Any auxiliary fault memory is retained in the description of the faulty maps and may change there; it is distinct from the untouched external reference, and nonfaulty locations leave that memory alone. An identity that retains fault memory must specify its output memory action rather than silently identify it with the reference identity.

The numerical computation and correction budgets needed for sparse induction are explicitly imposed in the separately stated proper-code gadget contract; the word spread alone supplies none of those identities. In particular, incoming-error propagation and the full noisy correction action must be checked. Zero-fault recovery on arbitrary inputs remains a separate requirement. No global equation moving arbitrary input faults through a recovery channel on its whole input space is asserted.

A proper fault-tolerant code contract consists of a finite-dimensional code subspace $Q$ in a fixed block of $m$ physical coordinates, a finite logical gate alphabet $G$, and a fixed finite family of encoder, initialization, error-correction, decoder/readout, gate, syndrome-measurement, reset, and idle gadgets. Throughout this page, **universal** means that the subgroup generated by $G$ and its adjoints is dense in the unitary group on the logical space, in the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm]] (the supremum over the unit ball). The parameter $d$ is a located-error correction capacity: for an encoding isometry $V:H_L\to H_P$ and the declared decoded recovery channel $\mathcal R$, every channel $\mathcal N$ with Kraus operators supported on at most $d$ physical coordinates satisfies $\mathcal R\circ\mathcal N\circ\operatorname{Ad}_V=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B(H_L)}$, including after tensoring the identity on any finite reference. It is distinct from the stabilizer distance $d(S)$ of [[def-qc-stabilizer-distance]], the minimum weight of a Pauli centralizer class outside scalar phases times the stabilizer; a distance argument certifies capacity $d$ only after separately verifying $2d<d(S)$ and the relevant error-family hypotheses. When the concatenated-threshold theorem uses $m\ge 2d+1$, this inequality is an explicit hypothesis.

For several live blocks, the noisy stage requirements use the joint encoded-instrument error sectors of [[def-qc-code-deviation-and-spread]]. Full-space CPTP deviations remain sufficient inputs, but an output instrument is not required to have a full-space CPTP error extension. The fixed-recovery transfer proved in [[lem-qc-encoded-error-instrument-and-cptp-distinction]] supplies exact decoding of these sectors. Thus a fault may have arbitrary correlations between blocks while its support budget is bounded in each block; the untouched reference is external to all live data. The tensor product of the declared block recoveries must recover every trace-preserving encoded instrument in the joint $d$-error span, with that external reference retained after internal outcomes and fault memory are traced. Recorded logical measurement outcomes retain their stated ideal instrument law.

Each gadget specifies its finite input and output registers, ideal logical channel or instrument, fault locations and supports, depth, size, literal unitary support bounds and effective spread budget $\ell$ in the sense of [[def-qc-code-deviation-and-spread]], and a uniform upper bound $a$ on its child rectangles. Zero-fault gadgets implement their ideal channels exactly on encoded inputs, with the reference system preserved. The encoder implements its exact isometry on arbitrary logical inputs in the zero-fault case; the noisy guarantees begin at an admitted encoded input or the protected prescribed initialization. Every encoder location inside such a protected factory is counted and its faults must be handled. No guarantee corrects an arbitrary first fault on an unknown unprotected logical input. For every integer $q\ge1$ with $2q\ell\le d$, the checked computation-stage contract must say that an incoming joint encoded error instrument of budget $q\ell$ and at most $q$ bad child rectangles has joint output budget $2q\ell$ before correction; the checked correction-stage contract must correct every admitted joint input sector of budget at most $d$ and, with at most $q$ bad children, return joint residual budget $q\ell$ with the same decoded logical channel. Residual branch maps have the encoded Kraus form specified above. Their full instrument is trace preserving on the admitted domain, and after declared decoded recovery and trace of internal records it equals the ideal logical channel. These are subnormalized branch identities for every measurement outcome, with any finite external reference retained; a branch is not replaced by a normalized physical CPTP map. They quantify over arbitrary CPTP maps supported on the union of the faulty child supports, not only product fault maps. An error-correction gadget must also map arbitrary inputs into the code subspace in the zero-fault case. Its noisy identities are required on the specified joint encoded error sectors, rather than as a full-space intertwining of every input fault through ideal recovery. Any auxiliary fault memory may be updated at a faulty location and is carried in the channel/instrument description; only the external reference is constrained to the identity, and nonfaulty locations leave that memory alone. All preparation, syndrome, readout, classical-control, reset, and scheduled idle locations are included in the size and spread bounds.

The finite physical gate alphabet is closed under recursive replacement: every operation used by each gadget is itself in the declared alphabet. The contract makes no claim that a concrete code or gadget family satisfying it has been constructed. That existence and verification obligation is a separate theorem.

Fix an integer $q\ge1$ and a recursively replaced gadget family with disjoint child rectangles as in [[def-qc-fault-location-path-and-rectangle]]. A level-zero rectangle is good exactly when its elementary location is fault-free, and is bad otherwise. Recursively, a level-$(r+1)$ rectangle is $q$-good exactly when at most $q$ of its level-$r$ child rectangles are bad; it is $q$-bad otherwise.

The implication from $q$-goodness to the ideal reference-preserving logical action is a property that must be proved from the gadget contracts in [[def-qc-ft-gadget-and-proper-code-contract]]. The definition of good and bad rectangles alone does not prove that implication. For each parent, the number of children is at most $a$, and their underlying elementary-location sets are pairwise disjoint.

derivations.claim: At the initial encoded boundary the identity encoded instrument has error budget zero, hence at most $q\ell$. This is the induction invariant before the first computation stage.

Suppose a computation stage begins with an encoded input instrument of budget at most $q\ell$ per block. The computation-stage contract [F2], including propagation of the incoming errors rather than a false full-space recovery intertwiner, bounds the output by $2q\ell$ supported errors in each block. This is a joint error-space statement: products of terms with per-block supports $S_b,T_b$ have support contained in $S_b\cup T_b$, so $\mathcal E_u^B\mathcal E_v^B\subseteq\mathcal E_{u+v}^B$ by expanding the finite sums. Thus coherent Kraus sums and correlated bad-child maps are covered, and $2q\ell\le d$ gives correctability before correction. Thus the input to the actual correction stage lies in its declared correctable sector; no extra ideal recovery is inserted into the physical circuit.

The correction stage itself has at most $q$ bad child rectangles. Its correction contract in [F2] maps that joint pre-correction instrument to the same encoded target with at most $q\ell$ residual supported errors. Thus the induction invariant holds after the correction stage.

Induction over the finite sequence of computation and correction stages at each concatenation level gives joint encoded error budget at most $q\ell\le d$ after every correction stage. Composition preserves complete positivity and full trace preservation on the admitted domain; branch probabilities are retained. The tensor product of declared block recoveries in [F2] corrects that full joint residual instrument, so the decoded logical output is the ideal target. The contract and every correction step retain the identity on the reference.

Consider a finite recursively closed distance-three stabilizer-code simulation encoding one logical qubit per block, with the following **checked local gadget conditions**. The finite logical alphabet consists of unitary gates, prescribed one-block pure-state preparations (in particular the usual $|0\rangle$, $|+\rangle$ and any verified pure magic-state preparation), and destructive rank-one basis measurements, together with explicitly retained classical records and their declared controls. Each template is a finite directed circuit with declared input/output quantum and logical classical ports. Syndrome-processing and ancilla records of an EC are internal to that EC; the checked channel or instrument identity includes every logical classical port, with decoded recovery acting as identity on ports it does not decode. Its internal ancillas are freshly allocated or reset for that invocation; every wire crossing invocations is an explicit template port. Recursive replacement refines these ported vertices and wires, rather than introducing an undeclared shared scratch register. These are hypotheses about elementary gadgets, rather than a hypothesis of exRec correctness or of a witness reduction. Use a complete stabilizer Pauli recovery, with one chosen Pauli correction for every syndrome, including uncorrectable syndromes. Let $D$ be this recovery followed by ideal decoding; require the zero-fault EC $E_0$ to obey $D E_0=D$ on every input. Let $P_s$, $s=0,1$, project onto the span of weight-at-most-$s$ Pauli errors applied to codewords. Equalities below hold as channel equalities on the indicated subspaces, with arbitrary finite reference systems. They must also hold when a faulty location interacts with an auxiliary memory; the memory is untouched at nonfaulty locations.

For multiple blocks, the indicated error sector is the joint linear span of tensor Pauli errors with the indicated weight in each block, tensored with an unchanged external reference. Arbitrary coherent errors and correlations between data blocks are allowed; no product noise or product state is required.

An EC with $f\le1$ faults maps every input into $P_f$. For $s+f\le1$, it preserves decoded recovery on $P_s$: $D E_f P_s=D P_s$, where a projection in a channel identity denotes restriction to its range. A gate gadget $G_f$, with ideal logical unitary $g$, on inputs in $\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$, where $f+\sum_i s_i\le1$, has each output in $P_{f+\sum_i s_i}$ and satisfies $D^{\otimes\mathrm{out}}G_f=gD^{\otimes\mathrm{in}}$ on those inputs. A one-block preparation of a prescribed pure state with $f\le1$ faults has output in $P_f$ and decoded output its prescribed ideal state, independent of a reference or memory. A destructive measurement on $P_s$ with $s+f\le1$ has precisely the ideal logical instrument after $D$, including its retained classical outcome. Classical processing of the final outcomes is reliable. Idle gadgets satisfy the gate conditions. All scheduled operations, ancilla preparations, syndrome processing and measurements belong to these finite gadgets. Unknown unencoded inputs are not covered: initial inputs are encoded or are the prescribed preparations.

A rectangle is a gate gadget followed by output ECs; its extended rectangle (exRec) also includes its input ECs. Preparations have no input EC; destructive measurements have no output EC. Shared ECs are the only overlaps at a fixed scale. Use the following truncation convention recursively: when a later bad exRec claims an input EC, erase that shared EC from the earlier exRec, **including every elementary location belonging to the recursively expanded later exRec**. Here the expanded support is defined by the recursive input-collar construction in the proof: start with the ordinary recursively replaced gadget cores, and adjoin the leading lower-scale ECs of opening child roots, descending one scale at a time. Thus an erased EC also erases those opening lower-level ECs. Complete erased output ECs by ideal recovery ECs, starting at the lowest scale. Assume $b\ge2$ uniformly bounds the number of child-location roots in any complete one-scale exRec template, including its leading ECs; erased roots retain their template labels. Every recursive path has the declared full depth.

Scan roots in reverse circuit order. At scale zero a retained location is bad exactly when faulty. At scale $r\ge1$, perform the scale-$(r-1)$ scan inside the retained exRec, completing erased ECs ideally. Call the retained exRec bad if at least two bad child roots survive this scan, and good otherwise. A bad root claims its entire retained exRec; an earlier root loses any locations so claimed. A good root removes only its rectangle during decoding, leaving its leading ECs for the earlier scan. Use any fixed reverse topological order when roots are incomparable.

Then every good complete or truncated exRec is correct: its retained rectangle followed by decoded recovery equals decoded recovery at its input followed by the ideal logical operation, on the state produced by its retained leading ECs. The scan reduces the circuit exactly to its ideal circuit with faults only at selected bad roots. Each selected bad level-$r$ root has a full binary witness tree of depth $r$, with distinct faulty elementary leaves; trees of jointly selected bad roots have pairwise disjoint leaves. A fixed root has at most $A^{2^r-1}$ possible labelled witness trees, where $A=\binom b2$. Consequently, for any specified $k$ roots which are required to be jointly selected bad at level $r$, the independent elementary fault model gives
$$
\mathbb P(\text{all specified roots are selected bad})\le \bigl(A^{2^r-1}\eta^{2^r}\bigr)^k.
$$
This bound includes the dependence of truncation on the fault pattern; it does not assert independence of the selected bad-root events.

For every finite family of events $A_0,\ldots,A_{n-1}$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i<n}A_i\right)\le\sum_{i<n}\mathbb P(A_i).$$

The replacement at one location may depend on the full pattern $F$. For each outcome, the conditional noisy denotation is the chronological schedule obtained by using those replacements at faulty locations and the ideal channels elsewhere. It is a composition of per-location channels; the model does not add a joint operation across distinct locations.

This is a separate noise model from the independent local replacement model. Its probability hypothesis is the bound on every specified subset of fault locations; it does not assert independence. Correlation is allowed in the fault-set law and in the pattern-dependent choice of local fault maps, while each map remains attached to its own location.

Fix an integer $q\ge1$ and a recursively replaced gadget family with disjoint child rectangles as in [[def-qc-fault-location-path-and-rectangle]]. A level-zero rectangle is good exactly when its elementary location is fault-free, and is bad otherwise. Recursively, a level-$(r+1)$ rectangle is $q$-good exactly when at most $q$ of its level-$r$ child rectangles are bad; it is $q$-bad otherwise.

The implication from $q$-goodness to the ideal reference-preserving logical action is a property that must be proved from the gadget contracts in [[def-qc-ft-gadget-and-proper-code-contract]]. The definition of good and bad rectangles alone does not prove that implication. For each parent, the number of children is at most $a$, and their underlying elementary-location sets are pairwise disjoint.

Let $r\ge0$ and let a finite rooted rectangle hierarchy have every root-to-leaf path of exactly $r$ edges. Each leaf is one elementary location; every internal node has at most $a$ children, and the elementary-location sets of distinct children are disjoint. Let $a,q$ be integers with $1\le q<a$. A leaf is bad exactly when its location is faulty, and an internal node is bad exactly when at least $q+1$ children are bad. $$

$$

Let a proper gadget family correct $d$ located errors and have effective spread budget $\ell$ with the explicit joint computation and correction identities below. Let $q\ge1$ and $2q\ell\le d$. Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **trace distance** is
$$D(\rho,\sigma):=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$

$$0\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le1.$$

The finite physical gate alphabet is closed under recursive replacement: every operation used by each gadget is itself in the declared alphabet. Fix a nonzero finite-dimensional ordered tensor register $H=H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$ and an integer $M\ge0$. A finite channel-location schedule is an ordered list of slots $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_M$. Slot $\ell_t$ has an ideal quantum channel $\Phi_{\ell_t}:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(H)$ and a declared support $S_{\ell_t}\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. A channel is supported on $S_{\ell_t}$ when it has a finite Kraus representation all of whose Kraus operators are supported there in the sense of [[def-qc-local-operator-support-and-weight]]. The order is chronological: slot $\ell_1$ acts first. Its circuit denotation is the linear map

$$\Phi_{\ell_M}\circ\cdots\circ\Phi_{\ell_1},$$

with the empty schedule denoting the identity map on $\mathcal L(H)$. The definition records the full-register channels at the slots; gate, preparation, measurement, reset, classical-control, and scheduled-idle operations are included only when their corresponding local channels and supports are supplied. Any ancillary or classical record registers they use are factors of $H$. No unlisted idle slot is implicit. A pattern-dependent replacement at slot $\ell$ must be a quantum channel supported on the same $S_\ell$; the chosen replacement may depend on the full fault pattern, but no extra joint operation across distinct slots is part of this schedule.

For a finite channel-location schedule and any finite probability law on its fault patterns, suppose each conditional pattern replaces faulty locations by CPTP maps on their declared supports. Every conditional denotation is a CPTP channel, and the probability-weighted average of these denotations is a CPTP channel. No independence assumption on the fault-pattern law is required.

For every finite family of events $A_0,\ldots,A_{n-1}$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i<n}A_i\right)\le\sum_{i<n}\mathbb P(A_i).$$
For $n=0$ both sides are $0$.

derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to each level-$r$ rectangle. Its proof counts fault-witness sets and uses only the local-stochastic subset bound, so it requires no independence between child fault indicators. Thus each top-level circuit rectangle is bad with probability at most $p_r=A^{-1/q}(A^{1/q}\eta)^{(q+1)^r}$.

If $\eta=0$, each single-location fault event has probability zero by the local-stochastic subset bound; the finite union bound gives no faults almost surely, so level zero suffices. Otherwise put $\theta=A^{1/q}\eta\in(0,1)$ and $c=-\log\theta>0$. Any $r$ with $(q+1)^r\ge c^{-1}\log(NA^{-1/q}/\delta)$ is sufficient; if the logarithm is nonpositive or its positive value is at most $c$, $r=0$ suffices. For fixed parameters, the least qualifying $r$ is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$ as $N/\delta\to\infty$.

By [F11], the probability $\alpha$ that at least one of the $N$ top-level circuit rectangles is bad satisfies $\alpha\le Np_r$. For every fault pattern, [F9] gives a conditional channel, so its output on the fixed joint data input and external reference is a density operator. On the complementary event, recursive goodness gives at most $q$ bad children in every stage. The contract [F8] and sparse-path correction guarantee [F4] make each corrected logical stage ideal for the per-location channels allowed by [F1]. Thus every pattern with no bad top-level rectangle outputs $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}$. If $\alpha>0$, the normalized finite mixture of bad-pattern outputs is a density operator $\tau$; if $\alpha=0$, choose any density operator for $\tau$. Then $\rho_{\mathrm{out}}=(1-\alpha)\rho_{\mathrm{id}}+\alpha\tau$, and [F10] confirms that the weighted schedule output is a channel.

By homogeneity of trace distance and [F6], $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})=\alpha D(\tau,\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le\alpha\le Np_r$. Applying [F7] to the final POVM bounds its output total-variation distance by $Np_r$, and every success event changes by at most that total-variation distance.

Because the gadget family is fixed and finite, choose a constant $\kappa\ge1$ bounding both the number of elementary locations and the scheduled depth of every replacement gadget, including preparation, control, reset, and idle locations. Replacing each location of a schedule of size $S$ and depth $D$ gives size at most $S\kappa$ and depth at most $D\kappa$: replace disjoint locations of each original layer in parallel and pad their gadgets to the common depth bound. Induction gives size at most $S\kappa^r$ and depth at most $D\kappa^r$ at level $r$. Thus the multiplicative size and depth overheads are at most $\kappa^r$, which is a fixed power of $\log(N/\delta)$ by step 1.2.

Every conditional denotation is a CPTP channel, and the probability-weighted average of these denotations is a CPTP channel. No independence assumption on the fault-pattern law is required.

derivations.claim: Since $q=\lfloor d/(2\ell)\rfloor$, we have $2q\ell\le d$. Also $A\ge1$, and $A\eta^q<1$ gives $\theta:=A^{1/q}\eta<1$. Apply [F2] to obtain $p_r\le A^{-1/q}\theta^{(q+1)^r}$.

If $\eta=0$, the product fault law gives probability zero to every nonempty fault pattern, so $p_0=0$ and level zero suffices. If $\eta>0$, put $c=-\log\theta>0$. Any $r$ with $(q+1)^r\ge c^{-1}\log(NA^{-1/q}/\delta)$ gives $Np_r\le\delta$ by [F2]; if the logarithm is nonpositive or its positive value is at most $c$, level $r=0$ suffices. For fixed $A,q,\eta$ with $0<\theta<1$, the least qualifying level is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$ as $N/\delta\to\infty$.

The event that any of the $N$ top-level circuit rectangles is bad is the union of $N$ events, each of probability at most $p_r$. The finite union bound [F8] gives $\alpha:=\mathbb P(\text{some top-level rectangle is bad})\le Np_r$.

For every fault pattern, [F9] gives a conditional channel, so its output on the fixed joint data input and external reference is a density operator. On the event that all top-level rectangles are $q$-good, recursive goodness gives at most $q$ bad children in each computation and correction stage. The gadget contracts [F7] and sparse-path induction [F3] then make every corrected stage ideal, so every such pattern outputs $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}$. If $\alpha>0$, the normalized finite mixture of outputs from bad patterns is a density operator $\tau$; if $\alpha=0$, choose any density operator for $\tau$. Thus $\rho_{\mathrm{out}}=(1-\alpha)\rho_{\mathrm{id}}+\alpha\tau$, and [F10] confirms that this weighted schedule output is a channel.

By homogeneity of the trace norm, $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})=\alpha D(\tau,\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le\alpha\le Np_r$, where the first inequality is [F5]. The same identity holds after tensoring any reference identity, since the gadget contracts preserve the external reference after internal outcomes and fault memory are traced.

Apply [F6] to the final finite POVM. Its output total-variation distance is at most $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le Np_r$. For any success event $E$, $|P_{\mathrm{out}}(E)-P_{\mathrm{id}}(E)|\le \tfrac12\sum_x|P_{\mathrm{out}}(x)-P_{\mathrm{id}}(x)|$, so the success-probability change is at most $Np_r$.

Because the gadget family is fixed and finite, choose a constant $\kappa\ge1$ bounding both the number of elementary locations and the scheduled depth of every replacement gadget, including preparation, control, reset, and idle locations. Replacing each location of a schedule of size $S$ and depth $D$ gives size at most $S\kappa$ and depth at most $D\kappa$: replace disjoint locations of each original layer in parallel and pad their gadgets to the common depth bound. Induction gives size at most $S\kappa^r$ and depth at most $D\kappa^r$ at level $r$. Thus the multiplicative size and depth overheads are at most $\kappa^r$, which is a fixed power of $\log(N/\delta)$ by step 1.2.

For each integer $d\ge2$, use the relative $d\times d$ square patch, which has $n=2d^2$ data qubits. On a finite probability space, let each data edge independently carry a $Z$ error with probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$. For each syndrome, choose any minimum-cardinality correction; the bound below holds for every such choice. Under one perfect syndrome round, the logical-memory failure probability satisfies
$$
P_{\mathrm{logical}}\le (d+1)\sum_{\ell=d}^{n}(36\epsilon)^{\ell/2}.
$$
Consequently $P_{\mathrm{logical}}$ decays exponentially in $d$, up to a polynomial prefactor, for $\epsilon<1/36$. This is an ideal-syndrome memory theorem; it is not a faulty-gate circuit threshold.

Applying [F1] yields the stated conditional failure-probability bound. The hypotheses include perfect syndrome extraction; this example makes no faulty-gate threshold claim.

Let $C_2\subseteq C_1\le\mathbb F_2^n$, $n\ge1$, and
$k=\dim C_1-\dim C_2$. The coset vectors from
[[def-qc-css-code-from-nested-binary-codes]] define an isometric encoding of
$k$ logical qubits. For every $c\in C_2$ and $h\in C_1^\perp$, $X^c$ and
$Z^h$ commute, and each fixes every encoded coset vector. Their common
$+1$ eigenspace is exactly this encoding. The conclusion requires only
$C_2\subseteq C_1$; it does not require
$C_2^\perp\subseteq C_1$.

Moreover, for every $x\in C_1$, the Hadamard transform is

$$H^{\otimes n}|x+C_2\rangle=2^{-k/2}\sum_{y+C_1^\perp\in C_2^\perp/C_1^\perp}(-1)^{x\cdot y}|y+C_1^\perp\rangle.$$

The phase is independent of the representatives $x+C_2$ and
$y+C_1^\perp$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be an abelian group of Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators with
$-I\notin S$, generated by $r$ independent checks. Then

$$P_S:=|S|^{-1}\sum_{g\in S}g$$

is the orthogonal projector onto the stabilizer code space and has rank
$2^{n-r}$. In particular, the code space is nonzero, including when $r=n$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer code on $n$ qubits whose code space has dimension
$2^k$. The stabilizer **distance** is

$$d(S):=\min\{\operatorname{wt}(E):E\in N(S)\setminus Z_nS\}\quad\text{if }k>0.$$

This is a set difference: it excludes scalar-phase multiples of stabilizers.
If $k=0$, define $d(S)=+\infty$, since there is no nontrivial logical Pauli
class.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer code on $n$ qubits of distance $d(S)$. Every Pauli error $E$ of
weight less than $d(S)$ either acts as a scalar on the code space (when
$E\in Z_nS$) or is detected by some stabilizer check. A finite error channel
whose Kraus operators lie in the span of Pauli operators of weight at most
$t$, for $t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, is correctable whenever $2t<d(S)$. In particular, all unknown Pauli
errors of weight at most $t$ are correctable.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

Consider one block of $m$ tensor factors $H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_m$, its code subspace $Q$, and an arbitrary finite reference system $R$. For an integer $s\ge0$, let $\mathcal E_s$ be the complex linear span of all operators on the block supported on at most $s$ physical coordinates, with support and weight as in [[def-qc-local-operator-support-and-weight]].

A density operator $\rho$ on the block and $R$ is $s$-deviated from a code-supported density operator $\sigma$ if there is a CPTP map $\mathcal N$ on the block with a finite Kraus family $K_1,\ldots,K_t\in\mathcal E_s$ such that $\rho=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\sigma)=\sum_{j=1}^t(K_j\otimes I_R)\sigma(K_j^\dagger\otimes I_R)$ and $\sum_{j=1}^tK_j^\dagger K_j=I$.
Here $\sigma$ is **code-supported** when its joint support is contained in $Q\otimes R$. The reference factor is retained in the identity above. Equality of reduced states outside a coordinate set is not the definition of deviation here.

For a finite family of live blocks indexed by $B$, use the joint error space $\mathcal E_s^{B}:=\operatorname{span}\{\bigotimes_{b\in B}A_b: A_b\text{ is supported on at most }s\text{ coordinates of block }b\}$. Joint $s$-deviation means the same Kraus formula with a single CPTP map on all live blocks, every Kraus operator in $\mathcal E_s^B$, and identity on the external reference alone. The ideal joint state is supported in $\bigotimes_{b\in B}Q_b\otimes R$. This includes the original one-block definition when $|B|=1$. The joint error map need not factor across blocks: a faulty multi-block gate can correlate their errors. Other live data blocks are part of the data system, not part of the unchanged external reference. Statements about deviation per block in a multi-block computation use this joint convention.

There is also a weaker **encoded instrument error-sector relation**, which does not require a CPTP extension to the whole physical input space. Fix the joint encoding $V_B=\bigotimes_{b\in B}V_b$. An $s$-supported encoded instrument is a finite family of completely positive branch maps from the joint logical register to the physical register, with Kraus operators

$$A_{\beta j}=E_{\beta j}V_B,\qquad E_{\beta j}\in\mathcal E_s^B,\qquad\sum_{\beta,j}A_{\beta j}^*A_{\beta j}=I_{H_L}.$$

Thus its full instrument is trace preserving on the admitted encoded input domain. A branch retains its actual subnormalized probability; neither it nor its normalized conditional output is required to extend to a full-space CPTP error map. With an ideal logical unitary $g$, replace $V_B$ in this formula by $V_Bg$. For other ideal logical instruments, state the analogous Kraus identities and output registers explicitly. Every equality is tensored with identity on an arbitrary finite external reference. With auxiliary fault memory $M$, allow coefficients on $M$, that is Kraus sums $\sum_a(E_aV_B)\otimes M_a$, and impose the full instrument's trace-preservation identity on $H_L\otimes M$. Memory output may change; after its trace, the logical/reference channel is the one required by the declared decoded-recovery identity.

A correcting gadget states the stronger input-sector/output-sector operator identity it needs: on every admitted incoming error term $EV_B$, its branch Kraus maps are sums of $E'V_Bg$ with the prescribed output support budget. Coefficients may depend on the incoming error term and on retained branch/memory registers, but not act on the logical factor. Linearity covers coherent incoming errors and correlated blocks. This is the sector convention for noisy correcting instruments. The earlier full-space CPTP deviation relation remains a sufficient, stronger relation; it is not redefined to mean this weaker encoded relation.

For an integer $\ell\ge1$, **literal support-propagation spread** applies to a specified unitary circuit segment: conjugating a fault operator supported on $S$ through the remaining fault-free unitary gates produces an operator supported on at most $\ell|S|$ output coordinates per block. For several faults, expand the finite Kraus families and take the union of their propagated supports. This gives the sum of the individual support bounds. The bound must account for all input blocks of a multi-block gate.

For a correcting, preparing or measuring gadget, an **effective spread budget** is instead part of an explicit input-sector/output-sector contract. The gadget declares its admitted joint error sectors, allowed fault supports, ideal logical channel or instrument, and joint residual-error sector for each allowed fault count. The required identities compare its decoded output with that ideal logical channel or instrument on every admitted input, with an arbitrary finite external reference. Measurement identities are identities of the subnormalized branch maps, not equations obtained by ignoring their probabilities. Any auxiliary fault memory is retained in the description of the faulty maps and may change there; it is distinct from the untouched external reference, and nonfaulty locations leave that memory alone. An identity that retains fault memory must specify its output memory action rather than silently identify it with the reference identity.

The numerical computation and correction budgets needed for sparse induction are explicitly imposed in the separately stated proper-code gadget contract; the word spread alone supplies none of those identities. In particular, incoming-error propagation and the full noisy correction action must be checked. Zero-fault recovery on arbitrary inputs remains a separate requirement. No global equation moving arbitrary input faults through a recovery channel on its whole input space is asserted.

derivations.claim: The columns of $B$ are the seven distinct nonzero vectors of $\mathbb F_2^3$, and its last three columns are the standard basis, so its rank is three. Each row has weight four and any two distinct rows have overlap two; hence $BB^{\mathsf T}=0$ and $D\subseteq D^\perp$. Every nonzero word of $D$ evaluates a nonzero linear functional on these seven columns. Such a functional takes value one on four of the eight vectors of $\mathbb F_2^3$, and takes value zero on the zero vector, so all seven nonzero words of $D$ have weight four. Also $Bx^{\mathsf T}=0$ and $\operatorname{wt}(x)=3$, so $x\in D^\perp\setminus D$. Since $\dim D^\perp=4$, it follows that $D^\perp=D\sqcup(x+D)$. The two coset sums defining $V$ are orthonormal.

The six checks $X^b,Z^b$, with $b$ ranging over the rows of $B$, are independent commuting Hermitian Paulis, and their common fixed space is $\operatorname{im}V$ by [F1]. A Pauli $i^kX^uZ^v$ centralizes them exactly when $u,v\in D^\perp$, and is a scalar-phase stabilizer exactly when $u,v\in D$. No nonzero word of $D^\perp=\ker B$ has weight one or two, since the columns of $B$ are nonzero and distinct. Thus a nontrivial centralizer class has weight at least three. The operators $X^x,Z^x$ attain three and act respectively as logical $X,Z$ on the displayed basis: translation by $x$ exchanges the cosets, and $x\cdot(ax+c)=a$ since $x\cdot x=1$ and $x\perp D$. Therefore this seven-qubit code has distance exactly three.

Since $D^\perp/D$ has representatives $0,x$, $x\cdot x=1$, and $D=(D^\perp)^\perp$, the exact Hadamard formula in [F1] gives $H^{\otimes7}V=VH$. For $c\in D$, its weight is zero or four, so $i^{\operatorname{wt}(c)}=1$. For $x+c$, the weight identity $\operatorname{wt}(x+c)=\operatorname{wt}(x)+\operatorname{wt}(c)-2|\operatorname{supp}(x)\cap\operatorname{supp}(c)|$ is congruent to three modulo four: the first weight is three, the second is divisible by four, and the intersection size is even because $x\perp D$. Thus $S^{\otimes7}V=VS^\dagger$, with no additional scalar phase. Taking adjoints of this diagonal action also gives $(S^\dagger)^{\otimes7}V=VS$.

Partition the $49$ coordinates into seven ordered inner blocks. Take the six inner checks from step 2.1 in each block, giving $42$ checks. Lift the six outer checks by replacing their single-qubit $X,Z$ factors with the inner representatives $X^x,Z^x$. All $48$ checks commute: inner checks commute with these representatives, and the representatives obey exactly the one-qubit Pauli commutation rule on each block because $x\cdot x=1$. The checks are independent. Indeed, reducing a relation among them modulo the seven inner stabilizer groups leaves a relation among the six independent outer Pauli labels; thus all six outer exponents vanish, and independence of the disjoint inner checks then makes the remaining $42$ exponents vanish. They fix every vector in $\operatorname{im}W$, so their group excludes $-I$. By [F2] their fixed space has dimension $2^{49-48}=2$ and consequently equals $\operatorname{im}W$.

On the pair of encoded computational basis states with logical bits $a,b$, coordinatewise CNOT sends the summand $|ax+c\rangle|bx+e\rangle$ to $|ax+c\rangle|(a+b)x+c+e\rangle$. The substitution $(c,e)\mapsto(c,c+e)$ is a bijection of $D\times D$, so the transformed sum is exactly $V|a\rangle\otimes V|a+b\rangle$. Linearity gives the seven-coordinate CNOT intertwining identity. Applying it first in every inner block pair and then to the outer encoding proves the stated $49$-coordinate identity. Likewise step 2.2 at the inner and outer levels gives $H^{\otimes49}W=WH$ and $S^{\otimes49}W=V^{\otimes7}(S^\dagger)^{\otimes7}V=WS$.

Let $E$ centralize these $48$ checks. Its restriction to each inner block centralizes the six inner checks. Modulo an inner stabilizer and scalar phase, that restriction is uniquely one of $I,X^x,Z^x,X^xZ^x$, by the description $D^\perp/D$ in step 1.1 and step 2.1. Its seven labels therefore define an outer Pauli. Commutation with the lifted outer checks says exactly that this outer Pauli centralizes the seven-qubit outer code. If its outer class is trivial, multiplying the corresponding lifted outer stabilizers leaves an inner stabilizer in each block; hence $E$ is a scalar-phase stabilizer of the $49$-qubit code. Otherwise at least three inner blocks have nontrivial labels by step 2.1, and each of those restrictions has weight at least three. Thus every nontrivial class has weight at least nine. Lift the weight-three outer logical $X^x$ using weight-three inner $X^x$ in its three occupied blocks. This gives a nontrivial logical Pauli of weight nine. The distance is therefore exactly nine.

Let $E_1,\ldots,E_M$ list all phase-free Paulis of weight at most four. Their normalized Kraus family $E_a/\sqrt M$ defines a channel, since each $E_a$ is unitary. Apply [F4] with $t=4$, since $2t=8<9$, and compose its recovery with inverse encoding to obtain a decoded recovery $\mathcal R$ with Kraus operators $R_j$. This one recovery works uniformly on the entire error span. Indeed its correction of the displayed mixed-Pauli channel means that the operators $R_jE_aW/\sqrt M$ are Kraus operators of the identity logical channel. Each must be a scalar multiple of the logical identity: for every pure logical input their output vectors must lie in its one-dimensional span, since their positive rank-one output sum is that pure input; applying this to a basis and its pairwise sums makes the scalar independent of the input. Thus $R_jE_aW=c_{ja}I_L$. For any channel with Kraus operators $K_h=\sum_a\alpha_{ha}E_a$, it follows that $R_jK_hW=(\sum_a\alpha_{ha}c_{ja})I_L$; trace preservation makes the sum of squared scalar moduli one. Therefore the decoded channel is the identity, also after tensoring every operator with $I_R$. This proves uniform capacity four and hence the declared smaller capacity two.

Each circuit consists of $49$ disjoint one- or two-qubit gates in one layer, so its size is $49$ and its depth is one. In a CNOT layer a location touches one coordinate in each block; in a one-block layer it touches one coordinate. Replacing any chosen locations by an arbitrary joint CPTP map supported on their union changes no other output coordinate, since all other gates are disjoint from that union. The same support assertion holds for every Kraus operator, including after tensoring $I_R$; no product assumption on the joint fault map is used. Thus one faulty location has spread at most one per block, and any collection has the union bound in [F6]. Conjugating an input-supported operator by a transversal layer also preserves coordinate labels, except that CNOT may transfer its support to the matching coordinate of the other block. Input supports $A,B$ therefore give output supports contained in $A\cup B$ in each block. This proves all gate and spread assertions.

citations.quote:
Let $C$ be a finite channel-location schedule as in [[def-qc-finite-channel-location-schedule]], with finite ordered location set $L(C)$. A location is a supplied gate, preparation, measurement, reset, or explicitly scheduled idle channel with declared support $S_\ell$. The model does not create idle locations that the schedule did not declare.

Fix $\eta\in[0,1]$. A fault pattern is a subset $F\subseteq L(C)$. Its probability is
$$
\mathbb P(F)=\eta^{|F|}(1-\eta)^{|L(C)\setminus F|},
$$
where integer powers use the empty-product convention $x^0=1$, including at $x=0$. Thus each location faults with probability $\eta$, and the event classes generated by the fault/no-fault indicator at each location form an independent family in the sense of [[def-independent-families-of-event-classes]]. Conditional on $F$, each $\ell\in F$ replaces only the ideal operation at $\ell$ by an arbitrary CPTP map supported on $S_\ell$; all other locations apply their ideal channels. A replacement map may depend on the full pattern, but it acts only at its own location. Faults at measurement and reset locations are represented by channels on their declared quantum and classical registers.

This definition is the independent, local fault model: location indicators are independent, and each fault map acts at its own scheduled location.

For every finite family of events $A_0,\ldots,A_{n-1}$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcup_{i<n}A_i\right)\le\sum_{i<n}\mathbb P(A_i).$$
For $n=0$ both sides are $0$.

derivations.claim: Choose a complete stabilizer syndrome decoder $U:H_P\to H_L\otimes H_S$, using the stipulated Pauli recovery representative for each syndrome. The stabilizer eigenspaces are mutually orthogonal copies of the code, so this map is unitary. Write $\mathcal U=\operatorname{Ad}_U$ and $D=\operatorname{Tr}_S\mathcal U$. Recursively, $U_j$ first applies $U_{j-1}$ to each subblock and then $U$ to the resulting logical coordinates, retaining every syndrome register. Thus $H_{P,j}=H_L\otimes H_{S,j}$ after applying $U_j$. A weight-filter sector becomes $H_L\otimes S_0$ or $H_L\otimes S_1$, where $S_s$ is the span of syndrome basis vectors of errors of weight at most $s$. For a degenerate code, errors with the same syndrome give the same copy of the logical space, so this assertion remains true. All tensor products below include the external reference unchanged.

Here are the actual circuit boundaries used below. An ordinary gadget core is its recursive replacement circuit, before adjoining leading ECs of its opening child roots. Give every child slot its schedule address and every shared EC one physical address. To expand an exRec, adjoin those opening leading EC cores, then their opening leading EC cores at the next lower scale, and continue downwards. An added leading $j$-EC is the output $j$-EC of the previous $j$-rectangle on precisely that wire; it does not include the previous gate. Thus after a later bad root claims its expanded support, its earlier neighbors lose only output ECs at the outer scale and at successively lower scales. Each affected lower rectangle still has the full input and output registers of its own gate. Its missing EC wires are connected directly from the last retained operation to the first operation owned by the later root. Register identity along that connection does not assert equality of their states after any recovery. This is a boundary in the actual retained directed circuit, not a factor of a remotely placed final decoder. Gates on other wires may lie between its endpoints in a linear schedule; none lies on that wire between these endpoints, by the definition of the preceding rectangle.

At scale one let $s_i$ count faults in the leading ECs, $f$ those in the gate, and $t_a$ those in the output ECs which are present. If their total is at most one, the leading ECs put the input in $\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$. The gate takes this entire sector into $P_{s+f}$ on each output, where $s=\sum_i s_i$, and has decoded logical action $g$. Every present output EC preserves that action because $s+f+t_a\le1$. If an output EC is absent, the decoded gate identity already gives precisely the same conclusion on that output; no EC is inserted. This proves, simultaneously for every subset $J$ of output ECs retained, $D_{\rm out}E_JG_f|_{\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}}=gD_{\rm in}|_{\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}}$. The corresponding preparation and destructive-measurement identities are exactly those in [A1]. This establishes the base assertion for complete and truncated rectangles together.

Contract ordinary recursively replaced cores first. By the stated port discipline this recovers their parent circuit DAG: all internal ancillas close within their invocation, and each external quantum or classical wire is a parent edge. Moving a shared EC from an earlier rectangle to a following selected bad exRec transfers an output-terminal subcircuit forward along that edge. No output of the moved piece returns to a retained operation of the earlier owner. To check the last assertion at nested boundaries, take the first lower EC core adjoined across the boundary: it is the trailing EC immediately before the first opening child in the already transferred piece. A retained gate on that wire between it and that child would contradict their being consecutive. Any other output of that EC is an internal ancilla, closed within the same EC, or another output in that same block bundle. Repeat at smaller scales. Thus every collar piece transferred forward is terminal on all its external output wires in the retained earlier owner. All external outputs of the transferred EC feed the claiming successor: syndrome-processing records are internal, and the quantum output is precisely that successor's input bundle. Thus each new quotient edge into the successor replaces an old forward path through the preceding owner and that EC; there is no new outgoing edge to a third owner. Such a transfer cannot create a quotient cycle, since replacing every new edge by its old forward path would give a cycle in the previous DAG. Repeating these finite transfers, in the prescribed reverse root order and descending collar scale, gives disjoint owners and a causal quotient DAG. The owner's interface can be staggered in elementary time; at a stagger use its complete child block bundles, descending until each bundle is exposed. Every primitive multi-register operation belongs to one owner and is never split. This also proves that the quotient's root labels and the addresses erased at its boundaries are exactly those in the stated scan.

We will retain the syndromes in that identity. If a CPTP map $M$ on $H_L\otimes K$ has logical marginal $g\operatorname{Tr}_K$ for every input, its conjugation by $g^{-1}$ has identity logical marginal. Its Choi matrix has marginal supported on the one-dimensional maximally entangled logical subspace. Positivity forces the entire Choi matrix to have support in that subspace tensored with the remaining registers; hence it factors as the identity-channel Choi matrix times the Choi matrix of a CPTP map on $K$. Consequently $M=\operatorname{Ad}_g\otimes T$. Apply this to the entire filter sector in step 2.1, which by step 1.1 is the full logical space tensored with an allowed syndrome subspace. It gives an exact syndrome-retaining identity on that sector, including all input correlations. Extend $T$ to the remaining syndrome space by first projecting onto this sector and its orthogonal complement and using any fixed channel on the complement. Only the restriction is used on reachable states. For a prescribed pure preparation, its pure logical marginal forces its joint logical/syndrome output to be that state tensored with a syndrome state; this follows by the same positivity-support argument. For a good destructive measurement there is no syndrome output: its full quantum-to-classical channel on the admitted sector is exactly the ideal measurement following $\operatorname{Tr}_S$, with all other-block syndromes included in the unchanged external reference. Retain its classical output as a logical wire. No tensor-factor theorem for a general instrument is being assumed.

Fix the elementary pattern. Its replacement maps are fixed local CPTP maps by [F1]; they have no unlisted persistent memory port. Contract each actual physical owner in the DAG of step 2.2, before introducing any syndrome coordinates. It is a channel $B$ on its declared block bundles and classical ports; other live blocks are references. Now change coordinates at its actual input and output bundles: $\widehat B=\mathcal U_{\rm out}B\mathcal U_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so $\mathcal U_{\rm out}B=\widehat B\mathcal U_{\rm in}$ exactly. Insert $\mathcal U^{-1}\mathcal U$ on each internal block edge of that DAG; the adjacent pairs cancel. At a staggered interface use the lower bundles of step 2.2 and keep the upper decoder on their logical outputs. No decoder crosses an intervening retained gate. In this construction a syndrome register is the coordinate of its particular physical block edge, not a new global bath: a multi-block operation can process syndromes only on its declared block ports, and a destructive measurement has no outgoing quantum or syndrome port. Thus the coordinate change introduces no extra cross-owner memory edge or cycle. In particular, for a bad owner $\widehat B$ is the conjugation of the ORIGINAL retained physical channel, with its original incoming syndromes. Its logical support is only its declared blocks and classical ports, and its elementary support has not enlarged. Neither a physical ideal recovery nor the false identity $U_j\mathcal E_j=U_j$ has been inserted.

To compare this exact network to the scan, distinguish a restored address from its original physical address: the former is a virtual ideal copy at the same template slot; the original, if claimed by a later bad owner, stays with that owner. Restore the erased cores and collars from the smallest scale upwards. We prove by address induction that every opening EC address of a virtual child is also virtual. Within its restored core this is immediate; at the input boundary the address is one of the leading ECs adjoined by the expanded-support rule of step 1.2, hence was claimed and erased together with that core, and is restored as a fresh ideal copy. Repeat down to elementary addresses. Therefore every wholly added child's entire expanded support is ideal, not merely its gate core. It is good at scale zero and, inductively, at every scale, so it makes no claim on a retained physical address. A retained child's new output EC pieces have just this property; its original physical faults and original leading addresses are unchanged. Induct on its scale: the added child roots are good and make no erasure, and the original child roots have unchanged bad flags and unchanged claims on original addresses. Hence the selected bad children and their template labels agree with the scan in which those output EC pieces are absent. This proves the needed scan mapping without replacing any retained real context by an ideal channel.

Specify the induction domain at one actual INPUT boundary, rather than intersecting constraints at different circuit times. Fix the fault pattern, root and truncation. At every exposed opening lower block port record the filter required by that opening component's leading EC; impose no filter at an opening bad component. Also record the outer one-scale filter $P_{s_i}$ on the decoded subblock coordinates of each parent input block, where $s_i$ counts the effective faults in its leading EC. These are all conditions on the same input registers. Under the recursive decoder each lower-port filter constrains the syndrome register of its decoder-tree node; the outer filter constrains the outer syndrome register. Each acts as identity on the final logical coordinates by step 1.1. Thus their joint allowed space is $U_{j,\rm in}^{-1}(H_{L,\rm in}\otimes K_\partial)$ for a syndrome subspace $K_\partial$ (use a direct sum of allowed syndrome tuples if several boundary cases are allowed). No filter at a later intermediate time is included in this definition. We prove simultaneously at scale $j$: a good retained rectangle has ideal logical action on EVERY state in this full input space, with arbitrary reference; its syndrome-retaining form is the factor in step 3.1; a bad owner is its original exact conjugation; and a leading-EC subnetwork with $f\le1$ effective child faults puts its decoded subblock coordinates in $P_f$, preserving their decoded logical state on $P_s$ when $s+f\le1$. The EC assertion is on those decoded coordinates, not a claim of weight-at-most-one elementary error at every concatenation level. At scale one these assertions are exactly [A1] and step 2.1 and step 3.1.

Suppose the assertion holds at every scale at most $j$. Decompose a retained level-$(j+1)$ exRec using the actual level-$j$ block interfaces of step 2.2, descending through staggered collars. All components used here have scale at most $j$. Start with an arbitrary state in the full input sector of step 4.1, and process this DAG in topological order. For each next good component its leading EC is either at the initial boundary, where the required filter is part of $K_\partial$, or is already in the processed prefix, where the lower-scale EC assertion forces that filter on EVERY incoming state. A bad component needs no input filter. This forward support induction proves eligibility of each lower-scale identity for every state in the parent input sector; it does not infer eligibility merely from one particular image of the parent leading EC. Contract their original channels and change coordinates as in step 3.2. The induction hypothesis replaces a good unitary component by its ideal logical gate and a syndrome-only channel; a good preparation by its prescribed pure logical state and a syndrome state; and a good destructive measurement by its ideal quantum-to-classical channel, discarding that measured block's syndrome. Classical outcomes remain explicit logical wires. On other blocks all syndrome registers remain references. The tensor syndrome channels on the surviving block edges commute with ideal logical gates on those edges, and with a measurement on its logical coordinate before its syndrome is discarded. If the parent is good there is at most one bad component by step 3.3. Keep each syndrome-edge channel in causal order. Its causal past supplies an arbitrary finite syndrome-memory input to that one fault; its causal future has no further access to logical data through a fault. After tracing the final syndromes, those future trace-preserving memory channels have no effect on the logical instrument and can be removed, even when conditioned on retained classical outcomes. With no bad component the whole syndrome network is of this harmless kind. Thus only the memory already arriving at the bad component is included in its effective fault map; no future outcome is pulled backwards and no other logical block is accessed. Classical controls are handled on each retained classical history, keeping the corresponding instrument branch and summing those branches at the end. This is the primitive one-scale template with at most one effective faulty location, the same classical ports, some output ECs omitted, and arbitrary finite memory only at that fault. It has not contracted multiple bad owners into a common channel or reordered memory interactions between them.

Apply [A1] to the resulting one-scale network. If $s_i$ effective faults are in leading EC $i$, the EC condition puts its coarse output coordinates in $P_{s_i}$ for every coarse input, with the smaller syndrome registers retained as reference or allowed fault memory. On a coarse $P_s$ input it also gives the asserted decoded preservation whenever $s+s_i\le1$. This proves the auxiliary EC assertion at the new scale. The gate filter condition similarly propagates the coarse input filters, and its decoded identity, followed by any present output ECs, gives step 2.1 for the parent. Its absent output ECs remain absent. Since step 5.1 established every lower component's eligibility for ALL states in the input sector defined in step 4.1, this is a channel identity on that full sector, not just on the image of a preceding channel. Step 3.1 now supplies the parent's syndrome-retaining factor, pure preparation factor, or destructive measurement identity, as applicable. It remains to verify the ENTIRE boundary sector for the actual parent leading-EC output. Use the following cover of the actual exposed ports. A retained good opening level-$a$ component $p$ has its immediately preceding level-$a$ EC $e$ and the descending input collar of $e$ available as physical context, possibly owned by an earlier rectangle. Here availability is relative to the network under consideration: if $p$ is inside a larger claimed owner, that owner contains this context. If a different later owner had erased $e$ from this context, its only external quantum outlet would lead to $p$. By step 1.2 and step 2.2 the claim must then include that immediately following opening region; it cannot pass through or jump across a retained gate. Thus $p$ would have been removed into that owner, or would itself be the selected bad claimant, which imposes no boundary filter. Private EC records give no alternative outlet. This excludes precisely the case of a retained good $p$ whose necessary EC has disappeared; it does not assert that an EC owned elsewhere is absent from the physical circuit. For each such good $p$, its scan contains at most one bad child in total, hence at most one in $e$. To apply the EC assertion to $e$, first cover the opening ports of $e$ and its retained collar in the same manner at scales STRICTLY BELOW $a$. At scale zero there is no decoder input filter to supply. Ascending this finite cover tree, the already proved lower-scale EC assertion therefore forces each required filter for every incoming state, including an arbitrary output of a preceding bad owner. A bad opening component requires no filter, and virtual opening components have entirely ideal collars by step 3.3. For a parent of scale $j+1$, the largest $a$ used in this cover is $j$, so no same-level EC assertion is invoked to establish its own input domain. The cover establishes all lower exposed-port constraints of $K_\partial$ independently; applying the elementary EC condition to the reduced actual parent leading EC then supplies its outer $P_f$ constraint. Their joint range is exactly the input-boundary sector defined in step 4.1. In particular no outer $P_f$ condition is used to infer a lower syndrome condition. A bad parent is still its original conjugated channel. This closes the simultaneous induction using only strictly smaller-scale identities in step 5.1 and in the cover descent, and elementary identities at the new scale. Encoded inputs or the prescribed pure preparations close the initial circuit boundary, and final destructive instruments give the ideal output law when all selected top roots are good.

A selected bad level-$r$ root, $r\ge1$, contains at least two selected bad child roots in its retained scan. Choose the first two in the fixed order, and repeat inside each of them down to scale zero. The result is a full binary tree of depth $r$. A later selected bad child claimed every location of its retained exRec before the earlier child was processed. Hence the two child supports are disjoint. This remains true at every nested boundary because [A2] erases all overlapping elementary locations, not just the nominal outer EC. Induction down the tree gives $2^r$ distinct faulty elementary leaves. The same argument gives disjoint leaves for trees from jointly selected roots. Ideal completions create no faulty leaves.

Count the trees before considering probabilities. At each internal vertex its two child roots have labels in its fixed complete exRec template, with at most $b$ possibilities; hence their unordered pair has at most $A=\binom b2$ possibilities. Order that pair by the fixed template order. A full depth-$r$ binary tree has $2^r-1$ internal vertices, so it has at most $A^{2^r-1}$ labelings. A label sequence fixes every elementary leaf's physical location in the original schedule, regardless of which ECs the scan erased: truncation deletes locations and never changes a root's template address. Thus no extra count of truncation patterns is needed. Some labelings cannot survive a scan or repeat a leaf; discard them. Every actual witness is among the remaining predetermined labelings, by step 7.1.

For $k$ specified selected bad roots, choose one of these labelled witness trees for each root. There are at most $A^{k(2^r-1)}$ such tuples. Keep only tuples with $k2^r$ distinct elementary leaves. For a fixed retained tuple the probability all its leaves fault is $\eta^{k2^r}$ by [F1]; no restriction on other locations, erasure decisions, or additional faults is imposed. Step 7.1 makes the event of interest a subset of the union of these fixed leaf-fault events. Applying [F2] proves $\mathbb P(\text{all specified roots selected bad})\le A^{k(2^r-1)}\eta^{k2^r}$. This proof uses independence only for fixed elementary locations and therefore remains valid for fault-dependent truncations.
