citations.quote:
Let $\mathbb B:=\{0,1\}$. A **binary encoding** of a set $X$ is an injective
function
$$ e:X\to\mathbb B^* $$
([[def-function]], [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]).

Fix a symbol $\mathtt{mal}$ not belonging to $X$. A **total decoder** for $e$
is a function
$$ d:\mathbb B^*\to X\cup\{\mathtt{mal}\} $$
such that
$$ d(e(x))=x\quad(x\in X),\qquad d(w)=\mathtt{mal}\quad(w\notin e[X]). $$
Thus $\mathtt{mal}$ is exactly the output on malformed codes, and the decoder
is defined on every binary word, not only on words in the image of $e$.

The encoding $e$ is **effective** when such a total decoder is specified.

The encoding is **prefix-free** when no codeword is a proper prefix of another:
there do not exist distinct $x,y\in X$ and a nonempty binary word $u$ with
$e(y)=e(x)u$.

Fix the explicit complete transition-table coding specified below. There are two distinct fixed finite-alphabet probabilistic interpreters, one for the sequential access profile and one for the erased-index head-access-only random-access profile. Each interpreter simulates valid descriptions $e$ with input $x$ and an external binary clock $b$, reproducing exactly the source acceptance or rejection reached in at most $b$ source transitions and rejecting nonhalting expiry. The simulated fair-bit distribution is exact. Writing $n=|x|$ and $L=|e|+1$, there are absolute constants $C,d$ such that each simulation takes time
$$ C L^d\bigl(n+(b+1)\log^d(n+b+L+2)\bigr). $$
For the index-only profile, jump addresses are written on one-way sequential write-only index tapes erased after use; the older nonerasing delimited-head profile is a distinct profile and is not covered by this index-only assertion. The fixed interpreter has a fixed finite physical head count even when the described source head count varies. Malformed descriptions halt rejecting. This is a time simulation; no preservation of the source's simultaneous space bound is asserted.

In particular, for each fixed polynomially bounded time-constructible $T(n)\ge n$ and fixed $c$, descriptions of length at most $c\log(n+2)$ are simulated in either one fixed declared profile in $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$ time, including the clock constructor. Arbitrary superpolynomial clocks retain the general displayed bound rather than this specialization.

For an explicitly coded machine in the derived full classical basis profile, input $x$ of length $n$, and external transition clock $b\ge n$, there is a fixed finite-head index-only erased-index interpreter reproducing exact acceptance, rejection and timeout probabilities. Writing $L=|e|+1$ for source description length, its time and maximum physical work-access address are bounded by
$$C L^d\bigl(n+(b+1)\log^d(n+b+L+2)\bigr)$$
for absolute constants $C,d$. In particular, logarithmic descriptions and each fixed polynomial clock $T(n)\ge n$ have $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$ overhead, including clock construction. This is a time-only normalization; it does not preserve a smaller original source space bound and makes no general equivalence claim for clocks below input length.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

derivations.claim: Use the declared sequential multitape model, with its fixed finite alphabet, fixed number of heads, and heads initially at zero. Make halting states absorbing. In $T$ steps a head visits only positions $0,\ldots,T$, so each head address has $O(\log(T+2))$ bits. A candidate trace lists, for every time $t<T$, its state, head addresses and scanned/written symbols, together with the final state and addresses. Constant-table transition checks, binary increment/decrement/clamping checks, the initial state/address checks and final acceptance check have bounded-fan-in circuits of total size $O(T\log(T+2))$. Each table lookup has constant size because the simulated machine is fixed.

For a fixed deterministic machine in the derived basis profile and $T\ge n$, the deterministic instance of [F2] gives an exact index-only interpreter of time $T'=T\log^{O(1)}(T+2)$ whose actually used physical addresses and index words have $O(\log(T+2))$ bits. The description is fixed and its fair-bit tables agree, so no probabilistic choices affect this computation. The interpreter's source input, code and clock have total length $O(n+\log(T+2))$. Its explicit time bound can be rounded up to a fixed uniformly computable $T\log^c(T+2)$ clock. No sublinear-space preservation is needed for this formula construction.

For every tape and time create an access record containing tape ID, address, time, read symbol and written symbol, copied by wires from the trace. A read-only access has equal read/write symbols. Include initial records at time $-1$ for the at most $T+1$ relevant cells of the input tape, each with its actual input symbol as written symbol. Other tapes are initially blank. Use a validity bit and pad the records to a power of two by dummy records. Sort by (validity,tape,address,time), putting dummies last. Require each real record's read symbol to equal the preceding record's written symbol when the tape/address keys agree; at a first access to an address with no initial record require blank. Initial records need no read check. Thus the trace satisfies all these checks if and only if every reported read is the last symbol actually written to its addressed tape cell, or the correct initial symbol.

Here is the complete sorting construction used in step 2.1. Compare two $b$-bit keys lexicographically using the first unequal bit, realized by a prefix equality chain and Boolean gates; select both output records with multiplexers. This costs $O(b)$ gates. A bitonic merge of $2h$ records compares pairs at distance $h$, retaining smaller records in the first half and larger in the second, then recursively merges each half. To verify this, it suffices to consider Boolean keys: if sorting failed, applying a threshold between two inverted output keys commutes with every comparator and gives a Boolean failure. In a circular bitonic Boolean sequence the ones form one circular interval. The distance-$h$ comparisons therefore either remove all ones from the smaller half or all zeros from the larger half; both halves remain circular bitonic, and every smaller-half bit is at most every larger-half bit. Induction proves merge correctness. Sort two halves in opposite directions recursively, concatenate to form a bitonic sequence and merge. For $L$ padded records the merge uses $O(L\log L)$ comparisons and the sort uses $O(L\log^2L)$ comparisons. Here $L=O(T+1)$ and record width $b=O(\log(T+2))$, yielding $O(T\log^3(T+2))$ Boolean gates.

Memory consistency and the transition checks determine the trace uniquely from the input: induction on time first determines the scanned symbols from the earlier writes, and then the fixed deterministic transition determines the state, writes and next head addresses. The true trace passes all checks exactly when the original computation accepts. All sorting and checking gates are deterministic functions of the candidate trace. Introduce one variable for each gate output and constant-size clauses enforcing that gate's truth table; require the final checking conjunction to be true. For each input there is therefore exactly one satisfying assignment of all trace/gate variables when it accepts and none when it rejects. The number of clauses is the circuit size, and explicit binary variable names increase formula encoding length by at most $O(\log(T+2))$.

Fix the formula as the concatenation of fixed-width padded encodings of those local clauses. A gate has a tuple address consisting of module type, trace time or sorting round, wire number and bit/gate offset. Bitonic sorting pairs wire $i$ with $i\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}2^j$ in its round $(k,j)$; its direction is fixed by the relevant $k$th bit of $i$. In the recursive implementation this same tuple rule follows by the successive half merges described in step 3.1. Ripple comparisons and multiplexers have locally indexed predecessors. Thus one requested clause/variable-name bit is generated by $O(\operatorname{polylog}T)$ operations on $O(\log T)$-bit counters, storing only a fixed number of such counters. Decoding fixed-width clause offsets is integer arithmetic on $O(\log T)$ bits and costs polynomial time in $\log T$ even with school algorithms. Fix input-gate variables by unit clauses in one initial ordered block, with a common fixed clause-slot width and the clause for $x_i$ in slot $i$. Only this block contains actual $x$ symbols; all other clauses refer to variable names. Unfixed $y$ symbols remain input variables. For isolated bit generation, the bit generator uses the declared direct access to the indicated input bit. For sequential consumers, a unit move of the formula-input head changes the required source-input position by at most one inside this block; outside it park the source head at the nearest endpoint. This monotone address map charges all source-head motion to formula-head motion plus initial setup, so sequential on-demand generation uses polynomial-logarithmic overhead per formula-input transition and $O(\log T)$ workspace without uncharged random access. This proves logarithmic workspace and polylogarithmic output-bit time for the sequential construction; the separate derived-basis extension follows below.

Apply step 1.1 and step 2.1 and step 3.1 and step 4.1 and step 5.1 to a trace of this bounded-address interpreter, with one addition: each fixed native index tape is represented by its $O(\log T)$-bit accumulating value and length, updated by shift-and-append on an emitted bit and reset on use. A jump's next head address must equal that accumulated value. Head collisions and the source's suppressed-write rule are fixed local checks; records at equal time are sorted further by head label, and colliding heads have no intervening writes, so the adjacent-record memory test remains correct. All addresses, states, index prefixes and counters use $O(\log T)$ bits, and the fixed number of heads contributes only a constant factor. The verifier and clauses consequently have size $T\log^{O(1)}T$ and the same local polylogarithmic-time/logspace generation. The deterministic interpreter has exactly one valid trace, so the unique-witness conclusion is unchanged. Input-dependent unit clauses remain in the ordered initial block. This establishes the claimed extension for the derived basis profile while retaining the sequential construction.

As $x\to\infty$,
$$\pi(x)\sim x/\log x,\qquad\theta(x)\sim x,\qquad\psi(x)\sim x.$$
These three asymptotic assertions are equivalent.
Every prime $p$ admits a primitive root modulo $p$.

For $m,w\ge1$, the exact sum of $m$ nonnegative $w$-bit integers has constant-depth polynomial-size circuits over AND, OR, NOT and MAJ, with $w+\lceil\log_2m\rceil$ output bits. The circuits are DLOGTIME-uniform under the following explicit array convention: the input bit $x_{i,j}$ has tuple address $(i,j)$; array dimensions and gate-coordinate domains may be padded to powers of two, with padded inputs zero. Gate addresses use a fixed number of binary coordinate fields, and the uniformity machine receives the binary dimensions and gate addresses. Equivalently, the input is a bit matrix with both dimensions padded to powers of two. Constants and output truncation are included in the family. The claim does not apply to arbitrary effectively decodable encodings.

derivations.claim: A function of a fixed number of short arguments has polynomially many argument tuples. If its table is logspace-computable, realize each output bit by an OR of equality conjunctions over the tuples yielding one. This is a constant-depth polynomial-size logspace-uniform Boolean lookup circuit. Short addition, multiplication, reduction, inverses modulo a prime, and the table $(a,e,p)\mapsto a^e\bmod p$ have this property. For the power table, use repeated squaring with a constant number of short residues and a short exponent counter; short multiplication uses grade-school arithmetic in logarithmic space. Find an inverse by trying every short candidate, and test primality by trial division. Enumerate the $j$-th prime by a counter and these primality tests whenever $j$ and that prime are polynomially bounded. We may also add polynomially many polynomial-width words by [F3], whose uniformity is stronger than required here.

For a fixed short prime $p>2$, [F2] gives a generator $g$ of the nonzero residues. Find the least such $g$ by testing all candidates and all exponents below $p-1$ with step 1.1. The tables $a\mapsto\ell(a)$, where $g^{\ell(a)}\equiv a\pmod p$ and $0\le\ell(a)<p-1$, and $(g,e,p)\mapsto g^e\bmod p$ are logspace-computable by enumeration and modular powering with a constant number of short counters. For nonzero inputs $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ with polynomially bounded $d$, their product modulo $p$ is $g^{\sum_i\ell(a_i)}\bmod p$. The exponent sum is polynomially bounded, so compute it with [F3] and use a short power lookup. If any input is zero, select zero instead. For $p=2$, the product is one exactly when all inputs are one. This gives iterated multiplication in any fixed polynomial-size residue basis in logspace-uniform constant depth. It uses only short tables and addition, without assuming binary iterated multiplication.

Convert a long word $X=\sum_j x_j2^j$ to residues by computing $x_j(2^j\bmod p)$ for each bit position and modulus, summing these short contributions with [F3], and reducing the result modulo $p$ by step 1.1. The sum is polynomially bounded in $N$, because its number of contributions and $p$ are. Each constant $2^j\bmod p$ is logspace-computable. Thus binary-to-residue conversion has the required circuit bounds; for $X$ outside the basis range, its vector represents its remainder in that range.

Fix a basis $T=\prod_{i=1}^k p_i$ of distinct short primes. Set $C_i=T/p_i$ and $h_i=(C_i\bmod p_i)^{-1}\bmod p_i$. The binary words $T,C_i$ need not be computed: their required short residues, and then $h_i$, are generated in logspace by scanning factors and multiplying modulo $p_i$. Since $C_i h_i$ is one modulo $p_i$ and zero modulo all other basis primes, for the residue vector $(x_i)$ of $0\le X<T$ we have $$\sum_i x_i h_i C_i=X+rT,\qquad S:=\sum_i\frac{x_i h_i}{p_i}=r+\frac XT$$ for a nonnegative integer $r$. Indeed a difference divisible by each of the distinct primes is divisible by their product, while two representatives in $[0,T)$ cannot differ by a nonzero multiple of $T$. Existence of a representative for every residue vector follows by taking the remainder modulo $T$ of the displayed nonnegative sum.

We give a comparison circuit with controlled rounding. Let $U$ bound the primes of the fixed basis, put $L=k\lceil\log_2U\rceil$, so $T\le2^L$, and choose $t=L+\lceil\log_2k\rceil+4$. Compute $F_i=\lfloor x_i h_i2^t/p_i\rfloor$ and $$Z=\frac{\sum_i F_i+k}{2^t},\qquad S\le Z\le S+\varepsilon,\qquad \varepsilon=k2^{-t}<\frac1{4T}.$$ Because $X/T$ is a multiple of $1/T$ in $[0,1)$, $\lfloor Z\rfloor=r$, including $X=0$ and $X=T-1$. The low $t$ bits of $\sum_i F_i+k$ therefore represent a dyadic fraction $f_X$ satisfying $X/T\le f_X\le X/T+\varepsilon$. Hence $X<Y$ if and only if $f_X<f_Y$: distinct representatives differ by at least $1/T$, and equal representatives give identical residue vectors and identical fractions. All bits of $F_i$ have the required circuits. Its integer part $\lfloor x_i h_i/p_i\rfloor$ is a short lookup. For odd $p_i$, bit $j\ge1$ after the binary point of $x_i h_i/p_i$ equals $(x_i h_i2^j\bmod p_i)\bmod2$: write $x_i h_i2^j=ap_i+b$; its even left side and odd $p_i$ imply that $a,b$ have the same parity. These residues are short lookups using modular-power constants. For $p_i=2$, only the first fractional bit can be nonzero. This computes precisely the truncation defining $F_i$. Sum with [F3] and compare the $t$-bit fractions by an OR over their highest differing position, with equality required at all higher positions. That comparator is constant-depth Boolean. Thus residue comparison is logspace-uniform constant depth. The upward offset is essential to handle an exact integer $S$ correctly.

Put $k=N+5$ and let $M$ be the product of the first $k$ primes, including $2$. Then $M\ge2^k>2^{N+4}$. For each output index $1\le s<N$, take $s$ disjoint blocks of $k$ consecutive primes beyond those first $k$ primes, and let $A_i$ be the product of block $i$. Every $A_i$ is odd and exceeds $M$, since each of its factors exceeds the corresponding factor of $M$. The $A_i$ are pairwise relatively prime and relatively prime to $M$. Only $O(N^2)$ primes are needed. By [F1], their numerical values are polynomially bounded in $N$ for all sufficiently large $N$; the finitely many smaller dimensions have fixed circuits. Enumeration of each block and its residues modulo any short prime is logspace-computable by scanning its factors as in step 1.1 and step 2.3. No bit of a long prime product is requested from the uniformity machine.

Extend the representation of $X\in[0,T)$ to a fixed short prime $q$ not in its basis by trying every possible residue $a\in[0,q)$. In basis $Tq$, each candidate has a unique representative $X_a$. The representatives with the old residues are exactly $X+jT$, $0\le j<q$, so exactly one is below $T$. The representation of $T$ in basis $Tq$ has zero on the old primes and the fixed short product $T\bmod q$ on the new prime. Compare each candidate with it using step 3.1 and select the unique successful $a$. This computes $X\bmod q$. Extend to any polynomial-size new basis in parallel, treating its new primes independently. Removing primes just discards coordinates. No binary value of $T$ is needed.

Fix a squarefree divisor $B$ of the basis product $T$ and put $P=T/B$. Restrict the representation of $X\in[0,T)$ to basis $B$ to obtain $R=X\bmod B$ in $[0,B)$, and extend $R$ back to basis $T$ by step 4.1. For each $p\mid P$, compute $(X-R)B^{-1}\bmod p$, where $B\bmod p$ and its inverse are fixed short constants from step 1.1. This is the representation of $Q=\lfloor X/B\rfloor$ modulo $P$; since $0\le Q<P$, it is the canonical one. Extend it from basis $P$ to basis $T$ by step 4.1. If $P=1$, output zero; if $B=1$, return $X$. All componentwise operations are short lookups. This proves constant-depth logspace-uniform division by these fixed squarefree products without assuming general binary division.

Let $X\in[0,M)$ be given in basis $M$ and fix $1\le s<N$. Put $A=\prod_{i=1}^s A_i$ and $P=MA$. Extend $X$ to basis $P$ by step 4.1. Compute each fixed $A_i$ modulo each basis prime and add one componentwise. This represents $A_i+1<P$. Since $2\mid P$ and $A_i$ is odd, step 5.1 computes $H_i=(A_i+1)/2$ in basis $P$. Using step 2.1, compute $Y=X\prod_i H_i$ in that basis. There is no wraparound, since $H_i<A_i$ and $X<M$ imply $Y<P$. Divide by $A$ with step 5.1 to obtain $Q=\lfloor Y/A\rfloor$ in basis $P$.

We have $Y/A=(X/2^s)\prod_i(1+1/A_i)$. Since $A_i>M$ and $M>2^{N+4}>s(s+1)$, the binomial coefficients bounded by powers of $s$ give $$\prod_i(1+1/A_i)<(1+1/M)^s\le\sum_{j\ge0}(s/M)^j=1+\frac{s}{M-s}<1+\frac{s+1}{M}.$$ Consequently $0\le Y/A-X/2^s<(s+1)/2^s\le1$. Thus $Q$ is either $\lfloor X/2^s\rfloor$ or that integer plus one. Retain $Q$ unless $Q2^s>X$, in which case subtract one. The comparison in basis $P$ is valid without wraparound: $Q2^s<X+2^s<M+2^N<2M<P$. Compute the residues of $2^s$ by step 1.1, multiply componentwise, and compare by step 3.1. Subtraction by one is componentwise and occurs only when $Q\ge1$. The selected vector represents $\lfloor X/2^s\rfloor$, whose residue modulo $2$ is bit $s$ of $X$. Bit zero is already the residue of $X$ modulo $2$. Thus all $N$ bits are recovered by parallel copies of a constant-depth circuit.

Convert the $m$ input words to basis $M$ by step 2.2 and multiply their residue vectors by step 2.1. Their exact product $Z$ satisfies $0\le Z<2^{mw}=2^N<M$, including zero factors, so this is its canonical residue vector. Apply step 3.2 and step 6.1 and step 7.1 in parallel at every index $s<N$. The result is its exact binary product, with precisely $mw$ output bits and leading zeros where required.

Every basis length, prime value, table argument, loop index and word width above is polynomially bounded in $N$. In step 3.1, the approximant width is $O(k'\log U)$ for its polynomial-size basis length $k'$, hence polynomial as well. Each table has a fixed number of short arguments and polynomially many rows. Each conversion, comparison, extension and division uses a fixed finite number of layers of tables, Boolean gates and [F3]; their nesting in step 1.1 and step 2.1 and step 2.2 and step 2.3 and step 3.1 and step 4.1 and step 5.1 and step 3.2 and step 6.1 and step 7.1 and step 8.1 has depth independent of all dimensions and prime counts. Trials over primes, residues, table rows and output bits are parallel copies. Thus the total size is polynomial and depth constant. Label gates by their stage and a fixed number of polynomially bounded coordinates. A logspace machine enumerates the fixed prime lists, computes needed residues by repeated modular multiplication, computes power and discrete-log table bits as in step 1.1 and step 2.1, and decides local wiring using short counters. The composition depth of subcircuit descriptions is fixed, so intermediate descriptions can be recomputed using $O(\log(N+2))$ workspace. The machine never stores $M,P,A_i$ or another long product. The addition circuits from [F3] are also logspace-uniform. This proves both logarithmic-space description generation and the gate-predecessor predicate, completing the Statement.

A probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) is a fixed multitape machine with two total ordinary transition tables. At each nonhalting transition a fresh independent fair bit selects the table. It is polynomial time if one fixed integer polynomial p bounds the number of transitions on every random branch on every input x by $p(|x|)$. This is a worst-case branch bound, using [[def-polynomial-time-verifier-and-reduction-interface]], not an expected-time bound.

For an input of length n, probabilities may be defined on the finite space $\Omega_n=\{0,1\}^{p(n)}$, giving every word mass $2^{-p(n)}$. A deterministic simulator uses bit j for transition j and ignores unused suffix bits after halting. Acceptance probability is the sum of masses of words giving acceptance. Independence has the finite-variable meaning of [[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]. The finite probability space is not itself storage charged to the machine.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

Let $t,s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

On this page, whenever a constructible bound is used to clock another machine,
we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

derivations.claim: At the fixed input let $R=R(n)$ and let $A$ count accepting strings among the $2^R$ fair-bit strings, including unused suffixes after early halting; then $p=A/2^R$ by [F1]. The new machine first reads $R+2$ selector bits, rejecting only the all-zero selector. On every nonzero selector it simulates the original machine for at most $R$ steps using $R$ fresh bits, records its outcome, and consumes any unused suffix bits in a no-op state. On the zero selector it consumes all $R$ fresh bits and rejects. By [F3] this is a well-defined clocked procedure. There are exactly $2^{2R+2}$ equiprobable strings and exactly $(2^{R+2}-1)A$ accepting ones, so $p'=(1-2^{-(R+2)})p$.

If $p\le1/2$ then $p'<1/2$. If $p>1/2$, then $A\ge2^{R-1}+1$, so $p-1/2\ge2^{-R}$; because $p\le1$, $p'-1/2=(p-1/2)-p\,2^{-(R+2)}\ge2^{-R}-2^{-(R+2)}>0$. Thus strict majority is preserved and an original tie becomes a strict no-instance.

The new acceptance probability cannot equal one half: such equality would require the integer $A$ to equal $2^{2R+1}/(2^{R+2}-1)$, which is not an integer because its denominator is odd and greater than one. Since no tie remains, swapping accepting and rejecting labels makes the complement machine accept strictly above one half exactly on the original no-instances. The selector and padding add $2R+2$ transitions, so the overhead is $O(R(n))$.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

derivations.claim: Fix the machine. Its input-head positions, finite state and logarithmic workspace have at most $n^c$ configurations, for a fixed integer $c$. A halting deterministic computation cannot repeat a configuration, so increase $c$ to bound its running time by $n^c$. Make both halting states absorbing. A configuration has $O(\log n)$ bits, including the conventional bounded input positions, charged input-address registers if used, finite state and work symbols. Small input lengths can be decided separately.

Put $b=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$ for sufficiently large $n$. To assert that configuration $u$ reaches $v$ in exactly $\ell$ steps, existentially specify $b-1$ intermediate configurations. Divide $\ell$ into $b$ consecutive intervals whose lengths differ by at most one. Universally select one interval and assert the corresponding endpoint reachability for that shorter length. This equivalence follows by taking the actual intermediate configurations in the forward direction and concatenating all verified segments in the reverse direction. Iterate for a fixed $r>2c$ levels; continue until the selected interval has bounded constant length. Indeed the recurrence $\ell_{j+1}\le\ell_j/b+1$ gives $\ell_r\le n^c/b^r+2$, bounded by three for a sufficiently large fixed $r>2c$. At each level the existential list uses $O(\sqrt n\log n)$ bits, and the universal index uses $O(\log n)$ bits. Zero-length intervals demand equal endpoints.

A fixed-level verification takes $O(n)$ sequential time. The machine reads/copies $x$ and checks the short configuration list by sequential scans. To pass a selected subproblem to its next level it writes $x$, the two selected endpoints and the interval length, using $O(n)$ symbols. At a leaf it initializes the fixed simulated tapes from the endpoint and moves the input head to its specified position by a scan of length at most $n$; it then simulates at most three transitions and checks the endpoint in $O(n)$ total time. If the conventional logspace predicate uses bounded random-access input queries, each of these constantly many queries can be performed by a sequential scan of $x$ of length $O(n)$. This makes no near-linear sequential simulation claim for an entire random-access computation. Arithmetic on the $O(\log n)$-bit interval lengths costs a fixed polylogarithmic amount, absorbed by $O(n)$.

Convert the constant alternating sequence to a fixed finite number of linear probabilistic oracle levels. For an existential block of $s=O(n)$ guessed bits with oracle-verifiable predicate $B$, use one extra fair bit: on branch 0 accept unconditionally; on branch 1 guess those $s$ bits and accept exactly when $B$ holds. Padding both branches to $s$ bits gives acceptance probability $1/2+\#B/2^{s+1}$, strictly above half precisely when a witness exists. Universal blocks are complements of existential blocks with complemented predicates. Complement is available with linear overhead by [[lem-qc-unbounded-error-tie-normalization]]: for a machine with exactly $R$ fair bits and acceptance probability $p$, first reject on the all-zero $(R+2)$-bit selector and otherwise run that machine. Its new acceptance probability $(1-2^{-(R+2)})p$ has the original strict-majority decision and never ties, since an original positive gap is at least $2^{-R}$. Exchanging accepting and rejecting labels therefore decides the complement. The same proof uses exact oracle answers and relativizes. Query lengths and per-level work are $O(n)$ by step 3.1; a fixed tagged union of the needed oracle predicates lies at their maximum level, after padding lower levels by dummy queries. Thus finitely many levels suffice. Finally existentially select the accepting endpoint at time $n^c$ and apply the reachability predicate. This decides the original machine's language in sequential $\mathrm{LCH}_k$ for some fixed $k$. Sequential fixed-tape machines embed into the published binary multihead profile with a fixed number of interleaved tracks: neighboring cells are a fixed stride apart, so local moves take constant time. This embeds each sequential hierarchy level into the corresponding published-profile level as well.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 separately decides finitely many small/empty input lengths.
Step 2.1 makes a zero-length interval require equal endpoints.
Steps 2.1, 3.1 terminate at constant-length segments, including a single transition.
Step 1.1 applies only to halting conventional logspace deciders with bounded input positions; no unrestricted unclocked index-memory premise is used.
Step 3.1 charges each leaf indexed input read to an O(n) sequential scan; step 4.1 charges written query lengths.

boundaries.reason: Existentially sampled finite checkpoint strings are computational branches, not uses of a choice axiom.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 obtains all checkpoints from an actual path.
Step 2.1 concatenates every universally checked segment to recover the original path.

citations.quote: There are two distinct fixed finite-alphabet multitape interpreters $U_{\rm time}$ and $U_{\rm space}$. On valid $(M,x,\operatorname{bin}(b))$ each reproduces acceptance or rejection reached in at most $b$ simulated transitions, and rejects at expiry; malformed inputs halt rejecting. Put $n=|\langle M,x\rangle|$, including self-delimiting syntax, and let $S$ be the sum of visited simulated cells. For each fixed $M$, the time cost of $U_{\rm time}$ is $O_M(n+b\log(b+2))$ and the visited space of $U_{\rm space}$ is $O_M(n+S+\log(b+2))$, including the decoder and clock. These bounds include $b=0,1$. No fast-time bound is asserted for $U_{\rm space}$, and no linear-$S$ space bound for $U_{\rm time}$.

Let $\mathbb B:=\{0,1\}$. A **binary encoding** of a set $X$ is an injective
function
$$ e:X\to\mathbb B^* $$
([[def-function]], [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]).

Fix a symbol $\mathtt{mal}$ not belonging to $X$. A **total decoder** for $e$
is a function
$$ d:\mathbb B^*\to X\cup\{\mathtt{mal}\} $$
such that
$$ d(e(x))=x\quad(x\in X),\qquad d(w)=\mathtt{mal}\quad(w\notin e[X]). $$
Thus $\mathtt{mal}$ is exactly the output on malformed codes, and the decoder
is defined on every binary word, not only on words in the image of $e$.

The encoding $e$ is **effective** when such a total decoder is specified.

The encoding is **prefix-free** when no codeword is a proper prefix of another:
there do not exist distinct $x,y\in X$ and a nonempty binary word $u$ with
$e(y)=e(x)u$.

Let $t,s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

On this page, whenever a constructible bound is used to clock another machine,
we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

derivations.claim: Specify the syntax rather than appealing to an arbitrary effective code. Use the numeric multitape extension and unary-length binary tuple blocks in [F1], with two complete transition tables in place of one. The virtual input tape is read-only, each work tape is initially blank, and each head starts at cell zero with clamped left motion. The finite input alphabet is the two binary input symbols, distinguished from blank. A header lists the tape count $k$, alphabet size $r$, state count $m$, start and two halting states; the two tables list every nonhalting state/scanned-symbol tuple in lexicographic order, each with its next state, written symbols, and local moves or stationary requests. For the read-only tape require its written symbol to equal the scanned symbol. All integers use canonical binary numerals, all blocks carry unary length headers, and the number of blocks is unary-prefixed. Include explicit table delimiters and a profile tag. This is prefix-free, includes each finite machine of the chosen numeric form, and has a total decoder. Because a complete table contains at least one row with $k$ symbol/move fields, and contains all states and scanned symbols, every valid description has $k\le L$, $r\le L+3$ and $m\le L+3$; each stored integer has at most $L$ bits even without these sharper bounds.

For this erased-index interpreter put $H=n+b+L+2$, $s=\lceil\log_2 H\rceil$ and $B=2^s$, so $B>n$ and $B>b$. Use the explicit unary-length tuple syntax from the sequential candidate, now adding finite head labels, the source index-tape labels, a profile tag, index-output actions and native jump actions to each transition row. A row specifies all source actions, and the complete table explicitly includes every state/scanned-symbol/bit case. Thus the number $h$ of source heads and index tapes, every alphabet width, and each instruction-record width are bounded by a fixed polynomial in $L$. The source's one binary work tape is included as a special case; any allowed finite additional tapes receive tape labels. Parse and validate by capped expected-count arithmetic without expanding an asserted table; this takes $L^{O(1)}$ time. State and scanned-symbol lookup by repeated scans of the saved table costs $L^{O(1)}$ per source transition. The fixed physical interpreter never acquires a new head or an alphabet depending on $e$.

Parse and check the actual blocks without expanding a claimed table. Count the actual rows first; compute expected products and powers by binary arithmetic capped one above that actual count, rejecting excess, invalid ranges, missing rows or extra data. This is the saturated-count method of [F1], now with all valid and invalid code processing bounded by a polynomial in $L$: the operands, counters and scans have length $O(L)$, there are $O(L)$ actual blocks, and every product/exponent loop is capped or uses at most $L$ exponent bits. Ordinary repeated scans and school arithmetic suffice, for example in $O(L^6)$ time and $O(L^2)$ space. Preserve a decoded table of length $O(L^2)$, runtime parameters and fixed-width symbol/state codes of width at most $L+O(1)$. Copy $x$ to a sequential archive and read/copy the clock in $O(n+\log(b+2))$ time. All subsequent routines use fixed physical tape counts and fixed alphabets; variable-size data remain on tapes.

For each source index tape reserve a separate contiguous region of $b+1$ binary cells, with its current length stored in metadata. Reserve these regions by arithmetic base offsets before the dictionary heap; reservation moves no head through the regions and requires no initialization sweep. A source index emits at most one bit per source transition, so its live word always fits. Appending a source bit writes at its region's base plus current length and increments that length. Use/reset sets the length to zero; future emission overwrites old bits, and reading only the current prefix ignores the discarded suffix. Interleaved emission onto different source indexes therefore never interleaves their physical words. Since at most $h$ bits are emitted per source transition, the sum $W$ of lengths of all words consumed at jumps, plus lengths still live at expiry, satisfies $W\le h b$, up to a harmless fixed-format constant. A jump using one word for several source heads in the same transition multiplies this accounting by at most $h$, still a polynomial in $L$. Reading, copying or canonicalizing each consumed word once, or a fixed number of times per affected head, therefore has total length $L^{O(1)}b$. The reserved regions' total extent is $O(h(b+1))$, consistent with later maximum-address bounds. This charged fresh-writing invariant is exactly what fails for the old nonerasing delimited-head model.

Split each numerical source head address $a$ uniquely as $a=PB+r$, where $0\le r<B$. Call $P$ its block prefix and $r$ its short offset. Store the short offset in $s$ bits. Maintain a global prefix dictionary assigning one compact integer block ID to each registered numerical prefix. A dictionary key for $P$ is the prefix-free word $1^{|w|}0w$, where $w$ is the canonical binary numeral of $P$, including $w=0$ at zero. Use a literal binary trie: each node has two child pointers, an optional terminal block ID and its fixed metadata. Reading/inserting a key follows or creates one node per bit. Numerical equality of prefixes is equality of their canonical words, hence exactly equality of terminal nodes. No balancing, probabilistic hashing, numerical unit-cost large integers or unspecified dictionary theorem is required. Include a tape label in this key when more than one virtual work tape is allowed.

Use the exact buffer representation and stack operations of [F1]. At level $i$, put $h_i=2^i$; each side has capacity $2h_i$, occupancy $0,h_i$ or $2h_i$, and complementary occupancies summing to $2h_i$. Each physical slot has $k$ delimited virtual fields, each of width at most $L+O(1)$, containing a symbol and an immutable origin bit, or a hole. Store the $k$ centre fields and the $k$ three-valued occupancy flags explicitly. A slot therefore has width $O(L^2)$; this uses no alphabet depending on $e$ and no additional physical tape for each virtual tape. A stationary move changes only the centre symbol. At the left origin a requested left move also changes only that symbol. For the input tape suppress writes. These modifications preserve the same stack and origin invariants.

On a source head's jump, read the consumed address word, discard leading zeros and split off its final $s$ bits as $r$, padding on the left with zeros if the word has fewer than $s$ bits. The remaining canonical prefix is $P$, or zero. Form canonical $P-1$ when $P>0$, $P$ and $P+1$ by ordinary binary scans; forming all three costs $O(A+s)$ for address-word length $A$. Register them in the prefix trie. Record their three compact IDs as a private cache for this head, and record that the current block is the middle one. Use a special clamped boundary marker instead of a negative block when $P=0$. Initialize each source head at address zero with this same cache for zero and one. If several source heads jump to the same address, their numerical prefixes receive the same global IDs. The total number of prefix-trie nodes is at most the total length of all registered keys, hence at most $L^{O(1)}(b+1)$: for each jump, all three prefix keys have length $O(A+1)$, and step 2.2 charges their summed lengths. Duplicated registrations only decrease the node count. Tape-label overhead adds at most $L^{O(1)}$ bits per jump.

Make the scan algorithms uniform as follows. To process virtual field $j$, keep a unary field index of length at most $L$; at each slot count through the delimited fields, copy or replace just field $j$, and copy the other fields unchanged. A full slot, its index operations, and returning a scratch head across the bounded parameter records cost at most $O(L^4)$. The same bound covers building one fresh slot by copying the saved width and tape-count templates. Midpoint/end markers specify half-zones, so the scans need no growing arithmetic per record. Copying the selected genuine field records to scratch, distributing the prescribed lists, restoring holes and flags, and returning the physical heads use a fixed number of prefix scans as in [F1]; at level $i$ they traverse $O(2^i)$ slots. Endpoint and optional level-label overhead is also $O(2^i)$, since the sum of the binary level-label lengths through $i$ is $O(2^i)$. Thus the work for a level-$i$ event on one virtual tape is at most $C_1L^6 2^i$, uniformly in $e,i$. This deliberately generous bound includes scans to find the least nonempty source zone, scratch copying, occupancy changes and allocating new levels by doubling the preceding unary capacity marker. Each operation is a scan, a finite-width copy, or an index operation of length at most $O(L)$; no unit-cost random memory operation is being assumed.

The event count is independent of field width. Fix a virtual tape and $i\ge1$. Its right occupancy below level $i$ starts at $H_i=2^i-1$. Each event at level at least $i$ resets it to $H_i$; a lower-level positive or negative move changes it by minus or plus one, and a stationary or clamped move leaves it fixed. An event at level at least $i$ requires the appropriate lower stack empty, hence occupancy zero or $2H_i$ immediately beforehand. It therefore requires at least $H_i$ preceding lower-level moves and then its triggering transition. Among $b$ simulated transitions there are at most $\lfloor b/2^i\rfloor$ such events, including the first. Level zero has at most $b$ events, and no level with $2^i>b$ is reached. This is precisely the integral reset argument of [F1]; successive operations on different virtual tapes do not change each other's fields.

Between two jumps of this head, its address changes by at most $b$ in total absolute distance from its most recent jump address, since every local move changes it by at most one and there are at most $b$ source transitions altogether. As $B>b$, every intervening address belongs to one of the three blocks $P-1,P,P+1$ cached at that jump. A local move updates the $s$-bit offset; overflow/underflow switches to the appropriate adjacent cached ID and wraps the offset. Store the current cache position as one of three finite values. Even if the head crosses the same block boundary many times, the existing IDs are reused, with no re-reading or arithmetic on long prefixes. From the lower cached block it cannot cross to an uncached lower block, and from the upper cached block it cannot cross to an uncached upper block: either would require more than $B$ local moves since the jump. Clamp a left move at numerical zero. Thus the pair (current block ID, short offset) is always an exact address representation, with $O(\log H+\log L)$ bits after accounting for the polynomial number of trie nodes.

Initially retain the input archive at position one and initialize only the centres. On first allocating level $i$, fill the first virtual tape's untouched right half from the next $h_i$ archive symbols, then blanks after exhaustion; initialize the other virtual fields with blank and unoccupied halves with holes. Levels are allocated in increasing order, and lower operations do not alter that untouched suffix, so every archive symbol is consumed at most once. A new level uses only the work charged to the event reaching it. This is the lazy initialization of [F1], with slot creation and symbol coding charged by step 4.1. Thus no full $n\log n$ distribution pass is hidden in initialization.

Before each virtual transition, test the saved state, then test expiry. If still nonhalting with positive countdown, consume one fresh fair bit to choose the corresponding decoded table. Deterministically scan its rows and compare the source state/scanned-symbol tuple with the saved state and centres, copying the unique instructions into scratch. At most $O(L)$ rows and $O(L^2)$ saved fields are involved; repeated full scans and resets take $O(L^6)$ per transition. Save all instructions before applying any virtual write/move, process the $k$ buffer operations in order, then update the state and decrement the binary countdown. Test the new halting state before the next expiry test, so a halt on transition $b$ is reported. A whole countdown scan costs $O(\log(b+2))$ per virtual transition. At $b=0$ the nonhalting initial configuration expires immediately.

Maintain a second literal binary trie for virtual work cells, keyed by the compact block ID and the $s$-bit offset, with explicit length delimiters (and virtual tape label if needed). The key length is $O(\log H+\log L)$. Every terminal stores the virtual symbol, initially zero/blank on first lookup. Each source transition touches at most $h$ virtual cells, so there are at most $h(b+1)$ terminal keys and $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\log H$ nodes in this trie. All keys with the same virtual cell get the same terminal, regardless of which source head or which jump registered that prefix. Source work-tape collisions can therefore be detected by comparing these compact address pairs for all relevant heads, in $L^{O(1)}\log H$ work per transition. Omit precisely the operations declared undefined by the source's collision convention. Read all source scanned symbols and save all source instructions before any virtual write or move.

Buffer correctness from [F1] and the saved-instructions ordering imply by induction that after each virtual transition the interpreter stores the exact virtual configuration prescribed by the consumed bits. Although the physical probabilistic machine receives a bit at every physical transition, ignore all of them except at the designated virtual-choice operation. Conditional on every past consumed bit and the corresponding completed deterministic simulation, the next designated bit is still unbiased and independent: its location depends only on previous bits, and disjoint future coordinates of a finite independent-bit string have the prescribed fair conditional law. Equivalently, for each fixed virtual choice prefix of length $j$, induction on its successive designated choice operations gives probability $2^{-j}$; ignored physical bits have total conditional probability one. Terminal virtual prefixes are disjoint. Summing their masses proves exact agreement of acceptance/rejection/timeout probabilities, including branch-dependent halt times.

Summing step 4.1 using step 4.2, first for each tape and then over $k\le L$, bounds total buffer and lazy-allocation work by $$ C_2L^7\left(b+\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\log_2 b\rfloor}2^i\lfloor b/2^i\rfloor\right)\le C_2L^7 b(1+\lfloor\log_2 b\rfloor) $$ when $b\ge1$. Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

For a fair-bit probabilistic machine with an explicit time-constructible integer clock $R(n)\ge1$, a machine with no exact $1/2$ acceptance probability can be formed with $O(R(n))$ additional time. It preserves strict-majority membership, and swapping its accept/reject labels decides the complement.

Use raw binary input pairs and the fixed-width clause encoding in the proof. For each fixed deterministic sequential multitape computation of worst-case time $T\ge1$ on $(x,y)$, there is a formula $F(x,y,z)$ of size $O(T\log^{O(1)}(T+2))$, each encoded output bit generated in $\log^{O(1)}(T+2)$ time and $O(\log(T+2))$ workspace with direct input-bit access. Its input-dependent constants form one ordered initial block, permitting sequential on-demand generation with the same polylogarithmic overhead per output-head transition. For fixed $x,y$ there is exactly one satisfying $z$ when the computation accepts, and none otherwise. The same conclusions hold for a fixed derived-basis machine when $T$ is at least its input length. Variable blocks and malformed-input behavior are fixed with the machine.

For an explicitly coded machine in the derived full classical basis profile, input $x$ of length $n$, and external transition clock $b\ge n$, there is a fixed finite-head index-only erased-index interpreter reproducing exact acceptance, rejection and timeout probabilities. Writing $L=|e|+1$ for source description length, its time and maximum physical work-access address are bounded by
$$C L^d\bigl(n+(b+1)\log^d(n+b+L+2)\bigr)$$
for absolute constants $C,d$. In particular, logarithmic descriptions and each fixed polynomial clock $T(n)\ge n$ have $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$ overhead, including clock construction. This is a time-only normalization; it does not preserve a smaller original source space bound and makes no general equivalence claim for clocks below input length.

derivations.claim: For $L\in\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}$, first tie-normalize its machine $M$ by [F1], then fix a linear integer clock $R(n)\ge1$ for the resulting machine. Let $A$ be its accepting count among the $2^{R(n)}$ fair strings $y$, including ignored suffixes. By [F4] its deterministic branch predicate has $n\log^{O(1)}n$ time: source choices read $y$ sequentially, and normalized short input indices map to the $x$ subword with charged offset arithmetic. Apply [F2], obtaining $F_x(y,z)$ with exactly one $z$ per accepting $y$ and none per rejecting $y$. Put $k=|z|$ and define $\psi_x=(v\wedge F_x(y,z))\vee(\neg v\wedge(\bigvee_i z_i\vee w))$. For fixed $y$, the $v=0$ branch has $2^{k+1}-1$ satisfying $(z,w)$ assignments, while $v=1$ adds two exactly when $y$ accepts. Each block is therefore one above or below half, and the total is at least half exactly when $A\ge2^{R(n)-1}$. The source has no tie, so this is its strict-majority decision. This same gadget applies to a quasilinear clock whenever needed below, with quasilinear output length.

For $L\in\mathrm{LCH}_{P,2}$, take its linear-time oracle machine and tie-normalize the first-level oracle decider. For query $q_i$, let $R_i=O(|q_i|+1)\ge1$ clock the chosen yes/no oracle machine, with ignored fair suffixes. A proposed answer is correct precisely when its tie-free yes/no machine has more than $2^{R_i-1}$ accepting strings. Then exactly one accepting string $w_i$ has exactly $2^{R_i-1}$ accepting strings lexicographically before it. Serialize all proposed queries, answers and witnesses with lengths and canonical zero padding; its length is $O(n)$ because $\sum_i(|q_i|+1)=O(n)$. On a record of length $N$, put $r_i=a_i-2^{R_i-1}$, where $a_i$ counts accepting strings before $w_i$. Let $\mathrm{bad}$ indicate invalid syntax and $\mathrm{invalid}_i$ indicate that the chosen witness path fails to accept. Then $G=\mathrm{bad}+\sum_i(r_i^2+\mathrm{invalid}_i)$ is nonnegative and is zero exactly when every answer has its unique rank witness. These are explicit differences of path counts: choose $i$ nondeterministically, assign zero gap to invalid padded indices, and use independent strings for products; expand $(a-b)^2=a^2+b^2-2ab$. A fixed number of these sums/products also gives $h=1-2G^2=A-B$, positive exactly when $G=0$. Deterministic syntax/witness tests give integer indicator counts; invalid syntax skips the remaining tests and sets $G=1$. Normalize each fixed basis component by [F4] before using it on a query subword; it then has no native subinput query, and short-offset access costs only polylogarithmic time. These count constructions thus take $N\log^{O(1)}N$ time, with no nondeterministic choices during deterministic interpreter work. Choose one common quasilinear choice bound $P$ and require unused suffix bits zero on accepting paths, preserving counts $A,B$ among $2^P$ choice strings. A leading fair bit selects $A$ on branch zero and the complement of $B$ on branch one. There are $2^P+(A-B)$ accepting choice strings out of $2^{P+1}$, so the transcript-validity language $C=\{h>0\}$ has a matching-profile quasilinear probabilistic decider. The original rank strings still have total linear length.

Normalize the original outer oracle machine by [F1] before this construction. Keep its original fixed-length fair-bit string $p$ separate from a guessed fixed-length transcript record $t$, whose unused suffix is canonically zero. Simulate the original machine on $p$ using the proposed answers in $t$, and record whether its queries match the listed queries and its final outcome accepts. Make a single final query to $C$ containing the record and this flag; extend $C$ to reject whenever the flag fails. There is exactly one correct answer/rank-witness record for each $p$ by step 1.2. Consequently exactly one $t$ gives a YES query when the original path accepts and none do when it rejects. The number of successful pairs $(p,t)$ is the original accepting-path count. No preservation of the acceptance probability after guessing $t$ is asserted; the next steps restore its threshold explicitly.

Let $q(p,t)$ be the deterministic final query from step 2.1, padded to fixed length $L$. Apply [F2] to its quasilinear-time computation using [F4] to obtain $D_x(p,t,q,z)$ with exactly one satisfying $(q,z)$ extension for every pair $(p,t)$. Apply the same unique-witness/majority gadget of step 1.1 with the quasilinear clock for $C$ on the variable input $q$, retaining $q$ as free Boolean variables, to obtain $\Psi_C(q,u)$ whose inner at-least-half test is true exactly when $q\in C$. Form the outer matrix $\Phi_x=(v\wedge D_x(p,t,q,z)\wedge\Psi_C(q,u))\vee(\neg v\wedge(\bigvee_i t_i\vee\bigvee_j q_j\vee\bigvee_k z_k\vee w))$. Here $w$ is one outer padding bit; the inner block $u$ has a fixed length independent of the value of $q$. All deterministic computations have quasilinear time in their input length in the selected profile, so [F2] gives total formula size $n\log^{O(1)}n$, logarithmic workspace and the claimed bit-generation and sequential-streaming interfaces.

Fix the original fair string $p$, and put $H=|t|$, $k=|z|$. Among $v=0$ outer assignments, the fallback is false at exactly one $(t,q,z,w)$ tuple, so $2^{H+L+k+1}-1$ assignments give a residual inner formula true on at least half of $u$. Among $v=1$ assignments, $D_x$ has exactly one $(q,z)$ extension for each $t$, and precisely one $t$ has $q(p,t)\in C$ if and only if the original path accepts. Its two choices of $w$ contribute two additional successful outer assignments. Thus each fixed-$p$ block contributes one below half on a rejecting original path and one above half on an accepting original path. Summing the equal-sized $p$ blocks makes outer at-least-half true exactly when at least half of the original fair strings accept; outer tie normalization in step 2.1 makes this the original strict-majority language.

Step 1.1 proves the first-level reduction, and step 1.2 and step 2.1 and step 3.1 and step 4.1 prove the second-level reduction in either fixed profile. All added blocks have $O(n)$ length before the near-linear formula encoding, and only a fixed number of these encodings are composed. The explicit clause order of [F2] preserves the sequential streaming property; the direct-input bit generator has the claimed polylogarithmic time and logarithmic workspace. This proves both reductions.

derivations.claim: Choose fixed rational $a>\alpha$ and $0<\gamma<\beta$. Appending a bit cannot decrease an overflowing value, and such a value is never used on a true $S$-space computation. For an input target saturate at $n+T+1$; an overflowing input jump stays beyond the input during every remaining local step, so a FAR marker returns blank until the next jump. Index tapes cannot read their emitted length or contents before use; leading zeroes and discarded overflow bits therefore have no other observable effect. Their reset returns the numeric prefix to zero. Current input positions up to $n+T+1$ and FAR markers use logarithmic length. The fixed number of indices contributes only $O(\log T+\log n)$ bits. Their descriptions have $O(S+\log T+\log n)$ bits and there are $2^{O(S+\log T+\log n)}$ of them. The accepting probability is the sum of path counts from the initial configuration to all accepting clock-$T$ configurations divided by $2^T$. The strict threshold is therefore comparison with $2^{T-1}$.

Put $q=\lceil n^\gamma\rceil$. For a segment of length $\ell$, split its time interval into $q$ consecutive intervals differing in length by at most one, sum over the $q-1$ checkpoint configurations, and multiply the corresponding segment path counts. Concatenation of the component paths bijects with the original paths, so this arithmetic identity counts each path exactly once, including parallel fair-bit edges. Each checkpoint tuple has $O(q(S+\log T+\log n))=O(n)$ bits. At each stage the sum fan-in is at most $2^{O(n)}$ and each product fan-in is $q$, polynomial in $n$.
