Let $\mathbb B:=\{0,1\}$. A **binary encoding** of a set $X$ is an injective
function
$$ e:X\to\mathbb B^* $$
([[def-function]], [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]).

Fix a symbol $\mathtt{mal}$ not belonging to $X$. A **total decoder** for $e$
is a function
$$ d:\mathbb B^*\to X\cup\{\mathtt{mal}\} $$
such that
$$ d(e(x))=x\quad(x\in X),\qquad d(w)=\mathtt{mal}\quad(w\notin e[X]). $$
Thus $\mathtt{mal}$ is exactly the output on malformed codes, and the decoder
is defined on every binary word, not only on words in the image of $e$.

The encoding $e$ is **effective** when such a total decoder is specified.

The encoding is **prefix-free** when no codeword is a proper prefix of another:
there do not exist distinct $x,y\in X$ and a nonempty binary word $u$ with
$e(y)=e(x)u$.

$$ C L^d\bigl(n+(b+1)\log^d(n+b+L+2)\bigr). $$

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

$$ n\le t(n) $$

Its source decider work extent is eventually below a known power-of-two bound $M=O(n^{1-\eta_1})$, because $\eta_1<\varepsilon$ absorbs fixed constants and polylogs in $N$. In the basis profile use [F6] to simulate both ordinary reads and native basis queries on this generated formula in time $O((n+N+N^d+1)\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ and space $O(M+\log n)$. In the sequential profile [F3]'s ordered source-constant block, or a logarithmic virtual-input-position counter, gives at most the same overhead for each local input move without changing work records. For any $\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^b)$ language, its self-delimited padded version at length $m=\Theta(n^B)$ has a linear-time decider. In the basis profile apply [F5] to the original fixed decider, then translate its short indices to the original-input portion of the actual padded word; the cost $n^b\mathrm{polylog}\,n$ fits $O(m)$ because $b<B$. Sequential simulation is no slower. Apply step 1.1 to that padded language. On the original word, its resulting time/space decider sees a generated input of length $m$. For the basis profile [F6] simulates this virtual padded input with a known work bound $M=O(m^{1-\eta})$ rounded to a power of two; its delimiter and zero bits have polylogarithmic-time/logspace generators. Time is $O(n^{Ba}\mathrm{polylog}\,n)\subseteq O(n^A)$ and work extent $O(m^{1-\eta}+\log n)=O(n^{1-\beta})$. The sequential virtual-input simulation has the same bounds. In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)\in\mathbb R^3$ with $\|\mathbf n\|_2=1$, put $\Sigma=\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}=n_xX+n_yY+n_zZ$. Then
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\Sigma\right)=\cos(\theta/2)I-i\sin(\theta/2)\Sigma,$$
and $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$ is unitary. For the endpoint $\theta=0$, it equals $I$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call unless the model explicitly combines them. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

derivations.claim: If $k=0$, take the one-element mask list containing the empty string. If $k>0$, construct the reflected Gray list recursively by $G_1=(0,1)$ and $G_k=(0G_{k-1},1\operatorname{rev}(G_{k-1}))$ for $k\ge2$. Induction shows that each $k$-bit string occurs once, consecutive strings differ in one coordinate, and the last string differs from the first in one coordinate; hence for $k>0$ the cycle has $2^k$ single-coordinate transitions. For its masks $p_0,\ldots,p_{2^k-1}$ set $H_{xj}=(-1)^{p_j\cdot x}$ and $\beta_j=2^{-k}\sum_yH_{yj}\theta_y$. Then $$\sum_jH_{xj}\beta_j=2^{-k}\sum_y\theta_y\sum_p(-1)^{p\cdot(x\oplus y)}=\theta_x,$$ because the inner sum factors as $\prod_{r=1}^k(1+(-1)^{x_r\oplus y_r})$, equal to $2^k$ for $x=y$ and $0$ otherwise.

Assume $k>0$. Apply $R_z(\beta_0)$ and follow the cyclic Gray list, placing one CNOT on the coordinate that changes between consecutive masks and one $R_z(\beta_j)$ at each mask, including the CNOT that returns from the last mask to the first. There are exactly $2^k$ of each. On a fixed control word $x$, the accumulated target bit flip before the $j$th rotation is $p_j\cdot x$ modulo two by [F5]. By [F2]–[F4], $R_z(t)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{-it/2},e^{it/2})$; direct multiplication with [F3] gives $XR_z(t)X=R_z(-t)$. Conjugating the target rotation by that parity network therefore gives $R_z((-1)^{p_j\cdot x}\beta_j)$. The final CNOT restores the parity network, so the full branch operator is the product of these rotations.

Rotations about the same axis satisfy $R_z(a)R_z(b)=R_z(a+b)$ by multiplying their diagonal matrices. Thus on branch $x$ the target operation is $R_z(\sum_jH_{xj}\beta_j)=R_z(\theta_x)$ by step 1.1. This proves the exact block action on every computational basis input and hence, by linearity, on every state. When $k=0$, the definition is the single gate $R_z(\theta_0)$.

The central block acts on each select word $x$ by $\begin{pmatrix}c_x&-s_x\\s_x&c_x\end{pmatrix}$. By [F6], choose $\phi_x$ with $c_x=\cos\phi_x$ and $s_x=\sin\phi_x$; this block is the $R_y(2\phi_x)$ convention used by [F3]. Thus the central block is one $(n-1)$-control multiplexed $R_y$ targeting the first wire.

Apply [F2] to each of the two block-diagonal factors from [F1]. Each factor becomes two $(n-1)$-qubit unitaries on the remaining contiguous interval and one $\operatorname{diag}(D,D^*)$. For each computational select word $x$, write the diagonal entry $D_{xx}=e^{i\alpha_x}$ using [F7]. Its action on the first wire is $\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\alpha_x},e^{-i\alpha_x})=R_z(-2\alpha_x)$, so this middle factor is one $(n-1)$-control multiplexed $R_z$. derivations.claim: Let $m=n-1$ be the number of controls and list them from nearest to farthest from the target. In a reflected Gray traversal, the nearest control is toggled at most $2^m$ times; the control at distance $k\ge2$ is toggled at most $2^{m-k+1}=2^{n-k}$ times. To see the bound, recursively form the reflected list $G_m=(G_{m-1}0,\operatorname{rev}(G_{m-1})1)$ and add the final edge returning the last word to the first: each non-farthest coordinate's toggle count is at most twice its count at the preceding recursion level, while the farthest coordinate changes at most twice (once at the join and once on return). The bound holds at $m=1$ and induction gives the displayed powers. Each toggle is one CNOT between the toggled control and the target. The total number of original CNOTs is $2^m$ by [F1].

For a CNOT whose endpoints are $k\ge2$ line edges apart, define $S_k$ to be the sequence of adjacent CNOTs along edges $0\to1,1\to2,\ldots,k-1\to k$, followed by the reverse sequence on edges $k-2\to k-1,\ldots,1\to2$. It has $2k-2$ gates. Starting from bits $(x_0,\ldots,x_k)$, the forward sweep makes wire $j$ hold $x_j\oplus\cdots\oplus x_0$. The reverse sweep, in descending order, restores wires $2,\ldots,k-1$ to $x_j$ and leaves wire 1 as $x_1\oplus x_0$ and wire $k$ as $x_k\oplus\cdots\oplus x_0$. Applying the same sequence a second time restores every intermediate wire and changes only wire $k$, to $x_k\oplus x_0$. Thus $S_kS_k$ is the required remote CNOT and uses $4k-4$ adjacent CNOTs. For the opposite ordered orientation, reflect the wire labels $j\mapsto k-j$ in this construction and reverse every adjacent CNOT arrow. Applying the same calculation to $(x_k,\ldots,x_0)$ shows that the mirrored square restores every intermediate wire and changes only the left endpoint target, to $x_0\oplus x_k$. Both directed adjacent orientations are permitted, and the mirrored network also uses $4k-4$ gates. The identities hold on every basis vector by [F2], hence as operators by linearity.

Leave every length-one CNOT unchanged and route each longer CNOT by step 2.1. Using the bounds in step 1.1, the routed count for one multiplexor is at most $$2^{n-1}+\sum_{k=2}^{n-1}(4k-4)2^{n-k}=9\cdot2^{n-1}-8n\le9\cdot2^{n-1}.$$ The original multiplexor has $2^{n-1}$ CNOTs by [F1], so the routed count is at most nine times its original count. This requires exact restoration of an arbitrary, initially unknown ancilla state and forbids residual data–ancilla correlation.

These are exact contracts for the complete subroutine. A temporary intermediate alteration of an ancilla is permitted if the full unitary satisfies the stated identity.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call unless the model explicitly combines them. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

Input is a finite word of H,T,T†,CNOT gates with ordered wire labels. Fix the rules H²→ε, T⁸→ε, TT†→ε, T†T→ε, and CNOT²→ε, where ε means the empty subword; apply the cancellation rules only when the adjacent gates have the same ordered support. Scan left-to-right, choose the first match, delete the matched subword, restart the scan, and halt when no rule matches. Empty words are permitted. The output remains a word over the input gate alphabet and is locally irreducible for this displayed rule set; it makes no global-minimum claim.

The gate labels use the exact matrices and ordered supports fixed by [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]].

Let $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$. The one-qubit generators and exact matrices in the
ordered computational basis are

$$H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\omega\end{pmatrix},\qquad T^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\omega^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$

On basis vectors, $H|q\rangle=(|0\rangle+(-1)^q|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and
$T^k|q\rangle=\omega^{kq}|q\rangle$ for $q\in\{0,1\}$.

Write $S=T^2=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ and
$Z=T^4=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Pauli $X,Y,Z$ are as in
[[def-qc-pauli-matrices]]. On two ordered wires,
$\operatorname{CNOT}|a,b\rangle=|a,b\mathbin\oplus a\rangle$; the first wire
is control and the second target. A circuit is a finite chronological word of
these gates at stated wire positions; its matrix is the product with later
gates on the left. No extra wire or controlled-$T$ operation is implicit.

The scalar phase $\omega I$ is an allowed Clifford phase in the one-qubit
matrix-word convention. Its scalar factor is retained in exact matrix products;
the convention that an overall scalar does not affect a resource count is
stated separately from matrix equality. It does not grant a controlled-$T$
operation or allow a scalar on a target wire to be discarded under control.

The exact one-qubit H/T algebra is generated by $H,T,T^\dagger$; $S$ and $Z$
are aliases for the displayed powers. The distinction between exact matrix
equality and [[def-qc-global-phase-equivalence|global-phase equivalence]] is
maintained. Resource costs are supplied by
[[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]] and remain separate from this matrix
definition.

derivations.claim: By [F2], $H^2=I$ by direct matrix multiplication, $T^8=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{2\pi i})=I$, and $TT^\dagger=T^\dagger T=I$. Use the **published VMW model** from Van Melkebeek and Watson, Theory of Computing 8 (2012), §2.3.1–2.3.2. It has three semi-infinite tapes: read-only binary input followed by blanks; a zero-initialized classical binary work tape; and a zero-initialized quantum work tape. There are a fixed finite number of heads, possibly several per tape. Classical finite control determines all head movements and chooses the local classical function and local quantum operation from its state, input/classical scanned symbols, and earlier measurement outcomes. These choices do not depend on the quantum basis path. A quantum operation is a unitary on the cells under the quantum heads or a single-qubit computational-basis measurement.

Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to a precomputed classical address. Addresses are written on special one-way sequential-access write-only index tapes and those tapes are erased after every use; all index-bit writing is charged to ordinary transitions. Coherent input access may apply $|i,b\rangle\mapsto|i,b\mathbin\oplus x_i\rangle$ to a contiguous quantum-work block, with out-of-range input bit zero. The endpoint convention is $[l,r]$: the MSB-first address occupies $[l,r)$ and the answer is cell $r$; use input indices $1,\ldots,n$, $x_0=0$, empty address zero, and omit a reversed-endpoint query. Its two endpoint addresses are likewise supplied on these erased index tapes. The coherent query itself costs one transition. The classical input tape's out-of-range cells are blank. These two output conventions are distinct and fixed by the source. If colliding work heads make an operation undefined, omit the operation on that work tape.

Input cells and the separate index tapes are not counted in the maximum-workhead-address space measure. Space is the maximum address of any work operand: ordinary classical/quantum head visits and the highest endpoint of every native query block are all charged; time and space maximize over every branch, including branches of probability zero. For each fixed unitary matrix entry, real and imaginary parts have deterministic approximators computing precision $p$ in time polynomial in $p$. This permits polylogarithmic time and workspace at precision $p=O(\log t)$; it does not assert linear-space approximators for arbitrary entries.

For a promise problem $(Y,N)$, $\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)$ means such a machine takes $O(t)$ transitions and maximum work address $O(s)$ on every branch, accepts $Y$ with probability at least $2/3$, and accepts $N$ with probability at most $1/3$. No acceptance guarantee is required off the promise; the resource bounds remain worst-case. $\mathrm{BQTIME}(t)$ omits the space bound. Its classical comparison classes are the explicitly derived full-basis comparison classes $\mathrm{PrTIME}_{\mathrm{basis}}$ and $\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\mathrm{basis}}$ in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]]. They permit a fixed finite product of classical basis tapes with the same native input-query operation. No generic inclusion into the narrower erased-index head-access-only class is assumed.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

Let $t,s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

On this page, whenever a constructible bound is used to clock another machine,
we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field. On the vector space
$\mathcal B(X,Y)$ of bounded linear operators, the operator norm of
[[def-operator-norm]] is a norm.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Fix a positive integer $k$ and a finite collection $\mathcal U$ of fixed unitary matrices, each on between one and $k$ qubits. Suppose every real and imaginary matrix coordinate has a deterministic Cauchy procedure returning error at most $2^{-p}$ in time polynomial in $p+1$. There exist exact no-ancilla one-qubit/CNOT factor lists for all $U\in\mathcal U$, with a common constant bound on their lengths, such that every coordinate of every one-qubit factor also has a polynomial-time Cauchy procedure. All scalar phases in the exact matrix products are retained.

The lists and Cauchy programs may depend on the fixed collection $\mathcal U$. In particular their finite zero/nonzero decisions and branch choices may be hardcoded. The claim is an existence statement for each fixed machine's finite transition set, not an algorithm that decides equality of arbitrary Cauchy-name inputs. It supplies effective target matrices for finite-precision compilation, not a compiler by itself.

Put $w=(2+i)/\sqrt5$, $F=\operatorname{diag}(1,w^2)$ and $H=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$. The alphabet
$$G=\{D,D^*,J,J^*\},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(\overline w,w),\quad J=iH$$
is an inverse-closed dense subset of $SU(2)$ with algebraic coordinates admitting fixed minimal-polynomial and rational-isolating-interval descriptions. For every fixed rational $0<\eta_0<1/4096$, it has a fixed finite base-net certificate of radius $\eta_0/4$ as in [[def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set]]. Erasing scalar phases maps its letters respectively to $F,F^*,H,H$ and preserves word length.

Fix a finite family of one-qubit unitary matrices whose first $b$ real and imaginary coordinate bits are computable in time polynomial in $b$. For every rational $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, each matrix $U$ in this family can be compiled deterministically into a word $W$ over $\{F,F^*,H\}$ with
$$\inf_{|\lambda|=1}\|W-\lambda U\|\le\varepsilon.$$
The expanded word length, bit time including output, and workspace are polynomial in $\log(1/\varepsilon)$ plus the binary encoding length of $\varepsilon$. Constants may depend on the fixed family. In particular, accuracy $1/(Ct)$ for fixed positive rational $C$ has polylogarithmic bit time, workspace and word length in $t$. The output acts on the original qubit and allocates no additional quantum work space.

derivations.claim: For a fixed machine, only finitely many local transition unitaries occur, each on a fixed number of qubits. Decompose each into a constant number of one-qubit gates and CNOTs using [A1], with polynomial-time Cauchy names for the resulting fixed one-qubit factors. Let $T\le c_Tt$ be the fixed-machine transition clock, with $c_T\ge1$, and let $c_M\ge1$ bound the one-qubit factors per transition. By [A2], compile each factor to projective error at most $1/(20c_Mc_Tt)$ as a word over $F=\operatorname{diag}(1,(3+4i)/5)$, its adjoint, and $H$; CNOT and query gates remain exact. Direct multiplication gives $F^*F=I$ because $(3-4i)(3+4i)=25$; [F3] gives unitary $H$ and CNOT, and [F1] gives the query basis permutation. The finite-bit compiler has word length, time and workspace polynomial in $\log t$, since the fixed-factor Cauchy procedures have polynomial query time and the requested tolerance has $O(\log t)$ bits. Execute its deterministic work sequentially while holding the original quantum operand heads stationary. Preserve the source's classical transition, fresh index-bit emissions and scheduled jumps/queries once; extra compiler cycles neither duplicate nor consume its pending index words. Use fixed interleaved classical tracks on the original single classical work tape: choose a fixed power-of-two stride $K$ and represent virtual classical cell $a$ on track $b$ at physical cell $Ka+b$. A local virtual move takes $K$ physical moves, and a freshly emitted classical jump index is translated by appending the fixed track-label bits, costing only a constant number of extra emitted bits per jump. Fixed extra classical heads access the compiler scratch track sequentially, whose used length is $\mathrm{polylog}(t)$; the resulting classical extent is $O(s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$. The original quantum work tape, operand positions and quantum-query endpoint indices are unchanged, so every native quantum-query block remains contiguous as in [F1]. The constructible bounds [F4] clock these loops, giving compiled time $t'=O(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$ and work extent $O(s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$.

For a computational-basis measurement [F1], put $P_j=|j\rangle\langle j|$ for $j=0,1$; direct calculation gives $P_j^*=P_j$, $P_j^2=P_j$, $P_0P_1=0$, and $P_0+P_1=I$. Postpone it in a proof-only deferred-measurement dilation by reserving a fresh two-qubit record slot, initialized to $|00\rangle$, at each of the $T$ transition times and using the isometry $\psi\otimes|00\rangle\mapsto P_0\psi\otimes|10\rangle+P_1\psi\otimes|11\rangle$. The output branches are orthogonal by [F8]–[F9], and their squared norms sum to $\|\psi\|^2$ by the projector identities just checked. A transition with no measurement leaves that slot at $|00\rangle$. Thus every complete history has a fixed-length record string over the $T$ slots; distinct histories differ in some slot, so [F8]–[F9] make their record subspaces orthogonal, and subsequent classically controlled operations preserve orthogonality by [F1]. These record slots are not allocated by the simulator. Projective compilation may multiply a one-qubit gate by a phase. Within each fixed history $h$ and transition time $r$, all one-qubit factors act on the same quantum state, so their phases multiply to one scalar $\lambda_{h,r}$ on that whole transition block. Rephase each compiled block by this scalar; telescoping its at most $c_M$ one-qubit replacements gives operator error at most $c_M/(20c_Mc_Tt)=1/(20c_Tt)$, since surrounding gates and exact measurement dilations have norm one. The direct sum over orthogonal history blocks has this same bound: for $v=\bigoplus_hv_h$ and block errors $E_h$, $\|(\bigoplus_hE_h)v\|^2=\sum_h\|E_hv_h\|^2\le(1/(20c_Tt))^2\sum_h\|v_h\|^2$. Across the full computation, the actual and rephased compiled final vectors differ by $D=\bigoplus_h\Lambda_h I_h$, where $\Lambda_h$ is the product of the phase factors along history $h$ and $|\Lambda_h|=1$. The accepting projection is block diagonal, $P=\bigoplus_hP_h$, so $\langle Dv,PDv\rangle=\sum_h|\Lambda_h|^2\langle v_h,P_hv_h\rangle=\langle v,Pv\rangle$. Thus the rephasing does not change acceptance probability. Telescope the $T$ phase-aligned transition products. Their exact and compiled prefixes and suffixes are norm one, so [F6]–[F7] give state-vector error at most $T/(20c_Tt)\le1/20$. For unit vectors $u,v$ and accepting projection $P$, $\langle u,Pu\rangle-\langle v,Pv\rangle=\langle u-v,Pu\rangle+\langle v,P(u-v)\rangle$. Cauchy–Schwarz [F10] and $\|Pz\|\le\|z\|$ bound the absolute difference by $2\|u-v\|\le1/10$. The compiled machine therefore accepts YES inputs with probability at least $17/30>1/2$ and NO inputs with probability at most $13/30<1/2$.

Fix one input and the compiled computation. For a complete measurement history $\mu$, let $f_\mu$ and $h_\mu$ count its $F/F^\dagger$ and $H$ gates. Let $\Sigma_{\rm acc}(\mu)$ be the final basis configurations accepted by the fixed machine after history $\mu$, as determined by its finite transition table and terminal acceptance rule. Use the exact matrices from [F3] and the stated $F$ matrix in step 1.1. Expand every $F$ entry with numerator $1$ as five unit terms over denominator $5$, and every numerator $3+4i$ (respectively $3-4i$) as three terms of phase $1$ and four terms of phase $i$ (respectively $-i$). Each Hadamard transition contributes phase $1$ or $-1$ over denominator $\sqrt2$; CNOT, query, and computational-basis measurement transitions contribute $0$ or $1$. Thus each path term has phase $\alpha\in\{1,-1,i,-i\}$ and denominator $5^{f_\mu}2^{h_\mu/2}$. For a final basis state $\sigma$, let $A_\alpha(\mu,\sigma)$ count path terms of phase $\alpha$. Its amplitude is $\sum_\alpha\alpha A_\alpha/(5^{f_\mu}2^{h_\mu/2})$. Summing squared magnitudes over the accepting configurations gives the joint probability of history $\mu$ and acceptance: $$p_\mu^{\rm acc}=\frac{\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma_{\rm acc}(\mu)}\left(A_1^2+A_{-1}^2+A_i^2+A_{-i}^2-2A_1A_{-1}-2A_iA_{-i}\right)}{25^{f_\mu}2^{h_\mu}}.$$ The identity follows by expanding the squared real and imaginary parts, and summing $p_\mu^{\rm acc}$ over histories gives the compiled acceptance probability.

Pad every branch to exactly $t'$ quantum gate slots with identities, and set $F_*=H_*=t'$ and $D=25^{F_*}2^{H_*}$. Multiply each joint accepting-history numerator in 2.1 by $25^{F_*-f_\mu}2^{H_*-h_\mu}$. A bounded nondeterministic machine simulates two path terms in lockstep, requires the same measurement history and final basis row, tests shared classical acceptance, and counts pairs with equal phases positively and opposite phases negatively. The scale factor is exactly realized by $H_*-h_\mu$ extra binary choices and two five-way choices per missing $F$ slot, rejecting invalid encodings. All phase and scale choices use $O(t')$ binary choices. At a measurement, guess one bit, require both basis rows to have it at the measured cell, feed it to their shared classical controller, then discard it. This sums histories without storing a transcript.

Store the two quantum basis rows on two separate binary work tapes and the shared classical configuration on separate fixed tapes, as permitted by [F2]. Corresponding heads on both rows make the same source local moves or fresh jumps; duplicate each newly emitted source index bit to the fixed number of required index tapes, so total address writing is multiplied only by a constant. Separate rows preserve contiguity of each query address block. For $Q_x$ on source cells $[l,r]$, apply native $Q_x$ to each row using copies of its freshly written endpoint indices. Its address bits are unchanged and only its answer cell $r$ is updated. Duplicate the right-endpoint stream also to auxiliary heads on both rows; at query time place these at $r$ to read the old and new answer bits. These heads remain within charged operand extent $s$. There is no copying or scanning of the possibly long address block, and no assertion that $\log n=O(\log t)$. Each row can read a different input bit, exactly as required by its distinct basis path. Maintain a counter $\Delta$ of positions where the two rows disagree. It starts zero; every local gate or query changes only a fixed number of bits, so mirrored operand heads supply the before/after disagreement indicators and update $\Delta$. Since at most $O(t')$ bit changes occur, $\Delta$ uses $O(\log t')$ bits; its final value is zero exactly when the rows agree, avoiding an $O(s)$ terminal scan. Each counter operation costs $\mathrm{polylog}(t')$ bit time. Thus the two bounded path-count machines have time $O(t'\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t')$ and extent $O(s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$, with accepting counts $N_+,N_-$ satisfying $\Pr[\text{compiled acceptance}]=(N_+-N_-)/D$.

The sign of $2(N_+-N_-)-D$ decides whether the compiled acceptance probability is above or below $1/2$. The denominator $D$ is itself a bounded path count: guess $H_*$ bits and, for each of $F_*$ factors, two three-bit numbers, accepting only values below $5$. Thus $D$ has exactly $2^{H_*}25^{F_*}$ accepting branches and is generated in $O(t')$ time and $O(\log t')$ work space. Build bounded nondeterministic machines with path counts $A=2N_+$ and $B=2N_-+D$ by disjointly tagging the component computations and rejecting noncanonical padding. Pad both to the same total number $2^q$ of paths for an explicitly bounded $q=O(t')$, using zero-only suffix padding to preserve each accepting-path count. A fair leading bit chooses the $A$ machine on branch 0 and the complement of the $B$ machine on branch 1. The resulting machine has $2^{q+1}$ equiprobable paths and $2^q+(A-B)$ accepting paths, so it accepts with probability strictly greater than $1/2$ exactly when $2(N_+-N_-)-D>0$. The constructible bounds in [F4] let the simulator choose and exhaust these fixed choice lengths. All choice counters can be maintained in $O(\log t')$ bits and $\mathrm{polylog}(t')$ time per choice. The total time is $O(t'\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t')=O(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$ and work extent is $O(s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$ in the derived basis profile.

Step 2.1 places compiled YES acceptance strictly above $1/2$ and NO acceptance strictly below $1/2$. Step 5.1 preserves that sign, giving the stated bounded-error quantum to unbounded-error classical inclusion with its full claimed resources in $\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm basis}$. The classical operand-space convention is explicit in [F1]–[F2]; literal head-only accounting with uncharged distant query operands is not claimed. No general simulation into the index-only erased-address or sequential profile has been proved here.

citations.quote:
For sufficiently constructible $t,s\ge\log n$, the published VMW model with charged operand extent satisfies
$$\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm basis}(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t,s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t).$$
The output uses the derived classical basis profile in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]], with a fixed finite number of separate binary work tapes and native basis input queries. All work cells addressed by local operations or a query, including the highest query endpoint, count toward work extent. This is the explicit operand-space formalization of the published model; no general conversion to the erased-index head-access-only or sequential profile is asserted.

For either fixed profile $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, every real $d$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c>1$ such that at least one of the following holds: $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTIME}_{P}(n^c)$, or $\mathrm{MajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTISP}_{P}(n^d,n^{1-\varepsilon})$. The basis profile is the derived full-basis comparison model. Formula thresholds are at least-half and machine acceptance is strict majority.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

derivations.claim: Fix $d,\varepsilon$ and choose rational $D>\max(d,1)$ and rational $0<\varepsilon'<\min(\varepsilon,1)$. By [F2] there is a classical time exponent $C>1$ for the alternative with parameters $D,\varepsilon'$. Choose rational $1<c<C$ and suppose, for contradiction, that both quantum algorithms in the statement exist. For the time-only $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ algorithm, choose rational $\tau_{\rm mm}$ with $c<\tau_{\rm mm}<C$ and use the constructible simulation clock $t_{\rm mm}=\lceil K_{\rm mm}(n+2)^{\tau_{\rm mm}}\rceil$. The published VMW model permits maximum work addresses exponential in the running time: in $t_{\rm mm}$ transitions only $O(t_{\rm mm})$ address bits can be emitted, so a constructible space majorant $s_{\rm mm}=2^{K t_{\rm mm}}$, for a fixed sufficiently large $K$, bounds every work operand and query endpoint of this fixed machine. Its binary numeral is a $1$ followed by $K t_{\rm mm}$ zeroes and is generated in $O(t_{\rm mm})$ time, within the required constructibility bounds. Both $t_{\rm mm},s_{\rm mm}\ge\log n$, so [F1] gives a matching-profile classical time $O(n^{\tau_{\rm mm}}\mathrm{polylog}\,n)\subseteq O(n^C)$ decider. For the $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ algorithm, choose rational $\tau_{\rm sat}$ with $\max(d,1)<\tau_{\rm sat}<D$ and use constructible majorants $t_{\rm sat}=\lceil K_{\rm sat}(n+2)^{\tau_{\rm sat}}\rceil$ and $s_{\rm sat}=\lceil K'_{\rm sat}(n+2)^{1-\varepsilon'}\rceil$. They are at least $\log n$ for large $n$ and dominate the assumed time $O(n^d)$ and space $O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$. Theorem [F1] then gives classical time $O(n^{\tau_{\rm sat}}\mathrm{polylog}\,n)\subseteq O(n^D)$ and space $O(n^{1-\varepsilon'}+\mathrm{polylog}\,n)\subseteq O(n^{1-\varepsilon'})$. These two classical algorithms contradict both sides of [F2]'s alternative.

Suppose $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ has time $n^{1+o(1)}$ and space $O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$. By [F3], a plain $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ encoding is already the identical bit string accepted as a $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ instance with an implicit fresh unused outer variable. Both of its outer assignments have the original inner majority value. First validate the plain encoding in $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace, rejecting malformed or partition-tagged inputs. Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Fix a length-$n$ finite promise computation from [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]], with input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, zero-initialized auxiliary register $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, circuit unitary $U_{C_n}$, and ordered output-wire tuple $O_n$. Let $P_{O_n}$ be the tensor-factor permutation that moves $O_n$, in its declared order, to the front, and let $W_n$ be the ordered tuple of all remaining wires ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]). Set
$$\psi_x:=U_{C_n}(|x\rangle\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle),\qquad v_x:=\operatorname{coord}(P_{O_n}\psi_x).$$
Here coordinates are in the ordered computational basis, and the root inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$ and $w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}$, write $e_{z,w}$ for the corresponding product-basis vector and define
$$p_{C_n}(z\mid x):=\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}}\left|\langle P_{O_n}\psi_x,e_{z,w}\rangle_{\rm root}\right|^2.$$
The acceptance probability is
$$p_{C_n}(x):=\sum_{\substack{z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}\\A_n(x,z)=1}}p_{C_n}(z\mid x).$$
Equivalently, if $E_{A,x}$ is the diagonal projection onto the basis vectors $(z,w)$ with $A_n(x,z)=1$, then $p_{C_n}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(E_{A,x}v_xv_x^\dagger)$; the matrix adjoint is conjugate transpose in an orthonormal basis ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]]).

These are finite sums. The definition itself does not assert normalization, positivity of the resulting operator expression, or a probability bound; those consequences are the purpose of [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]]. No Dirac bra convention is used here: every amplitude uses the root pairing displayed above.

A promise problem $\Pi=(Y,N)$ belongs to **BQP in the QC14 model** when there exist a full-list uniform family $(C_n)$ and a polynomial-time acceptance predicate $A_n$ as in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] such that, for every $x\in Y$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\ge\frac23,$$
and for every $x\in N$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\le\frac13.$$
By [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]], $p_{C_n}(x)$ is the probability of the specified acceptance event and lies in $[0,1]$. No condition is imposed for $x\notin Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). The gate alphabet is exactly $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$; its matrix entries lie in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$ as specified by [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. This definition does not assert a BQP-versus-classical separation, nor does it assert an unproved equivalence with another circuit-uniformity convention.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call unless the model explicitly combines them. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

derivations.claim: By [F3], gate budget $C$ counts gate occurrences and $W$ includes every workspace wire. A circuit with $j$ gate occurrences has at most $(AW^k)^j$ ordered gate-list descriptions on $W$ wire labels: there are $A$ gate types and at most $W^k$ ordered supports per type. By [A1], flattening each finite layer list in chronological order preserves its denotation, so every layered circuit of at most $C$ gates is represented by one of these lists. Choosing the designated output wire contributes a factor at most $W$. Thus the number of descriptions is at most $W\sum_{j=0}^{C}(AW^k)^j$. Since $A\ge1$, $W\ge1$, $C\ge n$, and $k$ is fixed, $W=O(C)$ for positive $C$ and $AW^k\ge1$. The sum is at most $(C+1)(AW^k)^C$, whose logarithm is $O(C\log C)$. Duplicate denotations only reduce the number of computed functions.

By [F1], a fixed description has one acceptance probability $p_C(x)$ at each input. If it computed two distinct Boolean functions with success threshold [F2], some input $x$ would require the same number $p_C(x)$ to be both at least $2/3$ and at most $1/3$, which is impossible. Therefore one description accounts for at most one truth table.

There are exactly $2^{2^n}$ Boolean functions on $n$ bits. By step 1.2, each description covers at most one function, so at least $99\%$ require more than $C_n=\Omega(2^n/n)$ gates. This is an almost-all lower bound, not a lower bound for each named function.

On the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(az)>1/2$, put $r=\sqrt{(1+\operatorname{Re}(az))/2}$ and $v=r+i\operatorname{Im}(az)/(2r)$. Then $r>\sqrt3/2$, $|v|=1$ and $v^2=az$ by direct calculation. Fix one algebraic square root $b$ of $a$ and set $\lambda=b/v$. Thus $|\lambda|=1$ and $\lambda^2z=1$, so $V=\lambda U\in SU(2)$. All denominators in this normalization are bounded below by a fixed positive constant. By [F3], its coordinates have polynomial-time Cauchy procedures. Fix, for example, $\eta_0=1/8192$ and the gate package furnished by [F1]. Apply [F2] to $V$ with tolerance $\varepsilon'=\min(\varepsilon,\eta_0/2)$. The fixed algebraic gate descriptions and base-net constants satisfy every gate-package hypothesis. The normalized target's Cauchy query exponent is a fixed constant by step 1.1. Thus the compiler prints a word $S$ in the lifted alphabet with $\|S-V\|\le\varepsilon'$, using polynomial bit time and polynomial expanded word length in the requested bit precision and tolerance-encoding length. Its work space is at most its bit time. This invocation uses the finite-bit theorem, not a unit-cost exact-real arithmetic count.

Erase scalar phases letter by letter using [F1]. The resulting physical word $W$ has the same length and differs from $S$ by one scalar of modulus one. Consequently its projective distance to $U$ is at most $\varepsilon'\le\varepsilon$. Printing the physical labels adds linear time in the expanded output length. All quantum letters act on the same one-qubit register. At tolerance $1/(Ct)$ the requested precision and binary encoding length are $O(\log t)$, so every classical resource bound becomes $\mathrm{polylog}(t)$; a fixed family has one uniform maximum exponent and constant over its finitely many members.

Fix a positive matrix dimension $d$ and an integer $c\ge1$. A dyadic interval is a
closed interval with dyadic-rational endpoints; a complex matrix interval
stores one such interval for every real and imaginary entry. Suppose each
input is given by a Cauchy procedure which, on unary request $1^q$, returns a
rational approximation to each real and imaginary entry with error at most
$2^{-q}$ and uses $O((q+1)^c)$ bit operations. Suppose exact scalar and
matrix inputs have entries of modulus at most $3$. Each fixed algebraic real
constant is supplied by a rational polynomial and an open rational interval
with nonroot endpoints on which the polynomial has opposite endpoint signs
and exactly one real root.
When each scalar divisor
and each norm used for normalization has modulus at
least $2^{-B}$, the following routines return dyadic intervals of diameter at
most $2^{-p}$ containing the exact answer, using
$O((p+B+1)^{\max(c,3)})$ bit operations:

- any fixed finite composition of sums and products;
- quotient by a scalar whose modulus is at least $2^{-B}$;
- the nonnegative square root of a real in $[0,1]$;
- normalization $v/\|v\|_2$ of a real vector with $\|v\|_2\ge2^{-B}$;
- the matrix exponential $e^A$ when $\|A\|\le1$; and
- the matrix logarithm $\log(I+E)=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^{j+1}E^j/j$
  when $\|E\|\le1/2$.

Here $d$ and the number of scalar operations in the fixed composition are
constants. The exponent $B$ is needed only for divisions and normalization;
the square-root routine also works at input zero. The constants in the
complexity bound may depend on the fixed dimension, routine, and Cauchy-time
constant.

Input: an exact-arithmetic representation of $U\in U(N)$, $N\ge1$, supporting addition, multiplication, conjugation, nonnegative square roots, exact zero tests, and exact division by nonzero positive real scalars. Output: a finite ordered factorization into two-level unitaries and a diagonal unitary. This is an exact algebraic procedure; no claim of a bit-time algorithm for arbitrary real input is made.

Initialize $M:=U$ and an empty chronological list. For each column $j=0,\ldots,N-2$, and for $r=N-1,N-2,\ldots,j+1$, set $a=M_{r-1,j}$ and $b=M_{r,j}$. If $b=0$, do nothing. Otherwise set $h=\sqrt{|a|^2+|b|^2}>0$ and left-multiply rows $(r-1,r)$ by
$$G=\frac1h\begin{pmatrix}\overline a&\overline b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix},$$
recording this two-level unitary in the order applied. Let the resulting matrix be $D$. Return the factorization $U=G_1^*\cdots G_s^*D$. In chronological circuit order, apply $D$ first and then $G_s^*,\ldots,G_1^*$.

For $U\in U(N)$, the elimination procedure of [[alg-qc-two-level-unitary-elimination]] terminates after at most $N(N-1)/2$ Givens steps and returns an exact factorization of $U$ into the recorded two-level adjoints followed by a diagonal unitary. The number of diagonal entries is $N$; entries equal to $1$ need no phase gate.

Input distinct $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, exact $V\in U(2)$, and for each controlled call a choice between the no-workspace and clean-bit constructions of [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. If any call selects the clean-bit construction, supply one clean bit initialized to $0$. Output: the chronological elementary-gate list on the $n$ data wires and, if selected, that one clean work wire.

Let $g_0=x,\ldots,g_d=y$ be the path that flips the differing bit positions once in increasing order, where $d$ is the Hamming distance. For $j=0,\ldots,d-2$, swap $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ by an $X$ on their differing bit controlled on the other $n-1$ bits matching their common pattern. Apply $V$ to the final pair $g_{d-1},y$ by a one-qubit target gate controlled on their common other bits, reversing the ordered $2\times2$ block if $g_{d-1}$ has target bit $1$. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multi-control using its selected construction; implement negative controls by conjugating that control wire with $X$.

Use the selected literal elementary gate list for each call without deleting identity gates or cancelling neighboring gates. In the one-control base use the three target matrices and one control phase as four arbitrary one-qubit gates. Use the same choices and reversed adjoint gate lists for the return swaps. Reuse the supplied clean bit sequentially; each selected clean-bit construction returns it to $0$.

For $m\ge1$ controls and exact $U\in U(2)$, define
$$C^m(U)=\sum_{x\ne1^m}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes I_2+|1^m\rangle\langle1^m|\otimes U.$$
This controlled operation has (i) a no-workspace exact construction with $O(m^2)$ one-qubit and CNOT gates, and (ii) an exact construction using one clean work bit, initially $0$ and returned to $0$, with $O(m)$ such gates. For nonscalar $U$, every exact circuit needs at least $m$ two-qubit gates, also when auxiliary wires are allowed with data-independent initial state and exact clean or dirty return. Clean auxiliary wires start at $0$ and return to $0$ for every data input; dirty auxiliary wires may start in any state and the full operation is $C^m(U)\otimes I$ on them, including correlated inputs. A fixed auxiliary state may be internally entangled but is initially independent of the data. These are upper/lower bounds; the quadratic no-work construction is not asserted optimal.

For every $U\in U(2)$, the exact controlled matrix $C(U)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,U)$ is realized with two CNOTs and one-qubit gates only. The scalar phase of $U$ is implemented as a phase gate on the control and is not discarded.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

derivations.claim: Fixed finite compositions of polynomial-Cauchy scalars remain polynomial-Cauchy under the operations of [F1], provided each nonzero divisor has a fixed positive lower bound. There are only finitely many scalars in a fixed finite expression tree, so for its nonzero divisors some integer $B$ has $|z|\ge2^{-B}$ throughout; $B$ may be hardcoded. A fixed zero is returned as zero. Nonnegative roots are allowed even at zero, and nested roots only multiply the requested precision by a fixed constant at each of finitely many levels. Thus the finite compositions still use polynomial time in $p+1$. Conjugation merely changes an imaginary sign.

The path instruction in [F3] is an exact factorization. Each prescribed pattern-controlled $X$ exchanges precisely the adjacent path labels $g_j,g_{j+1}$ and fixes every other computational-basis label, because its $n-1$ controls must match the common bits. Let $P$ be the permutation effected by the swaps in their stated order. Then $P(x)=g_{d-1}$ and $P(y)=y=g_d$. The middle block, with the stated block reversal when the target bit of $g_{d-1}$ is $1$, acts by $V$ on the ordered pair $(g_{d-1},g_d)$ and fixes its complement. The complete chronological list therefore has matrix $P^*MP$, where $M$ is that middle block. Since $P$ is a permutation and maps $x,y$ to the selected pair, no other basis label maps into that pair; the conjugate acts by $V$ on $(x,y)$ and fixes every other basis vector. The controlled-gate expansions are exact by [F4] and [F5], and the negative-control conjugations retain their exact matrices. Thus every two-level factor used here is exactly the one specified by [F3], including its scalar phase.

A square root of any fixed polynomial-Cauchy unit scalar $u$ can also be selected polynomially. Choose a fixed $\zeta\in\{1,-1,i,-i\}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(\zeta u)\ge1/2$; such a choice exists because the larger absolute coordinate of a unit complex number is at least $1/\sqrt2$. Put $v=\zeta u$ and $a=\sqrt{(1+\operatorname{Re}v)/2}$, $b=\operatorname{Im}v/(2a)$. Then $a\ge\sqrt3/2$ and $(a+ib)^2=v$. Multiply by either fixed algebraic square root of $\zeta^{-1}$ and choose its fixed sign to obtain either desired root of $u$. Step 1.1 applies with a positive constant denominator. Iterating gives any fixed finite tower of coherently chosen phase half-roots. A root of a fixed nonzero complex scalar $z$ is obtained by first normalizing $z/|z|$ and multiplying its unit root by $\sqrt{|z|}$; the zero case is hardcoded separately.

For each $U\in\mathcal U$, run the finite algebraic Givens construction [F2] as a mathematical factorization. Hardcode its actual finite skip decisions $b=0$; no run-time zero test on a varying Cauchy name is required. In each unskipped operation $h>0$ is a fixed constant, so all entries of that Givens matrix and the updated matrix are polynomial-Cauchy by step 1.1. There are at most $2^k(2^k-1)/2$ operations, a constant. The terminal diagonal entries and the exact two-level adjoints therefore have polynomial-Cauchy entries. A phase on one chosen computational word is a pattern-controlled $\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)$ or $\operatorname{diag}(\lambda,1)$ on a selected wire, with the other wires matching that word; hence the terminal diagonal is a fixed finite product of pattern-controlled one-qubit matrices of the same effective class.

The square roots required by [F4] preserve this effective class. For a fixed two-dimensional unitary $W$, if $W=\lambda I$ choose a unit root $\mu$ by step 2.1 and take $\mu I$. Otherwise the spectral theorem [F6] gives two distinct eigenvalues. The nonzero discriminant $d_0=(\operatorname{tr}W)^2-4\det W$ has a root $d$ as in step 2.1, and $\lambda_\pm=(\operatorname{tr}W\pm d)/2$ have modulus one. The projector $P_+=(W-\lambda_-I)/(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)$ and $P_-=I-P_+$ are orthogonal by [F6]. Choose unit roots $\mu_\pm$ and put $V=\mu_+P_++\mu_-P_-$. Then $V$ is unitary, $V^2=W$, and every entry is polynomial-Cauchy by step 1.1 and step 2.1. The scalar/nonscalar branch and the positive eigenvalue-gap lower bound are fixed choices, not input-dependent equality decisions.

The constant one-control construction [F5] is effective as well. Choose a unit root $\lambda$ of $\det W$ by step 2.1 and normalize $S=\lambda^{-1}W\in SU(2)$. Write $S=\begin{pmatrix}a&-\overline c\\c&\overline a\end{pmatrix}$ and $\rho=|a|$, $\sigma=|c|$. If $\rho>0$ use $a/\rho$ for its phase, otherwise fix its arbitrary phase to $1$; treat $c/\sigma$ the same way. Choose fixed real arguments $\gamma,\eta$ with $a=e^{-i\gamma}\rho$ and $c=e^{i\eta}\sigma$, and choose $0\le\theta\le\pi$ with $\cos(\theta/2)=\rho$, $\sin(\theta/2)=\sigma$. These are only notation: the algorithm never computes their real arguments. Every matrix entry of the Euler factors and of $A,B,C$ in [F5] is a finite sum or product of the unit phases and their coherently selected half-roots, together with $\rho,\sigma$, $\sqrt{(1+\rho)/2}$ and $\sqrt{(1-\rho)/2}$. Indeed the latter are $\cos(\theta/4),\sin(\theta/4)$; the z-rotation entries are exponentials of half-angles of $\alpha=\gamma+\eta$ and $\beta=\gamma-\eta$, hence phase roots from step 2.1. Choose their fixed signs to match these displayed arguments. Thus all four arbitrary one-qubit matrices in the exact controlled construction are polynomial-Cauchy; their multiplication retains the control phase $\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)$ exactly. No numerical angle oracle is assumed.

Apply the Gray-path implementation [F3] to each two-level block from step 2.2, and apply the no-workspace recursion [F4] to its pattern-controlled gates and to the diagonal phase gates. Negative controls and permutation gates have fixed algebraic entries. Each root step stays in the effective class by step 3.1 and each controlled base case does so by step 3.2. The number of controls, recursion depth, blocks, and elementary gates is bounded by a constant depending on $k$ and the finite fixed collection. Therefore only finitely many branch choices and divisor lower bounds are needed in total; hardcode them and the corresponding polynomial-Cauchy programs into the simulator. Exact factorization follows from step 1.2 and step 3.1 and step 3.2 and [F2]–[F5], including each scalar phase; the resulting gate factors and lengths have precisely the asserted properties.
