citations.quote: Let $d\ge0$ and let $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ have degree at most $d$, parity $d\bmod2$, and $|p(x)|\le1$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$. Then there is a QSP-admissible pair $P,Q$ of degree bound $d$ such that $\operatorname{Re}P(x)=p(x)$ on $[-1,1]$. In fact, the completion is exact, so for every $\delta>0$ it also satisfies $|\operatorname{Re}P(x)-p(x)|\le\delta$.

For every integer $d\ge0$, a pair $P,Q\in\mathbb C[x]$ is QSP-admissible of degree bound $d$ if and only if there is a real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ such that
$$U_\Phi(x)=\begin{pmatrix}P(x)&s(x)Q(x)\\(-1)^{d+1}s(x)Q^*(x)&(-1)^dP^*(x)\end{pmatrix}\quad (x\in[-1,1]).$$
The converse is constructive: a leading-coefficient phase peel reduces the degree at each nonconstant stage. The polynomial identity, determinant signs, product order, and phase convention are exactly those in [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]] and [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]].

Let $x\in[-1,1]$, put $s(x)=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ using the nonnegative real square root, and define the Hermitian-reflection signal matrix
$$W_R(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x&s(x)\\s(x)&-x\end{pmatrix}.$$
For each real $\phi$, define $Z(\phi)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\phi},e^{-i\phi})$. For an integer $d\ge0$ and real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$, the length-$d$ QSP sequence is the ordered matrix product
$$U_\Phi(x)=Z(\phi_0)\prod_{j=1}^{d}\bigl(W_R(x)Z(\phi_j)\bigr),$$
where the product is written left to right in increasing $j$ and matrix multiplication acts right to left. For $d=0$ this is $Z(\phi_0)$. This definition fixes the sign of the off-diagonal signal entry, both endpoint phases, and the product order.

The phases are in matrix order: when the factors are applied as chronological circuit layers, the rightmost factor acts first, in accordance with [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. In the ordered signal basis, if both coordinates are nonzero, applying $Z(\phi)$ multiplies the ratio of the second coordinate to the first by $e^{-2i\phi}$; if either coordinate is zero, that relative phase is undefined, while the displayed matrix action remains defined. This is the relative phase convention fixed by [[def-qc-relative-phase]].

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ is zero or has degree at most $d$, has parity $d\bmod2$, and satisfies $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

Let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection on a finite-dimensional space $H$, with reflection $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$ and $S_\Pi=I-2\Pi=-R_\Pi$. Suppose the control-first call $C(R_\Pi)$ is explicitly supplied, together with an ancilla initialized in $|0\rangle$ and exact one-qubit $H$ and $R_z$ gates. Then the unitary $e^{i\phi R_\Pi}$ is implemented exactly by two controlled-reflection calls and one variable phase rotation, with a constant number of additional one-qubit gates, and the ancilla is returned to $|0\rangle$. If an external branch qubit is present and a branch-controlled $R_z(2\phi)$ is supplied, controlling only that rotation implements the controlled projector phase; the two controlled-reflection calls remain unconditional with respect to the external branch. In QSVT the construction is applied separately to $\Pi_R$ and $\Pi_L$; each projector-phase slot uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection. The access and gate costs are charged separately.

**Inputs.** A finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$, a unitary $U:H\to H$, orthogonal projections $\Pi_R,\Pi_L$, an integer $d\ge0$, and an exact real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$. The input access contract states separately whether $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, and controlled-$U^*$ are supplied and gives their individual costs. The scalar signal sequence is $U_\Phi(x)=Z(\phi_0)\prod_{j=1}^{d}(W_R(x)Z(\phi_j))$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]], with its admissible polynomial pair from [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]. A desired polynomial target is supplied with a certificate that $\Phi$ realizes its scalar polynomial; generation of $\Phi$ is a separate classical/circuit input.

**Output.** The procedure returns the finite unitary sequence below and uses its compression from $H_R=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_R)$ to $H_L=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_L)$ for odd $d$, or from $H_R$ to itself for even $d$. No measurement or state-preparation circuit is implicit in this block description.

**Instructions.** For $d\ge0$, set the current side to $R$ and apply the projector phase $e^{i\phi_d(2\Pi_R-I)}$. For $j=d-1,d-2,\ldots,0$, apply $U$ and switch the current side from $R$ to $L$ if it is $R$; otherwise apply $U^*$ and switch from $L$ to $R$. Then apply $e^{i\phi_j(2\Pi_{\mathrm{current}}-I)}$. Thus there are $d$ alternating signal calls and $d+1$ projector-phase operations; $d=0$ has no signal call and consists only of the phase at $\Pi_R$.

For a real target polynomial, run the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ in coherent control branches, with the control initialized in $|+\rangle$, and take the $|+\rangle$-to-$|+\rangle$ block. The procedure uses the reflected signal convention $W_R$ throughout. If a circuit is built through the alternative SU(2) convention, its control-dependent scalar phase must be retained as a relative phase. The exact block action, the real-part extraction, and the implementation costs are established in the separate theorem items on this page. Every phase list, inverse call, controlled call, phase rotation, and finite-gate compilation is supplied or charged separately.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

derivations.claim: By [F1], choose a QSP-admissible pair $P,Q$ with $\operatorname{Re}P=p$. By [F2], choose a phase list $\Phi$ whose ordered signal product has upper-left entry $P_\Phi=P$. The real part identity is therefore exact for every real $x$.

Let control value $0$ select $\Phi$ and value $1$ select $-\Phi$. In each slot with phase $\phi$ about $\Pi$, apply the toggle $X_\Pi$ from [F5], then unconditional $R_z(2\phi)$, then a control-one-controlled $R_z(-4\phi)$, and then $X_\Pi$ again. In branch $0$ the middle rotation is $R_z(2\phi)$; in branch $1$ it is $R_z(-2\phi)$. The toggle places the clean ancilla in $|1\rangle$ on $\operatorname{ran}\Pi$ and in $|0\rangle$ on $\ker\Pi$, so the two system phases are $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ and $e^{-i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$, respectively, with the ancilla returned to $|0\rangle$. Thus each slot realizes the required $\Phi/-\Phi$ phase pair. By [F6] and [F10], the signal calls between slots are shared unconditioned calls, and the full controlled unitary has branch operators $U_\Phi$ and $U_{-\Phi}$. Projecting $|+\rangle$ to $|+\rangle$ gives their arithmetic mean, since $\langle+|b\rangle\langle b|+\rangle=1/2$ for each $b\in\{0,1\}$.

Since each entry of $W_R(x)$ is real and $\overline{Z(\phi)}=Z(-\phi)$, entrywise conjugation of the ordered product in [F3] gives $U_{-\Phi}(x)=\overline{U_\Phi(x)}$. Thus its upper-left polynomial is $P_{-\Phi}(x)=\overline{P_\Phi(x)}$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$.

Fix a positive singular pair $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$. By [F4], the two branch compressions contribute coefficients $P_\Phi(\sigma_j)$ and $P_{-\Phi}(\sigma_j)$. Their mean is $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)=p(\sigma_j)$ by steps 1.1–2.1. For even $d$, [F4] gives the same mean $p(0)$ on each vector in $\ker A$; for odd $d$, $p(0)=0$ and the output block annihilates that kernel. Thus the averaged compression has exactly the stated singular-value transform on all of $H_R$.

There are $d$ alternating signal positions and $d+1$ phase slots by [F7]. The signal list is unconditioned and shared. At each slot, the two toggles use two controlled-reflection calls, and the middle uses one unconditional $R_z(2\phi)$ plus one branch-controlled $R_z(-4\phi)$. By [F9], the controlled rotations and reflection calls are supplied and costed separately. For $d=0$, there is one paired phase slot and no signal call, so the same count applies.

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular-value decomposition $A=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|$. Let $p:[-1,1]\to\mathbb C$ be a scalar function.

If $p$ is **odd**, define the odd singular-value transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A):H_R\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|.$$

If $p$ is **even**, define its right-space transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A):H_R\to H_R,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A},$$

where $\Pi_{\ker A}$ is the orthogonal projection in $H_R$ onto $\ker A$. The left-space version is

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A):H_L\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A^*}.$$

The odd transform annihilates the right kernel because oddness gives $p(0)=0$; the even transforms use the canonical kernel projections. The resulting operators are independent of the chosen SVD by [[lem-qa-24-singular-transform-basis-independence]].

Let $A,B:H_R\to H_L$ be contractions between the same finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces, let $P$ be the scalar polynomial of an exact degree-$d$ QSVT phase sequence, and put $\delta=\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Then, for the corresponding odd or even singular-value transforms,

$$\|P^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)-P^{\mathrm{SV}}(B)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4d\sqrt{\delta}.$$

For $d=0$ the transform is constant on the relevant singular space and the difference is zero. The lemma is an operator statement; the unitary completions used in the proof are finite-dimensional existence constructions and do not supply an efficient implementation or any additional query access.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ is zero or has degree at most $d$, has parity $d\bmod2$, and satisfies $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $U:H\to H$ be unitary, and let $\Pi_R,\Pi_L:H\to H$ be orthogonal projections. Write $H_R=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_R)$ and $H_L=\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_L)$. The **projected-unitary encoding** (PUE) of this data is the linear map

$$A:H_R\to H_L,\qquad Ax=\Pi_L Ux.$$

Equivalently, its ambient-space compression is $\Pi_LU\Pi_R$, restricted to $H_R$ and regarded as taking values in $H_L$. The map $A$ is a contraction: $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1$.

Put $n=\dim H_R$, $m=\dim H_L$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. A singular-value decomposition consists of orthonormal bases $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $H_R$ and $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ of $H_L$, and positive singular values $1\ge\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$, such that

$$A=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|.$$

The remaining right basis vectors span $\ker A$ and the remaining left basis vectors span $\ker A^*$. Empty bases and sums are allowed when a dimension or the rank is zero. The pairing in each rank-one map is the root-linear-first Dirac conversion of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]].

An exact square block encoding is a special case: identify the system with the all-zero ancilla subspace and take $\Pi_L=\Pi_R$ equal to that subspace. Under the injection $J_a$ of [[def-qa-22-block-encoding]], the compression is $J_a^*UJ_a$; an exact $(\alpha,a,0)$ block encoding has compressed block $A/\alpha$.

A linear map $T:V\to W$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) is a **linear isometry** if

$$\lVert Tv\rVert=\lVert v\rVert$$

for every $v\in V$, where the norm is the induced norm [[def-inner-product-norm]]. An invertible linear isometry from a real finite-dimensional inner product space to itself is an **orthogonal operator**; over $\mathbb C$ it is a **unitary operator**.

Equivalently, once the finite-dimensional characterisation is proved, orthogonal and unitary operators are the endomorphisms satisfying $T^*T=TT^*=I$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner product spaces,

$$(S+T)^*=S^*+T^*,\qquad (\lambda T)^*=\overline\lambda T^*,\qquad (ST)^*=T^*S^*,\qquad T^{**}=T.$$

Also $I^*=I$ and $0^*=0$.

Let $W$ be a subspace of a finite-dimensional inner product space $V$. The orthogonal-decomposition theorem ([[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]]) gives

$$V=W\oplus W^\perp$$

and associates to every $v\in V$ unique vectors $w\in W$ and $z\in W^\perp$ with $v=w+z$. The **orthogonal projection onto $W$** is the function

$$P_W:V\longrightarrow W,\qquad P_Wv=w.$$

Equivalently, $P_Wv$ is the unique vector of $W$ such that $v-P_Wv\in W^\perp$.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_n$ be pairwise orthogonal vectors in a real or complex inner-product space, that is $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle=0$ whenever $i\ne j$ ([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). Then

$$\Bigl\|\sum_{j=1}^{n}x_j\Bigr\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\|x_j\|^2 ,$$

the empty sum on the right being $0$ at $n=0$.

derivations.claim: Let $E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out}$ be the declared isometric padding maps in [F1], so $\widehat A=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^*$ and $E_{\rm in}^*E_{\rm in}=I$. The adjoint identity [L3] then yields $\|E_{\rm in}^*z\|^2=\langle P_{\rm in}z,z\rangle=\|P_{\rm in}z\|^2\le\|z\|^2$. Since both padding maps preserve norms by [L2], [F9] gives $\|\widehat A\|_{\rm op}=\|E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^*\|_{\rm op}\le\|A\|_{\rm op}$; conversely $\widehat A E_{\rm in}x=E_{\rm out}Ax$ for every $x$, so taking maxima over unit vectors gives equality. Thus $A_0:=\widehat A/\alpha$ is a contraction. The PUE compression $B$ is a contraction by [L1], and [F1] gives $\|B-A_0\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon_{\rm BE}$. Applying [F3] gives $\|P^{\mathrm{SV}}(B)-P^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)\|_{\rm op}\le4d\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\rm BE}}$.

Choose the SVD bases of $A_0$ from [F8]. For odd parity, the difference $P^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)-f^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)$ sends each right singular vector $v_j$ to $(P(\sigma_j)-f(\sigma_j))u_j$ and annihilates $\ker A_0$. Orthonormality gives, for $x=\sum_j c_jv_j+x_0$, $\|(P^{\mathrm{SV}}-f^{\mathrm{SV}})x\|^2=\sum_j|P(\sigma_j)-f(\sigma_j)|^2|c_j|^2\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}^2\|x\|^2$. For even parity the same bound follows by diagonal action on the right singular basis, including $P(0)-f(0)$ on the kernel. Taking the maximum over unit vectors by [F6] yields $\|P^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)-f^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}$.

Replace the ideal phase operations one slot at a time by their implemented unitaries. The product difference is a sum of $d+1$ terms, each containing one phase difference and otherwise unitary factors. By [F9], multiplying by those unitary factors preserves or bounds the operator norm by their norm $1$; [F7] and [F6] then give $\|\widetilde U_\Phi-U_\Phi\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\sum_\ell\zeta_\ell$. Compression by the input and output projections is contractive, so the same upper bound holds for the compressed blocks. The exact ideal compressed block is $P^{\mathrm{SV}}(B)$ by [F10].

The implemented block differs from $f^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)$ by the sum of its phase-implementation, input-block, and scalar-approximation differences. Applying the triangle inequality to steps 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3 yields $\|\widetilde B-f^{\mathrm{SV}}(A_0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}+4d\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}}+\sum_\ell\zeta_\ell$. Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular-value decomposition $A=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|$. Let $p:[-1,1]\to\mathbb C$ be a scalar function.

If $p$ is **odd**, define the odd singular-value transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A):H_R\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|.$$

If $p$ is **even**, define its right-space transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A):H_R\to H_R,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A},$$

where $\Pi_{\ker A}$ is the orthogonal projection in $H_R$ onto $\ker A$. The left-space version is

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A):H_L\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A^*}.$$

The odd transform annihilates the right kernel because oddness gives $p(0)=0$; the even transforms use the canonical kernel projections. The resulting operators are independent of the chosen SVD by [[lem-qa-24-singular-transform-basis-independence]].

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

derivations.claim: For $A=0$, the entire domain and codomain are zero-singular spaces; both $u=1$ and $u=-1$ are unit left-kernel vectors, and $v=1$ is a unit right-kernel vector. With the first pairing, $|1\rangle\langle1|$ sends $x$ to $x$, so the false zero-pair sum with coefficient $f(0)=1$ is $I$.

The valid odd definition avoids the defect because odd polynomials have $f(0)=0$ and the sum contains only positive singular values; the valid even definition adds $f(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=I$, which is canonical and unchanged by the choice of kernel basis.

Direct multiplication gives $U_\sigma^*U_\sigma=U_\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma^2+s^2&\sigma s-\sigma s\\\sigma s-\sigma s&s^2+\sigma^2\end{pmatrix}=I$, so $U_\sigma$ is unitary. derivations.claim: Put $A=V-W$, and let $(r_j)$ be an orthonormal basis of $R$. By [F1], diagonalizing $A^*A$ in a right singular basis shows that $(A\otimes I_R)^*(A\otimes I_R)=A^*A\otimes I_R$ has the same largest eigenvalue as $A^*A$: its eigenvectors are the products of right singular vectors of $A$ with the $r_j$, and its eigenvalues are the corresponding squared singular values. Therefore $\|V_R-W_R\|_{\rm op}=\|A\otimes I_R\|_{\rm op}=\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\delta$. For every unit vector $\psi\in H\otimes R$, the vectors $a=V_R\psi$ and $b=W_R\psi$ have norm one and satisfy $\|a-b\|\le\delta$.

For $Z=V_R\rho V_R^*$, positivity follows from $y^*Zy=(V_R^*y)^*\rho(V_R^*y)\ge0$ for every $y$; the same holds with $W_R$. For a vector $z\in K\otimes R$, the entry-sum formula gives $z^*(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)Zz=\sum_e (I_K\otimes|e\rangle\otimes I_R\,z)^*Z(I_K\otimes|e\rangle\otimes I_R\,z)\ge0$, and likewise for $W_R$; hence both reduced outputs are positive. That formula also gives $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)Z)=\operatorname{tr}Z$. Since $V_R^*V_R=W_R^*W_R=I$, cyclicity of finite matrix trace gives $\operatorname{tr}Z=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ for both outputs. Thus $\rho_V,\rho_W$ are density matrices.

In an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{span}\{a,b\}$, write $b=za+s e_2$, where $z=a^*b$, $s=\sqrt{1-|z|^2}$, and $e_2\perp a$ is unit if $s>0$. The matrix of $aa^*-bb^*$ on this span is Hermitian, has trace zero and determinant $-s^2$, so its eigenvalues are $s,-s$; outside the span it is zero. Thus $\tfrac12\|aa^*-bb^*\|_1=s$. Also $s^2=1-|z|^2\le2-2\operatorname{Re}z=\|a-b\|^2$, because the difference of the right side and left side is $|1-z|^2$. This proves $D(aa^*,bb^*)\le\delta$ for every pure input, including $s=0$.

Let $X$ be Hermitian on $K\otimes E\otimes R$, and set $Y=(\operatorname{Tr}_E\otimes I_R)X$. For a matrix $B$ on $K\otimes R$, define $\widetilde B$ on $K\otimes E\otimes R$ by applying $B$ to the $K,R$ coordinates and leaving the $E$ coordinate fixed. The entry-sum definition of partial trace gives $\operatorname{tr}(B^*Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde B^*X)$. Reordering the product basis from $K,E,R$ to $K,R,E$ conjugates $\widetilde B$ to $B\otimes I_E$, so $\|\widetilde B\|_{\rm op}=\|B\|_{\rm op}$ by the same singular-basis argument as in step 1.1. For any square matrix $X=U\Sigma V^*$, [F1] gives its singular value decomposition, and $|\operatorname{tr}(C^*X)|=|\operatorname{tr}(V^*C^*U\Sigma)|\le\|C\|_{\rm op}\sum_j\Sigma_{jj}=\|C\|_{\rm op}\|X\|_1,$ since every diagonal entry of a contraction has modulus at most one. Taking the supremum over $\|B\|_{\rm op}\le1$, and using the equality case $B=U_YV_Y^*$ in a singular value decomposition of $Y$, proves $\|Y\|_1\le\|X\|_1$. This dual formula also gives the triangle inequality and homogeneity for $\|\cdot\|_1$ by applying it to a sum and scalar multiple.

For a pure input $\rho=\psi\psi^*$, step 2.1 bounds the trace distance before discarding $E$, and step 2.2 shows the partial trace cannot increase the trace norm of the Hermitian difference. Hence the reduced output distance is at most $\delta$. For general positive trace-one $\rho$, [F2] gives a spectral decomposition $\rho=\sum_j p_j\psi_j\psi_j^*$ with $p_j\ge0$ and $\sum_jp_j=1$. The maps and partial trace are linear; the triangle inequality and homogeneity from step 2.2 therefore bound the reduced output distance by $\sum_jp_j\delta=\delta$.

In this page a **Hamiltonian** is a self-adjoint endomorphism $H$ of a
finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $V$; no physical postulate is
part of the term. Let $\sigma(H)$ be the set of its distinct eigenvalues and
let $P_\lambda$ be the orthogonal projection onto the $\lambda$-eigenspace.
For real time $t$, define the finite matrix evolution

$$U_H(t):=\sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(H)}e^{-it\lambda}P_\lambda = f_t(H),\qquad f_t(\lambda)=e^{-it\lambda}.$$

The second expression uses the finite spectral functional calculus
[[def-functional-calculus-for-a-normal-endomorphism]]. If $V$ is the zero
space, the spectrum is empty and the empty sum is the unique endomorphism,
which is also the identity on $V$. This definition specifies a mathematical
unitary from a finite matrix; it makes no claim that the operation has an
efficient circuit or a free access cost.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$. For real $x$, the complex value $\exp(x+0i)$ equals the published real exponential $e^x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]], [[lem-cauchy-product-of-absolutely-convergent-complex-series]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[lem-binomial-theorem-over-complex-numbers]], [[thm-binomial-closed-formula]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

derivations.claim: The map $V_x$ permutes the finite orthonormal basis and satisfies $V_x^2=I$, so it is unitary. In a term indexed by $i,b$, the endpoints become $|i-1,b\oplus p_{i-1}\rangle$ and $|i,b\oplus x_i\oplus p_i\rangle$. Since $p_i=p_{i-1}\oplus x_i$, the second bit is $b\oplus p_{i-1}$; the edge is therefore an ordinary adjacent path edge with the spectator bit unchanged. Thus $V_xH_xV_x$ is two identical path matrices $H_0$, one for each bit $b$, and $V_x$ fixes $|0,0\rangle$ while sending $|n,0\rangle$ to $|n,p_n\rangle$.

Let $|D_i^n\rangle$ be the normalized uniform superposition of $n$-bit strings of Hamming weight $i$, and set $|D_{-1}^n\rangle=|D_{n+1}^n\rangle=0$. Counting the $i$ downward flips and $n-i$ upward flips gives $J|D_i^n\rangle=\tfrac12\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}|D_{i-1}^n\rangle+\tfrac12\sqrt{(i+1)(n-i)}|D_{i+1}^n\rangle$ for every $0\le i\le n$. Thus $(2/n)J$ has the stated path weights on the symmetric subspace.

Each Pauli $X_r$ has eigenvalues $\pm1$, so [F2] gives $\|X_r\|_{\rm op}=1$. The triangle inequality then gives $\|J\|_{\rm op}\le n/2$, so $\|H_0\|_{\rm op}\le1$; unitary conjugation in step 1.1 gives $\|H_x\|_{\rm op}\le1$.

For each sign string $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n$, put $u_\sigma=2^{-n/2}\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}(\prod_r\sigma_r^{y_r})|y\rangle$. Factorizing the finite inner-product sum gives $\langle u_\sigma,u_\tau\rangle=2^{-n}\prod_r(1+\sigma_r\tau_r)$, so these $2^n$ vectors form an orthonormal basis. Flipping bit $r$ gives $X_ru_\sigma=\sigma_ru_\sigma$. By [F1]–[F2], $e^{-i(\pi/2)\sum_rX_r}$ acts on $u_\sigma$ by $\exp(-i\pi\sum_r\sigma_r/2)$. The scalar addition law in [F1] factors this as $\prod_r\exp(-i\pi\sigma_r/2)$, and Euler's formula [F3] gives each factor as $-i\sigma_r$. Hence $e^{-i(\pi/2)\sum_rX_r}=(-i)^nX_1\cdots X_n$. This maps $|D_0^n\rangle=|0^n\rangle$ to $(-i)^n|D_n^n\rangle=(-i)^n|1^n\rangle$. The path basis identifies $|D_0^n\rangle,|D_n^n\rangle$ with $|0\rangle,|n\rangle$; step 1.1 then sends the endpoint to $|n,p_n\rangle$. Since $H_0=(2/n)J$, evolution for $t=\pi n/2$ is $e^{-itH_0}=e^{-i\pi J}$, which is the transfer established above.

citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$. For every $0<\sigma_j<1$, set

$$w_j=\frac{(I-\Pi_R)U^*u_j}{\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}},\qquad \widetilde w_j=\frac{(I-\Pi_L)Uv_j}{\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}}.$$

The vectors $w_j$ form an orthonormal family in $\ker\Pi_R$ and the vectors $\widetilde w_j$ form an orthonormal family in $\ker\Pi_L$. In the input basis $(v_j,w_j)$ and output basis $(u_j,\widetilde w_j)$,

$$U\big|_{\operatorname{span}(v_j,w_j)}=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_j&\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}\\\sqrt{1-\sigma_j^2}&-\sigma_j\end{pmatrix}.$$

For $\sigma_j=1$, $Uv_j=u_j$ and the complementary vector is absent. A right zero-singular vector $v\in\ker A\cap H_R$ satisfies $Uv\in\ker\Pi_L$; a left zero-singular vector $u\in\ker A^*\cap H_L$ satisfies $U^*u\in\ker\Pi_R$. Let $M_R$ be the orthogonal sum of all positive-singular input planes or lines, $\ker A$, and $U^*(\ker A^*)$; let $M_L$ be the corresponding sum of positive-singular output planes or lines, $U(\ker A)$, and $\ker A^*$. Then $U(M_R)=M_L$. The residual ambient subspaces $M_R^\perp$ and $M_L^\perp$ lie in $\ker\Pi_R$ and $\ker\Pi_L$, and $U(M_R^\perp)=M_L^\perp$. Thus each named block is invariant under its corresponding projector, with no implicit pairing of the two kernels.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

derivations.claim: Fix an eigenvector $\psi_j$ with unit norm and write $v_j=J\psi_j$. From [F1], $\Pi Uv_j=x_jv_j$ and $\Pi U^*v_j=x_jv_j$, because $K=K^*$. Since $U,U^*$ preserve norm, orthogonal decomposition by $\Pi$ gives $\|(I-\Pi)Uv_j\|^2=\|(I-\Pi)U^*v_j\|^2=1-x_j^2=s_j^2$. For $|x_j|<1$, the displayed $\eta_j,\widetilde\eta_j$ are therefore unit vectors in $\ker\Pi$.

If $i\ne j$, orthogonality of eigenvectors and [F4] give $\langle Uv_i,Uv_j\rangle=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=0$, while $\langle\Pi Uv_i,\Pi Uv_j\rangle=x_ix_j\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=0$. Subtracting the projected components shows $\langle\eta_i,\eta_j\rangle=0$; the same calculation for $U^*$ proves orthogonality of the $\widetilde\eta_j$.

Decomposing $Uv_j$ into its $\Pi$ and $I-\Pi$ parts gives $Uv_j=x_jv_j+s_j\eta_j$. Also $s_jU\widetilde\eta_j=U(I-\Pi)U^*v_j=v_j-U\Pi U^*v_j=v_j-x_jUv_j=s_j^2v_j-x_js_j\eta_j.$ Division by $s_j>0$ yields $U\widetilde\eta_j=s_jv_j-x_j\eta_j$, which is the second column of the displayed matrix. Taking adjoints gives the reverse-basis action of $U^*$.

If $|x_j|=1$, the orthogonal complement of $\Pi Uv_j=x_jv_j$ has squared norm $1-|x_j|^2=0$, so $Uv_j=x_jv_j$; the same argument for $U^*$ gives $U^*v_j=x_jv_j$. Thus the endpoint plane collapses. At $x_j=0$, step 1.1 has $s_j=1$, so both normalized vectors are well-defined. The mutually orthogonal paired spaces and endpoint lines exhaust the clean input and output signal spaces by the SVD decomposition in [F2]; their orthogonal residual complements stay in $\ker\Pi$ and cannot contribute to the clean compression.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

Let $(U,J,\alpha)$ be an exact Hermitian block encoding from [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $K\psi_j=\lambda_j\psi_j$. Put $x_j=\lambda_j/\alpha$ and $s_j=\sqrt{1-x_j^2}$. For $|x_j|<1$, define
$$\eta_j=(I-\Pi)UJ\psi_j/s_j,\qquad \widetilde\eta_j=(I-\Pi)U^*J\psi_j/s_j.$$
The $\eta_j$ are orthonormal in $\ker\Pi$, as are the $\widetilde\eta_j$. In the paired input basis $(J\psi_j,\widetilde\eta_j)$ and output basis $(J\psi_j,\eta_j)$, $U$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}x_j&s_j\\s_j&-x_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
The unitary $U^*$ maps in the reverse direction by the same matrix. If $|x_j|=1$, the complement is absent and $UJ\psi_j=x_jJ\psi_j=U^*J\psi_j$; no division by zero is used. The value $x_j=0$ is an ordinary two-dimensional signal plane.

Let $x\in[-1,1]$, put $s(x)=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ using the nonnegative real square root, and define the Hermitian-reflection signal matrix
$$W_R(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x&s(x)\\s(x)&-x\end{pmatrix}.$$
For each real $\phi$, define $Z(\phi)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\phi},e^{-i\phi})$. For an integer $d\ge0$ and real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$, the length-$d$ QSP sequence is the ordered matrix product
$$U_\Phi(x)=Z(\phi_0)\prod_{j=1}^{d}\bigl(W_R(x)Z(\phi_j)\bigr),$$
where the product is written left to right in increasing $j$ and matrix multiplication acts right to left. For $d=0$ this is $Z(\phi_0)$. This definition fixes the sign of the off-diagonal signal entry, both endpoint phases, and the product order.

The phases are in matrix order: when the factors are applied as chronological circuit layers, the rightmost factor acts first, in accordance with [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. In the ordered signal basis, if both coordinates are nonzero, applying $Z(\phi)$ multiplies the ratio of the second coordinate to the first by $e^{-2i\phi}$; if either coordinate is zero, that relative phase is undefined, while the displayed matrix action remains defined. This is the relative phase convention fixed by [[def-qc-relative-phase]].

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ is zero or has degree at most $d$, has parity $d\bmod2$, and satisfies $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

For every integer $d\ge0$, a pair $P,Q\in\mathbb C[x]$ is QSP-admissible of degree bound $d$ if and only if there is a real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ such that
$$U_\Phi(x)=\begin{pmatrix}P(x)&s(x)Q(x)\\(-1)^{d+1}s(x)Q^*(x)&(-1)^dP^*(x)\end{pmatrix}\quad (x\in[-1,1]).$$
The converse is constructive: a leading-coefficient phase peel reduces the degree at each nonconstant stage. The polynomial identity, determinant signs, product order, and phase convention are exactly those in [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]] and [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]].

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and let $\Pi$ be an orthogonal projection. The operators $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$ and $S_\Pi=I-2\Pi$ are self-adjoint unitary involutions, with $R_\Pi=-S_\Pi$. On $\operatorname{ran}\Pi$ they act as $+I$ and $-I$, respectively; on $\ker\Pi$ they act as $-I$ and $+I$. In control-first order,

$$C(S_\Pi)=(Z_C)C(R_\Pi),\qquad Z_C:=\operatorname{diag}(I_H,-I_H)=Z\otimes I_H.$$

Put $s=\sqrt{1-x^2}$, $W_R=\begin{pmatrix}x&s\\s&-x\end{pmatrix}$, $W_S=\begin{pmatrix}x&is\\is&x\end{pmatrix}$, and $C=Z(\pi/4)$. Then
$$CW_RC=iW_S^\dagger,\qquad W_S^\dagger=Z(\pi/2)W_SZ(-\pi/2).$$
For $d\ge1$, define $U_S(\Psi)=Z(\psi_0)\prod_{j=1}^d(W_SZ(\psi_j))$. If $\Psi$ is the SU(2)-convention phase list with $\psi_0=\phi_0+\pi/4$, $\psi_j=\phi_j-\pi/2$ for $1\le j<d$, and $\psi_d=\phi_d-3\pi/4$, then
$$U_R(\Phi)=i^dU_S(\Psi).$$
The affine phase-list map is invertible. The scalar $i^d$ is part of the identity: in a control-first block $\operatorname{diag}(I,U)$ it acts on the active control branch and cannot be discarded as a global phase.

derivations.claim: In control-first order, $F:=S\widetilde U=\begin{pmatrix}0&U^*\\U&0\end{pmatrix},$ so $F^*=F$ and $F^2=I$. Also $J'^*FJ'=\tfrac12(J^*U^*J+J^*UJ)=K/\alpha$ because $J^*UJ=K/\alpha$ is self-adjoint. For a unit eigenvector $K\psi_\lambda=\lambda\psi_\lambda$, put $g_\lambda=J'\psi_\lambda$, $x=\lambda/\alpha$, and $s=\sqrt{1-x^2}$. A **promise problem** is a pair $(Y,N)$ of disjoint subsets of $\{0,1\}^*$. Its promise is $Y\cup N$. A deterministic solver must accept every word of $Y$ and reject every word of $N$, with either answer allowed elsewhere. The pair belongs to $\mathrm{PromiseP}$ if such a solver has a polynomial time bound on every input.

It belongs to $\mathrm{PromiseNP}$ if there are a polynomial $p$ and a deterministic polynomial-time predicate $V(x,w)$ such that every $x\in Y$ has some $w$ with $|w|\le p(|x|)$ and $V(x,w)=1$, whereas for every $x\in N$ every such $w$ has $V(x,w)=0$. The promise need not be decidable; either side or both sides may be empty. When $Y\cup N=\{0,1\}^*$, this is the ordinary language decision convention.

A **full-list uniform quantum circuit family** is a sequence $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ together with one fixed deterministic one-tape Turing machine $G$ and constants $c\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that, on input the unary word $1^n$, $G$ halts within $c(n+1)^k$ transitions and its final tape is a valid self-delimiting binary description of the entire circuit $C_n$. The machine output convention is that of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]] and [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and running time is as in [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

The following fixed-order code makes the full circuit and its designated input/output wires effective. A unary natural $r\in\mathbb N$ is written $1^r0$, including the one-symbol code $0$ for $r=0$. A self-delimiting binary natural $r$ is written $1^{|\operatorname{bin}(r)|}0\operatorname{bin}(r)$, where $\operatorname{bin}(r)$ is its ordinary binary numeral with no leading zeros and $\operatorname{bin}(0)=0$. The header gives the input-wire count $n$ and total wire count $m$ in unary, followed by the gate count $g$ as a self-delimiting natural; validity requires $m\ge n$.

Each gate record consists of a two-bit label ($00,01,10,11$ for $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ respectively), followed by one self-delimiting wire index for $H,T,T^\dagger$ and two ordered self-delimiting indices for CNOT. Every index is less than $m$; CNOT indices are distinct, with the first the control and the second the target. The list contains exactly $g$ records. After the gate list, an output-count self-delimiting natural is followed by that many ordered, pairwise distinct wire indices, each less than $m$. Parsing rejects every other label, malformed or out-of-range index, repeated output index, truncated field, or trailing bit. This defines a total decoder by returning a fixed malformed-code symbol on any invalid word; effective binary encodings and total decoders are as in [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]].

The gate labels and matrices are the fixed finite library $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ of [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]], with entries in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$; CNOT is control-first. The remaining $m-n$ wires are auxiliary wires; their initial states are determined when a family is used in a computation model. This family convention adopts full-list generation. It makes no equivalence claim with indexed-gate uniformity and, in particular, does not assert that an indexed-gate generator can be expanded to the full list in polynomial time.

Let $n,m\ge0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be a total Boolean function on ordered bit strings. Its coherent XOR oracle is the linear extension of
$$
O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. The declared access contract states how many invocations count as queries and whether a controlled invocation is supplied. A query to this declared black box is counted separately from elementary gate size, depth, and width.

If $f$ is supplied instead by an explicit Boolean circuit, implementing $O_f$ means compiling that circuit and paying its reversible elementary-gate and workspace costs; the function description alone is not a free query. For this XOR oracle, its inverse is the same map, as proved in [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Controlled access remains a separate capability unless the contract explicitly provides it.

For every total Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$, including noninjective functions, the coherent XOR oracle $O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle$ is unitary and satisfies $O_f^2=I$. Hence $O_f^{-1}=O_f$.

derivations.claim: Put $z_i=(-1)^{x_i}\in\{-1,1\}$. On a basis query address $i$, the matrix entries of the XOR target flip are either $(1+z_i)/2$ or $(1-z_i)/2$; the input address and all other bits are unchanged. Thus one oracle call raises the degree of every amplitude polynomial in $z_1,\ldots,z_n$ by at most one. The inter-query unitaries are input-independent by [F2] and take fixed linear combinations of amplitudes. Induction over the $q$ queries shows each final amplitude is a multilinear polynomial of degree at most $q$, replacing any $z_i^2$ by $1$ without increasing degree.

The signed output expectation $p(z)=\Pr[y=0]-\Pr[y=1]$ is a sum of squared moduli of final amplitudes with fixed signs, so it is a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $2q$. If $\chi(z)=\prod_{i=1}^nz_i=(-1)^{\operatorname{parity}(x)}$, the error bound gives $\chi(z)p(z)\ge 1/3$ pointwise. Therefore the uniform average of $\chi p$ is positive.

If $2q<n$, every monomial of $p$ is $z_S=\prod_{i\in S}z_i$ for a proper subset $S\subsetneq[n]$. Under independent uniform signs, $\mathbb E[\chi z_S]=\mathbb E[\prod_{i\notin S}z_i]=0$, since at least one independent sign appears to the first power and has mean zero. Linearity gives $\mathbb E[\chi p]=0$, contradicting step 2.1. Hence $2q\ge n$.

derivations.claim: The maximum weight satisfies $1/2\le \max_iw_i\le1$: $i(n+1-i)\le(n+1)^2/4\le n^2$ gives the upper bound, and a central integer $i$ has $i(n+1-i)\ge n^2/4$ for the lower bound. Every edge satisfies $i(n+1-i)-n=(i-1)(n-i)\ge0$, so $w_i\ge w_1=1/\sqrt n>\eta$. The grid spacing $2^{-b}\le1/(3\pi n)=2\eta$, hence nearest rounding gives $|q_i-w_i|\le\eta$ and $q_i>0$; the support is unchanged. It follows that each row and column of $E_x=\widetilde H_x-H_x$ has at most two nonzero entries, each of magnitude at most $\eta$, and $2/9<\max_iq_i<2$; in particular $2\max_iq_i$ is bounded above and below by positive constants independent of $n,x$.

Order path vertices lexicographically by $(i,b_0)$. A location query's predecessor slot, when present, uses only $x_i$, and its successor slot, when present, uses only $x_{i+1}$; their order is fixed by the path index. For an arbitrary candidate pair of vertices, the value query tests the single relevant edge bit and returns the known dyadic $q_i$ or zero. Each oracle function can thus be computed reversibly using one parity-bit query into scratch, an XOR into the requested target, and a second parity-bit query to erase scratch. The same construction controls the target XOR by any query-control bit, so each controlled or uncontrolled sparse-oracle call costs at most two calls to the parity-bit oracle. The x-independent $q_i$ table is generated by integer arithmetic: binary search finds the nearest grid point by comparing squared integers with $2^{2b}i(n+1-i)/n^2$, using $O(\log(n+1))$-bit numbers and polynomially many steps in $n$. The location and value encodings are total, including sentinels, and this x-independent arithmetic is part of the fixed inter-query circuit.

For any vector $v$, Cauchy–Schwarz in each row gives $|(E_xv)_r|^2\le\Big(\sum_c|(E_x)_{rc}|\Big)\Big(\sum_c|(E_x)_{rc}||v_c|^2\Big).$ Summing over $r$, each row sum and each column sum of $|E_x|$ is at most $2\eta$. Hence $\|E_xv\|^2\le(2\eta)(2\eta)\|v\|^2$, proving $\|\widetilde H_x-H_x\|_{\rm op}\le2\eta$.

For $0\le s\le t$, differentiate $G(s)=e^{-i(t-s)\widetilde H_x}e^{-isH_x}$. By [F3], $G'(s)=i e^{-i(t-s)\widetilde H_x}(\widetilde H_x-H_x)e^{-isH_x}.$ The two outside factors are unitary, so [F4] gives $\|G'(s)\|_{\rm op}\le\|\widetilde H_x-H_x\|_{\rm op}$. Integrating from $0$ to $t$ and using step 2.1 yields $\|e^{-it\widetilde H_x}-e^{-itH_x}\|_{\rm op}\le t(2\eta)=\pi n\eta=\tfrac16.$

Apply the assumed simulator to the initial state $|0,0\rangle$ with clean work registers. The triangle inequality, step 3.1, and [F2] show that its output vector is within $1/3+1/6=1/2$ of $J_{\rm out}(-i)^n|n,\operatorname{parity}(x)\rangle$. The orthogonal projection onto outcomes whose second path bit is not $\operatorname{parity}(x)$ annihilates this target vector. Its norm on the simulator output is therefore at most $1/2$, so measuring the path bit computes parity with error at most $1/4$. This is a valid bounded-error parity algorithm on every $x$.

Replacing each of the algorithm's $q$ sparse-oracle calls by this reversible simulation yields a parity algorithm using at most $2q$ bit queries and error at most $1/4\le1/3$. By [F7], $2q\ge n/2$, hence $q\ge n/4$. From step 1.1 the sparse normalization is $\Theta(1)$, and $t=\pi n/2$, so the lower bound is equivalently $\Omega(n)=\Omega(t)=\Omega(\alpha_{\rm sp}t)$ on this family.

Checked n=1, boundary rows, sentinels, exact dyadic generation, and constant upper/lower normalization. The bound concerns sparse oracles only; no arbitrary block-access lower bound or AC. No routed finding.
