**Input.** A finite $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian matrix $H$, with $d_H\ge1$. Put $h_{\max}=\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$ and supply a certified nonnegative entry bound $h\ge h_{\max}$. Supply exact row and column enumerations. Write their neighbor labels as $\rho(i,k)$ and $\kappa(j,k)$, including $d_H$ distinct labels per row or column: every nonzero entry occurs once, and padded labels are sentinels. Supply reversible in-place permutations whose action on every valid row/slot and column/slot basis state is
$$O_r|i,k\rangle=|i,\rho(i,k)\rangle,\qquad O_c|j,k\rangle=|\kappa(j,k),j\rangle,$$
with their full reversible extensions, inverses, and actual query and gate costs. These permutations are explicit inputs; the row/column lists alone do not imply them. Supply an exact unitary $D_{d_H}$ preparing $d_H^{-1/2}\sum_{k=1}^{d_H}|k\rangle$, its inverse, and their costs. A classical table is not a free state-preparation circuit. If $h=0$, then $H=0$; use one flag qubit and return $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ with normalization $1$, whose all-zero flag compression is $0=H$. Otherwise set $\alpha=d_Hh$ and supply a total reversible value-decoding query that writes a finite exact encoding of $h_{ij}=H_{ij}/h$ on valid pairs and $0$ on invalid or sentinel pairs, together with its inverse and any controlled forms used, with their costs. Classical matrix entries alone do not provide this coherent access.

**Instructions when $h>0$.** Put $\widehat H=H/h$, so every queried entry $h_{ij}=\widehat H_{ij}$ obeys $|h_{ij}|\le1$. On the paired row/column index registers define
$$V_L=O_r(I\otimes D_{d_H})\,\mathrm{SWAP},\qquad V_R=O_c(D_{d_H}\otimes I).$$
Let $U_L=I_{\rm flag}\otimes V_L$. Define $U_R$ by first applying $V_R$, then querying $h_{ij}$, applying to the flag
$$\begin{pmatrix} h_{ij}&-\sqrt{1-|h_{ij}|^2}\\ \sqrt{1-|h_{ij}|^2}&\overline{h_{ij}} \end{pmatrix},$$
and unquerying the value and arithmetic workspace. The square root is the nonnegative real root. Invalid sentinel pairs use $h_{ij}=0$. Return $U_L^*U_R$ with the all-zero auxiliary block designated as the encoded block. Every index, flag, value, state-preparation, inverse, controlled, arithmetic, and finite-precision operation is supplied or charged separately.

The supplied-permutation mode requires the in-place location permutations as explicit input. The total XOR row-location oracle of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]] does not itself supply an $O(1)$-query in-place permutation or its inverse. Any scan or inverse-location construction must be specified and charged before claiming such a sparse-oracle cost.

The block identity and its exact query accounting are proved in [[thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding-correctness]].

**Sorted-XOR specialization.** As an alternative input mode, supply the exact sorted XOR location/value interface of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], or the sorted distinct support-superset variant allowing listed zero entries in [[lem-qa-25-sorted-xor-sparse-access-isometries]], a certified positive bound $h\ge\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$, and the same separately charged uniform preparation and value/flag arithmetic. Execute the explicit compute-location, binary-search inverse, slot-erasure and row/column-overlap construction of [[lem-qa-25-sorted-xor-sparse-access-isometries]]. It pads the system to $M=2^{\lceil\log_2(N+d_H)\rceil}$ and returns a clean block encoding of $(H\oplus0)/(d_Hh)$, with normalization $\alpha=d_Hh$. The location workspace is exactly clean on every prepared slot state. Each encoding, actual adjoint or coherent controlled encoding costs $O(\log(d_H+1))$ original location calls and $O(1)$ value calls; its sorting assumption is part of this mode's input. If $\|H\|\le1$, choose $h=1$ without computing a maximum. Keep the one-sided value amplitude on $U_R$ exactly as above. The original supplied-permutation mode and its sharper call count remain available.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

Fix $N\ge1$, a sparsity bound $d\ge1$, an integer $b\ge1$, and an injective code $\mathrm{enc}:C\to\{0,1\}^b$ for a finite set $C\subset\mathbb C$ containing $0$ and closed under conjugation. Put $w=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ and $v=\lceil\log_2d\rceil$, identify $[N]$ with the first $N$ strings in $\{0,1\}^w$, and regard any remaining strings as invalid labels. A valid $w$-bit index is zero-extended to $w+1$ bits. Let $H=(H_{xy})_{x,y\in[N]}$ be Hermitian, have entries in $C$, and have at most $d$ nonzero entries in every row. For each valid row $x$, list its nonzero column indices in increasing order. Define the total location function $f_H(x,\ell)$ to be the $\ell$-th listed index for a valid slot $0\le\ell<d$ when that slot exists, and a distinguished sentinel otherwise. Invalid row labels and invalid slot labels also return the sentinel. Encode the sentinel by a fixed $(w+1)$-bit word outside the valid index codes. Define the total value function $g_H(x,y)$ to return $\mathrm{enc}(H_{xy})$ on valid labels and $\mathrm{enc}(0)$ on invalid labels. All label widths and codes are part of the finite input description.

The **row-location oracle** and **entry-value oracle** are the coherent XOR maps $O_{f_H}|x,\ell,z\rangle=|x,\ell,z\oplus f_H(x,\ell)\rangle$ and $O_{g_H}|x,y,z\rangle=|x,y,z\oplus g_H(x,y)\rangle$, where the output target has respectively $w+1$ and $b$ bits. The slot register has $v$ bits; all unused slot strings are invalid and use the sentinel. These are total Boolean-function oracles on every bitstring basis input. They are instances of [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]], whose justified-by supplier proves unitarity and involutivity for arbitrary total functions. Each named call and any separately granted controlled or inverse call is charged under [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. This exact-code model describes the decoded matrix $H$; approximating a different target matrix requires a separate bound on the matrix difference. Row and value access alone does not supply a term list or term-evolution circuits.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $K=K^*$ on $H$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\alpha$. Put $A=K/\alpha$. Let $U$ be a unitary on an ancilla-system space $H_A\otimes H$, let $J:H\to H_A\otimes H$ be the isometry $Jv=|0^a\rangle\otimes v$, and let $\Pi=JJ^*$. An **exact Hermitian block encoding** is the data $(U,J,\alpha)$ with $J^*UJ=A$. The matrix $K$ is Hermitian; $U$ itself need not be Hermitian.

The signal-register reflection is $R_\Pi=2\Pi-I$. The access record lists, separately, each supplied call to $U$, $U^*$, controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, and $R_\Pi$, together with their circuit, query, gate, width, ancilla, precision, and classical-generation costs from [[def-qa-22-block-encoding-access-model]] and [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. A state description or block matrix alone supplies none of these calls. A controlled reflection is also separate. Any PREPARE, SELECT, sparse-location, value, or coefficient operation used by a construction is a separately supplied, reversible interface with its inverse and cost recorded.

Here is the standard-form **qubiterate** for this access instance. Add a flag qubit and define $\widetilde U=|0\rangle\langle0|\otimes U+|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes U^*$, $J'v=|+\rangle\otimes Jv$, $S=X\otimes I$, $F=S\widetilde U$, and $W_{\mathrm q}=(2J'J'^*-I)F$. Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

Let $H$ have the exact sorted $d$-sparse Hermitian XOR-location/value interface of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], with $N,d\ge1$. An optional support-list variant is also admissible: each row lists at most $d$ distinct columns in strictly increasing order, contains every nonzero column exactly once, and may additionally list zero-valued columns. Its row and column support lists agree under transposition; in the Hermitian case the row list at $j$ supplies the column list at $j$. The total XOR value oracle gives the exact decoded matrix, including any listed zeros. Missing slots use the same distinguished sentinel. No zero test on the matrix values is needed to form a supplied support union. An approximation to a different target matrix requires a separate operator-error bound. Put $M=2^{\lceil\log_2(N+d)\rceil}$ and $\widetilde H=H\oplus0$ on the $M$-label register. Given a positive certified bound $h\ge\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$, an exact costed preparation $d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|l\rangle$, and costed exact value-decoding and flag-rotation arithmetic, one can construct a unitary whose clean block is $\widetilde H/(dh)$. It and its actual adjoint and coherent controlled versions use $O(\log(d+1))$ QA20 location calls and $O(1)$ value calls each. Index bits, reversible workspace, search arithmetic, comparisons, uniform preparation, flags and gate precision remain separately charged. In particular $h=1$ is admissible when $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le1$, without computing the global maximum entry. The stronger separately supplied in-place-location interface keeps its original constant location-call count.

derivations.claim: First consider the supplied-permutation mode. If $h=0$, the promised bound implies every entry of $H$ is zero. The returned $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ is unitary and its compression against the clean flag $|0\rangle$ is $\langle0|X|0\rangle I=0$, so normalization $1$ encodes $H=0$. Now suppose $h>0$. Each row and, by Hermiticity, each column has at most $d_H$ nonzero entries, each of magnitude at most $h$. For any vector $v$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|(Hv)_i|^2\le(\sum_j|H_{ij}|)(\sum_j|H_{ij}||v_j|^2)$. Summing over $i$ and using the row and column bounds gives $\|Hv\|^2\le(d_Hh)^2\|v\|^2$, so $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le d_Hh$ and the stated normalization is valid in [F3]. For each system label $i$, $V_L|0,i\rangle=d_H^{-1/2}\sum_{k=1}^{d_H}|i,\rho(i,k)\rangle$, where $\rho(i,k)$ is its listed column or a distinct sentinel. For each system label $j$, $V_R|0,j\rangle=d_H^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^{d_H}|\kappa(j,\ell),j\rangle$. Each is normalized because its $d_H$ terms are orthonormal and have coefficient $d_H^{-1/2}$.

For $|h|\le1$, the two columns of the stated flag matrix have unit norm and inner product $\overline h(-\sqrt{1-|h|^2})+\sqrt{1-|h|^2}\,\overline h=0$; hence it is unitary and its flag-zero output amplitude from $|0\rangle$ is $h$. The value oracle is uncomputed after this rotation, so the good-flag overlap retains no value workspace.

With the root inner product linear in its first argument, the $(i,j)$ matrix entry of $U_L^*U_R$ is $\langle U_R(|0\rangle\otimes|j\rangle),\,U_L(|0\rangle\otimes|i\rangle)\rangle_{\rm root}$, by the adjoint identity and the ordered-basis coordinate convention in [F5]. The row and column lists contain the pair $(i,j)$ once each exactly when $H_{ij}\ne0$, by Hermiticity and the nonzero-entry enumeration. In that case the unique matching basis pair contributes $d_H^{-1}h_{ij}=H_{ij}/(d_Hh)$: the $U_R$ amplitude is first in the root pairing and equals $h_{ij}/\sqrt{d_H}$, while the row-state amplitude is $1/\sqrt{d_H}$. If $H_{ij}=0$, there is no valid matching pair, and the sentinel branch has flag-zero amplitude $0$. Thus every clean matrix entry is the stated one, proving the compressed block identity.

The displayed circuit for $U_L^*U_R$ applies the inverse row-location permutation once through $V_L^*$, the column-location permutation once through $V_R$, and the entry-value oracle twice to compute and uncompute the value. Its state preparations, inverses, arithmetic, flag rotations, controlled operations, and gate synthesis are separate declared costs, so no additional sparse-access operation has been counted as free.

In the optional sorted-XOR mode, apply [F7] to the supplied sorted QA20 interface and positive entry bound $h$. Its clean isometries insert $H_{ij}/h$ only on the column side, give the padded block $(H\oplus0)/(d_Hh)$, and clear the extra location and value work exactly on the prepared input subspaces. Its actual inverses and coherent controls have the same logarithmic location-query order. The supplied-permutation proof and counts in steps 1.1–3.1 are unchanged.

For a finite Hermitian $H$ with exact block-encoding normalization $\alpha>0$, $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$, and real time $t$, put $\tau=\alpha t$. On $x\in[-1,1]$ the scalar target is $f_\tau(x)=\exp(-i\tau x)$; if $H\psi_\lambda=\lambda\psi_\lambda$, then $f_\tau(\lambda/\alpha)=\exp(-it\lambda)$, the eigenvalue of the finite matrix evolution [[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]].

For $k\ge0$, define the Chebyshev polynomials by $T_0(x)=1$, $T_1(x)=x$, $T_{k+1}(x)=2xT_k(x)-T_{k-1}(x)$. Define the Bessel coefficients used here by the series
$$J_k(\tau)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^j(\tau/2)^{2j+k}}{j!(j+k)!}.$$
For $\tau\ne0$, the ratio of consecutive absolute summands is $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]\to0$, so the series converges absolutely. If $\tau=0$, at most its $j=0,k=0$ summand is nonzero, so it also converges absolutely. Thus the series defines $J_k(\tau)$ before any estimate is used. The exponential uses the series convention of [[def-complex-exponential]], whose absolute convergence is supplied by [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]. This definition specifies the target and coefficient series; it does not assert a Jacobi–Anger expansion or a truncation bound. A real QSP or QSVT theorem alone does not implement this full complex, non-parity target; the finite even/odd combination, complementary-polynomial certificates, normalization, and controlled relative phase are separate operations in the binding simulator.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

The complex exponential is entire, and

$$ \exp'(z)=\exp z $$

for every $z\in\mathbb C$.

For all $z,w\in\mathbb C$, $\exp(z+w)=\exp z\exp w$. For real $x$, the complex value $\exp(x+0i)$ equals the published real exponential $e^x$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]], [[lem-cauchy-product-of-absolutely-convergent-complex-series]], [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], [[lem-binomial-theorem-over-complex-numbers]], [[thm-binomial-closed-formula]].

**Inputs.** A finite Hermitian $H$, $\alpha>0$ with the certified norm promise $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$, rational time $t$, rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, and either (i) the exact $(\alpha,a,0)$ block encoding $U$ with clean injection $J$ and $J^*UJ=H/\alpha$, or (ii) a separately selected bounded-block-error mode with the same declared ancilla embedding $J$ and a unitary $U$ whose clean block satisfies $\|J^*UJ-H/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm BE}$ for a supplied certified rational upper bound $\epsilon_{\rm BE}\ge0$. The latter mode is accepted only if it passes the explicit post-degree error-budget test in steps 3 and 5. For either mode, declare the access and cost for $U,U^*,$ controlled-$U$, controlled-$U^*$, both projector-phase circuits, coefficient preparation, SELECT, OAA reflections, phase synthesis, data access, and classical arithmetic. The input description also supplies terminating certified comparisons and rational-interval evaluations for the scalar arithmetic below.

**Output.** Return the finite circuit list and error certificate for a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$. Its success claim is on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}|\psi\rangle=|0_{\rm work}\rangle|\psi\rangle$; auxiliary output registers are approximate and are not measured to clean an unknown system input. On a failed polynomial or phase certificate, return the phase routine's declared failure status and do not report a simulator.

**Generation and execution.** Set $\tau=\alpha t$ and $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$. For $t=0$, return the identity circuit and zero query count. Otherwise:

1. Starting at $d=\max(1,\lceil|\tau|\rceil)$, increase $d$ until $u=|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$ and
   $$\frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!(1-u)}\le\rho/8.$$
   Evaluate each strict comparison by the certified interval routine named in OP0 of the binding operational appendix; an undecided equality is not rounded toward success.
2. For each $k=0,\ldots,d$, compute $J_k(\tau)$ from the series in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]]. derivations.claim: The Chebyshev recurrence and $\cos((k+1)\theta)+\cos((k-1)\theta)=2\cos\theta\cos(k\theta)$ show by induction that $T_k(\cos\theta)=\cos(k\theta)$ for all $k\ge0$. Every $x\in[-1,1]$ is $\cos\theta$ for some real $\theta$, so $|T_k(x)|\le1$.

If $\tau\ne0$, the ratio of consecutive absolute terms in the defining series of $J_k(\tau)$ is $|\tau|^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]$, which tends to zero, so the series converges absolutely; for $\tau=0$ the series is immediate. For the integral $I_{k,j}=\int_0^1 u^{j-1/2}(1-u)^{k-1/2}\,du$, splitting $1=u+(1-u)$ and integrating the derivative of $u^{j+1/2}(1-u)^{k+1/2}$ gives $I_{k,j+1}/I_{k,j}=(j+1/2)/(j+k+1)$. Iterating yields $I_{k,j}/I_{k,0}=(2j)!k!/[4^j j!(j+k)!]$. Expanding $e^{i\tau t}$ uniformly on $[-1,1]$, substituting $u=t^2$, and using this moment ratio gives $J_k(\tau)=\frac{(\tau/2)^k}{k! I_{k,0}}\int_{-1}^{1}e^{i\tau t}(1-t^2)^{k-1/2}\,dt.$ The weight is nonnegative and its normalized integral is one; [F4] therefore gives $|J_k(\tau)|\le(|\tau|/2)^k/k!$.

Put $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)>0$, $\tau_0=|\tau|>\epsilon$, and $S=\tau_0+L/\ln(e+L/\tau_0)$. If $\tau_0\ge1/4$, then $S\ge1/4$. If $\tau_0<1/4$, put $u=1/\tau_0>4$, so $L>\ln u$. The function $g(y)=y/\ln(e+uy)$ is increasing for $y>0$, since its derivative has numerator $\ln(e+uy)-uy/(e+uy)>0$; the first term exceeds $1$ and the second is below $1$. Also $\ln u\le u/2$ for $u\ge4$ (the difference has positive derivative and is positive at $4$), and $e\le u^2/2$, so $e+u\ln u\le u^2$. Therefore $S\ge g(L)>g(\ln u)\ge1/2$. In all cases $S\ge1/4$. Set $m=\lceil64S\rceil$; then $m\ge16$, $m\ge64\tau_0$, and $d=m-1\ge\max(1,\lceil\tau_0\rceil)$, so this is an eligible candidate in the OP4 loop starting rule [F7]. The real parameter $\tau$ is defined in [F1].

For $x=\cos\theta$, [F6] writes $e^{-i\tau x}$ as the product of the absolutely convergent exponential series for $e^{-i\tau e^{i\theta}/2}$ and $e^{-i\tau e^{-i\theta}/2}$. Absolute convergence permits grouping terms by the exponent difference $k$; for each $k\ge0$ the coefficient of $e^{ik\theta}$ is $(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)$, and the coefficient of $e^{-ik\theta}$ is the same. Pairing these terms and using [F1] gives $e^{-i\tau x}=J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k\ge1}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x).$ By [F1], [F3], [F4], and [F6], the defining product is absolutely and uniformly convergent in $\theta$ on bounded intervals, so the regrouping is valid.

Subtracting the degree-$d$ partial sum in step 2.1, applying the triangle inequality, and using $|T_k(x)|\le1$ from step 1.1 gives error at most $2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)|$. With $m=d+1$, the ratio of consecutive factorial majorants $(|\tau|/2)^k/k!$ for $k\ge m$ is at most $u=|\tau|/(2(m+1))<1$. The geometric-series bound from step 1.2 now yields the stated factorial tail.

By [F7], each of the $d+1$ OP4 coefficient errors is at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$. Since a nonconstant Chebyshev term has coefficient multiplier $2$, their total uniform contribution is at most $(1+2d)\rho/(32(d+1))<\rho/16$; adding the tail $\rho/8$ from step 3.1 gives a combined error $<\rho$. The coefficients and multiplier $2$ are those of the expansion in [F1].

Let $r=L/\tau_0$. If $r\ge1$, then $m\ge64\tau_0(1+r/\ln(e+r))$. Since $\ln y\le\sqrt y$ for $y\ge1$ and $r/(e+r)\ge1/(e+1)$, we have $r/\ln(e+r)\ge\sqrt{e+r}/(e+1)$. Thus $2m/(e\tau_0)\ge[128/(e(e+1))]\sqrt{e+r}>\sqrt{e+r}$, because $e<3$ gives $128/(e(e+1))>128/12>1$; hence $\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))\ge\frac12\ln(e+r)$. If $r<1$, $m\ge64\tau_0$ gives $2m/(e\tau_0)\ge128/e$, hence $\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))>1$, since $e<3$ implies $128/e>42>e$. For $r\ge1$, these bounds give $m\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))\ge32\tau_0(\ln(e+r)+r)\ge32(L+\tau_0)$, because $\ln(e+r)>1$. For $r<1$, they give $m\ln(2m/(e\tau_0))>64\tau_0>32(L+\tau_0)$, because $L<\tau_0$. Also $u_m=\tau_0/[2(m+1)]\le1/128$, so $2/(1-u_m)\le256/127<4$, and the factorial tail expression is bounded by the estimate of step 3.1. The real $\tau$ is defined in [F1]. $\ln(m!)=\sum_{j=1}^m\ln j\ge\int_1^m\ln x\,dx\ge m\ln m-m,$ so $m!\ge(m/e)^m$. The factorial-tail test at $d=m-1$ is consequently at most $\frac{2(\tau_0/2)^m}{m!(1-u_m)} \le4\exp\!\left(-m\ln\frac{2m}{e\tau_0}\right) \le4e^{-32(L+\tau_0)} \le e^{-2L}/80000=\rho/8.$ The last inequality holds because $L+\tau_0>1$: for $0<\epsilon<1$, the function $\ln(1/\epsilon)-(1-\epsilon)$ is positive (its derivative is $(\epsilon-1)/\epsilon<0$ as $\epsilon$ increases to $1$, and its value at $1$ is zero), and $\tau_0>\epsilon$. The factorial tail is the estimate of step 3.1 and the OP4 threshold is [F7].

If $\tau_0\le\epsilon$, the derivative fact [F5] and $|e^{-isx}|=1$ from [F4] give $e^{-i\tau x}-1=\int_0^\tau -ix e^{-isx}\,ds,\qquad |e^{-i\tau x}-1|\le|\tau x|\le\epsilon$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$. Thus the wrapper [F8] has the stated small-time error, including $\tau=0$.

For each real QSVT extraction, [F3] bounds the exact phase-list polynomial mismatch plus the implemented phase-slot errors by $\delta_{\rm qsp}=\rho/64$ uniformly on $[-1,1]$. For the bounded mode, apply [F12] to the exact $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ phase sequences on the supplied block and on the target block; each branch changes by at most $4d\sqrt{\epsilon_{\rm BE}}$, so their average has the same block-perturbation bound. The coefficient-qubit average therefore gives a complete block $M_{\rm ph}/2$ with
$$\|M_{\rm ph}-M(H/\alpha)\|_{\rm op}\le2\delta_{\rm qsp}+8d\sqrt{\epsilon_{\rm BE}}.$$

Implementing $\widetilde U$ requires the separately declared controlled-$U$ and controlled-$U^*$ calls; $S$, the preparation of $|+\rangle$, and the reflection about $\operatorname{ran}(J')$ also have declared costs. [[thm-qa-25-qubitization-signal-sequence]] proves its compressed block and spectral relation.

For the QSVT simulation sequence, the signal operations are the alternating $U,U^*$ calls interleaved with the projector phases $e^{i\phi(2\Pi-I)}$ from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]]. Their exact phase list, parity, real-polynomial extraction, controls, inverse calls, and phase-synthesis precision are part of the supplied circuit description. The scalar polynomial pairs must satisfy [[def-qa-23-qsp-admissible-polynomial-pair]]; singular-value transformations use the convention of [[def-qa-24-singular-value-transform]].

derivations.claim: If $\alpha|t|>\epsilon$, the algorithm invokes OP4, and [F2] gives the clean-input isometry bound.

Suppose $\alpha|t|\le\epsilon$. For a unit vector $\psi$, the differential identity [F4] and the fundamental theorem of calculus give $U_H(t)\psi-\psi=\int_0^t -iHU_H(s)\psi\,ds$. Each integrand has norm at most $\|H\|_{\rm op}$, because $U_H(s)$ preserves norm. The triangle inequality for Riemann sums and continuity yield $\|(U_H(t)-I)\psi\|\le |t|\|H\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha|t|\le\epsilon$, using [F7]. Taking the maximum over unit $\psi$ proves the clean-input operator bound for the identity circuit. The work registers are exactly zero, so the same isometry bound holds.

In either branch, the implementation on clean inputs and the target $J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}$ are isometries whose operator-norm difference is at most $\epsilon$, by steps 1.1 and 1.2. Apply [F6] with $\delta=\epsilon$ to obtain the reference-system trace-distance conclusion after tracing work.

citations.quote:
**Input.** An exact Hermitian block encoding of $H/\alpha$, $\alpha>0$, a rational time $t$, $0<\epsilon<1$, and a terminating certified comparison of $\tau=\alpha|t|$ with $\epsilon$, charged under the access model.

**Instructions.**

1. If $\tau\le\epsilon$, return the identity circuit on the system, with every work register left at zero. The query, gate, and bit costs of this branch are zero.
2. If $\tau>\epsilon$, invoke [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] with $t,\epsilon$, and return its circuit and error certificate. Propagate any INVALID, CERTIFICATE_ERROR, or IMPLEMENTATION_ERROR result without labeling it a successful simulation.

The comparison cost is recorded separately. The second branch is exactly the OP4 procedure; this wrapper does not modify OP4 or infer inverse, controlled, state-preparation, or phase-synthesis access.

With $J_k,T_k$ defined in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]], for every real $\tau$ and integer $d\ge0$,
$$\sup_{|x|\le1}\left|\exp(-i\tau x)-\left(J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k=1}^{d}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x)\right)\right| \le 2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)| \le \frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!\left(1-|\tau|/(2(d+2))\right)}$$
whenever $|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$. In the OP4 simulator, $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$ and the factorial-tail stopping test therefore certifies truncation error at most $\rho/8$; rounding each coefficient to error at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$ keeps the combined polynomial error below $\rho$. For the nontrivial simulation regime $|\tau|>\epsilon$, an integer $d$ passing OP4's test exists with
$$d=O\left(|\tau|+\frac{\ln(1/\epsilon)}{\ln(e+\ln(1/\epsilon)/|\tau|)}\right).$$
For $|\tau|\le\epsilon$, the constant polynomial $1$ approximates the target within $\epsilon$; the wrapper algorithm uses the exact identity circuit in that branch.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

A length-$d$ sequence from [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]] has exactly $d$ signal factors $W_R(x)$ and exactly $d+1$ phase factors $Z(\phi_j)$, for $0\le j\le d$. In the scalar QSP model the signal acts on one two-dimensional signal register. If each $W_R$ is provided by a named query oracle, the sequence uses exactly $d$ calls to that oracle; it makes no controlled or inverse signal calls. The oracle's work registers, implementation, and query/gate charges are those explicitly supplied with it. The phase-rotation, ordinary-gate, circuit-description, bit, and numerical-precision coordinates remain separate as in [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]].

Let $A$ be a finite square or rectangular matrix with a declared isometric padding $\widehat A$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $B$ be the exact compressed PUE block of the supplied input unitary and assume

$$\|B-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}.$$

Let $P$ be the degree-$d$ parity polynomial of an admissible QSVT phase sequence, and let $f$ have the same parity. Put $S:=\{0\}\cup\{\sigma_j:\sigma_j>0\text{ is a singular value of }\widehat A/\alpha\}$, so zero is included even when the two matrix dimensions differ. If $\sup_{\sigma\in S}|P(\sigma)-f(\sigma)|\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}$, and the implemented phase operation at slot $\ell$ is a unitary within operator-norm error $\zeta_\ell$ of its ideal operation, then the implemented compressed block $\widetilde B$ satisfies

$$\|\widetilde B-f^{\mathrm{SV}}(\widehat A/\alpha)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\eta_{\mathrm{poly}}+4d\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{BE}}}+\sum_{\ell}\zeta_\ell.$$

The exact sequence uses $d$ calls alternating between $U$ and $U^*$, $d+1$ projector-phase operations, and the reflection and one-qubit resources in [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. A real-polynomial control wrapper has its separately listed controlled gates. Matrix-data access, block-encoding construction, inverse and controlled access, phase-list generation, finite-gate compilation, and classical bit costs are charged through their declared interfaces; no cost follows from a bare matrix.

For a $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian $H$, put $h_{\max}=\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$ and supply a certified bound $h\ge h_{\max}$. In the supplied-permutation mode, if $h=0$ then $H=0$ and the returned $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ has zero all-zero-flag compression and normalization $1$; if $h>0$, the designated all-zero auxiliary compression of $U_L^*U_R$ from [[alg-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding]] is $H/(d_Hh)$. One such block-encoding call uses one supplied inverse row-location permutation, one supplied column-location permutation, two entry-value queries (compute and uncompute), and the declared $D_{d_H}$, inverse, flag-rotation, and arithmetic implementations. In the optional sorted-XOR mode with $h>0$, the encoded matrix is $H\oplus0$ with normalization $d_Hh$, and each encoding, actual adjoint or coherent controlled call costs $O(\log(d_H+1))$ original location calls and $O(1)$ value calls. No constant-cost conversion from XOR locations to in-place permutations is asserted.

For the exact access model of [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], or its bounded-block-error variant satisfying the post-degree budget in [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]], rational $t$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$, a successful execution of [[alg-qa-25-qubitized-hamiltonian-simulation]] returns a unitary dilation $V_{\rm impl}$ satisfying
$$\|V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$$
on the clean-input isometry $J_{\rm clean}$, where $J_{\rm out}$ appends every work register in zero. Output work registers are approximate; no full-space error on arbitrary dirty work inputs or exact cleanup is asserted. For $t=0$, the declared identity branch is exact. For every reference system, tracing out work gives the corresponding system-output trace-distance bound at most $\epsilon$.

derivations.claim: If $\tau\le\epsilon$, [F1] returns the exact identity and makes no signal call. If $\tau>\epsilon$, the degree test of [F2] has a finite passing candidate and its least accepted degree obeys the stated $O(S)$ bound.

In one OAA application, $W$ contains one even and one odd real QSVT extraction. By [F3], they use $d_E+d_O$ signal calls and $d_E+d_O+2$ projector-phase slots. OAA uses $W,W^*,W$, so the total is exactly $3(d_E+d_O)$ signal calls and $3(d_E+d_O+2)$ phase slots, bounded above by $6d$ and $6d+6$, respectively.

By [F3], controlling each selected real extraction against identity needs one controlled signal call exactly when its degree is odd. OAA contains the three signal blocks $W,W^*,W$, so the even and odd extractions together use exactly $3(\mathbf1_{d_E\text{ odd}}+\mathbf1_{d_O\text{ odd}})$ such calls. By [F4], the control selecting $\Phi$ or $-\Phi$ acts only on phase rotations and adds no signal query. Any further external control invokes the separately supplied controlled-$U$ or controlled-$U^*$ operations by [F5].

The lists in OP4 are generated once, while the OAA circuit reuses the declared phase lists, coefficient preparation, and SELECT circuits in its three block calls and their inverses. Every implementation cost named in the Statement is retained from [F5]; the sparse branch multiplies these signal counts by the supplied block-encoding operations and normalization in [F6]. In the optional sorted-XOR branch this explicitly multiplies the signal count by $O(\log(d_H+1))$ location and $O(1)$ value calls; the supplied-permutation branch retains its original sharper count. Thus no sparse location/value, phase-synthesis, or classical bit cost is absorbed into an oracle count.

When $0<c\le\tau\le C<\infty$ and $\epsilon\to0$, $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)\to\infty$ and $\ln(e+L/\tau)=\Theta(\ln L)$, since $L/C\le L/\tau\le L/c$. Substituting this comparison into $S$ gives $O(\tau+L/\ln L)$, the stated standard-regime form. Correctness remains the separate theorem [F7].

Let $(U,J,\alpha)$ be an exact Hermitian block encoding from [[def-qa-25-qubitization-access-model]], and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $K\psi_j=\lambda_j\psi_j$. Put $x_j=\lambda_j/\alpha$ and $s_j=\sqrt{1-x_j^2}$. For $|x_j|<1$, define
$$\eta_j=(I-\Pi)UJ\psi_j/s_j,\qquad \widetilde\eta_j=(I-\Pi)U^*J\psi_j/s_j.$$
The $\eta_j$ are orthonormal in $\ker\Pi$, as are the $\widetilde\eta_j$. In the paired input basis $(J\psi_j,\widetilde\eta_j)$ and output basis $(J\psi_j,\eta_j)$, $U$ has matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}x_j&s_j\\s_j&-x_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
The unitary $U^*$ maps in the reverse direction by the same matrix. If $|x_j|=1$, the complement is absent and $UJ\psi_j=x_jJ\psi_j=U^*J\psi_j$; no division by zero is used. The value $x_j=0$ is an ordinary two-dimensional signal plane.

derivations.claim: Since $s^2=1-x^2$, direct multiplication gives $U_x^*=U_x$ and $U_x^2=I$. Also $J^*U_xJ=[x]=K/\alpha$, so $U_x$ is unitary and has the claimed block encoding. Its clean and complementary components are $U_x|0\rangle=x|0\rangle+s|1\rangle$.

If $|x|<1$, then $s>0$, so the normalized complement defined in [F1] is $|1\rangle$; both input and output paired bases are $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and the matrix is exactly $U_x$. At $x=0$, $s=1$, hence $U_0=X$, confirming that zero is a regular two-dimensional signal plane.

If $x=1$ or $x=-1$, then $s=0$ and $U_x|0\rangle=x|0\rangle=U_x^*|0\rangle$. No complement vector is normalized in these cases; this verifies the endpoint convention and the encoded eigenvalue $\lambda/\alpha=x$.

Let $\mathcal B_n$ be the complex inner-product space with orthonormal basis $\{|y\rangle:y\in\{0,1\}^n\}$. For $1\le r\le n$, define $X_r|y_1\cdots y_n\rangle=|y_1\cdots(y_r\oplus1)\cdots y_n\rangle$, and put $J=\frac12\sum_{r=1}^nX_r$. For $0\le i\le n$, let $|D_i^n\rangle$ be the normalized uniform sum of basis vectors of Hamming weight $i$; define $\mathcal S_n=\operatorname{span}\{|D_i^n\rangle:0\le i\le n\}$. On a separate path space with orthonormal basis $\{|i\rangle:0\le i\le n\}$, define $H_0$ to have off-diagonal entries $w_i=\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}/n$ between $|i-1\rangle$ and $|i\rangle$ for every 1≤i≤n, and all other matrix entries zero.

Let $n\ge1$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $p_0=0,\ p_i=x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_i$. On the basis $\{|i,b\rangle:0\le i\le n,\ b\in\{0,1\}\}$, put
$$H_x=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\sum_{b=0}^1\left(|i-1,b\rangle\langle i,b\oplus x_i|+|i,b\oplus x_i\rangle\langle i-1,b|\right).$$
Write $\operatorname{parity}(x)=p_n=x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_n$. The basis permutation $V_x|i,b\rangle=|i,b\oplus p_i\rangle$ conjugates $H_x$ to two copies of $H_0$. The counting identity proved below gives $H_0=(2/n)J|_{\mathcal S_n}$, under the isometry $|i\rangle\mapsto|D_i^n\rangle$. Consequently $\|H_x\|_{\rm op}\le1$ and
$$e^{-iH_x\pi n/2}|0,0\rangle=(-i)^n|n,\operatorname{parity}(x)\rangle.$$

For a $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian $H$, put $h_{\max}=\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$ and supply a certified bound $h\ge h_{\max}$. In the supplied-permutation mode, if $h=0$ then $H=0$ and the returned $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ has zero all-zero-flag compression and normalization $1$; if $h>0$, the designated all-zero auxiliary compression of $U_L^*U_R$ from [[alg-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding]] is $H/(d_Hh)$. One such block-encoding call uses one supplied inverse row-location permutation, one supplied column-location permutation, two entry-value queries (compute and uncompute), and the declared $D_{d_H}$, inverse, flag-rotation, and arithmetic implementations. In the optional sorted-XOR mode with $h>0$, the encoded matrix is $H\oplus0$ with normalization $d_Hh$, and each encoding, actual adjoint or coherent controlled call costs $O(\log(d_H+1))$ original location calls and $O(1)$ value calls. No constant-cost conversion from XOR locations to in-place permutations is asserted.

For $n\ge1$, let $H_x$ be the $2(n+1)$-dimensional, at-most-two-sparse Hermitian path matrix of [[lem-qa-25-parity-path-transfer]] for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, with weights $w_i=\sqrt{i(n+1-i)}/n$. Put $\eta=1/(6\pi n)$, choose $b=\lceil\log_2(3\pi n)\rceil$, and round each nonzero weight to the nearest dyadic $q_i=2^{-b}\operatorname{round}(2^bw_i)$, with ties rounded upward. Let $\widetilde H_x$ be the same path matrix with weights $q_i$, and encode its entries exactly in the row-location/value XOR-oracle model of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], using $O(\log(n+1))$ value bits for the finite set $\{0,q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$. Then $\|H_x-\widetilde H_x\|_{\rm op}\le2\eta$ and the sparse normalization $\alpha_{\rm sp}=2\max_i q_i$ lies between positive absolute constants.

Suppose a uniform sparse-oracle query algorithm uses $q$ total row-location and value-oracle calls and returns a clean-input isometry $V_xJ_{\rm clean}$ satisfying
$$\|V_xJ_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-it\widetilde H_x}\|_{\rm op}\le\tfrac13, \qquad t=\pi n/2,$$
where $J_{\rm out}$ appends its work registers in zero. Then $q\ge n/4$. Thus this sparse row/value model requires $\Omega(n)=\Omega(t)=\Omega(\alpha_{\rm sp}t)$ queries for this family. The result does not assert a lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access.

derivations.claim: Substituting $n=2$ gives $w_1=w_2=\sqrt2/2$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$, edge 1 joins $|0,b\rangle$ to $|1,b\oplus x_1\rangle$, and edge 2 joins $|1,b\rangle$ to $|2,b\oplus x_2\rangle$. Starting with $b=0$, these two edges produce the four paths in the table; each endpoint bit is $x_1\oplus x_2$. Each internal path vertex has degree two and each endpoint degree one.
Therefore $d_H=2$ and $h_{\max}=1/\sqrt2$, so [F2] gives $\alpha_{\rm sp}=d_Hh_{\max}=\sqrt2$. This is the $n=2$ instance of the constant-normalization family in [F3].

In the parity-free basis, the path matrix is $H_0=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad H_0^2=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\0&2&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$ Its eigenvalues are $1,0,-1$, so spectral functional calculus gives $e^{-i\pi H_0}=I-2H_0^2$, which sends $|0\rangle$ to $-|2\rangle$. The prefix-parity basis permutation of [F1] restores the endpoint bit $x_1\oplus x_2$; equivalently, [F1] gives $(-i)^2=-1$ times the same endpoint.

For a finite Hermitian $H$ with exact block-encoding normalization $\alpha>0$, $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$, and real time $t$, put $\tau=\alpha t$. On $x\in[-1,1]$ the scalar target is $f_\tau(x)=\exp(-i\tau x)$; if $H\psi_\lambda=\lambda\psi_\lambda$, then $f_\tau(\lambda/\alpha)=\exp(-it\lambda)$, the eigenvalue of the finite matrix evolution [[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]].

For $k\ge0$, define the Chebyshev polynomials by $T_0(x)=1$, $T_1(x)=x$, $T_{k+1}(x)=2xT_k(x)-T_{k-1}(x)$. Define the Bessel coefficients used here by the series
$$J_k(\tau)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^j(\tau/2)^{2j+k}}{j!(j+k)!}.$$
For $\tau\ne0$, the ratio of consecutive absolute summands is $\tau^2/[4(j+1)(j+k+1)]\to0$, so the series converges absolutely. If $\tau=0$, at most its $j=0,k=0$ summand is nonzero, so it also converges absolutely. Thus the series defines $J_k(\tau)$ before any estimate is used. The exponential uses the series convention of [[def-complex-exponential]], whose absolute convergence is supplied by [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]. This definition specifies the target and coefficient series; it does not assert a Jacobi–Anger expansion or a truncation bound. A real QSP or QSVT theorem alone does not implement this full complex, non-parity target; the finite even/odd combination, complementary-polynomial certificates, normalization, and controlled relative phase are separate operations in the binding simulator.

With $J_k,T_k$ defined in [[def-qa-25-hamiltonian-simulation-polynomial]], for every real $\tau$ and integer $d\ge0$,
$$\sup_{|x|\le1}\left|\exp(-i\tau x)-\left(J_0(\tau)+2\sum_{k=1}^{d}(-i)^kJ_k(\tau)T_k(x)\right)\right| \le 2\sum_{k>d}|J_k(\tau)| \le \frac{2(|\tau|/2)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!\left(1-|\tau|/(2(d+2))\right)}$$
whenever $|\tau|/(2(d+2))<1$. In the OP4 simulator, $\rho=\epsilon^2/10000$ and the factorial-tail stopping test therefore certifies truncation error at most $\rho/8$; rounding each coefficient to error at most $\rho/(32(d+1))$ keeps the combined polynomial error below $\rho$. For the nontrivial simulation regime $|\tau|>\epsilon$, an integer $d$ passing OP4's test exists with
$$d=O\left(|\tau|+\frac{\ln(1/\epsilon)}{\ln(e+\ln(1/\epsilon)/|\tau|)}\right).$$
For $|\tau|\le\epsilon$, the constant polynomial $1$ approximates the target within $\epsilon$; the wrapper algorithm uses the exact identity circuit in that branch.

derivations.claim: The recurrence gives $T_2(x)=2xT_1(x)-T_0(x)=2x^2-1$. The $k=0$ term of the Chebyshev expansion is $J_0$; the $k=1$ coefficient is $2(-i)J_1=-2iJ_1$; and the $k=2$ coefficient is $2(-i)^2J_2=-2J_2$. Therefore the degree-two truncation is exactly the displayed $P_2$.

The series in [F1] is real for real $\tau$, so $J_0,J_1,J_2$ are real. Since $T_2$ is even and $T_1$ is odd, $\operatorname{Re}P_2=J_0-2J_2T_2$ is even and $\operatorname{Im}P_2=-2J_1T_1$ is odd. Applying [F2] with $d=2$ gives the uniform tail $2\sum_{k>2}|J_k(\tau)|$; its factorial denominator condition is $|\tau|/[2(2+2)]=|\tau|/8<1$.
At $\tau=0$, the series gives $J_0(0)=1$ and $J_1(0)=J_2(0)=0$, so $P_2(x)=1=e^0$. At $x=\pm1$, $T_1(x)=x$ and $T_2(x)=1$, and the same tail bound from [F2] applies without an endpoint exception.

Fix $N\ge1$, a sparsity bound $d\ge1$, an integer $b\ge1$, and an injective code $\mathrm{enc}:C\to\{0,1\}^b$ for a finite set $C\subset\mathbb C$ containing $0$ and closed under conjugation. Put $w=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ and $v=\lceil\log_2d\rceil$, identify $[N]$ with the first $N$ strings in $\{0,1\}^w$, and regard any remaining strings as invalid labels. A valid $w$-bit index is zero-extended to $w+1$ bits. Let $H=(H_{xy})_{x,y\in[N]}$ be Hermitian, have entries in $C$, and have at most $d$ nonzero entries in every row. For each valid row $x$, list its nonzero column indices in increasing order. Define the total location function $f_H(x,\ell)$ to be the $\ell$-th listed index for a valid slot $0\le\ell<d$ when that slot exists, and a distinguished sentinel otherwise. Invalid row labels and invalid slot labels also return the sentinel. Encode the sentinel by a fixed $(w+1)$-bit word outside the valid index codes. Define the total value function $g_H(x,y)$ to return $\mathrm{enc}(H_{xy})$ on valid labels and $\mathrm{enc}(0)$ on invalid labels. All label widths and codes are part of the finite input description.

The **row-location oracle** and **entry-value oracle** are the coherent XOR maps $O_{f_H}|x,\ell,z\rangle=|x,\ell,z\oplus f_H(x,\ell)\rangle$ and $O_{g_H}|x,y,z\rangle=|x,y,z\oplus g_H(x,y)\rangle$, where the output target has respectively $w+1$ and $b$ bits. The slot register has $v$ bits; all unused slot strings are invalid and use the sentinel. These are total Boolean-function oracles on every bitstring basis input. They are instances of [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]], whose justified-by supplier proves unitarity and involutivity for arbitrary total functions. Each named call and any separately granted controlled or inverse call is charged under [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. This exact-code model describes the decoded matrix $H$; approximating a different target matrix requires a separate bound on the matrix difference. Row and value access alone does not supply a term list or term-evolution circuits.

Let $n,m\ge0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be a total Boolean function on ordered bit strings. Its coherent XOR oracle is the linear extension of
$$
O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. The declared access contract states how many invocations count as queries and whether a controlled invocation is supplied. A query to this declared black box is counted separately from elementary gate size, depth, and width.

If $f$ is supplied instead by an explicit Boolean circuit, implementing $O_f$ means compiling that circuit and paying its reversible elementary-gate and workspace costs; the function description alone is not a free query. For this XOR oracle, its inverse is the same map, as proved in [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Controlled access remains a separate capability unless the contract explicitly provides it.

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and $D=2^n$. An explicit amplitude-table input is a list of $D$ exact complex numbers $(a_x)_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}$ in the ordered basis convention of [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]; it is valid when $\sum_x|a_x|^2=1$. Its target is the pure-state ray $[a]$ under [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]]: nonzero scalar multiples represent the same ray, and $a$ is a unit representative when the table is normalized. A claim must state whether its output error is projective chord distance [[def-qc-projective-chord-distance]] or a representative-level vector error.

The cost record keeps these quantities separate: (1) the classical encoding length and table-reading/preprocessing work; (2) continuous-angle gate occurrences, or finite-alphabet gate occurrences when that model is specified; (3) width, clean-workspace and serial-depth usage; and (4) the declared output-error metric. If an encoding assigns exactly $b$ bits to each real coordinate and $b$ bits to each imaginary coordinate, with basis order implicit, the dense table contains exactly $2Db$ input bits. Those bits must decode to the input table in an exact-table claim; finite-precision approximations are separate inputs with separate error hypotheses. An explicit table is classical input: this definition grants no coherent table oracle, QRAM, or free loading operation. Ideal exact complex arithmetic and finite-precision bit cost are distinct models.

derivations.claim: For $x<M$ and $l<d$, let $F_x(l)$ be the listed column if $x<N$ and that slot exists, and $N+l$ otherwise; set $F_x(l)=0$ on $l\ge d$. This is a total function of finite bitstrings. On $[d]$ it is strictly increasing: actual indices are distinct, sorted and below $N$, followed by distinct pads $N+l$. All outputs are below $N+d\le M$. For an invalid $x$, use a valid dummy query input and mask its answer, giving exactly the padded branch. The same masking handles padded physical slot strings. Every masked or externally controlled XOR evaluation can use two ordinary calls: compute the function to clean work, conditionally XOR-copy it to the desired target, and uncompute. Thus no controlled oracle is assumed free.

For each $x,y<M$, compute a total inverse lookup $G_x(y)$ by lower_bound search of the strictly increasing list $F_x(0),\ldots,F_x(d-1)$. Start $lo=0,hi=d$; for $\lceil\log_2(d+1)\rceil+1$ rounds, if $lo<hi$, set $m=\lfloor(lo+hi)/2\rfloor$ and update $lo=m+1$ if $F_x(m)<y$, otherwise $hi=m$. In inactive rounds use a masked dummy call. Each active interval shrinks to at most the ceiling of half its old width, and width one becomes zero at the next round, so the stated round count suffices. If the final $lo<d$ and $F_x(lo)=y$, output $lo$; otherwise output zero. Retain and then reverse the fixed finite search history after copying its answer, so all history and oracle workspace are clean. There are $O(\log(d+1))$ forward/reverse location calls including the final equality test. Strict increase gives $G_x(F_x(l))=l$ for every $l<d$, including $l=0$; off the image no inversion is asserted.

On two $\log_2M$-bit registers apply the total permutation circuit $|l,0\rangle\mapsto|l,F_x(l)\rangle\mapsto|l\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}G_x(F_x(l)),F_x(l)\rangle\mapsto|F_x(l),0\rangle$, where the middle map is XOR evaluation of $G_x$ into the first register and the final map swaps the registers. The displayed clean formula is asserted only on $l<d$ and follows from step 2.1. Each constituent is a total reversible gate sequence on every bitstring, so its actual inverse exists with the same query order. Coherent row labels and references are untouched. Applying the separately supplied uniform preparation first gives $d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|F_x(l)\rangle$ with all additional work zero. This constructs the required row-neighbor and column-neighbor isometries; Hermiticity identifies the column list at $j$ with the row list at $j$.

Let $V_L|0,i\rangle=d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|i,F_i(l)\rangle$ and $V_R|0,j\rangle=d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|F_j(l),j\rangle$, including the common zero work registers from step 3.1. Put $U_L=I_{\rm flag}\otimes V_L$. After $V_R$, compute $a_{ij}=\widetilde H_{ij}/h$ and apply the flag unitary with first column $(a_{ij},\sqrt{1-|a_{ij}|^2})^T$ and second column $(-\sqrt{1-|a_{ij}|^2},\overline{a_{ij}})^T$, then uncompute values and arithmetic. Its columns are orthonormal because $|a_{ij}|\le1$, so this defines $U_R$. Only $U_R$ inserts the value amplitude; $U_L$ has good-flag amplitude one.

Each row and, by Hermiticity, each column has at most $d$ nonzero entries, each of magnitude at most $h$. For any vector $v$, $|(Hv)_i|^2\le(\sum_j|H_{ij}|)(\sum_j|H_{ij}||v_j|^2)$ by Cauchy–Schwarz. Summing over $i$ and using the row and column bounds gives $\|Hv\|^2\le(dh)^2\|v\|^2$, so $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le dh$. The zero extension has the same operator norm, so the normalization $dh$ is valid for the block encoding in [F3]. By [F3], the clean $(i,j)$ matrix entry of $U_L^*U_R$ is $\langle U_R(0,j),U_L(0,i)\rangle$. For a valid nonzero $H_{ij}$, the ordered pair $(i,j)$ occurs once on each side, with coefficients $H_{ij}/(h\sqrt d)$ and $1/\sqrt d$, respectively. Their root pairing is $H_{ij}/(dh)$. A zero or invalid entry contributes zero even if its padded pair happens to match, since its good-flag value amplitude is zero. Every value workspace has been uncomputed, and each location workspace is zero by step 3.1, so no unmatched work suppresses the desired overlap. This proves the exact compressed block, including zero rows, $H=0$, $d>N$, $N=1$, $d=1$, padded labels and repeated sentinel replies.

Each clean location circuit uses $O(\log(d+1))$ QA20 location calls by step 1.1 and step 2.1 and step 3.1, and computing/uncomputing its value uses a constant number of value calls. Reversing the actual circuit has identical counts. Coherently controlling it controls all known gates, and step 1.1 replaces each controlled XOR query by a constant number of ordinary XOR queries; hence the same asymptotic holds. All other operations remain in [F4]'s separate cost coordinates. Finally $|H_{ij}|=|\langle H e_j,e_i\rangle|\le\|H\|_{\rm op}$, so $h=1$ is a valid supplied bound in the normalized HHL mode.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

derivations.claim: The exact identity $U^*(JV-UJ)V^*=U^*J-JV^*$, together with unitary invariance, gives $\|U^*J-JV^*\|_{\rm op}=\|JV-UJ\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$. Thus reversing the actual circuit supplies the inverse clean-input bound, without applying a forward error promise to dirty work.

If $E:H\to K$ has singular values $s_j$, [F2] gives orthonormal bases in which $\|E\psi\|^2=\sum_j s_j^2|\psi_j|^2$. Tensor those bases with any orthonormal reference basis; for $\Psi=\sum_{j,r}c_{j,r}e_j\otimes f_r$, $\|(E\otimes I)\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j,r}s_j^2|c_{j,r}|^2\le\|E\|_{\rm op}^2\|\Psi\|^2$. A top singular vector tensored with any unit reference vector attains equality, so $\|E\otimes I\|_{\rm op}=\|E\|_{\rm op}$. If the reference space is zero, the amplified map is zero and its bound is immediate. For coherent control against identity, the difference between the actual and ideal clean-input maps is zero on the control-zero summand and $E$ on the orthogonal control-one summand; its norm is at most $\|E\|_{\rm op}$. These statements apply to step 1.1 as well as to the original forward bound.

For $s\ge1$, expansion and cancellation give $$U_s\cdots U_1J-JV_s\cdots V_1=\sum_{j=1}^s U_s\cdots U_{j+1}(U_jJ-JV_j)V_{j-1}\cdots V_1.$$ Every factor outside the local difference is unitary, so each summand has norm at most $\eta_j$. The triangle inequality yields the claimed sum. On the right of each local difference are only ideal system unitaries followed by $J$, so this expansion evaluates that difference on clean ideal inputs. The actual later unitaries on the left propagate the error without any cleanliness assumption. For $s=0$, both products are identity maps, so the difference is zero.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let
$A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. A matrix $B\in M_{n\times m}(\mathbb F)$ is a
**Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse** of $A$ when

$$ABA=A,\qquad BAB=B,$$

and the two square products are self-adjoint:

$$ (AB)^*=AB,\qquad (BA)^*=BA. $$

When such a matrix exists and is unique, it is denoted by $A^+$.

The four displayed relations are the **Penrose equations**. They are written in
the matrix product and adjoint conventions of
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]] and
[[thm-matrix-of-the-adjoint-is-the-conjugate-transpose]].

For every matrix $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$ over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or
$\mathbb C$, there exists a unique matrix $A^+\in M_{n\times m}(\mathbb F)$
satisfying the four Penrose equations of
[[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]].

derivations.claim: The block matrix of $H_A$ is $\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\A^*&0\end{pmatrix}$. Its adjoint, by [F2], is the same block matrix, so $H_A^*=H_A$.

Multiplying the SVD in [F1] gives $Av_j=\sigma_j u_j$ and $A^*u_j=\sigma_jv_j$. Therefore $H_A(u_j,v_j)=\sigma_j(u_j,v_j)$ and $H_A(u_j,-v_j)=-\sigma_j(u_j,-v_j)$. After division by $\sqrt2$ these are unit eigenvectors. Orthonormality of the singular pairs makes all such vectors mutually orthogonal.

In the SVD bases, write $A=U\Sigma V^*$ with positive diagonal entries $\sigma_j$. The diagonal matrix $\Sigma^+$ that replaces each positive entry by $1/\sigma_j$ and leaves zero entries zero satisfies $\Sigma\Sigma^+\Sigma=\Sigma$, $\Sigma^+\Sigma\Sigma^+=\Sigma^+$, and both products $\Sigma\Sigma^+$ and $\Sigma^+\Sigma$ are diagonal projections. Unitary transport shows $V\Sigma^+U^*$ satisfies the four equations in [F3], so uniqueness gives $A^+=V\Sigma^+U^*$ and $A^+u_j=v_j/\sigma_j$.

The equation $H_A(x,y)=0$ is equivalent to $Ay=0$ and $A^*x=0$, so $\ker H_A=\ker(A^*)\oplus\ker(A)$. Together with step 1.2, the nonzero eigenvalue magnitudes are exactly the positive singular values, each appearing with both signs. Thus when there is positive rank their maximum-to-minimum ratio is unchanged.

The vectors from step 1.2 together with orthonormal bases of $\ker(A^*)$ and $\ker(A)$ form an orthonormal eigenbasis of the direct sum. Define $G$ on this basis by $Gw_{j,+}=w_{j,+}/\sigma_j$, $Gw_{j,-}=-w_{j,-}/\sigma_j$, and $G=0$ on the kernel. Then $H_AG$ and $GH_A$ are self-adjoint projections, while diagonal multiplication gives $H_AGH_A=H_A$ and $GH_AG=G$. Thus $G$ satisfies [F3], and uniqueness gives $G=H_A^+$. Since $(u_j,0)=(w_{j,+}+w_{j,-})/\sqrt2$, this definition gives $H_A^+(u_j,0)=(0,v_j/\sigma_j)$. Complete the positive left singular vectors to the left singular basis from [F1]. The remaining basis vectors have zero singular coordinates, so the diagonal SVD gives $A^*u_j=0$ for each; hence they span the complementary part $\ker(A^*)$. Thus every $b\in\mathbb C^m$ has a decomposition $b=\sum_{j:\sigma_j>0}\beta_j u_j+b_0$ with $b_0\in\ker(A^*)$. Applying the positive-pair calculation to the other summands gives $H_A^+(b,0)=(0,A^+b)$ for arbitrary $b$, including $b\notin\operatorname{ran}(A)$.

columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.

derivations.claim: In the eigenbasis from [F1], if $H u_j=\lambda_j u_j$, self-adjointness and [F5] give $$\lambda_j\|u_j\|^2=\langle Hu_j,u_j\rangle=\langle u_j,H^*u_j\rangle=\langle u_j,Hu_j\rangle=\overline{\lambda_j}\|u_j\|^2,$$ so every $\lambda_j$ is real. Define $G u_j=\lambda_j^{-1}u_j$ for $\lambda_j\ne0$ and $G u_j=0$ for $\lambda_j=0$. Diagonal multiplication gives $HGH=H$, $GHG=G$, and $HG=GH$ equal to the orthogonal projection onto the nonzero-eigenvalue span; both products are self-adjoint. Thus $G$ satisfies [F2], and uniqueness gives $H^+=G$.

Expand $|b\rangle=\sum_j\beta_j|u_j\rangle$ in [F1], with $\sum_j|\beta_j|^2=1$. Every nonzero coefficient has $|\lambda_j|\ge1/\kappa$, so [F3] multiplies it by $(2\kappa\lambda_j)^{-1}$. Step 1.1 therefore gives the well vector $v=\sum_j\beta_j(2\kappa\lambda_j)^{-1}|u_j\rangle=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$. Its normalization is the state in [F4].

Orthonormality gives $p=\sum_j|\beta_j|^2/(4\kappa^2|\lambda_j|^2)$. Since $1\le|\lambda_j|^{-1}\le\kappa$, each weight factor lies in $[1/(4\kappa^2),1/4]$. Their convex average lies in the same interval, proving $1/(4\kappa^2)\le p\le1/4$.

The probability that all rounds fail is at most $\rho$. The conditional well state in every successful round is the same pure-state ray as the normalized well component of $V|0\rangle$. The total number of $V,V^\dagger$ calls is at most $2RK$.

Input a self-adjoint $H$ with $\|H\|\le1$, a unit input state $|b\rangle$ supported only on eigenvalues satisfying $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, and a supplied finite exact representation of the cutoff $\kappa\ge1$ that supports certified arithmetic and rational comparisons. Supply costed $B,B^\dagger$ and controlled/inverse simulation access as in [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]]. The accuracy and failure inputs are exact rational values $\epsilon=p_\epsilon/q_\epsilon$ and $\rho=p_\rho/q_\rho$, with positive binary-encoded integers and $0<p_\epsilon<q_\epsilon$, $0<p_\rho<q_\rho$. Rectangular systems $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ use [[lem-qa-26-hermitian-dilation]]: choose a supplied rational scale $\Lambda\ge\|H_A\|$, use $H=H_A/\Lambda$, and set $\kappa=\Lambda/\gamma$ from the QLSP support gap $\gamma$. The QLSP definition supplies $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$ whenever the left singular coefficient of $b$ is nonzero; the dilation eigenvalues on this input support are $\pm\sigma_j/\Lambda$, so $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$. On $(\mathbb C^m\otimes W)\oplus(\mathbb C^n\otimes W)$ prepare the normalized codomain-supported input $(b/\|b\|,0)$ with the tagged preparation $B_A:=B\oplus I_{\mathbb C^n\otimes W}$. Implement its $B$ block with the supplied tag-controlled form of $B$ and charge that controlled preparation cost. The QLSP promise $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)$ removes the kernel component, and the output is tagged in the domain summand. All parameter comparisons, reversible arithmetic and finite-precision synthesis use the separately charged routines in the access model. The algorithm is the finite OP5 program:

1. Apply the supplied $B$ (or $B_A$ for a rectangular system) to prepare the input and its fixed work state, set $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, choose the least power of two $T\ge8(t_0+1)$ by certified comparisons, and let $L=\log_2T$. Initialize the phase register to $|0^L\rangle$ in big-endian order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$. This carrier chooses OP5's explicit table variant for preparing [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]]. Build the complete binary prefix tree on the $T$ leaves. At each level $\ell=0,\ldots,L-1$ and for each interval node $[a,b)$ at that level, put $m=(a+b)/2$ and compute the child masses $W_T(a,m)$ and $W_T(m,b)$ from the formula in that definition. Store $r=W_T(a,m)/W_T(a,b)$ and apply $R_y(2\arcsin\sqrt r)$ to wire $q_{L-1-\ell}$, controlled on the preceding $\ell$ wires matching the path to $[a,b)$; encode bit $1$ as the left child and bit $0$ as the right child. The root has no controls. Thus the ideal circuit prepares $|\Psi_T\rangle$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]]. Put $\epsilon_\Psi=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. Each nonempty mass is at least $T^{-2}$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Use certified interval arithmetic with absolute mass error at most $\epsilon_\Psi^2/(10^6L^2T^4)$; refine until each stored angle and its finite gate synthesis together give controlled-rotation operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi/(100T)$. The cases $r=0$ and $r=1$ use the identity and $\pi$ rotations, respectively. Store each other angle with at least $\lceil\log_2(100\pi T/\epsilon_\Psi)\rceil+2$ bits. There are $T-1$ rotations; [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]] bounds their total operator error by $\epsilon_\Psi/100$ from the displayed combined per-node operator tolerance. The table contains $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations. Charge its one-time construction/data cost $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ and each forward/inverse preparation cost $C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ from [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]], including reversible lookup, control and finite gate synthesis. Thus the sine-preparation unitary and its inverse each have operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi$; this variant pays linear-in-$T$ table and rotation resources rather than assuming a loaded amplitude table.

2. In either the original full-space or alternative clean-workspace simulation mode, initialize all simulator work in zero and retain it coherently. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, set $t_j=2^jt_0/T$ and allocate $\eta_j=\epsilon/(8192\kappa L)$ to both its forward controlled call $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ and its reverse call. Apply the negative-sign QFT, decode $y$ to signed $k=y$ for $y<T/2$ and $k=y-T$ otherwise, and set $\widetilde\lambda=2\pi k/t_0$. The total forward evolution time is $\sum_{j<L}t_j=t_0(1-1/T)<t_0$, and the sum of the $2L$ simulation error allocations is $\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. This uses the signed convention in [[lem-qa-26-phase-to-eigenvalue-unwrapping]].

3. Reversibly compute the flag angles and sign from $\widetilde\lambda$ using [[def-qa-26-hhl-reciprocal-filter]]. Use the two-qubit computational basis $|q_1q_0\rangle$ with labels $|\mathrm{nothing}\rangle=|00\rangle$, $|\mathrm{well}\rangle=|01\rangle$, $|\mathrm{ill}\rangle=|10\rangle$, and unused label $|11\rangle$. Write $p=|f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|$, $r=\sqrt{1-p^2}$, $\alpha=2\arcsin p$, and $\beta=2\arcsin(g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)/r)$. These are defined at every decoded grid point because [[lem-qa-26-hhl-filter-geometry]] gives $p\le1/2$, $0\le g\le1/2$, and $r\ge\sqrt3/2$, so $g/r\le1/\sqrt3<1$. First apply $R_y(\alpha)$ to $q_0$ conditioned on $q_1=0$, acting as identity on the $q_1=1$ subspace. Next apply $R_y(\beta)$ to $q_1$ conditioned on $q_0=0$, acting as identity on the $q_0=1$ subspace. Here $R_y(\theta)=\exp(-i\theta Y/2)$ with the exact convention and unitary formula of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and [[thm-qc-axis-rotation-pauli-formula]]. Finally apply $D_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,s,1,1)$ in the ordered flag basis, where $s=-1$ if $\widetilde\lambda<0$ and $s=+1$ otherwise (in particular at zero, where $f_\kappa(0)=0$). All three factors fix the unused label $|11\rangle$. 4. Reverse the QFT, every actual controlled simulation circuit, and sine preparation, retaining the flag and all simulator work. This gives a unitary flagged preparation $V$ and its exact circuit inverse $V^\dagger$. Let $\Pi_{\rm good}$ be the well-flag projection in Hermitian mode and the product of the well-flag projection and tagged domain projection in rectangular mode; these two projections act on distinct registers and commute. Let $p=\|\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle\|^2$. Apply the finite capped amplification procedure proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-capped-amplification]] with success projection $\Pi_{\rm good}$, lower bound $p_{\mathrm{low}}=1/(16\kappa^2)$ and failure target $\rho$. Its success reflection and verification test both the well flag and the domain tag in rectangular mode; charge their actual costs to $C_{\rm ref}$ and $C_{\rm ver}$. Measure $\{\Pi_{\rm good},I-\Pi_{\rm good}\}$ and return the conditional state, tagged output and success bit on success; return FAIL otherwise.

The circuit uses no uniform-register phase-tail estimate: its phase distribution is the sine-window kernel proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-kernel-moment]]. Its $G_\Psi,C_\Psi,C_{\rm sim},C_{\rm QFT}^{+/-},C_{\rm flag}$, reflection, verification and $B/B^\dagger$ costs remain separate inputs.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.
