No matrix description supplies a circuit, oracle, controlled call, inverse call, or term exponential for free; uniform-family and cost conventions are those of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]], [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]], [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]]. No polynomial resource bound is asserted by this definition.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

For a Hermitian $H$ on a finite-dimensional register, with operator norm as in [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]], the **HHL access instance** supplies: (i) a unitary $B$ with $B|0_{I,W}\rangle=|b/\|b\|\rangle_I|g_B\rangle_W$ for a fixed normalized work state $|g_B\rangle$ (which may be $|0_W\rangle$) and declared costs for $B,B^\dagger$ and any controlled forms used; (ii) for every requested real $t$ and tolerance $\eta$, a controlled simulation circuit $S_H(t,\eta)$ with operator-norm error at most $\eta$ from $e^{+iHt}$, and separately declared inverse/negative-time costs; and (iii) separate actual resource functions $C_B,C_{B^\dagger}$, $C_{\rm sim}(t,\eta)$, $C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ for each forward or inverse sine-table preparation, $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ for its one-time classical table generation/data bits, $C_{\rm QFT}^{+/-}(T)$, $C_{\rm flag}(\kappa,\eta_R)$, $C_{\rm arith}(T,\kappa,\epsilon)$, $C_{\rm ref}$, and $C_{\rm ver}$, and costs for reversible arithmetic, registers and finite-precision gate synthesis. Here $C_{\rm QFT}^{-}$ is the negative-sign Fourier circuit and $C_{\rm QFT}^{+}$ its positive-sign inverse, $C_{\rm arith}$ is the per-attempt reversible decode/filter arithmetic cost, and $C_{\rm ref},C_{\rm ver}$ are the per-call reflection and well-verification costs. These functions count the stated circuit implementation in the chosen gate/access model; they assert no polylogarithmic bound on table generation or rotation synthesis. The positive exponential sign is the OP5 convention. An implementation of $H$ from matrix entries or a sparse oracle is additional data and must include its own proof and cost. A bare matrix, sparsity promise, or list of amplitudes is not a circuit. A rational scale $\Lambda\ge\|H\|$ may be supplied; after replacing $H$ by $H/\Lambda$, the supported gap $\gamma$ gives $\kappa=\Lambda/\gamma$.

**Clean-workspace simulation mode.** The original full-operator-norm access mode remains admissible. Alternatively, supply a unitary dilation $S$ with a fixed clean-work embedding $J$ and $\|SJ-Je^{+iHt}\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$, including arbitrary timing/control/reference registers. The ideal operation leaves this simulator workspace in zero; other ideal HHL operations do not touch it. Actual output work may be dirty. Supply actual circuit inverses and controls and charge their full workspace and query costs. [[lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid]] proves the same clean-input error for the actual adjoint, coherent controls and arbitrary references, and proves accumulation along the ideal all-clean trajectory. The inverse used in HHL uncomputation/amplification is the literal reverse physical circuit, not a separately approximated negative-time routine. Include simulator work in the joint output comparison and the ideal all-zero algorithm registers. A full-space error on arbitrary dirty inputs is neither required nor inferred in this alternative mode.

derivations.claim: The geometric sum of forward times is $\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}2^jt_0/T=(T-1)t_0/T<t_0$. The reverse list has the same absolute times, so one $V$ or $V^\dagger$ call uses less than $2t_0$. By [F2], there are at most $RK$ calls in each direction, giving total absolute time below $4RKt_0$. Since $K\le5\kappa$, $R\le16\ln(1/\rho)+17$, and $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, the stated order follows.

Each $V$ or $V^\dagger$ circuit contains one forward and one inverse QFT, two sine-table circuits, one flag circuit, and one forward/reverse simulation list by [F1]. Multiplying their actual counts by the separate cost functions in [F3] gives the displayed additive charge; the fixed table $G_\Psi$ is generated once, and every B, inverse B, reflection, and verifier use is counted in its own coordinate.

citations.quote: For the ideal exact-eigenvalue version of [[alg-qa-26-hhl-phase-estimation]], on a normalized $|b\rangle$ supported on $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, the well-flag vector is $v=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$. Its probability $p=\|v\|^2$ satisfies $1/(4\kappa^2)\le p\le1/4$, and its normalized state is the QLSP target.

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

derivations.claim: Under the absolute-error alternative, the reverse triangle inequality from [F2] gives $\|u\|\ge\|v\|-\|u-v\|\ge(1/2-1/8)/\kappa=3/(8\kappa)>0$. Under the relative alternative, $\|u\|\ge(1-9\epsilon/100)\|v\|>0$ because $9\epsilon/100<1$. Thus both normalizations exist.

Add and subtract $u/\|v\|$ and use [F2]: $$\left\|\frac{u}{\|u\|}-\frac{v}{\|v\|}\right\|\le\frac{|\|v\|-\|u\||}{\|v\|}+\frac{\|u-v\|}{\|v\|}\le\frac{2\|u-v\|}{\|v\|}.$$ The absolute alternative makes this at most $2(\epsilon/(8\kappa))/(1/(2\kappa))=\epsilon/2$. The relative alternative makes it at most $18\epsilon/100<\epsilon$.

citations.quote: For the ideal exact-eigenvalue version of [[alg-qa-26-hhl-phase-estimation]], on a normalized $|b\rangle$ supported on $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, the well-flag vector is $v=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$. Its probability $p=\|v\|^2$ satisfies $1/(4\kappa^2)\le p\le1/4$, and its normalized state is the QLSP target.

Let $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, $0<\epsilon\le1$, $\kappa\ge1$, and let $T$ be the least power of two at least $8(t_0+1)$. For any $\lambda\in[-1,1]$, prepare [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]], apply the controlled phases $e^{i\lambda\tau t_0/T}$ and the negative-sign Fourier transform, then decode $y$ to signed $k$. With probability $p_k(\lambda)$, put $\delta_k=\lambda t_0-2\pi k$. Then
$$\sum_{k=-T/2}^{T/2-1}p_k(\lambda)\,\delta_k^2<300.$$

Let $\kappa\ge1$, $t_0>0$, and $\lambda,\delta\in\mathbb R$ with $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$. Set $\widetilde\lambda=\lambda-\delta/t_0$. For the well/ill amplitude pair $m(z)=(f_\kappa(z),g_\kappa(z))$ from [[def-qa-26-hhl-reciprocal-filter]],
$$\|m(\widetilde\lambda)-m(\lambda)\|_2\le10\kappa\frac{|\delta|}{t_0}|f_\kappa(\lambda)|.$$

Let a unitary flagged preparation $V$ have well probability $p\ge p_0:=1/(16\kappa^2)$, $\kappa\ge1$, and exact inverse access. Set $K=\lceil4\kappa\rceil$, $R=\lceil16\ln(1/\rho)\rceil+16$ for $0<\rho<1$. In each of $R$ fresh rounds, draw $b=\lceil\log_2K\rceil$ uniform bits; reject the round without queries if the resulting integer $j\ge K$, and otherwise run $j$ amplitude-amplification iterations from $V|0\rangle$, then verify the well flag. The probability that all rounds fail is at most $\rho$. The conditional well state in every successful round is the same pure-state ray as the normalized well component of $V|0\rangle$. The total number of $V,V^\dagger$ calls is at most $2RK$.

Let $v$ be an ideal flagged vector with $\|v\|\ge1/(2\kappa)$. If $0<\epsilon\le1$ and either $\|u-v\|\le\epsilon/(8\kappa)$ or $\|u-v\|\le(9\epsilon/100)\|v\|$, then $u\ne0$ and $\|u/\|u\|-v/\|v\|\|\le\epsilon$.

Input a self-adjoint $H$ with $\|H\|\le1$, a unit input state $|b\rangle$ supported only on eigenvalues satisfying $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, and a supplied finite exact representation of the cutoff $\kappa\ge1$ that supports certified arithmetic and rational comparisons. Supply costed $B,B^\dagger$ and controlled/inverse simulation access as in [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]]. The accuracy and failure inputs are exact rational values $\epsilon=p_\epsilon/q_\epsilon$ and $\rho=p_\rho/q_\rho$, with positive binary-encoded integers and $0<p_\epsilon<q_\epsilon$, $0<p_\rho<q_\rho$. Rectangular systems $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ use [[lem-qa-26-hermitian-dilation]]: choose a supplied rational scale $\Lambda\ge\|H_A\|$, use $H=H_A/\Lambda$, and set $\kappa=\Lambda/\gamma$ from the QLSP support gap $\gamma$. The QLSP definition supplies $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$ whenever the left singular coefficient of $b$ is nonzero; the dilation eigenvalues on this input support are $\pm\sigma_j/\Lambda$, so $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$. On $(\mathbb C^m\otimes W)\oplus(\mathbb C^n\otimes W)$ prepare the normalized codomain-supported input $(b/\|b\|,0)$ with the tagged preparation $B_A:=B\oplus I_{\mathbb C^n\otimes W}$. Implement its $B$ block with the supplied tag-controlled form of $B$ and charge that controlled preparation cost. The QLSP promise $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)$ removes the kernel component, and the output is tagged in the domain summand. All parameter comparisons, reversible arithmetic and finite-precision synthesis use the separately charged routines in the access model. The algorithm is the finite OP5 program:

1. Apply the supplied $B$ (or $B_A$ for a rectangular system) to prepare the input and its fixed work state, set $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, choose the least power of two $T\ge8(t_0+1)$ by certified comparisons, and let $L=\log_2T$. Initialize the phase register to $|0^L\rangle$ in big-endian order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$. This carrier chooses OP5's explicit table variant for preparing [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]]. Build the complete binary prefix tree on the $T$ leaves. At each level $\ell=0,\ldots,L-1$ and for each interval node $[a,b)$ at that level, put $m=(a+b)/2$ and compute the child masses $W_T(a,m)$ and $W_T(m,b)$ from the formula in that definition. Store $r=W_T(a,m)/W_T(a,b)$ and apply $R_y(2\arcsin\sqrt r)$ to wire $q_{L-1-\ell}$, controlled on the preceding $\ell$ wires matching the path to $[a,b)$; encode bit $1$ as the left child and bit $0$ as the right child. The root has no controls. Thus the ideal circuit prepares $|\Psi_T\rangle$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]]. Put $\epsilon_\Psi=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. Each nonempty mass is at least $T^{-2}$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Use certified interval arithmetic with absolute mass error at most $\epsilon_\Psi^2/(10^6L^2T^4)$; refine until each stored angle and its finite gate synthesis together give controlled-rotation operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi/(100T)$. The cases $r=0$ and $r=1$ use the identity and $\pi$ rotations, respectively. Store each other angle with at least $\lceil\log_2(100\pi T/\epsilon_\Psi)\rceil+2$ bits. There are $T-1$ rotations; [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]] bounds their total operator error by $\epsilon_\Psi/100$ from the displayed combined per-node operator tolerance. The table contains $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations. Charge its one-time construction/data cost $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ and each forward/inverse preparation cost $C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ from [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]], including reversible lookup, control and finite gate synthesis. Thus the sine-preparation unitary and its inverse each have operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi$; this variant pays linear-in-$T$ table and rotation resources rather than assuming a loaded amplitude table.

2. In either the original full-space or alternative clean-workspace simulation mode, initialize all simulator work in zero and retain it coherently. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, set $t_j=2^jt_0/T$ and allocate $\eta_j=\epsilon/(8192\kappa L)$ to both its forward controlled call $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ and its reverse call. Apply the negative-sign QFT, decode $y$ to signed $k=y$ for $y<T/2$ and $k=y-T$ otherwise, and set $\widetilde\lambda=2\pi k/t_0$. The total forward evolution time is $\sum_{j<L}t_j=t_0(1-1/T)<t_0$, and the sum of the $2L$ simulation error allocations is $\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. This uses the signed convention in [[lem-qa-26-phase-to-eigenvalue-unwrapping]].

3. Reversibly compute the flag angles and sign from $\widetilde\lambda$ using [[def-qa-26-hhl-reciprocal-filter]]. Use the two-qubit computational basis $|q_1q_0\rangle$ with labels $|\mathrm{nothing}\rangle=|00\rangle$, $|\mathrm{well}\rangle=|01\rangle$, $|\mathrm{ill}\rangle=|10\rangle$, and unused label $|11\rangle$. Write $p=|f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|$, $r=\sqrt{1-p^2}$, $\alpha=2\arcsin p$, and $\beta=2\arcsin(g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)/r)$. These are defined at every decoded grid point because [[lem-qa-26-hhl-filter-geometry]] gives $p\le1/2$, $0\le g\le1/2$, and $r\ge\sqrt3/2$, so $g/r\le1/\sqrt3<1$. First apply $R_y(\alpha)$ to $q_0$ conditioned on $q_1=0$, acting as identity on the $q_1=1$ subspace. Next apply $R_y(\beta)$ to $q_1$ conditioned on $q_0=0$, acting as identity on the $q_0=1$ subspace. Here $R_y(\theta)=\exp(-i\theta Y/2)$ with the exact convention and unitary formula of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and [[thm-qc-axis-rotation-pauli-formula]]. Finally apply $D_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,s,1,1)$ in the ordered flag basis, where $s=-1$ if $\widetilde\lambda<0$ and $s=+1$ otherwise (in particular at zero, where $f_\kappa(0)=0$). The resulting full flag unitary is $D_sG_{02}(\beta)G_{01}(\alpha)$: the two conditional rotations act as $R_y$ on the indicated two-label subspaces and as identity on their orthogonal complements, and $D_s$ is diagonal unitary. All three factors fix the unused label $|11\rangle$. On $|00\rangle$ the product gives $h(\widetilde\lambda)|00\rangle+f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|01\rangle+g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|10\rangle$, since $\cos(\beta/2)=h/r$ and $\sin(\beta/2)=g/r$. Uncompute the arithmetic. Synthesize the phase-controlled map with uniform operator error at most $\eta_R:=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$, charged through $C_{\rm flag}$ and $C_{\rm arith}$.

4. Reverse the QFT, every actual controlled simulation circuit, and sine preparation, retaining the flag and all simulator work. In clean-workspace mode the ideal trajectory has this work in zero; [[lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid]] bounds the complete attempt on that ideal trajectory without assuming actual intermediate work is clean. This gives a unitary flagged preparation $V$ and its exact circuit inverse $V^\dagger$. Let $\Pi_{\rm good}$ be the well-flag projection in Hermitian mode and the product of the well-flag projection and tagged domain projection in rectangular mode; these two projections act on distinct registers and commute. Let $p=\|\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle\|^2$. Apply the finite capped amplification procedure proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-capped-amplification]] with success projection $\Pi_{\rm good}$, lower bound $p_{\mathrm{low}}=1/(16\kappa^2)$ and failure target $\rho$. Its success reflection and verification test both the well flag and the domain tag in rectangular mode; charge their actual costs to $C_{\rm ref}$ and $C_{\rm ver}$. Measure $\{\Pi_{\rm good},I-\Pi_{\rm good}\}$ and return the conditional state, tagged output and success bit on success; return FAIL otherwise.

The circuit uses no uniform-register phase-tail estimate: its phase distribution is the sine-window kernel proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-kernel-moment]]. Its $G_\Psi,C_\Psi,C_{\rm sim},C_{\rm QFT}^{+/-},C_{\rm flag}$, reflection, verification and $B/B^\dagger$ costs remain separate inputs.

Let $T=2^L\ge2$, and let $W_T(a,b)$ and $|\Psi_T\rangle$ be as in [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]]. In the binary prefix tree, order the register bits from root to leaf. At level $\ell=0,\ldots,L-1$, each interval node $[a,b)$ has midpoint $m=(a+b)/2$ and split $r=W_T(a,m)/W_T(a,b)$. Apply $R_y(2\arcsin\sqrt r)$ to the next bit, controlled on the preceding prefix that names $[a,b)$, encoding bit $1$ as the left child and bit $0$ as the right child. Starting from $|0^L\rangle$, this ideal prefix circuit prepares $|\Psi_T\rangle$. If a finite state-preparation circuit contains $N$ controlled $Y$ rotations and each implemented rotation differs from its ideal rotation by operator norm at most $\delta$, the product unitary differs from the ideal product by operator norm at most $N\delta$. In the OP5 table variant $N=T-1$ and $\delta=\epsilon_\Psi/(100T)$, so the preparation error is less than $\epsilon_\Psi/100$; using the same bound for its inverse gives the stated unpreparation cost.

Let $J:H\to K$ be an isometry of nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, $V$ a unitary on $H$, and $U$ a unitary on $K$. If $\|UJ-JV\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$, then $\|U^*J-JV^*\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$. The same inequalities hold after adjoining an arbitrary finite reference space or coherently controlling $U$ and $V$ against identity.

More generally, let $U_1,\ldots,U_s$ be actual unitaries on $K$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_s$ ideal unitaries on $H$, with $\|U_jJ-JV_j\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j$. Then
$$\|U_s\cdots U_1J-JV_s\cdots V_1\|_{\rm op}\le\sum_{j=1}^s\eta_j.$$
The empty products give zero error. Each bound concerns the clean input subspace $\operatorname{ran}J$; none assumes that an actual intermediate state belongs to that subspace or claims a full-space approximation on arbitrary dirty-work inputs.

For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, define $H_A:\mathbb C^m\oplus\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m\oplus\mathbb C^n$ using the adjoint $A^*$ of [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]] by $H_A(x,y)=(Ay,A^*x)$. Then $H_A$ is Hermitian; its nonzero eigenvalues are $+\sigma_j,-\sigma_j$ for the positive singular values of $A$, its kernel is $\ker(A^*)\oplus\ker(A)$, and $H_A^+(b,0)=(0,A^+b)$. When $A$ has positive rank, its nonzero condition number is preserved; the output is tagged in the domain summand.

derivations.claim: First take the exact sine preparation, exact simulations and exact flag rotation. Before reversing phase estimation, different decoded labels are orthogonal. For a fixed eigenvalue $\lambda$, the well-flag projection keeps only the $f_\kappa$ coordinate, so the squared error is $$\sum_y p_y(\lambda)\,|f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda_y)-f_\kappa(\lambda)|^2\le\sum_y p_y(\lambda)\,\|m(\widetilde\lambda_y)-m(\lambda)\|_2^2.$$ By [F2] and [F3], this is at most $(10\kappa/t_0)^2\,300\,|f_\kappa(\lambda)|^2$. Summing with the eigenbasis weights shows that the exact-kernel well vector differs from $v$ by at most $(10\sqrt{300}\kappa/t_0)\|v\|$. Reversing the phase transform is unitary and preserves this norm bound.

Replacing the exact preparation, simulations and flag map by their implementations changes the attempt on its clean initial input by at most the sum of their norm errors. In the full-space mode this is ordinary unitary telescoping; in the clean-workspace mode [F7] applies because all ideal other gates leave simulator work untouched and ideal simulations return it to zero. The actual intermediate work need not be clean. In either mode the sum consists of two sine-table preparation uses, the total forward/reverse simulation budget, and one flag map, at most $4\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. The success projection is contractive and fixes $v$: in rectangular mode this follows from [F8], and otherwise it is just the well flag. Applying it to both the exact-kernel comparison and the implementation error therefore gives $$\frac{\|u-v\|}{\|v\|}\le\frac{10\sqrt{300}\kappa}{t_0}+\frac{4\epsilon/(4096\kappa)}{1/(2\kappa)}<\left(\frac{180}{2048}+\frac{1}{512}\right)\epsilon<0.09\epsilon=:q,$$ using $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$ and $\sqrt{300}<18$. Hence $\|u\|\ge(1-q)\|v\|>1/(4\kappa)$ and the implemented well probability exceeds $1/(16\kappa^2)$.

The exact filter on supported eigenvalues is $v=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$, so $v/\|v\|$ is the target. The normalization inequality in [L1] applies because step 2.1 gives relative error below $0.09\epsilon$: directly, $\|u/\|u\|-v/\|v\|\|\le2q/(1-q)<\epsilon$. By [F4], every successful amplified branch is the same ray as $u/\|u\|$; choose the representative $u/\|u\|$ to obtain the stated distance. The preparation work factors as $|g_B\rangle$ and is untouched by the HHL circuit; the ideal uncomputation leaves the other algorithmic registers zero and the measured flag in $|\mathrm{well}\rangle$. Tensoring these unit vectors does not change any norm above. For a rectangular map with $H=H_A/\Lambda$ and $\Lambda>0$, [[lem-qa-26-hermitian-dilation]] gives $H_A^+(b,0)=(0,A^+b)$; the singular values of the scaled dilation are $\sigma_j/\Lambda$, so $H^+(b,0)=\Lambda(0,A^+b)$. This positive scalar cancels on normalization, leaving the ideal QLSP ray in the tagged domain summand. The actual successful vector $u$ also lies in that summand because $\Pi_{\rm good}$ includes its domain projection. Tracing out work gives the corresponding output density state.

boundaries.reason: The OP5 input is a normalized supported state; an empty supported eigenspace cannot supply it.

citations.quote: Let $H$ have the exact sorted $d$-sparse Hermitian XOR-location/value interface of [[def-qa-20-sparse-hamiltonian-oracle-model]], with $N,d\ge1$. An optional support-list variant is also admissible: each row lists at most $d$ distinct columns in strictly increasing order, contains every nonzero column exactly once, and may additionally list zero-valued columns. Its row and column support lists agree under transposition; in the Hermitian case the row list at $j$ supplies the column list at $j$. The total XOR value oracle gives the exact decoded matrix, including any listed zeros. Missing slots use the same distinguished sentinel. No zero test on the matrix values is needed to form a supplied support union. An approximation to a different target matrix requires a separate operator-error bound. Put $M=2^{\lceil\log_2(N+d)\rceil}$ and $\widetilde H=H\oplus0$ on the $M$-label register. Given a positive certified bound $h\ge\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$, an exact costed preparation $d^{-1/2}\sum_{l<d}|l\rangle$, and costed exact value-decoding and flag-rotation arithmetic, one can construct a unitary whose clean block is $\widetilde H/(dh)$. It and its actual adjoint and coherent controlled versions use $O(\log(d+1))$ QA20 location calls and $O(1)$ value calls each. Index bits, reversible workspace, search arithmetic, comparisons, uniform preparation, flags and gate precision remain separately charged. In particular $h=1$ is admissible when $\|H\|_{\rm op}\le1$, without computing the global maximum entry. The stronger separately supplied in-place-location interface keeps its original constant location-call count.

Let $\tau=\alpha|t|$ and $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)$, with $0<\epsilon<1$. In the nontrivial branch $\tau>\epsilon$, put $S=\tau+L/\ln(e+L/\tau)$. The small-time-aware simulator of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]] uses zero signal queries when $\tau\le\epsilon$. When $\tau>\epsilon$, the OP4 degree satisfies $d=O(S)$. The complete OAA circuit uses at most $3(d_E+d_O)\le6d$ ordinary $U/U^*$ signal calls, where $d_E,d_O\le d$ are the even and odd QSP degrees. It uses $3(d_E+d_O+2)$ projector-phase slots and therefore $6(d_E+d_O+2)$ controlled-reflection calls, by [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. Coherent selection of each real sequence against identity uses exactly one controlled signal call when that sequence degree is odd and none when it is even; because the selection occurs in each of the three OAA blocks $W,W^*,W$, the total is $3(\mathbf1_{d_E\text{ odd}}+\mathbf1_{d_O\text{ odd}})\le6$ controlled signal calls. The $\Phi/-\Phi$ branch itself controls phases, not signal calls. Any external control of the complete simulator controls and charges the whole block.

Gate, depth, width, ancilla, classical bit, precision, PREPARE/SELECT, phase-list-generation, and sparse-location/value costs remain separate coordinates. For a $d_H$-row-sparse input with supplied-permutation bound $h\ge h_{\max}$, the $h=0$ branch encodes $H=0$ with normalization $1$ and uses no location or value calls. If $h>0$, [[thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding-correctness]] gives normalization $\alpha=d_Hh$; choosing the tight bound $h=h_{\max}$ gives $\alpha=d_Hh_{\max}$. Multiply the signal-query count by the actual supplied sparse-encoding cost, including any location-permutation completion. The optional sorted-XOR mode has the same normalization $d_Hh$ for a supplied positive entry bound $h$ and multiplies the signal count by $O(\log(d_H+1))$ location calls and $O(1)$ value calls per signal, including inverses and coherent controls. No cost-free conversion from XOR row-location access is claimed. If $\tau$ is bounded above and below by positive constants as $\epsilon\to0$, the query bound specializes to $O(\tau+L/\ln L)=O(\tau+\ln(1/\epsilon)/\ln\ln(1/\epsilon))$. This is an upper bound; no matching lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access or for the additive precision term is asserted.

For every promised input of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]], a successful output satisfies the clean-input isometry error bound $\|V_{\rm impl}J_{\rm clean}-J_{\rm out}e^{-itH}\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon$. It also satisfies the corresponding reference-system trace-distance bound after tracing the work registers.

Let $J:H\to K$ be an isometry of nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, $V$ a unitary on $H$, and $U$ a unitary on $K$. If $\|UJ-JV\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$, then $\|U^*J-JV^*\|_{\rm op}\le\eta$. The same inequalities hold after adjoining an arbitrary finite reference space or coherently controlling $U$ and $V$ against identity.

More generally, let $U_1,\ldots,U_s$ be actual unitaries on $K$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_s$ ideal unitaries on $H$, with $\|U_jJ-JV_j\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j$. Then
$$\|U_s\cdots U_1J-JV_s\cdots V_1\|_{\rm op}\le\sum_{j=1}^s\eta_j.$$
The empty products give zero error. Each bound concerns the clean input subspace $\operatorname{ran}J$; none assumes that an actual intermediate state belongs to that subspace or claims a full-space approximation on arbitrary dirty-work inputs.

Input a self-adjoint $H$ with $\|H\|\le1$, a unit input state $|b\rangle$ supported only on eigenvalues satisfying $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, and a supplied finite exact representation of the cutoff $\kappa\ge1$ that supports certified arithmetic and rational comparisons. Supply costed $B,B^\dagger$ and controlled/inverse simulation access as in [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]]. The accuracy and failure inputs are exact rational values $\epsilon=p_\epsilon/q_\epsilon$ and $\rho=p_\rho/q_\rho$, with positive binary-encoded integers and $0<p_\epsilon<q_\epsilon$, $0<p_\rho<q_\rho$. Rectangular systems $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ use [[lem-qa-26-hermitian-dilation]]: choose a supplied rational scale $\Lambda\ge\|H_A\|$, use $H=H_A/\Lambda$, and set $\kappa=\Lambda/\gamma$ from the QLSP support gap $\gamma$. The QLSP definition supplies $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$ whenever the left singular coefficient of $b$ is nonzero; the dilation eigenvalues on this input support are $\pm\sigma_j/\Lambda$, so $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$. On $(\mathbb C^m\otimes W)\oplus(\mathbb C^n\otimes W)$ prepare the normalized codomain-supported input $(b/\|b\|,0)$ with the tagged preparation $B_A:=B\oplus I_{\mathbb C^n\otimes W}$. Implement its $B$ block with the supplied tag-controlled form of $B$ and charge that controlled preparation cost. The QLSP promise $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)$ removes the kernel component, and the output is tagged in the domain summand. All parameter comparisons, reversible arithmetic and finite-precision synthesis use the separately charged routines in the access model. The algorithm is the finite OP5 program:

1. Apply the supplied $B$ (or $B_A$ for a rectangular system) to prepare the input and its fixed work state, set $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, choose the least power of two $T\ge8(t_0+1)$ by certified comparisons, and let $L=\log_2T$. Initialize the phase register to $|0^L\rangle$ in big-endian order $q_{L-1}\cdots q_0$. This carrier chooses OP5's explicit table variant for preparing [[def-qa-26-hhl-sine-window]]. Build the complete binary prefix tree on the $T$ leaves. At each level $\ell=0,\ldots,L-1$ and for each interval node $[a,b)$ at that level, put $m=(a+b)/2$ and compute the child masses $W_T(a,m)$ and $W_T(m,b)$ from the formula in that definition. Store $r=W_T(a,m)/W_T(a,b)$ and apply $R_y(2\arcsin\sqrt r)$ to wire $q_{L-1-\ell}$, controlled on the preceding $\ell$ wires matching the path to $[a,b)$; encode bit $1$ as the left child and bit $0$ as the right child. The root has no controls. Thus the ideal circuit prepares $|\Psi_T\rangle$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]]. Put $\epsilon_\Psi=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. Each nonempty mass is at least $T^{-2}$ by [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-prefix-masses]]. Use certified interval arithmetic with absolute mass error at most $\epsilon_\Psi^2/(10^6L^2T^4)$; refine until each stored angle and its finite gate synthesis together give controlled-rotation operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi/(100T)$. The cases $r=0$ and $r=1$ use the identity and $\pi$ rotations, respectively. Store each other angle with at least $\lceil\log_2(100\pi T/\epsilon_\Psi)\rceil+2$ bits. There are $T-1$ rotations; [[lem-qa-26-hhl-prefix-table-synthesis-error]] bounds their total operator error by $\epsilon_\Psi/100$ from the displayed combined per-node operator tolerance. The table contains $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations. Charge its one-time construction/data cost $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ and each forward/inverse preparation cost $C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$ from [[def-qa-26-hhl-access-model]], including reversible lookup, control and finite gate synthesis. Thus the sine-preparation unitary and its inverse each have operator error at most $\epsilon_\Psi$; this variant pays linear-in-$T$ table and rotation resources rather than assuming a loaded amplitude table.

2. In either the original full-space or alternative clean-workspace simulation mode, initialize all simulator work in zero and retain it coherently. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, set $t_j=2^jt_0/T$ and allocate $\eta_j=\epsilon/(8192\kappa L)$ to both its forward controlled call $S_H(t_j,\eta_j)$ and its reverse call. Apply the negative-sign QFT, decode $y$ to signed $k=y$ for $y<T/2$ and $k=y-T$ otherwise, and set $\widetilde\lambda=2\pi k/t_0$. The total forward evolution time is $\sum_{j<L}t_j=t_0(1-1/T)<t_0$, and the sum of the $2L$ simulation error allocations is $\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$. This uses the signed convention in [[lem-qa-26-phase-to-eigenvalue-unwrapping]].

3. Reversibly compute the flag angles and sign from $\widetilde\lambda$ using [[def-qa-26-hhl-reciprocal-filter]]. Use the two-qubit computational basis $|q_1q_0\rangle$ with labels $|\mathrm{nothing}\rangle=|00\rangle$, $|\mathrm{well}\rangle=|01\rangle$, $|\mathrm{ill}\rangle=|10\rangle$, and unused label $|11\rangle$. Write $p=|f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|$, $r=\sqrt{1-p^2}$, $\alpha=2\arcsin p$, and $\beta=2\arcsin(g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)/r)$. These are defined at every decoded grid point because [[lem-qa-26-hhl-filter-geometry]] gives $p\le1/2$, $0\le g\le1/2$, and $r\ge\sqrt3/2$, so $g/r\le1/\sqrt3<1$. First apply $R_y(\alpha)$ to $q_0$ conditioned on $q_1=0$, acting as identity on the $q_1=1$ subspace. Next apply $R_y(\beta)$ to $q_1$ conditioned on $q_0=0$, acting as identity on the $q_0=1$ subspace. Here $R_y(\theta)=\exp(-i\theta Y/2)$ with the exact convention and unitary formula of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and [[thm-qc-axis-rotation-pauli-formula]]. Finally apply $D_s=\operatorname{diag}(1,s,1,1)$ in the ordered flag basis, where $s=-1$ if $\widetilde\lambda<0$ and $s=+1$ otherwise (in particular at zero, where $f_\kappa(0)=0$). The resulting full flag unitary is $D_sG_{02}(\beta)G_{01}(\alpha)$: the two conditional rotations act as $R_y$ on the indicated two-label subspaces and as identity on their orthogonal complements, and $D_s$ is diagonal unitary. All three factors fix the unused label $|11\rangle$. On $|00\rangle$ the product gives $h(\widetilde\lambda)|00\rangle+f_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|01\rangle+g_\kappa(\widetilde\lambda)|10\rangle$, since $\cos(\beta/2)=h/r$ and $\sin(\beta/2)=g/r$. Uncompute the arithmetic. Synthesize the phase-controlled map with uniform operator error at most $\eta_R:=\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$, charged through $C_{\rm flag}$ and $C_{\rm arith}$.

4. Reverse the QFT, every actual controlled simulation circuit, and sine preparation, retaining the flag and all simulator work. In clean-workspace mode the ideal trajectory has this work in zero; [[lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid]] bounds the complete attempt on that ideal trajectory without assuming actual intermediate work is clean. This gives a unitary flagged preparation $V$ and its exact circuit inverse $V^\dagger$. Let $\Pi_{\rm good}$ be the well-flag projection in Hermitian mode and the product of the well-flag projection and tagged domain projection in rectangular mode; these two projections act on distinct registers and commute. Let $p=\|\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle\|^2$. Apply the finite capped amplification procedure proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-capped-amplification]] with success projection $\Pi_{\rm good}$, lower bound $p_{\mathrm{low}}=1/(16\kappa^2)$ and failure target $\rho$. Its success reflection and verification test both the well flag and the domain tag in rectangular mode; charge their actual costs to $C_{\rm ref}$ and $C_{\rm ver}$. Measure $\{\Pi_{\rm good},I-\Pi_{\rm good}\}$ and return the conditional state, tagged output and success bit on success; return FAIL otherwise.

The circuit uses no uniform-register phase-tail estimate: its phase distribution is the sine-window kernel proved in [[lem-qa-26-hhl-sine-window-kernel-moment]]. Its $G_\Psi,C_\Psi,C_{\rm sim},C_{\rm QFT}^{+/-},C_{\rm flag}$, reflection, verification and $B/B^\dagger$ costs remain separate inputs.

Let $L=\log_2T$, $t_j=2^jt_0/T$, $K=\lceil4\kappa\rceil$, and $R=\lceil16\ln(1/\rho)\rceil+16$. The capped HHL circuit uses at most $RK$ calls to each of $V$ and $V^\dagger$, at most $RK$ calls to each supplied preparation form (the tagged $B_A$ in dilation mode) and its inverse, and one table construction $G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)$. Each $V$ or $V^\dagger$ contains two sine-table preparation/unpreparation circuits, one forward and one inverse QFT, the flag circuit, and $2L$ controlled simulation calls at signed times $\pm t_j$; its absolute evolution times sum to less than $2t_0$. Therefore the total absolute simulation time is less than $4RKt_0=O(\kappa^2\epsilon^{-1}(1+\log(1/\rho)))$. More precisely, the simulation charge is the actual sum over all $V,V^\dagger$ calls of $\sum_{j<L}(C_{\rm sim}(t_j,\eta_j)+C_{\rm sim}(-t_j,\eta_j))$. The remaining charge is
$$G_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)+n_VC_B+n_{V^\dagger}C_{B^\dagger}+2(n_V+n_{V^\dagger})C_\Psi(T,\epsilon_\Psi)+(n_V+n_{V^\dagger})(C_{\rm QFT}^{+}(T)+C_{\rm QFT}^{-}(T)+C_{\rm flag}(\kappa,\eta_R)+C_{\rm arith}(T,\kappa,\epsilon))+N_{\rm ref}C_{\rm ref}+N_{\rm ver}C_{\rm ver},$$
where $n_V,n_{V^\dagger}\le RK$ and $N_{\rm ref},N_{\rm ver}$ are the actual reflection and verification counts. The table itself has $O(T\log(T/\epsilon_\Psi))$ data bits and $T-1$ controlled rotations; no polylogarithmic table-generation or finite-rotation synthesis bound is asserted.

Under the promises and precision allocations in [[alg-qa-26-hhl-phase-estimation]], let $u=\Pi_{\rm good}V|0\rangle$ be the actual joint success vector for one prepared attempt, where rectangular-mode success includes the domain-tag projection. Write $v_{\rm sys}=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$ and $v=v_{\rm sys}\otimes|g_B\rangle\otimes|0_{\rm alg}\rangle\otimes|\mathrm{well}\rangle$ for the ideal joint vector, including the unchanged preparation work and clean algorithmic registers. For $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $0<\rho<1$, the conditional returned joint pure-state ray (including unchanged preparation work) has a unit representative within vector norm $\epsilon$ of the normalized QLSP target tensored with the preparation work, clean algorithmic registers and well flag, and the capped amplification returns FAIL with probability at most $\rho$. The same assertion holds for the Hermitian dilation, with the output in its tagged domain summand.

Let $H$ be a self-adjoint endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex
inner-product space $V$. For real $t,s$, the evolution from
[[def-qa-19-finite-matrix-dynamics]] satisfies
$$U_H(0)=I_V,\qquad U_H(t)^*U_H(t)=I_V,\qquad U_H(t+s)=U_H(t)U_H(s),\qquad \frac{d}{dt}U_H(t)=-iHU_H(t).$$
Moreover, $U_H$ is the unique differentiable map $Y:\mathbb R\to
\operatorname{End}(V)$ satisfying $Y'(t)=-iHY(t)$ and $Y(0)=I_V$.

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

derivations.claim: Apply [F1] with $h=1$, valid because $|H_{ij}|\le\|H\|\le1$. The extra padded system labels carry zero eigenvalues; the input remains in the original supported subspace, so its nonzero gap and inverse-state target do not change. The full unitary oracle circuits, controls and reversals act on all physical labels, including invalid labels, as constructed in [F1]; no padded-branch overlap contributes a matrix value.

Put $\eta=\epsilon/(8192\kappa L)$. For each phase time $t_j$, certified arithmetic selects a rational $q_j\in[0,t_j]$ with $t_j-q_j\le\eta/2$ and a rational simulator tolerance $\zeta_j$ with $\eta/4\le\zeta_j\le\eta/2$; their construction cost remains in the separately charged arithmetic/phase-generation coordinates. Invoke QA25 at rational signed time $-q_j$ and tolerance $\zeta_j$. By [F2], its clean-input error from $e^{+iHq_j}$ is at most $\zeta_j$, and by [F6]–[F7] the time-rounding error from $e^{+iHt_j}$ is at most $t_j-q_j$. Thus each effective forward call has clean-input error at most $\eta$. Use its actual adjoint for the reverse call; [F3] gives the same clean-input error without assuming full-space accuracy on dirty inputs. The $2L$ effective errors sum to $\epsilon/(4096\kappa)$ as required in OP5, so [F5] applies with the stated state and failure guarantees.

In one $V$ or $V^\dagger$, sum the loose signal-call bound in [F2] over all signed rational times $\pm q_j$. Since $q_j\le t_j$, their absolute values sum to less than $2t_0$ by [F4], so this uses $O(dt_0+L\log(32768\kappa L/\epsilon))$ signal calls; also $\zeta_j\ge\eta/4$ makes $\log(1/\zeta_j)=O(\log(1/\eta))$. Multiplying by [F1]'s location/value conversion and then by the at most $2RK$ preparation/inverse-preparation calls gives $$O\!\left(R\kappa\left[dt_0+L\log(32768\kappa L/\epsilon)\right]\log(d+1)\right)$$ sparse-oracle calls, with a possibly smaller constant value-query count. Literal reversals and coherent controls change only constants already covered by [F1]–[F3].

Since $T<16(t_0+1)$, $L=O(\log(2+\kappa/\epsilon))$. With $d,\kappa\ge1$, $0<\epsilon\le1$, and $t_0=2048\kappa/\epsilon$, the expression in step 3.1 is $O(d\kappa^2\epsilon^{-1}(1+\log(1/\rho))\operatorname{polylog}(2+d\kappa/\epsilon))$. For fixed constant $\rho$ this gives the displayed order. The separate $B$ and $B^\dagger$ counts are at most $RK$ each by [F4]. Padding only appends clean high index bits to their input/output register convention; no extra sparse query is needed for this embedding. Their actual implementation and any controls used remain charged as supplied costs. All other direct-simulation resource coordinates stay in [F4]'s explicit sum, so no table, phase-generation, gate or bit-time claim is inferred from the sparse-query bound.

citations.quote:
Let $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ be a finite-dimensional linear map, $m,n\ge1$, and let $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)\setminus\{0\}$, where $\operatorname{ran}(A)$ is the image defined in [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **quantum linear-systems state-output task (QLSP)** is to prepare the normalized domain-register state
$$|x\rangle:=\frac{A^+b}{\|A^+b\|}\in\mathbb C^n,$$
where $A^+$ is the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. By [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]], write $b=\sum_{j:\sigma_j>0}\beta_j u_j$ in left singular vectors; the promised support gap is a supplied rational or exactly represented $\gamma>0$ such that every $j$ with $\beta_j\ne0$ has singular value $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$. The input includes a costed unitary $B$ mapping its designated all-zero input to $|b/\|b\|\rangle$ in the codomain register, tensored with a fixed work state. Its inverse, controlled access, and resource coordinates are specified in the separate HHL access model. If $b$ is multiplied by $c\ne0$, the normalized representative is multiplied by $c/|c|$, so its pure-state ray is unchanged. The task returns a quantum state (and may return a success flag); it does not promise a classical list of coordinates.

derivations.claim: For each $x$, the ratios $(b_x)_j/(b_x)_1=c_j/a$ are $1$ or $4$ when $a=1$, and $1/2$ or $2$ when $a=2$. Since $N\ge2$, at least one ratio determines $a$; each ratio then determines its corresponding $c_j$. Thus the $2^N$ inputs give $2^N$ distinct solution rays, with no ambiguity from a global phase.

Let $z$ be a classical coordinate output for one of these rays, phase-fixed so that its first coordinate is positive real. If $|z_j-(b_x)_j|<\delta:=1/(100\sqrt N)$ for every $j$, then $(b_x)_1\ge1/(4\sqrt N)$ because $a\ge1$ and $\|a e_1+\sum_{j\ge2}c_je_j\|\le4\sqrt N$. Hence $|z_1|\ge6/(25\sqrt N)$. For each $j\ge2$, $$\left|\frac{z_j}{z_1}-\frac{(b_x)_j}{(b_x)_1}\right|\le\frac{\delta}{|z_1|}\left(1+\frac{(b_x)_j}{(b_x)_1}\right)\le\frac5{24}<\frac14.$$ The four candidate ratios have pairwise separation at least $1/2$, so nearest-ratio decoding recovers $a$ and every $c_j$, hence all $N$ bits. Any unambiguous classical output code for all these rays therefore needs at least $2^N$ codewords and at least $N$ bits. This output-length requirement is independent of the ability to prepare or measure the corresponding quantum state.

citations.quote: For the ideal exact-eigenvalue version of [[alg-qa-26-hhl-phase-estimation]], on a normalized $|b\rangle$ supported on $1/\kappa\le|\lambda|\le1$, the well-flag vector is $v=(2\kappa)^{-1}H^+|b\rangle$. derivations.claim: Direct inversion gives $H^+|b\rangle=(|0\rangle+\kappa|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$. Its norm is $\sqrt{1+\kappa^2}/\sqrt2$, so the target is $(|0\rangle+\kappa|1\rangle)/\sqrt{1+\kappa^2}$.

Put $u=t+x$ and $v=t-x$. Since $|x|\le s$ and $s+t\le1$, each of $u,v$ is at most $t+s\le1$ and at least $t-s\ge2t-1\ge-1$; also $u+v=2t\ge2g$. If both $u,v\ge g$, [A2] gives $S(u)+S(v)\ge2-\eta$. Otherwise one of them, say $u$, is less than $g$, and then $v=2t-u>2g-u>g$; [A1]–[A2] give $S(u)+S(v)\ge-1+(1-\eta/2)=-\eta/2$. In every case [A1] also gives $S(u)+S(v)\le2$. Thus $-\eta/2\le S(u)+S(v)\le2$, and substitution into the formula for $R$ yields $\eta(1+\eta)/4\le R(x)\le1-\eta/2$, which implies $0\le R(x)\le1$.

If $|x|\le t-g$, both $u=t+x$ and $v=t-x$ are at least $g$. Their sign approximations lie in $[1-\eta/2,1]$ by [A1]–[A2], so $2-\eta\le S(u)+S(v)\le2$. Substituting gives $1-\eta+\eta^2/2\le R(x)\le1-\eta/2$, hence $1-\eta\le R(x)\le1$. Since $D(x)=(1-\eta/2-R(x))/(1-\eta)$, the interval $R(x)\in[1-\eta,1]$ gives $|D(x)|\le\eta/(2(1-\eta))$.

If $x\ge t+g$, then $u\ge g$ and $v\le-g$. By [A1]–[A2], $S(u)\in[1-\eta/2,1]$ and $S(v)\in[-1,-1+\eta/2]$, so $|S(u)+S(v)|\le\eta$. Evenness gives the same conclusion for $x\le-(t+g)$. Step 1.2 gives $R(x)\in[0,1]$. Using $D(x)=(1-\eta/2-R(x))/(1-\eta)$, its minimum over that interval is $-\eta/(2(1-\eta))$ and its maximum is $1+\eta/(2(1-\eta))$. This proves the global bound.

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

An **access instance** for a finite family of block-encoding unitaries $U_j$ records, as separate supplied operations, each of $U_j$, $U_j^{\dagger}$, controlled-$U_j$, and controlled-$U_j^{\dagger}$ that an algorithm may call. It also records whether the family SELECT unitary $\sum_j |j\rangle\langle j|\otimes U_j$ is supplied as one oracle or must be assembled from the separately controlled calls. A call to one operation does not imply access to another.

For every supplied circuit operation $O$, the instance records the applicable circuit-description length, gate count and gate set, depth, total width, and clean and dirty work-ancilla counts; for a uniform family it records the full-description generator time. It separately records each named oracle-query count, classical postprocessing time and space, matrix-data and coefficient-table reading or storage, state-preparation cost, and target precision and its bit encoding when the task is approximate. These coordinates follow [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]] and [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]; an inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently zero. A bare matrix $A$ supplies none of these circuits or access rights. If an operation is compiled from matrix entries or a coefficient table, its data access, synthesis, precision, and classical costs are recorded separately. The cost of a SELECT implementation includes its controls and relative phases unless those are listed as separate supplied primitives. These block-encoding constructions include no measurement or classical-output step; a consumer's measurement and output costs are accounted separately.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

Let $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$ be a finite-dimensional linear map, $m,n\ge1$, and let $b\in\operatorname{ran}(A)\setminus\{0\}$, where $\operatorname{ran}(A)$ is the image defined in [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **quantum linear-systems state-output task (QLSP)** is to prepare the normalized domain-register state
$$|x\rangle:=\frac{A^+b}{\|A^+b\|}\in\mathbb C^n,$$
where $A^+$ is the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. By [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]], write $b=\sum_{j:\sigma_j>0}\beta_j u_j$ in left singular vectors; the promised support gap is a supplied rational or exactly represented $\gamma>0$ such that every $j$ with $\beta_j\ne0$ has singular value $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$. The input includes a costed unitary $B$ mapping its designated all-zero input to $|b/\|b\|\rangle$ in the codomain register, tensored with a fixed work state. Its inverse, controlled access, and resource coordinates are specified in the separate HHL access model. If $b$ is multiplied by $c\ne0$, the normalized representative is multiplied by $c/|c|$, so its pure-state ray is unchanged. The task returns a quantum state (and may return a success flag); it does not promise a classical list of coordinates.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let
$A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. A matrix $B\in M_{n\times m}(\mathbb F)$ is a
**Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse** of $A$ when

$$ABA=A,\qquad BAB=B,$$

and the two square products are self-adjoint:

$$ (AB)^*=AB,\qquad (BA)^*=BA. $$

When such a matrix exists and is unique, it is denoted by $A^+$.

The four displayed relations are the **Penrose equations**. They are written in
the matrix product and adjoint conventions of
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]] and
[[thm-matrix-of-the-adjoint-is-the-conjugate-transpose]].

For every matrix $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$ over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or
$\mathbb C$, there exists a unique matrix $A^+\in M_{n\times m}(\mathbb F)$
satisfying the four Penrose equations of
[[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]].

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

derivations.claim: By [F1], in ordered orthonormal singular bases write $A=U\Sigma V^*$ with positive diagonal entries $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r$. Define $B=V\Sigma^+U^*$ by replacing each positive $\sigma_j$ with $1/\sigma_j$ and leaving zeros zero. Direct multiplication gives $ABA=A$, $BAB=B$, $AB=U\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0)U^*$ and $BA=V\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0)V^*$, both self-adjoint. Thus [F3] makes $B$ a Moore–Penrose inverse, and [F4] gives $B=A^+=\sum_j\sigma_j^{-1}|v_j\rangle\langle u_j|$.

Since $b$ is normalized and its coefficients in the orthonormal singular vectors are $\beta_j$, $\sum_j|\beta_j|^2=1$. Each $v_j$ is a unit vector and $Av_j=\sigma_j u_j$, so [F1] and [F5] give $\sigma_j=\|Av_j\|\le\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$. Step 1.1 therefore yields $\|A^+b\|^2=\sum_j|\beta_j|^2/\sigma_j^2\ge\alpha^{-2}>0$. Thus its normalized state is defined.

The singular values of $\bar A=A/\alpha$ are $\sigma_j/\alpha$ with the same left and right vectors. Repeating the construction in step 1.1 gives $(A/\alpha)^+=\alpha A^+$ because $\alpha>0$. Hence $(\delta/2)\bar A^+b=(\gamma/2)A^+b$, and multiplication by the positive scalar $\gamma/2$ preserves the normalized vector.

By [F2], coefficients outside the supported positive singular subspace vanish. By [F1] and [F5], each unit right singular vector satisfies $\sigma_j=\|Av_j\|\le\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$. Since $\delta=\gamma/\alpha$, step 2.2 gives $\| (\delta/2)\bar A^+b\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r|\beta_j|^2(\gamma/(2\sigma_j))^2\ge\sum_{j=1}^r|\beta_j|^2\gamma^2/(4\alpha^2)=\delta^2/4$. This is the ideal QSVT flag weight; any implementation error requires a separate error budget.

$$\sup_{x\in[\delta,1]}\left|p(x)-\frac{\delta}{2x}\right|\le e.$$
For a normalized block $\bar A=A/\alpha$ whose supported singular values lie in $\{0\}\cup[\delta,1]$, this gives the singular-space approximation $p^{\rm SV}(\bar A^\dagger)\approx(\delta/2)\bar A^+=(\gamma/2)A^+$ on the supported input, where $\delta=\gamma/\alpha$.

In the uncapped phase-generation route, the exact phase list returned by [[alg-qa-27-qsvt-pseudoinverse]] has ordered QSP product equal to the completed polynomial pair used by its generator, and the algorithm's coefficientwise product check passes before QSVT execution. Numerical angle and compiler errors remain subject to their separate certificates; a failed exact product check returns `PHASE_PRODUCT_ERROR` and is never treated as a successful transform.

In the block-encoded QLSP model, let $|b\rangle$ be the normalized codomain input, let $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$, and suppose $|b\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^r\beta_j|u_j\rangle$ is supported on positive singular values $\sigma_j\ge\gamma>0$. Then
$$\frac{(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle}{\|(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle\|}=\frac{A^+|b\rangle}{\|A^+|b\rangle\|},\qquad \left\|(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle\right\|^2\ge\frac{\delta^2}{4},\qquad \delta=\gamma/\alpha,\quad\bar A=A/\alpha.$$
In particular the ideal inverse-branch success probability is positive and has the stated crude lower bound.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ is zero or has degree at most $d$, has parity $d\bmod2$, and satisfies $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. For $a>0$, the expected total number of calls made by [[alg-qa-12-unknown-amplitude-search]] to $A$, $A^\dagger$, the good and zero-input phase operations, and any one-call verifier is $\Theta(a^{-1/2})$. Let $A,\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},a,|G\rangle,|B\rangle$ be as in [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]], with $0<a<1$, and let $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$ be the unique angle satisfying $\sin^2\theta=a$. For
$
Q:=-A S_0 A^\dagger S_{\mathrm{good}},
$
the subspace $\operatorname{span}\{|B\rangle,|G\rangle\}$ is invariant. In the ordered orthonormal basis $(|B\rangle,|G\rangle)$, the restriction of $Q$ is
$
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\
\sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)
\end{pmatrix}.
$
For $a=0$ the prepared vector spans an invariant bad line and $Q|\psi\rangle=|\psi\rangle$; for $a=1$ it spans an invariant good line and $Q|\psi\rangle=-|\psi\rangle$.

This is a sequential randomized procedure, not a bounded-$T$ circuit family. Fix $c=3/2$. For rounds $\ell=1,2,\ldots$, compute the finite integer $M_\ell=\lceil c^\ell\rceil$ by exact rational arithmetic. In classical-output mode, require the diagonal-predicate specialization of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]] and a costed verifier that accepts exactly the basis labels designated good by $\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}$; measure the designated output basis only after the good/bad instrument and then run the verifier.

1. On a fresh register prepare $A|0\rangle$ and perform the declared good/bad projective instrument. On a bad outcome, continue to step 2. On a good outcome, return the conditional quantum state in quantum-output mode; in classical-output mode, measure the designated output basis, verify the candidate, and return it if accepted.

2. Prepare $A|0\rangle$ on a second fresh register. Draw $j$ uniformly from the finite set $\{1,\ldots,M_\ell\}$, apply exactly $j$ standard $Q$-iterates, and perform the good/bad instrument. On a good outcome, return the conditional quantum state in quantum-output mode; in classical-output mode, measure the designated output basis, verify the candidate, and return it if accepted. If the outcome is bad or verification rejects, discard the registers and continue to round $\ell+1$.

The random choice is fresh and independent in each round; the schedule depends only on $\ell$, never on the unknown $a$. Every round is finite. When $a=0$, the loop runs forever and does not decide whether the good set is empty.

For $0<a<1$, let $\sin^2\theta=a$. For every integer $M\ge1$, the second fresh sample with $j$ uniform on $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ has good-outcome probability
$
p_M=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\sin^2((2j+1)\theta)
=\frac12-\frac1{2M}\sum_{j=1}^M\cos((4j+2)\theta)
\ge\frac12-\frac1{2M|\sin(2\theta)|}.
$
For every $a>0$, the procedure [[alg-qa-12-unknown-amplitude-search]] returns a good output with probability $1$. If $a=0$, it never returns a good output and does not halt.

Generate every product coefficient with the stated total rounding budget. Check exact odd parity and degree. Run the OP1 exact critical-point check for $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$. Construct the reciprocal certificate on $[\delta,1]$ by the specified dyadic rational partitions and nonnegative Bernstein coefficients for both $ex\pm(xp(x)-\delta/2)$. Refine precision when intervals are undecided; on an actually failed certificate halve $u,v$ and regenerate. Any declared cap returns `CONSTRUCTION_TIMEOUT`; any failed exact certificate returns its stated non-success branch.

On a successful polynomial certificate, set the rational phase-synthesis tolerance to $e/100$ and call [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]] in `efficient-numerical` mode with the checked real odd polynomial $p$, its degree, and that tolerance. Retain the exact pre-angle target $p_0$ produced by its deterministic shrink/round rule, complementary pair $B,C$, exact phase-scalar descriptors, and numerical phase certificates. Charge its target shrink/round error and numerical-angle/compiler errors to the separate phase term in the supplied error budget. Before any QSVT call, form the ordered matrix product from the returned exact phase-scalar descriptors, using the recurrence in [[def-qa-23-qsp-signal-sequence]] and coefficient arithmetic in the basis $\mathbb C[x]\oplus\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\mathbb C[x]$. Compare its four entries coefficientwise with
$$\begin{pmatrix}p_0+iB&\sqrt{1-x^2}\,C\\(-1)^{d+1}\sqrt{1-x^2}\,C^*&(-1)^d(p_0-iB)\end{pmatrix}.$$
This finite exact check validates the phase list actually returned by the peeling routine, rather than relying on existence of some phase list. Charge its arithmetic and certificate output with phase generation. If any comparison fails, return `PHASE_PRODUCT_ERROR` with the generated polynomial record and mismatch witness, and do not execute QSVT. Only after the check passes may the execution use the returned phase list. The subsequent rational-angle and optional compiler errors remain separately bounded by the returned phase certificates and the supplied error budget; the exact product check does not replace those bounds. No exact phase rotation or finite-basis compiler is free.

**Execution.** Execute the QA24 odd QSVT sequence on the adjoint projected-unitary encoding of $\bar A$, with left and right projectors swapped, using the generated phase list and the separately supplied controlled/inverse access. The ideal supported singular-value multiplier is $p(\sigma/\alpha)$; the intended target is $(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle=(\gamma/2)A^+|b\rangle$. Apply the declared success projector and return its conditional state only on a positive-probability success branch. The scalar polynomial, block-encoding, phase-synthesis, and circuit-implementation errors are separate terms in the supplied error budget.

An optional certified-input branch accepts finite polynomial, phase, and reciprocal-certificate lists; it verifies their parity, interval, identity, and Bernstein checks before execution and returns `INVALID` if a check fails. It does not prove that bare rational inputs can be converted into such a certificate.

derivations.claim: Write the finite SVD $A=\sum_j\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|$. Since $b=\sum_j\beta_j u_j$ is supported on $\sigma_j\ge\gamma$, applying the odd transform to $\bar A^\dagger$ maps each $u_j$ to $v_j$ with multiplier given by the verified phase-sequence polynomial. By [F9] this ideal polynomial is exactly the generated completed-pair target before numerical phase approximation; its total difference from the intended $p$ transform, including polynomial shrink and phase/circuit errors, is included in $\zeta$. The target multiplier is $\delta/(2(\sigma_j/\alpha))=\gamma/(2\sigma_j)$, the coefficient of $F=(\delta/2)\bar A^+$; [F1] and [F3] therefore bound the operator error on the supported subspace by $\zeta$.

Put $v=F|b\rangle$ and let $w$ be the implemented success vector. Then $\|w-v\|\le\zeta$. By [F2], $\|v\|\ge\delta/2$, so reverse triangle inequality gives $\|w\|\ge\delta/2-\zeta>0$ and $p_{\rm impl}=\|w\|^2\ge(\delta/2-\zeta)^2$. Moreover,
$$\left\|\frac{w}{\|w\|}-\frac{v}{\|v\|}\right\|\le\frac{|\|v\|-\|w\||+\|w-v\|}{\|v\|}\le\frac{2\zeta}{\|v\|}\le\frac{4\zeta}{\delta}.$$
The conditional state is defined because $\|w\|>0$.

By [F2], $p_{\rm ideal}=\|v\|^2\ge\delta^2/4$. In the implemented case, if $\zeta\le\delta/4$, step 1.2 gives $p_{\rm impl}\ge\delta^2/16$. By [F4], one attempt uses $m$ block-encoding signal calls, and phase/reflection and controlled-call resources remain separate.

Put $|G\rangle=w/\|w\|$ for the one-attempt good vector. By [F6], after any integer number $j$ of amplitude-amplification iterates the unnormalized good component is $s_j|G\rangle$ for a scalar $s_j$. On a positive-probability good branch $s_j\ne0$, and the normalized ket is $(s_j/|s_j|)|G\rangle$; its phase can differ from that of $|G\rangle$. Each such branch has exactly the density operator $|G\rangle\langle G|$, including after the stopping history is forgotten. Thus any returned unit representative is $\psi=c|G\rangle$ with $|c|=1$, and choosing $\omega=\overline c$ gives $\omega\psi=|G\rangle$ and the error bound of step 1.2. This identifies the terminal state ray without rephasing any coherent circuit or controlled call. Fresh rounds use the same preparation circuit, and [F7] returns only on that good measurement; [F8] supplies eventual success for $p_{\rm impl}>0$. Applying [F5] to the actual success weight $p_{\rm impl}$ gives expected $O(p_{\rm impl}^{-1/2})$ attempts, hence expected $O(m/\sqrt{p_{\rm impl}})$ signal calls. If [F1] is established, substitute $m=O(\delta^{-1}\ln(1/e))$; if $\zeta\le\delta/4$, step 2.1 gives $p_{\rm impl}^{-1/2}\le4/\delta$. All other resource coordinates remain separate by [F4]–[F5].

Write $T^{\dagger}$ for the adjoint $T^*$ characterized by [[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]. Fix integers $m,n\ge1$, $a\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(m,n)$. On each coordinate space $\mathbb C^r$ use $\langle x,y\rangle_{\rm root}:=\sum_{q=1}^r x_q\overline{y_q}$, linear in the first argument. Put the ancilla register before the system register in every tensor product, and let $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ be the first standard basis vector in $\mathbb C^{2^a}$. For $A:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m$, choose as part of the data padding maps $E_{\rm in}:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^d$ and $E_{\rm out}:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^d$ satisfying $E_{\rm in}^{\dagger}E_{\rm in}=I_n$ and $E_{\rm out}^{\dagger}E_{\rm out}=I_m$. The default padding sends a coordinate vector to the same coordinates followed by zeros. Set $\widehat A:=E_{\rm out}AE_{\rm in}^{\dagger}:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^d$.

Let $J_a:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$ be $J_ax=e_0\otimes x$, where $e_0$ is the all-zero computational basis vector, and let $\Pi_a:=J_aJ_a^{\dagger}$. For a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^{2^a}\otimes\mathbb C^d$, its **projected block** is the endomorphism $B_U:=J_a^{\dagger}UJ_a$ of $\mathbb C^d$. It is not asserted to be unitary.

For $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon\ge0$, the tuple $(U,a,\alpha,\varepsilon,d,E_{\rm in},E_{\rm out})$ is an **$(\alpha,a,\varepsilon)$ block encoding of $A$** when $\alpha\ge\|A\|_{\rm op}$ and $\|B_U-\widehat A/\alpha\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$. The exact case is $\varepsilon=0$. For square $A$, take $m=n=d$ and both embeddings equal to the identity. For rectangular $A$, the dimensions and embeddings remain part of the encoding data.

The equivalent projector notation identifies $B_U$ with the restriction of $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ to $\operatorname{ran}(\Pi_a)$, transported to $\mathbb C^d$ by $J_a$; it does not regard $\Pi_aU\Pi_a$ as a unitary.

Let $x\in[-1,1]$, put $s(x)=\sqrt{1-x^2}$ using the nonnegative real square root, and define the Hermitian-reflection signal matrix
$$W_R(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x&s(x)\\s(x)&-x\end{pmatrix}.$$
For each real $\phi$, define $Z(\phi)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\phi},e^{-i\phi})$. For an integer $d\ge0$ and real phase list $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$, the length-$d$ QSP sequence is the ordered matrix product
$$U_\Phi(x)=Z(\phi_0)\prod_{j=1}^{d}\bigl(W_R(x)Z(\phi_j)\bigr),$$
where the product is written left to right in increasing $j$ and matrix multiplication acts right to left. For $d=0$ this is $Z(\phi_0)$. This definition fixes the sign of the off-diagonal signal entry, both endpoint phases, and the product order.

The phases are in matrix order: when the factors are applied as chronological circuit layers, the rightmost factor acts first, in accordance with [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. In the ordered signal basis, if both coordinates are nonzero, applying $Z(\phi)$ multiplies the ratio of the second coordinate to the first by $e^{-2i\phi}$; if either coordinate is zero, that relative phase is undefined, while the displayed matrix action remains defined. This is the relative phase convention fixed by [[def-qc-relative-phase]].

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular pairs $(\sigma_j,v_j,u_j)$, and let $\Phi=(\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_d)$ be the exact phase list in [[alg-qa-24-qsvt]]. Let $P_\Phi$ be the upper-left scalar polynomial of its QSP signal sequence. On every positive two-dimensional singular plane from [[lem-qa-24-pue-svd-invariant-subspaces]], the QSVT sequence is exactly $U_\Phi(\sigma_j)$. Consequently, if $d$ is odd,

$$\Pi_LU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A),$$

and if $d$ is even,

$$\Pi_RU_\Phi\Pi_R\big|_{H_R}=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_\Phi(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+P_\Phi(0)\Pi_{\ker A}=\bigl(P_\Phi\bigr)^{\mathrm{SV}}_R(A).$$

The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ is zero or has degree at most $d$, has parity $d\bmod2$, and satisfies $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

derivations.claim: The matrices $A,S$ are self-adjoint, commute, and satisfy $A^2+S^2=I$. Thus $U^*=U$ and $U^2=\begin{pmatrix}A^2+S^2&AS-SA\\SA-AS&S^2+A^2\end{pmatrix}=I$. The all-zero ancilla compression of $U$ is its top-left block $A$, so [F1] gives an exact $(1,1,0)$ block encoding.

The diagonal entries of $A$ are its singular values. Both inputs are supported on singular values at least $\gamma=1/2$, and $\|A\|_{\rm op}=\alpha=1$, so $\delta=\gamma/\alpha=1/2$. For $x\in[1/2,1]$, $-x\le2x^2-1\le x$ because $2x^2+x-1=(2x-1)(x+1)\ge0$ and $x-(2x^2-1)=(1-x)(2x+1)\ge0$. Hence $|p(x)-\delta/(2x)|=|2x^2-1|/(4x)\le1/4$. Also $p$ is odd, has degree one, satisfies $p(0)=0$, and $|p(x)|\le1/2$ on $[-1,1]$.

For $\Phi=(0,\pi/3)$, [F2] gives upper-left entry $e^{i\pi/3}x$; the conjugate list gives $e^{-i\pi/3}x$. Their coherent real extraction is $\frac12(e^{i\pi/3}+e^{-i\pi/3})x=\frac12x=p(x)$ by [F3]. Thus the exact response multipliers on the two singular vectors are $p(1)=1/2$ and $p(1/2)=1/4$.

For $|b\rangle=|0\rangle$, the QSVT success probability is $|p(1)|^2=1/4$ and the ideal inverse-block probability is $|(\delta/2)(1/1)|^2=1/16$. For $|b\rangle=|1\rangle$, these probabilities are $|p(1/2)|^2=1/16$ and $|(\delta/2)(1/(1/2))|^2=1/4$. Each successful state is the same basis vector as the normalized QLSP solution because the singular space is one-dimensional and both multipliers are positive. For the optional Bernstein reciprocal check, set $x=(1+u)/2$ for $0\le u\le1$. Then the two polynomials are $\frac14(2x^2+x-1)=\frac18(3u+u^2)$ and $\frac14(1+x-2x^2)=\frac18(2-u-u^2)$, with degree-two Bernstein coefficient lists $(0,3/16,1/2)$ and $(1/4,3/16,0)$. All coefficients are nonnegative, so the finite reciprocal certificate is valid.
