Unique row/column overlap of the actual h=1 sparse block gives tilde A/d even with listed zero values. Odd adjoint QSVT gives signed phi_j/(2lambda), and dilution yields 1/(alpha lambda), with 4kappa<=alpha<8kappa. Clean-subspace hybrid, including Duhamel value errors and actual adjoints, is applied along ideal clean trajectories without resetting actual work. Two adjacent admissible stops cover all but <=2m zeta^2 mass, including endpoints; event-probability hybrid controls the RMS observable. Budgets yield T_av<=5Hx, p>=x^2/(4alpha^2), x>=1 and ratio<=10Halpha. Projected good vector differs from A'Xb/alpha by <=epsilon*/(128alpha); actual uncompute, external herald and final all-zero-work test give pure system error <=epsilon and failure <=rho/4096. Initial/final selected projectors exclude terminal bad T=1, preserve clean W_B and give the estimator floor on good construction transcripts. Fourier-table costs are not used for the efficient-mode bound. Contract-only reader delta refreshes the model quotation; current source is pre/post-identical. No refuter finding.

citations.quote:
**Inputs.** A finite Hermitian $d$-sparse $A$ with $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le1$, normalized $|b\rangle$ supported on eigenvalues $|\lambda|\ge1/\kappa$, rational $0<e<1$ and failure budget $0<\rho<1/3$, the full reversible row/reverse-location and entry-value access of [[def-qa-27-cks-sparse-oracle-model]], and supplied $B,B^\dagger$ preparing $|b\rangle$. The preparation contract is $B(|0\rangle_I|0\rangle_{W_B})=|b\rangle_I|0\rangle_{W_B}$ for a declared preparation-work register $W_B$; stage lists act as identity on $W_B$. Every controlled, inverse, state-preparation, simulation, reflection, arithmetic, classical table, precision, and compilation cost is an input coordinate.

**Modes.** The input selects `efficient-qsvt` or the original `fourier-table` inverse constructor, and retains its declared capped or uncapped construction policy. The Fourier table, coefficient-generation and common-normalization instructions below are the complete original alternate mode. Their generic table/preparation costs remain charged. The complexity guarantee uses `efficient-qsvt`; no such guarantee is inferred for an arbitrary supplied Fourier SELECT circuit or generic coefficient table.

**Finite-precision matrix and simulation budget (both modes).** Let $\widetilde A$ be the Hermitian sparse matrix decoded from the finite-precision value oracle, and require a certified induced error $\|A-\widetilde A\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm val}$; exact value access is the case $\epsilon_{\rm val}=0$. A non-Hermitian decoded table, an entry with $|\widetilde A_{ij}|>1$, or a missing error certificate returns `INVALID_ACCESS`. Construct the exact sparse block encoding with compression $\widetilde A/d$ and normalization $d$ by the QA25 supplied-permutation $U_L^\dagger U_R$ circuit using the known entry bound $h=1$ (not the unknown maximum entry). Use the Hermitian row-location and reverse-location permutations on swapped system registers to supply the column enumerations; charge the swaps and every inverse/control form. The value flag circuit is: On a valid value slot use the flag rotation $\begin{pmatrix}\widetilde A_{ij}&-\sqrt{1-|\widetilde A_{ij}|^2}\\\sqrt{1-|\widetilde A_{ij}|^2}&\overline{\widetilde A_{ij}}\end{pmatrix}$, with value query/unquery as in that circuit. This changes only the value amplitude in the QA25 supplied-permutation circuit, so its row/reverse-location, value-query, uniform-state-preparation, inverse, and controlled-call counts are unchanged and separately charged. The location maps enumerate the support of $A$ and may therefore list additional zero-valued entries of $\widetilde A$; their flag-zero contribution is zero. In `efficient-qsvt` mode, for each QSVT stage, $\epsilon_{{\rm BE},j}$ is a certified bound on its actual PUE compression error relative to $A/d$, including at least $\epsilon_{\rm val}/d$ and any block-circuit error; the stage is admissible only if $4D_j\sqrt{\epsilon_{{\rm BE},j}}\le\eta_I/8$.

Let $\mathcal Q$ be the finite multiset of simulator-call sites in one complete $A$ list and one complete $A'$ list, including every dyadic QPE power and coherent repetition. At call site $q$, the QA25 circuit uses the exact encoding of $\widetilde A/d$ to simulate $e^{\pm i\widetilde A t_q}$, and has a certified clean-input isometry error $\xi_q$ relative to that unitary; the actual controlled or inverse form has the same bound and is separately charged. Choose the value precision and simulator precisions so that
$$\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\xi_q+\epsilon_{\rm val}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}|t_q|\le\eta_S.$$
Here $\eta_S$ is the total clean-subspace error for the two base lists, not an error claim on arbitrary dirty work inputs. The matrix term follows from the finite-dimensional Duhamel bound $\|e^{\pm iAt}-e^{\pm i\widetilde A t}\|_{\rm op}\le |t|\epsilon_{\rm val}$; the clean-subspace unitary hybrid then sums all call-site errors. If these value, block, or simulation budgets cannot be certified, return `INVALID_ACCESS` before production. Their bit precision and access costs remain explicit.

**Efficient inverse mode.** Put $m=\lceil\log_2\kappa\rceil+1$ and $e_*=\min(e,\rho)$ and use this strengthened accuracy in all efficient-mode budgets below. Set $n=m+1$, $\phi_j=2^{-j}$ and $\alpha_{\max}=2/\phi_m$. Use the exact QA25 sparse block encoding of $\widetilde A/d$ specified above, with every inverse/control form used and its precision/cost; its relative error to the ideal $A/d$ is charged in $\epsilon_{{\rm BE},j}$. For each stage generate the OP1A polynomial from [[alg-qa-27-qsvt-pseudoinverse]] with gap $\delta_j=\phi_j/d$ and error $e_j\le\min(\delta_j/2,\eta_I/8)$; this invokes its scalar generation instructions only, rather than assuming the stage input has a global gap $\phi_j$. Execute the QA24 real odd QSVT circuit on the adjoint encoding, with its actual real-part-extraction control and zero-workspace success projector. On the ideal block $A/d$, its compression on eigenvalues $|\lambda|\ge\phi_j$ is $(\phi_j/2)A^{-1}$; the actual $\widetilde A/d$ compression differs from this ideal map by the certified QSVT input-block error, while off that supported subspace it is simply the declared bounded circuit. Compute a success flag for the whole zero-workspace projector, and dilute its successful component by a separately supplied/constructed flag rotation of amplitude $\phi_m/\phi_j$. This gives the common target $A^{-1}/\alpha_{\max}$; no unspecified PREPARE or SELECT operation occurs in this mode.

In this mode choose the least admissible dyadic QPE scales and least admissible odd repetition counts, and construct the corresponding simulator circuits at their declared precision. Use $\eta_I\le e_*/(4096m\alpha_{\max})$, phase-test amplitude error $\zeta\le\min(e_*/(4096m\alpha_{\max}),1/(4096m\kappa^2))$, and the $\eta_S$ budget above, bounded by the same minimum. For each stage $j$, pass phase-synthesis tolerance $e_j/100$ to its QSP call and allocate the resulting polynomial shrink, angle, compiler and circuit errors so the actual diluted inverse compression error is at most $\eta_I$. The $\epsilon_{{\rm BE},j}$ constraint above includes the actual generated degree $D_j$ and the finite-value/block error of $\widetilde A/d$ relative to $A/d$. Sum all implemented phase/flag/projector errors within the remaining budget. If an OP1A polynomial/phase constructor returns a declared non-success status, propagate it before any QSVT call or success flag; the theorem's success guarantee applies when uncapped construction completes. The QA25 small-time-aware simulator is invoked only through its clean-input isometry contract, with an initially clean embedding and the controlled/inverse clean-subspace hybrid of [[lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid]]. Within repeated calls and reversal, retain the actual work coherently; only the ideal comparison trajectory has clean work, and actual approximate work is not reset or discarded. Numerical accuracy, all signal/query/gate counts, coefficient/phase generation and arithmetic bit implementation are separate input cost coordinates. The QA23 efficient numerical arithmetic mode grants its stated ideal exact-algebraic operation count only.

**Registers and stopping semantics.** Put $m=\lceil\log_2\kappa\rceil+1$. Use clock bits $C_1,\ldots,C_m$, success bit $F$, system register $I$, separate phase workspaces $P_j$, and coefficient workspace $Q$. Once a clock bit first records a stopped branch, every later stage is controlled on all earlier clock bits being zero. All clock, outcome, and step branches are orthogonal; there are no intermediate measurements in a branch later inverted.

**Finite Fourier inverse (`fourier-table` mode).** For each requested $\phi\in(0,1]$ and error $e_0>0$, `GenerateInverse(φ,e₀)` chooses rational $Y,Z>0$ by increasing integer squares until
$$e^{-\phi^2Y^2/2}/\phi\le e_0/8,\qquad 2Y e^{-Z^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\le e_0/8.$$
Set $L_y=Z^2$, $L_z=1+Z^2+YZ$, and choose positive dyadic $\Delta_y,\Delta_z$ with $2YZ(L_y\Delta_y+L_z\Delta_z)/\sqrt{2\pi}\le e_0/8$. Increase $Y,Z$ to multiples of those steps and recheck. For $j=0,\ldots,J-1$, $J=Y/\Delta_y$, and $k=-K,\ldots,K-1$, $K=Z/\Delta_z$, use $y_j=j\Delta_y$, $z_k=k\Delta_z$, and
$$c_{jk}=i\Delta_y\Delta_z z_k e^{-z_k^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$$
for the controlled simulator $e^{-iAy_jz_k}$. Round the coefficients to exact rational complex values $\widetilde c_{jk}$ with total absolute error at most $e_0/8$. In lexicographic $(j,k)$ order, omit zero rounded coefficients and call the remaining list $\beta_\ell$, retaining each associated simulation time. Put $\lambda_\phi=\sum_\ell|\beta_\ell|$ and choose a certified rational upper bound $\alpha_\phi\ge\max(1,\lambda_\phi)$ for this rounded list. Execute the normalized coefficient construction below with normalization $a=\alpha_\phi$; the coefficient phases belong to SELECT, not PREPARE. If $\widetilde c_{jk}$ are the used rounded coefficients and $\xi_{jk}$ bounds the clean-input simulation error relative to $e^{-i\widetilde A y_jz_k}$, require
$$\frac1{\alpha_\phi}\sum_{j,k}|\widetilde c_{jk}|\bigl(\xi_{jk}+|y_jz_k|\epsilon_{\rm val}\bigr)\le e_0/16.$$
This includes both the simulator's own precision error and the value-table error by the Duhamel bound. Allocate all other PREPARE/SELECT and controlled/inverse implementation errors jointly to at most $e_0/16$, so their total normalized LCU-block error is at most $e_0/8$. If these finite budgets cannot be certified, return `INVALID_ACCESS` (or the declared construction timeout when its cap is reached). The analytic identity being discretized is
$$\frac1x=\frac{i}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_0^\infty\!dy\int_{\mathbb R} z e^{-z^2/2}e^{-ixyz}\,dz\quad(|x|\ge\phi).$$
The coefficient PREPARE/SELECT block is the conditional identity proved in [[lem-qa-27-lcu-projected-block-identity]]. The chosen cutoffs and finite coefficients do not by themselves certify the approximation or its gate/bit cost.

**Normalized coefficient construction (`fourier-table` mode).** Given the retained rounded list and a normalization $a\ge\lambda_\phi$, $a>0$, append two distinct identity-term labels with coefficients $+(a-\lambda_\phi)/2$ and $-(a-\lambda_\phi)/2$ if $a>\lambda_\phi$; append neither if equality holds. Keep the original ordered labels followed by the positive and negative padding labels, without merging their cancelling terms. Denote this nonzero coefficient list by $(\gamma_\ell,V_\ell)_{\ell<M}$, where an original $V_\ell$ is its indicated simulation and a padding $V_\ell$ is the identity. Even when the rounded list is empty, the two padding terms give $M\ge1$ and total absolute coefficient sum $a$. Choose $q=\lceil\log_2M\rceil$, or a larger declared common index width, and $D=2^q$. Form the exact positive normalized table
$$a_\ell=\begin{cases}\sqrt{|\gamma_\ell|/a},&0\le\ell<M,\\0,&M\le\ell<D.\end{cases}$$
Use this table, whose squared amplitudes sum to one, in [[alg-qc-state-preparation]], following the unit-component-scale LCU interface of [[alg-qa-22-lcu-block-encoding]]. Its first nonzero amplitude is positive real, so its omitted reference phase is zero. Supply exact arithmetic descriptors for the amplitudes and angles in that supplier's ideal continuous-gate model; square roots need not have exact finite rational coordinate encodings. Include the actual PREPARE work in a declared clean register $W_P$ within $Q$, so $P|0^q,0_{W_P}\rangle=\sum_{\ell<M}a_\ell|\ell,0_{W_P}\rangle$. Retain the complete unitary circuit, not only its zero-input state, and use its literal reversed adjoint circuit for $P^\dagger$.

Supply the full SELECT unitary on all physical index labels: for $\ell<M$ it applies $(\gamma_\ell/|\gamma_\ell|)V_\ell$ to the system and its declared simulation work, and for $M\le\ell<D$ it applies identity. It acts as identity on $W_P$; all component work spaces are embedded in a common register with unused wires idle. In particular the two slack labels apply $+I$ and $-I$, respectively. Coefficient phases are not loaded into PREPARE or unprepare, where they would cancel. The returned LCU circuit is $P^\dagger\mathrm{SELECT}P$, with its success projector testing the coefficient index, $W_P$ and component work all zero. After this block, coherently XOR that all-zero predicate into the initially zero success bit $F$, using a supplied or explicit reversible predicate circuit and its charged control/work costs; this flagged circuit is the Fourier inverse call used by the stage list. Apply the conditional LCU identity to the actual component compressions with scale one; their deviations from the ideal evolutions are charged by the weighted simulation budget above, without assuming full-space simulation accuracy on dirty work. Retain all work coherently, and supply every controlled or adjoint form actually used, including the coefficient phases under an outer control; reverse the complete circuits for adjoints rather than an ideal postselected state.

Charge the complete explicit table's generation, exact descriptors, reading, storage and angle arithmetic, each PREPARE/SELECT/adjoint/control call, register and clean-work width, and precision and compilation separately. The QC24 expanded circuit uses $O((q+1)D)$ ideal bounded-arity occurrences and serial depth per generic PREPARE, with at most $\max(q-1,0)$ reusable clean work bits; it grants no finite-alphabet exactness or bit-time bound. A finite implementation instead supplies certified table/angle/whole-circuit errors, including controlled and adjoint forms, within the already allocated $e_0/16$ nonsimulation LCU error budget. For example, whole-unitary PREPARE error $\delta_P$ and additional SELECT error $\delta_{\rm sel}$ must include $2\delta_P+\delta_{\rm sel}$ in that budget; compile complete controlled blocks so no discarded scalar becomes a relative phase. A raw rounded table without these certificates is not an implementation. This construction adds no efficient coefficient-generation, Fourier-approximation or uncapped-termination guarantee.

**Common normalization (`fourier-table` mode).** Set $L=\lceil\log_2(1024m\kappa/e)\rceil$ and $\zeta=e/2^L$. Generate at every $\phi_j=2^{-j}$ with error $m\zeta$ and set $\alpha_{\max}=\max_j\alpha_{\phi_j}$. Rebuild each stage from its original rounded coefficient list (discarding its earlier slack labels) by the normalized coefficient construction with $a=\alpha_{\max}$: append the explicit pair $\pm(\alpha_{\max}-\lambda_{\phi_j})I/2$ when its slack is positive. Use the maximum of the resulting index widths as a common $q$ and zero-pad every amplitude table to $D=2^q$; embed all stage work in the common $Q$. Rebuild PREPARE, SELECT and their required adjoint/control circuits at these sizes and recheck their actual error and cost certificates. The weighted simulation error uses denominator $\alpha_{\max}$ for these rebuilt blocks; the added identity terms have no simulation error. If $m\alpha_{\max}\zeta>e/256$, increment $L$ and regenerate. Also require $\eta_S\le\min(e/(4096m\alpha_{\max}),1/(4096m\kappa^2))$ in the finite-precision simulator budget above. A declared finite cap returns `CONSTRUCTION_TIMEOUT`; an uncapped run relies on the separate termination and growth proof.

**Gapped phase estimation and stages.** Use QPE on controlled $e^{i\widetilde A}$ with its dyadic powers constructed through the actual QA25 clean-work simulator. For each $\phi_j$, `GPE(φ_j,ζ)` uses a dyadic phase scale at least $64\pi/\phi_j$, an odd number $r\ge8\ln(1/\zeta^2)+8$ of coherent QPE repetitions on the same eigencomponent, and reversible majority comparison of the unwrapped phase magnitude with $3\phi_j/2$. Threshold equality selects the large branch. The ideal comparison is QPE for $A$ with promise cases $|\lambda|\le\phi_j$ and $|\lambda|\ge2\phi_j$; the transition band is unconstrained. The finite-precision implementation uses $\widetilde A$, and its entire call-site error relative to that ideal QPE is bounded by the $\eta_S$ allocation above. Retain all phase work in $P_j$ and make no intermediate measurement.

At stage $j$, conditional on the active prefix $C_1=\cdots=C_{j-1}=0$, run GPE into $C_j,P_j$. On the same prefix and $C_j=1$, execute the common-normalized inverse circuit of the selected mode on $F,Q,I$; otherwise leave the branch unchanged. Let $A_j$ be this stage list, $A=A_m\cdots A_1$, and let $A'_j$ replace its inverse call by a flip of $F$, with $A'=A'_m\cdots A'_1$. The inverse lists are literal reversal with the corresponding inverse calls. The $\mathcal Q$-budget in the finite-precision contract includes the simulator call sites of both complete lists.

**Terminal bad branch (both modes).** Add a clean terminal bit $T$. After the last GPE/inverse stage, coherently set $T=1$ on the branch with all clock bits zero and leave its success flag zero. This branch is stopped and bad at the final stopping time; it is no longer unfinished. Append the same terminal-bit computation to $A'$ and reverse it inside $(A')^\dagger$. Thus all branches stop by $t_m$, including phase-test failures; the last stopping subspace is the orthogonal union of the ordinary last-stage stop and this terminal-bad branch. For $1\le i\le m$, define the good-or-unfinished projector as the orthogonal sum of (a) branches with $F=1$, $T=0$, and first-stop clock word $C_1=\cdots=C_{j-1}=0,C_j=1$ for some $j\le i$ (later clock bits remain zero), and (b) branches with $F=0$, $T=0$, and $C_1=\cdots=C_i=0$. Previously stopped bad branches and the terminal branch $T=1,F=0$ are excluded. Since $T$ is set after stage $m$, the unfinished term is empty at $i=m$. The final target is only $F=1$. These projectors act as identity on the clean $W_B$ factor.

**Finite variable-time amplification wrapper (both modes).** Pad cumulative stage counts to increasing dyadic stopping times, preserving stopped branches. Each interval budget includes the supplied input/selected reflections, controlled/inverse list implementations and reversible clock predicates; their costs remain explicit. Form the first sampler by preparing $B|0\rangle$ and running the first interval. Later $B_i$ runs the prior amplified list and the original continuation on unfinished branches only. The initial reflection is about the all-zero state before $B$; $A'$ contains the eigenvalue stages and does not undo $B$. The preparation-work factor $W_B$ stays zero throughout.

Let $n=m+1$, $c=1/100$ and $p_{\min}=1/(256n\alpha_{\max}^2)$. Use [[alg-qa-relative-probability-estimation]] with $B_i$, the good-or-unfinished projector (the final target is $F=1$), relative error $c$, failure $\rho/(16n)$ and floor $p_{\min}$. The efficient-QSVT mode selects its `efficient-grid` rounding branch; the Fourier-table mode retains its declared rounding branch. This is an arbitrary-sampler estimate, not a Boolean marked-count estimate. Every controlled sampler/inverse and reflection is supplied or built gatewise from an explicit circuit and charged; missing access returns `INVALID_ACCESS`. All estimator registers are fresh construction data, discarded before fresh production execution. A returned estimate $\widehat q_i=0$ gives `ESTIMATION_FAIL`. If $\widehat q_i>1/(9n)$, use $V_i=B_i$. Otherwise choose the least nonnegative integer $k$ with $(2k+1)^2\widehat q_i\ge1/(9n)$, within $k\le\lceil1/\sqrt{p_{\min}}\rceil$; exact rational comparisons or integer binary search implement this selection. A missing crossing gives `ESTIMATION_FAIL`. Execute exactly $k$ ordinary iterates with this sampler and projector. The inequality $(2k+1)^2\widehat q_i\le1/n$ concerns the estimate; no identical actual-success upper bound is assumed.

At the final interval apply [[alg-qa-27-capped-lower-bound-amplification]] to the selected sampler with lower bound $1/(18n)$ and failure $\rho/4$. Copy/measure a separate success record before applying $(A')^\dagger$ to erase internal phase/clock/flag work on the successful branch. In `efficient-qsvt` mode also apply the supplied/constructed projective instrument onto zero for every work/clock/internal-flag register, including $W_B$, after this uncompute; return the system only if every tested register is zero, and set the external herald to failure otherwise. This makes the conditional returned system state pure; its work-check error/failure is budgeted with $e_*$. The instrument and its controlled-zero reflection/cost are included in $H$. Return the system and external heralding record; a failed branch returns `FAIL`.

For each chosen quantum resource coordinate, construct an integer $H\ge1$ from the actual original-stage, controlled/inverse, selected/input-reflection, dilution and predicate lists, so their interval cost is at most $H2^{j-1}$; enlarge $H$ to include all actually needed gatewise-control depths. For gate coordinates also include the uniform upper bound for the finite estimator's QFT, efficient-grid rounding, rational medians and loop/predicate overhead over every allowed scale through its declared cap; these scales are a finite explicit function of $p_{\min},c,\rho$. Since each sampler-list cost is at least one, this common per-call polynomial-logarithmic factor absorbs that ordinary overhead without treating it as an oracle call. Pad cumulative original stage times to $t_j=H2^j$. Let $r$ be the actual median repetition count of the shared estimator, using its floor and confidence. In `efficient-qsvt` mode impose the additional total primitive-cost cap
$$K=\left\lceil2^{30}(r/c)H\alpha_{\max}n^4\right\rceil.$$
Count construction estimation, list invocations, production, inverse/control/reflection calls and final amplification against this cap and return `RESOURCE_TIMEOUT` before exceeding it. Each coordinate uses its actual $H$ and corresponding cap. Classical coefficient/phase construction, exact algebraic comparisons, output rounding, compiler construction and arithmetic bit work keep their own charged coordinates. The original Fourier mode retains its original declared construction/estimation caps; its distinct table and SELECT costs are not hidden by the efficient-mode quantum cap.

For the CKS dyadic eigenvalue-resolution procedure with $m=\lceil\log_2\kappa\rceil+1$ stages, a supported eigenvalue $\lambda$ is routed to one of two adjacent stopping intervals by the source's gapped phase-estimation test; the transition-band and estimator-failure mass must be included in the error budget. If $c_k$ are the input spectral amplitudes, the source analysis gives stage costs $t_j=\widetilde O(d2^j)$, maximum time $T_{\max}=\widetilde O(d\kappa)$, and, up to the allocated approximation error, a success amplitude proportional to $1/(\alpha_{\max}\lambda)$ on eigenvalue $\lambda$. Consequently
$$T_{\rm av}^2=\widetilde O\!\left(d^2\sum_k\frac{|c_k|^2}{\lambda_k^2}\right),\qquad \sqrt{p_{\rm succ}}=\widetilde\Theta\!\left(\frac1{\alpha_{\max}}\sqrt{\sum_k\frac{|c_k|^2}{\lambda_k^2}}\right).$$
In the explicitly declared `efficient-qsvt` mode of the local constructor, the proof below establishes these bounds with its actual charged interval budget. The source coefficient estimate $\alpha_{\max}=\widetilde O(\kappa)$ then gives $T_{\rm av}/\sqrt{p_{\rm succ}}=\widetilde O(d\kappa)$. These are the source-efficient stopping quantities; the proof below establishes the corresponding finite estimated-wrapper floor, normalization, error and stopping bounds in this mode, while the retained Fourier-table mode keeps its distinct actual costs.

For every promised input of [[alg-qa-relative-probability-estimation]], the procedure terminates. If $p=0$, it returns $\widehat p=0$ with certainty. If $p>0$, then
$$\Pr\{|\widehat p-p|\le cp\}\ge1-\beta.$$

Let $C$ count all invocations of the declared sampler and inverse capabilities: each controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, and initial ordinary $A$ preparation is counted once in this total, while their individual resource coordinates remain distinct. Put $p_*=\max\{p,p_{\min}\}$, and let $L,r,M_L$ be the algorithm's finite parameters. Then
$$\mathbb E C=O\!\left(\frac{r}{c\sqrt{p_*}}\right),\qquad r=O\!\left(1+\log\frac{L+2}{\beta}\right),\qquad L=O\!\left(1+\log\frac1{p_{\min}}\right).$$
Every execution satisfies the charged cap
$$C<\frac{65rM_L}{c}<\frac{4160r}{c\sqrt{p_{\min}}}.$$
With probability at least $1-\beta$, both $|\widehat p-p|\le cp$ and $C<4160r/(c\sqrt{p_*})$ hold; when $p=0$, both hold deterministically. Thus the expected sampler-and-inverse count is
$$O\!\left(\frac{1+\log((2+\log(1/p_{\min}))/\beta)}{c\sqrt{\max\{p,p_{\min}\}}}\right).$$

These bounds require the algorithm's explicit controlled-access contract. They do not identify a controlled black-box call with an ordinary uncontrolled black-box call. Controlled reflections, control phases, QFT and other ordinary gates, measurements, and classical postprocessing retain separate charged costs. In the retained `exact-cyclotomic` mode, rounding uses finitely many exact algebraic comparisons and produces a rational with $O(\log N)$ bits in each of numerator and denominator at a final scale $N$; no polynomial or polylogarithmic classical-bit bound is asserted. The optional `efficient-grid` mode instead has the helper's uniform polynomial-in-$\log M$ rounding gates, work and generation, while preserving every probability/query bound. Estimation measures only its own construction workspaces, so a subsequent fresh sampler execution, conditional on the returned classical transcript, retains that sampler's prescribed output state and conditional good state.

Let $n\ge1$ be an integer. Let a coherent sampler have success weight $q>0$, and suppose an estimate $\widehat q>0$ satisfies $|\widehat q-q|\le q/100$ and $\widehat q\le1/(9n)$. Choose the least integer $k\ge0$ such that $(2k+1)^2\widehat q\ge1/(9n)$, and put $d=2k+1$, $x=d^2\widehat q$, $y=d^2q$. Applying $k$ standard iterates of [[alg-qa-12-amplitude-amplification]] gives success weight $r$ satisfying
$$\frac1{9n}\le x\le\frac1n,\qquad \frac{100}{101}x\le y\le\frac{100}{99}x,\qquad y\left(1-\frac2{5n}\right)\le r\le y.$$
In particular $1/(16n)\le r\le\min\{1,100/(99n)\}$, and the positive-probability conditional good state is unchanged. The total number of sampler/inverse calls in this fixed amplification is exactly $d$, charging reflections separately.

For any $s\le n$ such amplifications, indexed by $i$, with the same parameter $n$, their multiplicative losses obey
$$\prod_{i=1}^s\frac{r_i}{d_i^2q_i}\ge\frac35,\qquad \prod_{i=1}^s d_i\le\sqrt{\frac53}\prod_{i=1}^s\sqrt{\frac{r_i}{q_i}}.$$

Under the inputs and promise of [[alg-qa-27-capped-lower-bound-amplification]], that finite procedure succeeds with probability at least $1-\beta$. Conditional on success, its returned register has exactly the density operator $|g\rangle\langle g|$, where $|g\rangle=PU|0\rangle/\sqrt p$. This includes all output and workspace registers of the original conditional good state.

Its deterministic caps are $2RM$ total calls to $U,U^\dagger$, $R(M-1)$ zero-input reflections and $R(M+1)$ good reflections, including the controlled good-reflection calls implementing at most two instruments per trial. It uses at most $R\log_2M$ unbiased random bits. Consequently its primitive-call cap is $O(p_0^{-1/2}(1+\ln(1/\beta)))$, or $O(p_0^{-1/2}\ln(1/\beta))$ when $\beta\le1/2$. Query calls, gates, initialization, instruments, control variants and classical preprocessing are separately charged.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

Let $\tau=\alpha|t|$ and $L=\ln(1/\epsilon)$, with $0<\epsilon<1$. In the nontrivial branch $\tau>\epsilon$, put $S=\tau+L/\ln(e+L/\tau)$. The small-time-aware simulator of [[alg-qa-25-small-time-aware-simulator]] uses zero signal queries when $\tau\le\epsilon$. When $\tau>\epsilon$, the OP4 degree satisfies $d=O(S)$. The complete OAA circuit uses at most $3(d_E+d_O)\le6d$ ordinary $U/U^*$ signal calls, where $d_E,d_O\le d$ are the even and odd QSP degrees. It uses $3(d_E+d_O+2)$ projector-phase slots and therefore $6(d_E+d_O+2)$ controlled-reflection calls, by [[thm-qa-24-qsvt-query-count]]. Coherent selection of each real sequence against identity uses exactly one controlled signal call when that sequence degree is odd and none when it is even; because the selection occurs in each of the three OAA blocks $W,W^*,W$, the total is $3(\mathbf1_{d_E\text{ odd}}+\mathbf1_{d_O\text{ odd}})\le6$ controlled signal calls. The $\Phi/-\Phi$ branch itself controls phases, not signal calls. Any external control of the complete simulator controls and charges the whole block.

Gate, depth, width, ancilla, classical bit, precision, PREPARE/SELECT, phase-list-generation, and sparse-location/value costs remain separate coordinates. For a $d_H$-row-sparse input with supplied-permutation bound $h\ge h_{\max}$, the $h=0$ branch encodes $H=0$ with normalization $1$ and uses no location or value calls. If $h>0$, [[thm-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding-correctness]] gives normalization $\alpha=d_Hh$; choosing the tight bound $h=h_{\max}$ gives $\alpha=d_Hh_{\max}$. Multiply the signal-query count by the actual supplied sparse-encoding cost, including any location-permutation completion. The optional sorted-XOR mode has the same normalization $d_Hh$ for a supplied positive entry bound $h$ and multiplies the signal count by $O(\log(d_H+1))$ location calls and $O(1)$ value calls per signal, including inverses and coherent controls. No cost-free conversion from XOR row-location access is claimed. If $\tau$ is bounded above and below by positive constants as $\epsilon\to0$, the query bound specializes to $O(\tau+L/\ln L)=O(\tau+\ln(1/\epsilon)/\ln\ln(1/\epsilon))$. This is an upper bound; no matching lower bound for arbitrary block-encoding access or for the additive precision term is asserted.

For a $d_H$-row-sparse Hermitian $H$, put $h_{\max}=\max_{i,j}|H_{ij}|$ and supply a certified bound $h\ge h_{\max}$. In the supplied-permutation mode, if $h=0$ then $H=0$ and the returned $X_{\rm flag}\otimes I$ has zero all-zero-flag compression and normalization $1$; if $h>0$, the designated all-zero auxiliary compression of $U_L^*U_R$ from [[alg-qa-25-sparse-hamiltonian-block-encoding]] is $H/(d_Hh)$. One such block-encoding call uses one supplied inverse row-location permutation, one supplied column-location permutation, two entry-value queries (compute and uncompute), and the declared $D_{d_H}$, inverse, flag-rotation, and arithmetic implementations. In the optional sorted-XOR mode with $h>0$, the encoded matrix is $H\oplus0$ with normalization $d_Hh$, and each encoding, actual adjoint or coherent controlled call costs $O(\log(d_H+1))$ original location calls and $O(1)$ value calls. derivations.claim: For each quantum coordinate construct $H$ from the finite stage/control/inverse/reflection/dilution lists as in [F1]. For gate coordinates its computed bound also includes the QFT/efficient-grid rounding/median overhead over the estimator's finite allowed scales, so the sampler-call estimate multiplies actual ordinary-gate overhead rather than ignoring it. The assigned dyadic times have increments $\Delta_j$, and every interval's reflection-pair and reversible-predicate cost is included in its increment. Let $s_j$ be original good-or-unfinished mass, $r_j$ the amplified selected mass, $q_j=r_{j-1}s_j/s_{j-1}$ and $v_j$ the amplified circuit cost. With $d_j=2k_j+1$ the ordinary amplification multiplier, $v_j\le d_j(v_{j-1}+\Delta_j)$. Here the $d_j$ sampler/inverse invocations plus $k_j$ reflection pairs fit this allocated budget; none of those costs is free.

To evaluate $H$, an inverse stage has gap $\delta_j=\phi_j/d$ and polynomial degree $O(d2^j\log(d\kappa/\epsilon))$, and exactly that many signal calls plus one more phase slot by [F6]. The real-extraction, dilution and success-projector circuits are explicit. Gapped phase estimation uses the least admissible dyadic label size $O(2^j)$ and $O(\log(1/\zeta))$ coherent repetitions. At each QPE power, the actual QA25 small-time-aware simulation has $O(d|t|+\log(1/\eta))$ signal cost, with a separately counted zero-signal branch for sufficiently small time; summing its dyadic evolution times gives $O(d2^j)$ and summing the additive precision term gives only additional logarithmic factors. Controlled/inverse calls and sparse block construction carry their actual costs. Thus the query-coordinate interval bound is $H=O(d\,\operatorname{polylog}(d\kappa/\epsilon,1/\rho))$, with an additional $O(\log(d+1))$ factor only if the optional sorted-XOR sparse bridge is chosen. Under the explicit gate specialization in the Statement, the $B$ and sparse-access calls, controlled/inverse forms, QA25 simulator, phase compiler, reflections, clock predicates, dilution rotations and final instrument have the stated uniform gate costs; substituting these bounds into the same interval list gives $H=O(d\,\operatorname{polylog}(N,d,\kappa,1/\epsilon,1/\rho))$ for the gate coordinate. No bare matrix or arbitrary black-box unitary is assigned free access.

Put $S_i=\sum_{j\le i}\Delta_j\sqrt{s_{j-1}}$ and $S=S_m$. Expanding the recurrence and substituting $q_j$ telescopes the probability factors. The product loss in [F4], together with $r_{j-1}\ge1/(16n)$, gives $v_i\le6\sqrt n\sqrt{r_i/s_i}\,S_i$. Also $s_{j-1}\le p+u_{j-1}$, where $u$ is original unfinished mass. The first dyadic increment is at most $T_{\rm av}$ and later increments equal the preceding deadline, so $\Delta_j\sqrt{u_{j-1}}\le T_{\rm av}$. Thus by [F2], $$S\le T_{\max}\sqrt p+mT_{\rm av}\le12nH\alpha\sqrt p.$$ Consequently the next unamplified sampler's cost $b_i=v_{i-1}+\Delta_i$ satisfies $$\frac{b_i}{\sqrt{q_i}}\le\frac{10\sqrt n S}{\sqrt p}\le128n^{3/2}H\alpha.$$ These estimates also hold at the initial interval with $r_{-1}=s_{-1}=1$ and zero preceding cost.

Use confidence $\beta=\rho/(16n)$ for each of at most $n$ generic estimator invocations and relative error $c=1/100$. On the intersection of their joint accuracy-and-cost events, [F3] and step 2.1 bound the total quantum estimation cost by $n\cdot4160(r/c)\cdot128n^{3/2}H\alpha<2^{20}(r/c)n^{5/2}H\alpha$. The floors and both scheduler branches are valid by [F2]. The final production cost is at most $72n^{3/2}H\alpha$, since $r_m\le1$ in the bound for $v_m$.

The final lower-bound amplifier has $p_0=1/(18n)$, dyadic trial range $M<4\sqrt{18n}<17\sqrt n$, and $R\le1+\ln(4/\rho)/\ln(4/3)$. Its sampler/reflection budget is therefore at most $2^{13}Rn^2H\alpha$. The median repetition choice in [F3] implies $R\le32r$ by comparing its defining geometric confidence inequality with $(3/4)^R\le\rho/4$. The final cost is at most $2^{18}rn^2H\alpha$. All these costs fit strictly below the specified cap $K=\lceil2^{30}(r/c)H\alpha n^4\rceil$. Thus on the good confidence event the resource-timeout branch is never reached, and on every transcript the primitive-cost budget is at most $K$.

The union bound for the estimator events is at most $n\beta\le\rho/16$, including their joint cost failures. Conditional on the good construction transcript, [F5] fails with probability at most $\rho/4$. The final zero-work test has additional failure at most $\rho/4096$ by [F2]. Hence the finite solver succeeds with probability at least $1-5\rho/16-\rho/4096\ge1-\rho$. For a fixed good construction transcript, [F5] gives the same conditional good-state density operator as the actual sampler on every successful terminal amplification branch. Let $g$ be its phase-fixed one-attempt good unit vector, to which [F2] applies. A unit ket on any such branch is $c g$ with $|c|=1$. Applying the actual internal uncompute and projecting work onto zero multiplies the resulting canonical system vector by the same $c$; normalization preserves this unit phase. Thus choosing the representative with this phase removed gives exactly the normalized vector estimate of [F2], and every other unit representative satisfies the stated bound after multiplication by a unit scalar. The external herald is recorded before uncomputing internal flag/bucket work. No relative phase between eigencomponents or coherent stages is changed. All numerical implementation errors used here are the deterministic vector bounds already allocated in [F1], so they are not omitted probabilistic failures.

Since $n=O(1+\log\kappa)$, $\alpha\le8\kappa$ and $r=O(1+\log((2+\log(1/p_{\min}))/\rho))$, the cap in step 4.1 is $O(d\kappa\operatorname{polylog}(d\kappa/\epsilon,1/\rho))$ in the query specialization, and has only the stated polynomial-logarithmic gate overhead. Fixing a constant $\rho<1/3$ gives the original source target. If a smaller support-gap promise $1/\kappa'$ is supplied, run the same construction with that declared parameter and replace $\kappa$ throughout. Output remains a quantum state. Classical polynomial/phase generation, exact algebraic comparisons, arithmetic bit implementation and compiler construction remain separately charged coordinates; this quantum gate/query result asserts no polylogarithmic total bit-time for them. The retained full Fourier-table and capped alternates preserve their actual costs and are not used to infer the efficient-mode bound.

citations.quote:
A finite coherent variable-time algorithm has a finite family of stopping times $0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=T_{\max}$, a designated output space, and a finite clock/step register. A run is **unfinished** at stage $j$ if it has not entered a stopping subspace by $t_j$; otherwise it is **stopped**. The stopping subspaces are pairwise orthogonal, and the output register labels each stopped branch as **good** or **bad**. Every later stage is controlled on the unfinished projector, so a stopped branch is not advanced. Admissibility requires the first-stop subspaces to exhaust the reachable state at $T_{\max}$ for every allowed input; no branch remains unfinished after the final stage. The input specifies each stage unitary, its inverse and every controlled form used, and the gate/query cost for each.

For a normalized input state, let $p_i$ be the Born probability mass in the subspace that first stops at $t_i$. These are nonnegative masses of orthogonal subspaces whose sum is the reachable state at the final time, so $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1$. Define the root-mean-square stopping time
$$T_{\rm av}:=\left(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i t_i^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Let $p_{\rm succ}$ be the total Born probability of the good-output subspace. When $p_{\rm succ}>0$, the good output means the normalized conditional state of the declared good projector; it is defined only on that positive-probability branch. The mean stopping time $\sum_i p_i t_i$ is a different quantity and is not substituted for $T_{\rm av}$.

A measured adaptive procedure qualifies only if it has a finite coherent implementation with the same stopped/unfinished branch semantics and the required inverse/coherent access. Measurement records used to choose a circuit may be classical construction data; no intermediate measurement is inserted into a branch whose later inverse must erase that record. All stopping times, branch probabilities, reflections, inverses, controlled calls, and state preparation remain explicit resource inputs. Complexity statements use an actual normalized primitive-operation coordinate: positive counts are at least one, and the declared interval budgets include the preparation, controlled/inverse and input/selected-reflection operations used in the construction. Other weighted time coordinates may be recorded, but arbitrary uncharged subunit weights do not inherit logarithmic operation-count bounds.

A supplied-probability production regime must specify finite probability/schedule certificates rather than infer them from black-box unitary access. For each dyadic interval it supplies the odd amplification multiplier and certificates relating the actual original good-or-unfinished mass $s_j$, prior selected mass $r_{j-1}$, next mass $q_j=r_{j-1}s_j/s_{j-1}$ and amplified mass $r_j$ to the numerical inequalities required by its theorem; it also supplies a rational constant-factor lower enclosure for the final selected mass. Data may use exact rational/algebraic representations, certified rational enclosures with the stated valid inequalities, or a separately declared exact-real representation/comparison resource. The finite construction and verification cost $C_{\rm build}$ includes every oracle call used to acquire or certify probability information, as well as classical arithmetic, list generation and output costs. No zero-query method obtaining these data is assumed. A uniform regime without those certificates must instead state its supplied probability floor, confidence and complete estimation/production costs. Branch probabilities defined above remain valid analysis quantities even when they are unknown to the implementation.

Let $a\in[0,1]$ be the initial success weight and let $\theta\in[0,\pi/2]$ be the unique angle satisfying $\sin^2\theta=a$. After exactly $k\ge0$ standard amplitude-amplification iterates, the probability of the good outcome of $\{\Pi_{\mathrm{good}},I-\Pi_{\mathrm{good}}\}$ is
$
\sin^2((2k+1)\theta).
$
The endpoints $a=0$ and $a=1$ are included by direct evaluation, without normalizing a zero component.

Let $n\ge1$ be an integer. Let a coherent sampler have success weight $q>0$, and suppose an estimate $\widehat q>0$ satisfies $|\widehat q-q|\le q/100$ and $\widehat q\le1/(9n)$. Choose the least integer $k\ge0$ such that $(2k+1)^2\widehat q\ge1/(9n)$, and put $d=2k+1$, $x=d^2\widehat q$, $y=d^2q$. Applying $k$ standard iterates of [[alg-qa-12-amplitude-amplification]] gives success weight $r$ satisfying
$$\frac1{9n}\le x\le\frac1n,\qquad \frac{100}{101}x\le y\le\frac{100}{99}x,\qquad y\left(1-\frac2{5n}\right)\le r\le y.$$
In particular $1/(16n)\le r\le\min\{1,100/(99n)\}$, and the positive-probability conditional good state is unchanged. The total number of sampler/inverse calls in this fixed amplification is exactly $d$, charging reflections separately.

For any $s\le n$ such amplifications, indexed by $i$, with the same parameter $n$, their multiplicative losses obey
$$\prod_{i=1}^s\frac{r_i}{d_i^2q_i}\ge\frac35,\qquad \prod_{i=1}^s d_i\le\sqrt{\frac53}\prod_{i=1}^s\sqrt{\frac{r_i}{q_i}}.$$

For every promised input of [[alg-qa-relative-probability-estimation]], the procedure terminates. If $p=0$, it returns $\widehat p=0$ with certainty. If $p>0$, then
$$\Pr\{|\widehat p-p|\le cp\}\ge1-\beta.$$

Let $C$ count all invocations of the declared sampler and inverse capabilities: each controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, and initial ordinary $A$ preparation is counted once in this total, while their individual resource coordinates remain distinct. Put $p_*=\max\{p,p_{\min}\}$, and let $L,r,M_L$ be the algorithm's finite parameters. Then
$$\mathbb E C=O\!\left(\frac{r}{c\sqrt{p_*}}\right),\qquad r=O\!\left(1+\log\frac{L+2}{\beta}\right),\qquad L=O\!\left(1+\log\frac1{p_{\min}}\right).$$
Every execution satisfies the charged cap
$$C<\frac{65rM_L}{c}<\frac{4160r}{c\sqrt{p_{\min}}}.$$
With probability at least $1-\beta$, both $|\widehat p-p|\le cp$ and $C<4160r/(c\sqrt{p_*})$ hold; when $p=0$, both hold deterministically. Thus the expected sampler-and-inverse count is
$$O\!\left(\frac{1+\log((2+\log(1/p_{\min}))/\beta)}{c\sqrt{\max\{p,p_{\min}\}}}\right).$$

These bounds require the algorithm's explicit controlled-access contract. They do not identify a controlled black-box call with an ordinary uncontrolled black-box call. Controlled reflections, control phases, QFT and other ordinary gates, measurements, and classical postprocessing retain separate charged costs. In the retained `exact-cyclotomic` mode, rounding uses finitely many exact algebraic comparisons and produces a rational with $O(\log N)$ bits in each of numerator and denominator at a final scale $N$; no polynomial or polylogarithmic classical-bit bound is asserted. The optional `efficient-grid` mode instead has the helper's uniform polynomial-in-$\log M$ rounding gates, work and generation, while preserving every probability/query bound. Estimation measures only its own construction workspaces, so a subsequent fresh sampler execution, conditional on the returned classical transcript, retains that sampler's prescribed output state and conditional good state.

Under the inputs and promise of [[alg-qa-27-capped-lower-bound-amplification]], that finite procedure succeeds with probability at least $1-\beta$. Conditional on success, its returned register has exactly the density operator $|g\rangle\langle g|$, where $|g\rangle=PU|0\rangle/\sqrt p$. This includes all output and workspace registers of the original conditional good state.

Its deterministic caps are $2RM$ total calls to $U,U^\dagger$, $R(M-1)$ zero-input reflections and $R(M+1)$ good reflections, including the controlled good-reflection calls implementing at most two instruments per trial. It uses at most $R\log_2M$ unbiased random bits. Consequently its primitive-call cap is $O(p_0^{-1/2}(1+\ln(1/\beta)))$, or $O(p_0^{-1/2}\ln(1/\beta))$ when $\beta\le1/2$. Query calls, gates, initialization, instruments, control variants and classical preprocessing are separately charged.

derivations.claim: Group the original operation-count execution into dyadic deadlines, assigning each stopped branch the first deadline after its original stopping count. All counts are positive integers in the declared coordinate. Treat an original stage as indivisible: group all stages ending by each deadline and use twice that deadline as its padded cumulative budget. The interval then covers every grouped whole-stage call. This changes maximum and RMS counts by at most four and leaves stopped branches untouched. There are at most $n$ intervals with increments $\Delta_j$ summing to at most $4T_{\max}$. Their input/selected-reflection and preparation/control budgets are included, rather than treated as free additional operations. We retain this factor in the numerical constants below.

Let $s_j$ be the original probability of being already good or still unfinished at deadline $j$, with $s_{-1}=1$. It decreases, is at least $p>0$, and has final value $p$. Construct $B_j$ by running the preceding amplified list and continuing the original algorithm only on unfinished branches. Inductively its selected component is proportional to the original selected component, with probability $q_j=r_{j-1}s_j/s_{j-1}$; initially $r_{-1}=1$. Amplify by the chosen odd multiplier. By [F2] this preserves the conditional selected state, and at the last deadline that state is the exact original conditional good state.

Let $v_j$ be the production-list cost and $d_j$ its amplification multiplier. Then $v_j\le d_j(v_{j-1}+\Delta_j)$, with $v_{-1}=0$. The supplied-regime certificate or [F3] gives $d_j\le\sqrt{r_j/q_j}(1-2/(5n))^{-1/2}$ on amplified intervals, with no loss on unamplified intervals. Expand the recurrence. For each summand, $$\prod_{\ell=j}^{h}\sqrt{r_\ell/q_\ell}=\sqrt{\frac{r_hs_{j-1}}{r_{j-1}p}}.$$ The total loss is at most $\sqrt{5/3}$, and $r_{j-1}\ge1/(16n)$ (with initial value one), so $$v_h\le6\sqrt{nr_h/p}\sum_j\Delta_j\sqrt{s_{j-1}}.$$ The same bound holds for every prefix with its corresponding $r_i,s_i$.

In the uniform regime use [F4] with $c=1/100$, floor $q_{\min}=p_0/(64n)$ and failure $\beta=\rho/(16n)$ at each of at most $n$ intervals. All estimation workspaces are fresh construction data, discarded before production. On the estimator-good event, a returned $\widehat q>1/(9n)$ uses $d=1$ and actual $r=q>(100/101)/(9n)>1/(16n)$, with loss one. Otherwise choose the least odd $d$ with $d^2\widehat q\ge1/(9n)$; search only through $k\le\lceil1/\sqrt{q_{\min}}\rceil$ and return failure if no crossing is found. [F3] gives the same surviving floor and loss bound in this case. Inductively $q_j\ge p/(16n)\ge p_0/(16n)>q_{\min}$, so every estimator promise is met on this joint event; a zero estimate or exhausted search is then impossible. The actual upper bound $r\le1/n$ is neither claimed nor used.

Write $u_{j-1}$ for original unfinished mass at the preceding deadline. Since $s_{j-1}\le p+u_{j-1}$ and $\Delta_j\sqrt{u_{j-1}}\le2T_{\rm av}$ by the dyadic stopping convention (also at the first interval, because stopping counts are at least one), $$S:=\sum_j\Delta_j\sqrt{s_{j-1}}\le4(T_{\max}\sqrt p+nT_{\rm av}).$$ In the supplied-data regime apply [F5] at lower bound $\ell\ge r_h/2$ and constant failure $1/2$. Its $O(r_h^{-1/2})$ factor cancels $\sqrt{r_h}$ in step 3.1, proving production cost $O(T_{\max}\sqrt n+(T_{\rm av}/\sqrt p)n^{3/2})$. Substitute $n=O(\ln L_T)$ and add the actual $C_{\rm build}$, including its probability-acquisition oracle calls. Independent repetitions give the stated confidence. No construction-cost bound follows solely from existence of true-probability-selected multipliers.

The prefix version of step 3.1 and $r_{j-1}\ge1/(16n)$ give the next sampler cost $b_i$ the bound $b_i/\sqrt{q_i}\le10\sqrt nS/\sqrt p$. Use step 4.1 and [F4] to charge every estimation call. Summing at most $n$ stages gives at most $2^{18}(r/c)(n^{3/2}T_{\max}+n^{5/2}T_{\rm av}/\sqrt p)$ with slack for dyadic padding. Final production has $v_h\le6\sqrt nS/\sqrt p$. Apply [F5] with floor $1/(18n)$ and failure $\rho/4$: its range is $M<17\sqrt n$, and its trial count $R$ is at most $32r$. Thus its complete additional cost fits within $2^{20}(r/c)n^{5/2}(T_{\max}+T_{\rm av}/\sqrt p)$, again with slack for the already charged reflection/interval overhead. This proves the stated joint-event bound and includes the quantum cost of acquiring probability data.

The computable integer $P_0$ satisfies $P_0\ge1/\sqrt{p_0}$ and $P_0<2/\sqrt{p_0}$. Since $T_{\rm av}\le T_{\max}$ and $p\ge p_0$, the joint-event cost in step 5.1 is below $K$. Count all construction, production, inverse/control/reflection stage calls and final amplification against $K$, stopping before an excess. The resource timeout therefore never occurs on the joint estimator-good event. Its complement has probability at most $n\beta\le\rho/16$ by [F4] and the union bound. Conditional on the good construction event, final capped amplification fails with probability at most $\rho/4$. Total failure is at most $5\rho/16<\rho$. Every heralded good branch has the same conditional original state by step 2.1, even after averaging the classical construction transcript. The procedure is finite on every branch by its explicit caps.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be normal. If $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $T$,
then there are pairwise orthogonal projections $P_1,\dots,P_r$ such that

$$T=\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j P_j,$$

each $P_j$ projects onto the eigenspace $E_{\lambda_j}(T)$, and every $P_j$ is
a polynomial in $T$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, let $T:V\to V$ be
normal, and write the spectral resolution from
[[thm-spectral-resolution-and-polynomial-spectral-projections]] as

$$T=\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j P_j,$$

where the $\lambda_j$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $T$ and $P_j$ is the
orthogonal projection onto $E_{\lambda_j}(T)$. For a function
$f:\sigma(T)\to\mathbb C$ on the spectrum of $T$, define

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be normal. If $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $T$,
then there are pairwise orthogonal projections $P_1,\dots,P_r$ such that

$$T=\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j P_j,$$

each $P_j$ projects onto the eigenspace $E_{\lambda_j}(T)$, and every $P_j$ is
a polynomial in $T$.

Let $H$ be a Hermitian endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with distinct eigenvalues $\lambda$ and orthogonal spectral projections $P_\lambda$. Let $\psi$ be a unit vector representing a pure state. Its **state-dependent spectral distribution** is the finite measure on $\sigma(H)$ defined by
$$\mu_\psi(\{\lambda\})=\|P_\lambda\psi\|^2=\langle\psi|P_\lambda|\psi\rangle.$$
The support is restricted to eigenvalues with nonzero weight; degeneracies are represented by one atom per distinct eigenvalue, not one atom per chosen eigenvector. The formula is the definition; its nonnegativity, total mass one, and functional-calculus moment identity are established in [[thm-qa-28-spectral-law-measurement]].

**Inputs.** An instance of [[def-qa-28-spectral-estimation-access]], a phase-register size $m\ge1$ with $Q=2^m$, and an input system register already prepared in the normalized state $\psi$ declared by the access instance. The caller invokes and charges $A_\psi$ for that preparation; this procedure does not prepare the system again. The access instance fixes the phase encoding $\theta(\lambda)$ and decoder.

**Instructions.** Initialize the phase register to $|0^m\rangle$. Apply the coherent QPE gate list through the inverse QFT from [[alg-qa-quantum-phase-estimation]] to this prepared system, using the supplied controlled powers for $j=0,\ldots,m-1$, or synthesize each required power from the declared controlled-$U$ interface. Perform its specified computational-basis Lüders measurement once on the phase register and record $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$. Return $y/Q$ as a circular phase sample and apply the specified decoder to return an eigenvalue estimate when the injective encoding promise holds. If $U=e^{iH}$ and $\sigma(H)\subseteq[-1,1]$, use the principal representative in $(-1/2,1/2]$ and output $2\pi\operatorname{unwrap}(y/Q)$.

The phase register, controlled powers, gates, decoder arithmetic, measurement, and output costs follow the access record. In particular, with only a controlled-$U$ oracle, implementing the binary powers uses $\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}2^j=Q-1$ controlled-$U$ calls.

Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and let the input be an eigenvector with
$U\psi=\exp(2\pi i\theta)\psi$, where $\theta\in[0,1)$.
For each $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, the probability of measuring $y$ in the algorithm of [[alg-qa-quantum-phase-estimation]] is
$$P_\theta(y)=Q^{-2}\left|\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}\exp\!\left(2\pi i j(\theta-y/Q)\right)\right|^2.$$
Thus the finite outcome kernel is defined at every phase, including $Q\theta\in\mathbb Z$; no quotient with a zero denominator is needed in this formula.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

**Input.** An integer $m\ge1$; an $m$-qubit phase register; a finite-dimensional system register $H$; a unitary $U:H\to H$; a unit eigenvector $\psi$ with promised phase $\theta\in[0,1)$; and one of the forward access capabilities in [[def-qa-eigenphase-estimation-model]].

**Output.** A classical label $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$ and its phase estimate $y/Q$, where $Q=2^m$.

**Instructions.**

1. Initialize the phase register in $|0^m\rangle$ and the system register in $\psi$.
2. Apply the Hadamard $H=(X+Z)/\sqrt2$ of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] to each phase wire. This prepares $Q^{-1/2}\sum_{x=0}^{Q-1}|x\rangle\otimes\psi$ in the declared big-endian order.
3. For $j=0,\ldots,m-1$, apply the supplied controlled $U^{2^j}$ to control wire $q_{m-1-j}$ and the system. Under single controlled-unitary access, implement that operation with $2^j$ sequential calls to $C(U)$, as specified by the access model.
4. Apply the inverse of the positive-sign exact binary QFT circuit of [[def-qa-cyclic-quantum-fourier-transform]] and [[thm-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit-correct]]. Construct it by reversing the chronological gate list and replacing each gate by its adjoint, including the final swaps and negating controlled-phase angles.
5. Perform the computational-basis projective measurement on the phase register. Its specified Lüders instrument has branch map $Z\mapsto (|y\rangle\langle y|\otimes I_H)Z(|y\rangle\langle y|\otimes I_H)$ for each label $y$ ([[def-qc-projective-measurement]], [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]). Output the observed label $y$ and the ratio $y/Q$.

The inverse in step 4 is the inverse QFT, not $U^{-1}$; a forward QPE run makes no controlled inverse-unitary query. The coherent prefix is the circuit through step 4 before measurement. A consumer that coherently uncomputes this prefix needs the separate controlled inverse-power capability from [[def-qa-eigenphase-estimation-model]].

This is the **spectral functional calculus** of $T$. For the identity function

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

derivations.claim: The orthogonality in [F1] gives $\psi=\sum_\lambda P_\lambda\psi$ and $\|\psi\|^2=\sum_\lambda\|P_\lambda\psi\|^2=1$. Thus the weights in [F2] are nonnegative and sum to one. By [F5]–[F6], $\langle\psi|g(H)|\psi\rangle=\sum_\lambda g(\lambda)\langle\psi|P_\lambda|\psi\rangle=\sum_\lambda\mu_\psi(\{\lambda\})g(\lambda)$.

By linearity, the QPE unitary sends the initial phase state and $\psi$ to $\sum_\lambda\sum_y a_y(\lambda)|y\rangle\otimes P_\lambda\psi$, using [F3] on each eigenspace. Projecting the phase register onto $|y\rangle$ gives the system vector $v_y=\sum_\lambda a_y(\lambda)P_\lambda\psi$. Since the summands for distinct $\lambda$ are orthogonal by [F1], [F4] yields $\Pr(Y=y)=\|v_y\|^2=\sum_\lambda |a_y(\lambda)|^2\|P_\lambda\psi\|^2=\sum_\lambda\mu_\psi(\{\lambda\})P_{\bar\theta(\lambda)}(y)$. Summing these probabilities over the finite output set gives one, as each eigenphase kernel is a measurement law.

When $\Pr(Y=y)>0$, [F4] normalizes the projected branch to $v_y/\|v_y\|$, which is the displayed formula. Its coefficients $a_y(\lambda)$ need not vanish outside one eigenvalue, so no exact eigenspace-collapse claim follows; the formula itself gives the precise conditional state.

For each $j\in J$, supply a positive scale $\gamma_j$ satisfying $|g_j(t)|\le\gamma_j$ on that interval, a tolerance $\tau_j\ge0$, a nonnegative degree bound $d_j$, and a real polynomial $p_j$ of degree at most $d_j$ and parity $d_j\bmod2$ (including when $p_j=0$), with $|p_j(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$ and
$$\left|p_j(x)-\frac{g_j(\alpha x)}{\gamma_j}\right|\le\tau_j\qquad(-1\le x\le1).$$
For each active component, also supply either a reflected-convention phase-list certificate of length $d_j+1$ for which the real part of the QSP sequence's upper-left entry equals $p_j$ (exactly or within a certified uniform error bound), or, when $p_j$ has rational or exact algebraic coefficients, a positive rational phase-synthesis tolerance $\nu_j$ for OP1. Here the four real component functions are
$$g_0(t)=\frac{\Re\bar f(t)+\Re\bar f(-t)}2,\quad g_1(t)=\frac{\Re\bar f(t)-\Re\bar f(-t)}2,$$
$$g_2(t)=\frac{\Im\bar f(t)+\Im\bar f(-t)}2,\quad g_3(t)=\frac{\Im\bar f(t)-\Im\bar f(-t)}2.$$
Thus $g_0,g_2$ are even, $g_1,g_3$ are odd, and $\bar f=g_0+g_1+i g_2+i g_3$. The zero certificates and scale bounds give $|\bar f(t)|\le B:=\sum_{j\in J}\gamma_j$; the construction makes no optimal-normalization claim. The formulas include singular values $0$ and $1$, repeated singular values, unmatched left and right kernels, and zero-dimensional singular spaces. If $p\in\mathbb R[x]$ is zero or has degree at most $d$, has parity $d\bmod2$, and satisfies $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, the exact completion and phase-factorization suppliers give a phase list with $\operatorname{Re}P_\Phi=p$. The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

Let $A:H_R\to H_L$ be the PUE map of [[def-qa-24-pue-svd-data]], with positive singular-value decomposition $A=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|$. Let $p:[-1,1]\to\mathbb C$ be a scalar function.

If $p$ is **odd**, define the odd singular-value transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A):H_R\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{\mathrm{odd}}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|.$$

If $p$ is **even**, define its right-space transform by

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A):H_R\to H_R,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{R}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A},$$

where $\Pi_{\ker A}$ is the orthogonal projection in $H_R$ onto $\ker A$. The left-space version is

$$p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A):H_L\to H_L,\qquad p^{\mathrm{SV}}_{L}(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}p(\sigma_j)|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|+p(0)\Pi_{\ker A^*}.$$

The odd transform annihilates the right kernel because oddness gives $p(0)=0$; the even transforms use the canonical kernel projections. The resulting operators are independent of the chosen SVD by [[lem-qa-24-singular-transform-basis-independence]].

Under the exact inputs and instructions of [[alg-qa-22-lcu-block-encoding]], the all-zero coefficient-index and component-ancilla block of $W=P^{\dagger}\mathrm{SELECT}P$ is

$$\frac{\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\beta_jA_j}{\Lambda}.$$

Moreover, $\|\sum_j\beta_jA_j\|_{\rm op}\le\Lambda$, so the constructed unitary is an $(\Lambda,b+a_*,0)$ block encoding of $\sum_j\beta_jA_j$.

Let $p$ be supplied in the rational/exact-algebraic target representation of [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]], with any supplied real complement represented through its explicitly charged ideal-real interface, with degree bound $d\ge0$, parity $d\bmod2$, $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, and rational tolerance $\delta>0$. On a `SUCCESS` output of [[alg-qa-23-qsp-phase-synthesis]], the exact phase list has an ideal QSP matrix whose upper-left matrix entry $P$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re}P=p$ in exact mode and $|\operatorname{Re}P(x)-p(x)|\le\delta_0/8\le\delta/8$ in numerical mode, for every $x\in[-1,1]$, where $\delta_0=\min(\delta,8)$. If numerical phase gates are used, each compiled phase error is at most $\delta_0/(8(d+1))$ in operator norm, so the implemented upper-left matrix entry has real-part error at most $\delta_0/4\le\delta$. This is a matrix-entry accuracy claim; no measurement or scalar-extraction circuit is included. The algorithm terminates on every promised input when its optional compiler terminates with a certificate or an explicit failure result; failed exact checks return their declared non-success branch.

In `efficient-numerical` mode without a supplied complement or finite-basis compiler, the algorithm requires $\operatorname{poly}(d,1+\log_+(1/\delta))$ charged arithmetic operations, ideal exact algebraic field/equality/order tests, root-descriptor operations, and polynomially many written tower/DAG certificate bits. Here $\log_+(x)=\max(0,\log x)$. Input reading and conversion from an arbitrary original coefficient encoding, expanded minimal-polynomial conversion, operation implementation bit cost, and optional compiler work are separate resource coordinates. This is the explicit exact-algebraic arithmetic model of the algorithm; complete modes retain finite termination without the same height-independent bound.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be normal. If $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $T$,
then there are pairwise orthogonal projections $P_1,\dots,P_r$ such that

$$T=\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j P_j,$$

each $P_j$ projects onto the eigenspace $E_{\lambda_j}(T)$, and every $P_j$ is
a polynomial in $T$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, let $T:V\to V$ be
normal, and write the spectral resolution from
[[thm-spectral-resolution-and-polynomial-spectral-projections]] as

$$T=\sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j P_j,$$

where the $\lambda_j$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $T$ and $P_j$ is the
orthogonal projection onto $E_{\lambda_j}(T)$. For a function
$f:\sigma(T)\to\mathbb C$ on the spectrum of $T$, define

$$f(T):=\sum_{j=1}^r f(\lambda_j)P_j.$$

This is the **spectral functional calculus** of $T$. For the identity function
$\operatorname{id}_{\sigma(T)}$, one has $\operatorname{id}_{\sigma(T)}(T)=T$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, let $T:V\to V$ be
normal, and let $f,g:\sigma(T)\to\mathbb C$.

1. $(f+g)(T)=f(T)+g(T)$.
2. $(fg)(T)=f(T)g(T)$.
3. If $\overline f(\lambda)=\overline{f(\lambda)}$, then $\overline f(T)=f(T)^*$.
4. If $h:f(\sigma(T))\to\mathbb C$, then $(h\circ f)(T)=h(f(T))$.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

derivations.claim: On a Hermitian input $A$, each active parity singular-value transform in [F4] equals ordinary polynomial functional calculus. Indeed, for an eigenvector with eigenvalue $x>0$, choose its left and right singular vectors equal, so its transform coefficient is $p_j(x)$. For $x<0$, choose singular value $|x|$ and left vector the negative of the right vector; the coefficient is $-p_j(|x|)=p_j(x)$ when $p_j$ is odd, while for even parity it is $p_j(|x|)=p_j(x)$. At $x=0$, an odd polynomial vanishes and the even transform assigns $p_j(0)$ on the kernel. The spectral resolution [F7] and basis-independence in [F4] make these equalities independent of choices within degenerate eigenspaces. Also [F1] gives $|f(\lambda)|\le\sum_{j\in J}\gamma_j=B$ on $\sigma(H)$; apply [F2] to the zero polynomial and $f$ to obtain $\|f(H)\|\le B$.

By [F2], $\|p_j(A)-g_j(H)/\gamma_j\|\le\tau_j$, since $A=H/\alpha$ and the scalar bound holds on its spectrum. By [F3]–[F4], replacing the exact signal block $A$ by $\widetilde A$ changes the ideal transform $p_j^{\mathrm{SV}}$ by at most $4d_j\sqrt{\varepsilon_{BE}}$; step 1.1 identifies the transform at $A$ with $p_j(A)$. The implemented component adds at most $\kappa_j$ by its definition, including numerical phase and signal implementation errors. For any unit vector $v$, the vector triangle inequality in [F9] bounds the action of the total difference by the sum of these three operator bounds; taking the supremum over unit $v$ gives $\|Y_j-g_j(H)/\gamma_j\|\le\tau_j+4d_j\sqrt{\varepsilon_{BE}}+\kappa_j$, where $Y_j$ is its actual top-left block.

The exact LCU block for these $Y_j$ is $B^{-1}\sum_{j\in J}c_j\gamma_jY_j$ by [F5]; its actual circuit differs from that block by at most $\kappa_{LCU}$. The decomposition in [F1] gives $f(H)=\sum_{j\in J}c_jg_j(H)$ on the spectrum. For each unit vector $v$, apply the vector triangle inequality [F9] to the weighted sum of component errors from step 2.1 and the LCU implementation error; taking the supremum over $v$ gives the displayed operator-norm bound after multiplying each component bound by $\gamma_j/B$.

The exact signal-call count for component $j\in J$ is $d_j$ by [F8]; a SELECT branch invokes its designated component sequence, so no path uses more than $\max_{j\in J}d_j$ base signal calls in that SELECT. The remaining resource coordinates are the declared preparation, inverse, control, coefficient, phase, reflection, compilation, and output costs in [F1], [F6], and [F8]; neither a degree count nor an exact phase list supplies those costs automatically.
