A finite-dimensional complex matrix input of dimension $d$ is **effectively encoded** if its complete binary description specifies $d$ and conforms to one fixed deterministic entry-approximation machine. Given the description, an entry index, and unary precision request $1^p$, that machine returns rational real and imaginary parts within $2^{-p}$ of the exact entry in time bounded by one fixed polynomial in the total description length plus $p$, uniformly over all valid encodings. Rational entries use their exact binary numerator and denominator; algebraic entries use a finite encoding compatible with this same evaluator and bound. A **uniform matrix family** supplies one polynomial-time description-generation procedure for each member. Hermiticity, dimensions, and norm bounds are promises on the exact matrices, not conclusions inferred from a finite approximation.

This interface includes finite output size and all approximation bit costs. It does not supply a matrix oracle, exact comparisons on arbitrary computable reals, or a free unitary implementation.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces.

If $V=0$, then

$$\lVert T\rVert=0.$$

If $V\ne0$ and $s_1$ is the largest singular value of $T$, then

$$\lVert T\rVert=s_1.$$

In the nonzero case, the maximum in
[[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]] is attained at
a right-singular vector for $s_1$.

Fix an integer $k\ge1$. An encoded instance of input length $N$ gives $n,m\ge1$, with $n$ polynomially bounded in $N$ and $m$ polynomially bounded in $n$. For each term it lists a support set $S_j\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ of size $r_j\le k$ and a Hermitian $2^{r_j}\times2^{r_j}$ matrix $H_j$ in the computational basis of those qubits, ordered by increasing index in $S_j$. It also gives a positive rational polynomial bound $B$ with $\|H_j\|\le B$ for every exact term. Matrix descriptions and their approximation procedures use [[def-qa-33-effective-finite-matrix-encoding]]. Embed each term as $H_j$ on the factors indexed by $S_j$ in increasing order and the identity on every other qubit, and put $H=\sum_{j=1}^m H_j$ on $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. Given rational thresholds $a<b$ with $b-a\ge1/p(n)$ for a polynomial $p$, the promise problem has YES instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ and NO instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$. $$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

By Hermiticity and the norm bound, every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $K/B$ lies in $[-1,1]$; hence the eigenvalues of $E$ lie in $[0,1]$. The finite-dimensional spectral theorem therefore gives positive square roots $S=\sqrt E$ and $R=\sqrt{I-E}$. The block matrix $U_0=U=\begin{pmatrix}S&R\\R&-S\end{pmatrix}$ is unitary: $S,R$ are commuting functions of $E$, $S^2+R^2=I$, and the off-diagonal products cancel. For input flag $0$, its flag-$0$ block is $S$. Follow the dilation by $X$ on the flag, so the accepted branch is labeled outcome $1$; define the marked-accept dilation $U_{acc}$ to be this full unitary. Its accepted effect is $S^*S=E$.

Choose degree $d\ge1/(4\delta^4)$ and use [F1] to form Bernstein polynomials $S_d=B_d(E)$ and $R_d=B_d(I-E)$. Functional calculus on the eigenbasis gives $\|S_d-S\|,\|R_d-R\|\le\delta$. Thus the block matrix $M=\begin{pmatrix}S_d&R_d\\R_d&-S_d\end{pmatrix}$ satisfies $\|M-U\|\le2\delta$ by the triangle inequality for its two block columns. Taking $\delta\le1/16$ and applying [F2] gives an exactly unitary polar correction $Q$ with $\|Q-U\|\le4\delta$.

Polynomial-time Cauchy names for the ideal dilation require a precision-polynomial construction. For $A=E$ or $I-E$, put $X_0=I$, $X_{j+1}=(X_j+AX_j^{-1})/2$. On each eigenvalue $a\in[0,1]$, the scalar iterate satisfies $x_j\ge\max\{\sqrt a,2^{-j}\}$ and $0\le x_{j+1}-\sqrt a=(x_j-\sqrt a)^2/(2x_j)\le(x_j-\sqrt a)/2$. Thus $\|X_j-\sqrt A\|\le2^{-j}$ and $\|X_j^{-1}\|\le2^j$, even when $a=0$. For error $2^{-p}$, take $m=p+3$, approximate $A$ once to operator error $h=2^{-10(m+1)^2}$, and round every iterate to dyadic entries with total operator rounding error at most $h$. If the iterate error is $e_j\le2^{-j-1}$, the inverse identity bounds inverse error by $2^{2j+1}e_j$ and approximate inverse norm by $2^{j+1}$. Therefore $e_{j+1}\le2^{2j+2}e_j+2^{j+1}h+h$. With $e_0=0$, this gives $e_j\le2^{2(m+1)^2}h$ for $j\le m$, smaller than $2^{-m}$ and $2^{-j-1}$, so the bounds hold throughout. In fixed local dimension $D$, rational inversion by adjugate and determinant uses a fixed number of arithmetic operations; the approximate iterates have least singular value at least $2^{-j-1}$ and determinant modulus at least $2^{-D(j+1)}$. Rounding after each iteration keeps all stored entries at $O_D(m^2)$ bits. The $m$ iterations and the input approximation consequently cost polynomial time in the encoding length and $p$. They supply polynomial-time Cauchy names for $S,R$ and $U_{acc}$.

Select $\delta\le\eta/16$, and compile $Q$ to a circuit with a phase representative $V'$ satisfying $\|V'-Q\|\le\eta/4$ using [F3]. The accepted flag outcome effect of the physical circuit is $\widetilde E=V_{00}^*V_{00}$, where $V_{00}$ is the flag-$0$ compression before the final $X$ relabeling; the global scalar relating the physical unitary to $V'$ cancels in this effect. For every fixed deterministic Turing machine $M$ that halts in polynomial
time, there is a polynomial-size logspace-uniform Boolean circuit family
$(C_n)$ such that $C_n(x)=1$ exactly when $M$ accepts
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$.

A **full-list uniform quantum circuit family** is a sequence $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ together with one fixed deterministic one-tape Turing machine $G$ and constants $c\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that, on input the unary word $1^n$, $G$ halts within $c(n+1)^k$ transitions and its final tape is a valid self-delimiting binary description of the entire circuit $C_n$. The machine output convention is that of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]] and [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and running time is as in [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

The following fixed-order code makes the full circuit and its designated input/output wires effective. A unary natural $r\in\mathbb N$ is written $1^r0$, including the one-symbol code $0$ for $r=0$. A self-delimiting binary natural $r$ is written $1^{|\operatorname{bin}(r)|}0\operatorname{bin}(r)$, where $\operatorname{bin}(r)$ is its ordinary binary numeral with no leading zeros and $\operatorname{bin}(0)=0$. The header gives the input-wire count $n$ and total wire count $m$ in unary, followed by the gate count $g$ as a self-delimiting natural; validity requires $m\ge n$.

Each gate record consists of a two-bit label ($00,01,10,11$ for $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ respectively), followed by one self-delimiting wire index for $H,T,T^\dagger$ and two ordered self-delimiting indices for CNOT. Every index is less than $m$; CNOT indices are distinct, with the first the control and the second the target. The list contains exactly $g$ records. After the gate list, an output-count self-delimiting natural is followed by that many ordered, pairwise distinct wire indices, each less than $m$. Parsing rejects every other label, malformed or out-of-range index, repeated output index, truncated field, or trailing bit. This defines a total decoder by returning a fixed malformed-code symbol on any invalid word; effective binary encodings and total decoders are as in [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]].

The gate labels and matrices are the fixed finite library $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ of [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]], with entries in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$; CNOT is control-first. The remaining $m-n$ wires are auxiliary wires; their initial states are determined when a family is used in a computation model. This family convention adopts full-list generation. It makes no equivalence claim with indexed-gate uniformity and, in particular, does not assert that an indexed-gate generator can be expanded to the full list in polynomial time.

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

A Boolean circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with numbered input nodes,
constant nodes, and gates from the fixed basis $\{\mathsf{AND},\mathsf{OR},\mathsf{NOT}\}$;
AND and OR gates have two predecessors, NOT gates have one, and constants
have values zero or one. Its output is one designated node. A family
$(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ has exactly $n$ input nodes labeled $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in
$C_n$ and polynomially many nodes as a function of $n+2$. The family is
**logspace-uniform** when a deterministic read-only-input logspace transducer,
on input $1^n$ and a query with binary node indices of length $O(\log(n+2))$,
halts and answers the size, gate-type (including input labels and constant
values), and predecessor queries for the
topologically numbered encoding of $C_n$, and answers which numbered gate is
the designated output. In particular, it can stream that polynomial-length
encoding without storing it.

Fix a nonnegative integer $q$ and dimension $D=2^q$, independent of input length. Given a $D\times D$ unitary whose entries have polynomial-time Cauchy names from a finite description and a rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure outputs a circuit on its $q$ data wires, with a constant number of clean ancillas returned to zero, for which there is a unit scalar $\lambda$ with $\|V-\lambda U\|\le\eta$. The procedure has polynomial bit cost and polynomial gate count in the description length and $1/\eta$. Scalar phase is immaterial only for this unconditional circuit. The construction uses complex Givens elimination with robust pivoting, a constant-width decomposition into unconditional one-qubit $SU(2)$ rotations and CNOT gates, and the finite-precision compiler of [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]]. Its exact reversible-control subconstruction gives Toffoli from $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ by the parity-phase identity in the proof.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

derivations.claim: For each output position $i\le L(n)$, define a fixed polynomial-time machine $M'(x,i)$ that runs $M(x)$ and returns the $i$th bit of its padded record string. Apply [F1] to $M'$. The uniform generator can specialize the index input $i$ to each constant $1,\ldots,L(n)$, enumerate every Boolean gate record using [F4]'s logarithmic-space size/type/predecessor queries, and concatenate the $L(n)$ circuits. The resulting multi-output Boolean circuit computes the entire gate program; it has polynomial size and is generated in polynomial time from $1^n$.

Allocate one clean value wire per Boolean node and traverse the circuit's topological order. A constant zero leaves its target zero; a constant one applies $X=HT^4H$; a NOT node writes $1\oplus a$ by $X$ followed by CNOT; an AND node writes $ab$ into a zero target with Toffoli; and an OR node writes $a\oplus b\oplus ab=a\lor b$ with two CNOTs and one Toffoli. If both input ports name the same source, one CNOT copies that source for either AND or OR. Copy each designated circuit output into its separate program bit by CNOTs, then reverse all node computations to return their value wires to zero. The exact Toffoli circuit is supplied by [F5]'s construction.

For each record position $t$ and each candidate gate/address tuple, compute into a clean condition bit the conjunction that all type and address fields match that tuple. Bitwise comparison uses $X$ on negative controls and an AND tree of Toffoli gates; reverse it after the controlled operation. Apply the fixed controlled target $I\oplus G$ to this bit and the one or two selected data wires, where $G$ is the candidate gate $H,T,T^\dagger$, or CNOT. The target dimension is at most $2^3$ and its matrix is fixed, so [F5] produces a QC14 template with operator error $\xi$ up to one global phase on the full target. For a valid record exactly one candidate condition is true; the exact product of all candidate templates at position $t$ is therefore the specified gate, while a blank record applies identity.

Put $P_0(n)=L(n)(3W(n)+W(n)(W(n)-1))$ and $P(n)=\max\{1,P_0(n)\}$; there are at most $P_0(n)$ candidate templates, including the case $P_0(n)=0$. Choose $\xi=\delta(n)/(2P(n))$. Each comparison and its inverse are exact, so conjugating a template error preserves its operator norm; the global phases of the templates multiply the entire unconditional interpreter by one scalar. Telescoping the $P_0(n)$ unitary replacements bounds the implemented program's operator error by $P_0(n)\xi\le\delta(n)/2$; when $P_0(n)=0$ there are no replacements and the error is zero. The reversible program generator is exact on every basis input and leaves $x$ unchanged; its program bits can be included among the terminal unmeasured wires. Thus the full circuit implements $P_x$ to error at most $\delta(n)$ for every classical $x$.

If two output unitaries differ by operator norm at most $\delta$, then for every unit input vector their output vectors differ in norm by at most $\delta$; for any accepting projection $P$, the acceptance probabilities differ by at most $2\delta$, since $|\langle Pv,v\rangle-\langle Pw,w\rangle|\le\|v-w\|(\|v\|+\|w\|)\le2\delta.$ This also holds for mixed inputs by finite linearity. The polynomial bounds on $L,W$ and $1/\delta$ make the complete full-list generator and circuit size polynomial in the separate coordinates of [F8]. No nonstandard axiom is used.

citations.quote:
For an input length $n$, let $X_n=\mathcal Q_n$ be the ordered classical-input register, $W_n=\mathcal Q_{w(n)}$ a witness register, and $A_n=\mathcal Q_{a(n)}$ a clean-ancilla register; $w(n),a(n)$ are polynomially bounded and zero qubits means the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C$. A verifier family is one full-list uniform family of finite circuits on $X_n\otimes W_n\otimes A_n$, generated in polynomial time from $1^n$. Its gate order and unitary denotation are those of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]], [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], and [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. The first register holds the classical basis input $|x\rangle$, the witness may be any density operator $\rho$ on $W_n$, and the clean ancillas start in $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$. Thus this definition adds an explicit quantum witness register to the classical-input, zero-ancilla promise-computation convention of [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]]; a witness is not an initialized ancilla.

Let $O_n$ be the ordered tuple of distinct terminally measured wires. A total polynomial-time predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z)$ determines acceptance from the measured output string $z$. Let $J_x:W_n\to X_n\otimes W_n\otimes A_n$ be $J_x\psi=|x\rangle\otimes\psi\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, and let $P_x$ be the orthogonal projection onto all computational-basis output strings accepted by $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,\cdot)$, tensored with the identity on every unmeasured wire. Define the witness acceptance effect and its probability by

$$E_x:=J_x^*U_n^*P_xU_nJ_x,\qquad p_V(x,\rho):=\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho).$$

The projection $P_x$ sums over every unmeasured output wire. The positivity of this compression and its equality with the terminal outcome law are proved separately. The matrix input, gate list, generator, output predicate, and all circuit and classical costs are charged according to [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]; no intermediate measurement or free random source is assumed in this base interface.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$, the partial
trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B:\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)\to
\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_B R)\circ T\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R\circ(T\otimes I_{H_B})\bigr)\quad\text{for every }R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)\text{ and }T\in\operatorname{End}(H_A).$$

Here $I_{H_B}$ is the identity map $y\mapsto y$ on $H_B$; $\operatorname{End}$
is the notation defined in [[def-qc-partial-trace]].

Its coordinate formula is independent of the chosen ordered orthonormal basis
of $H_B$. The assertion includes zero-dimensional factors.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite POVM on $H$. Then

$$p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)\in[0,1]\quad\text{for each }a\in\Omega,\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1.$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first argument ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for its complex-linear endomorphisms ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]) and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite POVM** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ with each $E_a$ nonnegative and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}E_a=I_H$; after any enumeration of $\Omega$, these operators form the finite complete positive family of [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]]. Reordering does not alter the finite sum. The complete-family lemma [[lem-qc-complete-effect-family-members-are-effects]] shows that every $E_a$ also has nonnegative complement $I_H-E_a$, so each is an effect.

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (a nonnegative operator of trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), its **POVM outcome weights** are

$$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

For a complex vector space $H$, write $\operatorname{End}(H)$ for the set of
linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-linear-map]]).

Let $H_A,H_B$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed
ordered orthonormal bases $(e_i)_{i<a}$ and $(f_j)_{j<b}$, respectively. The
ordered product basis of $H_A\otimes H_B$ has the $A$ index first. For
$R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$ define
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\in\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ by

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\bigr)_{i i'}:=\sum_{j<b}R_{(i,j),(i',j)}.$$

Rows are output coordinates and columns are input coordinates, as in
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]. If $b=0$, the sum is
empty and equals $0$. The notation $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ means that the second
factor is contracted; the first factor and its order are retained.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

derivations.claim: Put $Q=U_nJ_x$. The input basis vector and clean zero state are unit vectors, so $J_x$ is an isometry; $U_n$ is unitary, hence $Q^*Q=I$. Then $E_x=Q^*P_xQ$ and $I-E_x=Q^*(I-P_x)Q$. For every $v\in W_n$, $\langle E_xv,v\rangle=\langle P_xQv,Qv\rangle=\|P_xQv\|^2\ge0$, and $\langle(I-E_x)v,v\rangle=\|(I-P_x)Qv\|^2\ge0$. Therefore $0\le E_x\le I$.
For a density operator $\rho$, [F7] gives the state hypotheses for the two-outcome POVM $(E_x,I-E_x)$ defined in [F5]. Applying [F4] gives $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\in[0,1]$.

The post-circuit state is $\sigma=U_n(J_x\rho J_x^*)U_n^*$. By [F6] and the partial-trace identity [F2], the probability of the accepting projection on the named output register equals $\operatorname{Tr}(P_x\sigma)$, where $P_x$ is the accepting projection tensored with identity on all unmeasured wires; [F5] gives this projective measurement outcome law. Cyclicity [F3] and finite matrix multiplication give $\operatorname{Tr}(P_xU_nJ_x\rho J_x^*U_n^*)=\operatorname{Tr}(J_x^*U_n^*P_xU_nJ_x\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)$. The projection $P_x$ sums the probabilities over all unmeasured basis strings, so this is the stated terminal acceptance probability.

If the accepting set is empty, P_x=0 and step 1.1 gives E_x=0 and acceptance probability zero.
If every output is accepted, P_x=I and step 1.1 gives E_x=I and probability one.
Step 2.1 sums over all unmeasured output strings by partial trace, including multiple strings with the same acceptance predicate value.
Steps 1.1–1.2 prove the effect bounds 0≤E_x≤I and probabilities in [0,1], including both endpoints.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

For every verifier interface of [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]], the compression $E_x=J_x^*U_n^*P_xU_nJ_x$ is a positive contraction on $W_n$. For every witness density operator $\rho$, its terminal acceptance probability, summed over every unmeasured wire, equals $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\in[0,1]$.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

For every natural $n$, the map
$\operatorname{tr}:M_n(F)\to F$ is linear:

$$\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\lambda A)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(A).$$

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem, $0\le s(n)<c(n)\le1$ efficiently encoded rational thresholds, and $w(n),a(n)$ polynomially bounded witness and clean-ancilla lengths. Require $c(n)-s(n)\ge1/p(n)$ for some polynomially bounded positive $p$. Then $\Pi\in\mathrm{QMA}(c,s)$ if there is a full-list uniform verifier interface as in [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]] such that every $x\in Y$ has a witness density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\ge c(|x|)$, and every $x\in N$ and every witness density operator satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\le s(|x|)$. Behavior outside $Y\cup N$ is unrestricted. The standard bounded-error class uses $c=2/3$ and $s=1/3$. The effect and probability are well-defined by [[lem-qa-33-witness-acceptance-effect]].

derivations.claim: By [F1]–[F2], choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ for $\rho$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_j\ge0$. Basis independence [F6] and its diagonal-sum definition give $\sum_j\lambda_j=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=1$. Thus $\rho=\sum_j\lambda_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$, with zero eigenvalue terms allowed.

Linearity [F5] gives $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)=\sum_j\lambda_j\operatorname{Tr}(E_x|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|)$. By [F3], these terms are precisely the verifier's pure-state acceptance probabilities. By [F4], in an orthonormal basis beginning with $u_j$, the rank-one factor has only its first diagonal entry nonzero after multiplication by $E_x$; [F6] therefore gives $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|)=\langle E_xu_j,u_j\rangle$. This is a convex average; if every positive-weight term were below $c$, its finite weighted average would be below $c$. Hence some $j$ with $\lambda_j>0$ has acceptance at least $c$, so [F7] gives a pure witness meeting the QMA completeness threshold.

Let a verifier circuit have $T\ge1$ gates $U_1,\ldots,U_T$, each acting on at most two computation qubits, with its accept/reject predicate reversibly computed into one output qubit (accept is $|1\rangle$). Let $N=T+1$ and encode time $t$ by the unary clock word $|c_t\rangle=|1^t0^{T-t}\rangle$ on $T$ clock qubits. For an initial computation vector $\phi$ define its normalized history
$$|\eta_\phi\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{t=0}^T(U_t\cdots U_1\phi)\otimes|c_t\rangle,$$
where the $t=0$ product is $I$. ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and

derivations.claim: Set $V_0=I$ and $V_t=U_t\cdots U_1$. The block diagonal map $W=\sum_{t=0}^T V_t\otimes|c_t\rangle\langle c_t|$ is unitary because every $V_t$ is unitary and clock sectors are orthogonal. Conjugating an edge term by $W$ replaces $U_t$ in its off-diagonal block by $V_t^*U_tV_{t-1}=I$; its diagonal clock blocks remain unchanged. The ket-bra multiplications use the convention [F3]. Summing gives $W^*H_{prop}W=L_T\otimes I$. Thus the kernel consists of vectors constant across clock time, and undoing $W$ gives exactly the normalized histories.

Put $M=T+1$. For $j=0,\ldots,M-1$, the vector with coordinates $v_j(r)=\cos(\pi j(r+1/2)/M)$, $r=0,\ldots,M-1$, is nonzero. The cosine addition identity verifies the interior eigenvalue equation for $L_T$ with eigenvalue $1-\cos(\pi j/M)$; the same identity with the endpoint degree-one rows verifies both endpoint equations. These $M$ eigenvalues are distinct, so symmetry of $L_T$ makes the corresponding vectors orthogonal; by [F2] they form a full eigenbasis. The $j=0$ vector is constant and the smallest positive eigenvalue is the $j=1$ value.
For $x\in[0,\pi/2]$, concavity of sine gives $\sin x\ge2x/\pi$. Hence $1-\cos(\pi/M)=2\sin^2(\pi/(2M))\ge2/M^2.$ This proves the stated gap and includes $T=1$ ($M=2$).

Here $A$ indexes initially clean verifier ancillas, and the output predicate is computed into the displayed accept qubit. derivations.claim: The sum is diagonal in the computational clock basis. It has eigenvalue equal to the number of pairs $i<j$ with bit $i=0$ and bit $j=1$. This number is zero exactly when no zero precedes a one, which is equivalent to a word $1^t0^{T-t}$; every other word has at least one such pair and hence eigenvalue at least one. Thus its zero space and gap are as stated.

Apply [F1] with $S=S_{legal}$, $H_1=H_0$ and $H_2=J_{clock}H_{clock}^{KKR}$. The spectral penalty on $S^\perp$ is at least $J_{clock}$, while it vanishes on $S$. The chosen strict bound gives $J_{clock}-2K>4K^2/g$, and so the correction $K^2/(J_{clock}-2K)<g/4$. If $K$ and $1/g$ are polynomially bounded, this integer weight and the $O(T^2)$ term list have polynomial size.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be mutually independent Bernoulli$(p_i)$ variables on a finite probability space. Set $S=\sum_iX_i$ and $\mu=\sum_i p_i$. For $\delta\ge0$,
$$\mathbb P(S\ge(1+\delta)\mu)\le\exp\{-\mu((1+\delta)\log(1+\delta)-\delta)\}.$$
For $0\le\delta<1$,
$$\mathbb P(S\le(1-\delta)\mu)\le\exp\{-\mu(\delta+(1-\delta)\log(1-\delta))\}.$$
For $0\le\delta\le1$ the upper and lower tails are respectively at most $\exp(-\mu\delta^2/3)$ and $\exp(-\mu\delta^2/2)$, and
$$\mathbb P(|S-\mu|\ge\delta\mu)\le2\exp(-\mu\delta^2/3).$$
At $\delta=1$ the lower optimized bound is $\exp(-\mu)$, proved directly rather than by taking $\log0$. Empty sums and $\mu=0$ are included. Also, for $N>0$ and $t\ge0$,
$$\mathbb P(|S-\mu|\ge t)\le2\exp(-2t^2/N).$$

Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem, $0\le s(n)<c(n)\le1$ efficiently encoded rational thresholds, and $w(n),a(n)$ polynomially bounded witness and clean-ancilla lengths. Require $c(n)-s(n)\ge1/p(n)$ for some polynomially bounded positive $p$. Then $\Pi\in\mathrm{QMA}(c,s)$ if there is a full-list uniform verifier interface as in [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]] such that every $x\in Y$ has a witness density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\ge c(|x|)$, and every $x\in N$ and every witness density operator satisfy $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\le s(|x|)$. Behavior outside $Y\cup N$ is unrestricted. The standard bounded-error class uses $c=2/3$ and $s=1/3$. The effect and probability are well-defined by [[lem-qa-33-witness-acceptance-effect]].

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

**Inputs:** A length-$n$ verifier from [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]], its classical basis input $|x\rangle$ with $|x|=n$, an $r$-block witness register, rational thresholds $0\le s<c\le1$, and an integer $r\ge1$. Each verifier has input register $X_n$, witness register $W_n$, clean ancillas $A_n$, terminally measured tuple $O_n$, and total predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z)$. The admissible parameters are those of the verifier's promise-class contract, with $r$ polynomially bounded when polynomial resources are claimed.

**Procedure:** Partition the witness into $r$ blocks $W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(r)}$. Use the given input register as $X^{(1)}$, allocate $r-1$ fresh zero-initialized $n$-bit registers $X^{(2)},\ldots,X^{(r)}$, and for every bit position $i$ and $j=2,\ldots,r$, apply a CNOT from $X^{(1)}_i$ to $X^{(j)}_i$. Since $x$ is a computational-basis string, this copies $|x\rangle$ exactly and leaves every input register in $|x\rangle$. Give each verifier copy its own fresh clean ancillas and distinct output wires, then run its finite circuit on $(X^{(j)},W^{(j)},A^{(j)})$. At termination measure each copy's tuple $O^{(j)}$ and evaluate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z_j)$ on that outcome. Let $S$ be the number of copies whose predicate accepts. Output $1$ exactly when

$$S\ge\left\lceil\frac{r(c+s)}2\right\rceil.$$

The rational midpoint and integer threshold are computed exactly from the binary encodings of $c,s,r$. The input-copy registers, verifier ancillas and output registers are separate across copies; no copy uses a shared quantum input register after the CNOT fanout. The acceptance predicate is evaluated separately on each copy's terminal outcome. Completeness and soundness for arbitrary joint witnesses, including witnesses entangled across the $r$ blocks, are established in the separate entangled-witness amplification theorem.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first argument ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for its complex-linear endomorphisms ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]) and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite POVM** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ with each $E_a$ nonnegative and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}E_a=I_H$; after any enumeration of $\Omega$, these operators form the finite complete positive family of [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]]. Reordering does not alter the finite sum. The complete-family lemma [[lem-qc-complete-effect-family-members-are-effects]] shows that every $E_a$ also has nonnegative complement $I_H-E_a$, so each is an effect.

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (a nonnegative operator of trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), its **POVM outcome weights** are

$$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite POVM on $H$. Then

$$p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)\in[0,1]\quad\text{for each }a\in\Omega,\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1.$$

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

derivations.claim: Put $\tau=(c+s)/2=s+\gamma/2$. By [F6], the midpoint test accepts at $\lceil r\tau\rceil$. Its CNOT fanout prepares a separate register $|x\rangle$ for every verifier copy from the classical basis input, and the outputs are evaluated using the same predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,\cdot)$, so each block realizes the acceptance effect $E_x$ of [F1]. On a YES input, choose a witness $\rho$ with acceptance $p\ge c$ and give the product witness $\rho^{\otimes r}$. Each copy acts on a distinct input, witness and ancilla block, so its accept bit is an independent Bernoulli$(p)$ variable by the product rule in [F2] and the finite POVM law. If the midpoint test rejects, then $S<\lceil r\tau\rceil$, hence $S<r\tau$ and $S-rp\le-r\gamma/2$. The lower-tail inequality in [F3] bounds this event by $\exp(-r\gamma^2/2)$.

Fix a NO input and any joint witness density $\sigma$ on the $r$ blocks. By the exact basis-state fanout in [F6], every verifier copy starts with its own fixed $|x\rangle$ input and its own clean ancillas; hence its acceptance effect on its witness block is the same $E_x$ from [F1]. On one block, [F1] and [F4] give $\langle E_xv,v\rangle\le s$ for every unit witness vector $v$; as $E_x$ is an effect, this means $0\le E_x\le sI$. Let $A_j=I\otimes\cdots\otimes E_x\otimes\cdots\otimes I$ on the full $r$-block space. An eigenbasis of $E_x$ from [F9], tensored with the other block bases, shows $0\le A_j\le sI$. Distinct $A_j$ act on distinct tensor factors, so they commute by [F2].

Define the full-space effects $B_{j,1}=A_j$ and $B_{j,0}=I-A_j$. The joint outcome $b\in\{0,1\}^r$ has effect $\prod_jB_{j,b_j}$ on this same space: equivalently it is $\bigotimes_j C_{b_j}$ for the one-block effects $C_1=E_x$, $C_0=I-E_x$. This product/tensor identity follows on elementary tensors by [F2]. The finite POVM trace rule and normalization [F7]–[F8] therefore give, for $t>0$, $\mathbb E_\sigma e^{tS}=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma\sum_b e^{t|b|}\prod_j B_{j,b_j}\right)=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma\prod_{j=1}^r\bigl(I+(e^t-1)A_j\bigr)\right)$. Each factor is positive and at most $(1-s+se^t)I$ by step 1.2. In the product of the single-block eigenbases from [F9], their product is diagonal with entries bounded by $(1-s+se^t)^r$, so the product is at most that scalar times identity. Taking its trace against the density $\sigma$ gives $\mathbb E_\sigma e^{tS}\le(1-s+se^t)^r$, without any tensor product of full-space effects.

Apply the single-Bernoulli moment bound in [F3] with parameter $s$: $e^{-ts}(1-s+se^t)\le e^{t^2/8}$. Thus $\mathbb E_\sigma e^{t(S-rs)}\le e^{rt^2/8}$. Since $S\ge\lceil r\tau\rceil$ implies $S-rs\ge r\gamma/2$, the finite-sum Markov bound gives $\Pr_\sigma(S\ge\lceil r\tau\rceil)\le\exp(-tr\gamma/2+rt^2/8).$ Taking $t=2\gamma$ makes this at most $e^{-r\gamma^2/2}$. No independence assumption is used for $\sigma$.

The choice $r\ge2\gamma^{-2}\ln(1/\delta)$ gives $e^{-r\gamma^2/2}\le\delta$ on both promise sides by [F5]. The threshold is the exact integer rule in [F6], and repeating a polynomial-size full-list verifier $r$ times gives polynomial gate count, witness width, and generator time whenever $r$ is polynomially bounded. For the least admissible integer, $r\le2\gamma^{-2}\ln(1/\delta)+1$, which is polynomial under the resource hypotheses of the Statement.

For $T$ clock qubits let $S_{legal}=\operatorname{span}\{|1^t0^{T-t}\rangle:0\le t\le T\}$ and
$$H_{clock}^{KKR}=\sum_{1\le i<j\le T}I\otimes|01\rangle\langle01|_{C_iC_j}.$$

$$J_{clock}>2K+4K^2/g$$

On the legal clock space spanned by $|c_0\rangle,\ldots,|c_T\rangle$, the propagation Hamiltonian of [[def-qa-33-feynman-kitaev-history-hamiltonian]] is unitarily conjugate to
$$L_T=\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T(|t\rangle-|t-1\rangle)(\langle t|-\langle t-1|)$$
tensor the identity on computation space. Its kernel is the uniform clock vector, equivalently the valid computation histories, and its first positive eigenvalue is
$$1-\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{T+1}\right)\ge\frac{2}{(T+1)^2}.$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $S\subseteq H$ be a nonzero subspace. Let $H_1,H_2$ be Hermitian endomorphisms, with $H_2|_S=0$ and $\langle H_2v,v\rangle\ge J\|v\|^2$ for every $v\in S^\perp$, where $J>2\|H_1\|$. Write $\lambda_S=\lambda_{\min}(H_1|_S)$. Then

$$\lambda_S-\frac{\|H_1\|^2}{J-2\|H_1\|}\le\lambda_{\min}(H_1+H_2)\le\lambda_S.$$

Here $H_1|_S$ is the compression $P_SH_1P_S$ on $S$, where $P_S$ is orthogonal projection. Assume $S\ne\{0\}$ so that $\lambda_S$ is defined. If $S^\perp=\{0\}$, the lower spectral hypothesis is vacuous and the conclusion reduces to equality.

It also gives a positive rational polynomial bound $B$ with $\|H_j\|\le B$ for every exact term. Matrix descriptions and their approximation procedures use [[def-qa-33-effective-finite-matrix-encoding]]. Embed each term as $H_j$ on the factors indexed by $S_j$ in increasing order and the identity on every other qubit, and put $H=\sum_{j=1}^m H_j$ on $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. Given rational thresholds $a<b$ with $b-a\ge1/p(n)$ for a polynomial $p$, the promise problem has YES instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ and NO instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$. No local matrix is treated as a free gate or oracle.

For every natural $n$, the map
$\operatorname{tr}:M_n(F)\to F$ is linear:

$$\operatorname{tr}(A+B)=\operatorname{tr}(A)+\operatorname{tr}(B),\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\lambda A)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(A).$$

Fix a nonnegative integer $q$ and dimension $D=2^q$, independent of input length. Given a $D\times D$ unitary whose entries have polynomial-time Cauchy names from a finite description and a rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure outputs a circuit on its $q$ data wires, with a constant number of clean ancillas returned to zero, for which there is a unit scalar $\lambda$ with $\|V-\lambda U\|\le\eta$. The procedure has polynomial bit cost and polynomial gate count in the description length and $1/\eta$. Scalar phase is immaterial only for this unconditional circuit. The construction uses complex Givens elimination with robust pivoting, a constant-width decomposition into unconditional one-qubit $SU(2)$ rotations and CNOT gates, and the finite-precision compiler of [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]]. Its exact reversible-control subconstruction gives Toffoli from $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ by the parity-phase identity in the proof.

Use the fixed QC14 alphabet $\{H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}\}$. Let $M$ be one fixed deterministic polynomial-time classical machine that, on each binary input $x$ of length $n$, outputs a valid circuit description $P_x$ of at most $L(n)$ gate records on at most $W(n)$ data wires, where $L,W$ are fixed polynomials. Encode the output as exactly $L(n)$ fixed-width records: each record is either blank, a one-qubit label $H,T,T^\dagger$ with one wire address, or a CNOT label with an ordered pair of distinct wire addresses; unused address fields are zero. Let $\delta(n)$ be any inverse-polynomial rational tolerance produced by a fixed polynomial-time machine from $1^n$, with polynomial bit length. There is a full-list uniform QC14 family generated from $1^n$ which on classical basis input $x$ and data state $|\psi\rangle$ outputs a state within operator error $\delta(n)$, up to a global scalar, of
$$|x\rangle\otimes P_x|\psi\rangle\otimes|M(x)\rangle\otimes|0^w\rangle$$
for a polynomially bounded work width $w(n)$. Its size and generator time are polynomial in $n$ and $1/\delta(n)$. The program and arithmetic registers are terminal unmeasured wires; their presence changes the data-register outcome law from executing $P_x$ by at most $2\delta(n)$. This lemma converts a polynomial-time input-dependent compiler into the input-length-uniform verifier model.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space; the pairing is linear in its first argument ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Write $\mathcal L(H)$ for its complex-linear endomorphisms ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]) and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set. A **finite POVM** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $E=(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ with each $E_a$ nonnegative and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}E_a=I_H$; after any enumeration of $\Omega$, these operators form the finite complete positive family of [[def-qc-finite-positive-effect-family]]. Reordering does not alter the finite sum. The complete-family lemma [[lem-qc-complete-effect-family-members-are-effects]] shows that every $E_a$ also has nonnegative complement $I_H-E_a$, so each is an effect.

For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (a nonnegative operator of trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), its **POVM outcome weights** are

$$p_\rho(a):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a),\qquad a\in\Omega.$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

The positivity and normalization of these weights are proved in [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]. A POVM specifies this outcome law; it does not by itself prescribe a conditional output state.

A finite-dimensional complex matrix input of dimension $d$ is **effectively encoded** if its complete binary description specifies $d$ and conforms to one fixed deterministic entry-approximation machine. Given the description, an entry index, and unary precision request $1^p$, that machine returns rational real and imaginary parts within $2^{-p}$ of the exact entry in time bounded by one fixed polynomial in the total description length plus $p$, uniformly over all valid encodings. Rational entries use their exact binary numerator and denominator; algebraic entries use a finite encoding compatible with this same evaluator and bound. A **uniform matrix family** supplies one polynomial-time description-generation procedure for each member. Hermiticity, dimensions, and norm bounds are promises on the exact matrices, not conclusions inferred from a finite approximation.

This interface includes finite output size and all approximation bit costs. It does not supply a matrix oracle, exact comparisons on arbitrary computable reals, or a free unitary implementation.

derivations.claim: Let $N=|x|$. Because $n$ is polynomially bounded in $N$, choose fixed polynomial envelopes $P(N)\ge\max\{1,p(n)\}$ and $Q(N)\ge1$ bounding both $m$ and $B$ on every valid length-$N$ input; these envelopes are computable in polynomial time from $1^N$. Put $g_*(N)=1/(4Q(N)^2P(N))$. Since $d<2m$ for $m>1$ and $d=1$ for $m=1$, the exact gap $g=(b-a)/(2dB)$ satisfies $g\ge g_*(N)$. Prepare the address uniformly with Hadamards using [F8]. The controlled target has fixed dimension at most $2^{k+2}$; [F2] supplies its Cauchy matrix description, and [F6] compiles each full selector-controlled block to operator error at most $g_*(N)/(32m)$, up to a whole-circuit scalar. Telescoping the $m$ block replacements gives total operator error at most $g_*(N)/32$, hence acceptance error at most $g_*(N)/16$ for the complete address test; this also bounds leakage from approximate selector controls. The compiler's full output list has polynomial length because $m,B$ are polynomially bounded and each matrix encoding has the uniform polynomial-time approximation routine of [F10]. The compiler is uniformized by [F7] with operator error $\delta(N)=g_*(N)/32$ after appending the threshold normalization below; the single full-list family generated from $1^N$ computes the complete list from $x$ and interprets it. A fixed polynomial time limit makes the classical compiler total, emitting a fixed rejecting circuit on malformed input or overrun; promised encodings satisfy the established bounds.

Thus the exact acceptance gap is $(b-a)/(2dB)$. If $m>1$, $d<2m$; if $m=1$, $d=1$, so in either case it is at least $(b-a)/(4mB)$.

By [F2] and [F7], the implemented energy test has acceptance error at most $g_*(N)/16+2(g_*(N)/32)=g_*(N)/8$. Its ideal instance-dependent thresholds are $c_x=m/(2d)-a/(2dB)$ and $s_x=m/(2d)-b/(2dB)$, with $c_x-s_x=g$. Compute $t_x=(c_x+s_x)/2$ exactly. For $0\le t_x\le1$, use a fair branch coin: on one branch perform the energy test, and on the other accept with probability $1-t_x$. The ideal combined acceptance is $q=(p+1-t_x)/2$, at least $1/2+g/4$ on YES and at most $1/2-g/4$ on NO. The second coin is prepared by synthesizing the one-qubit real rotation with first column $(\sqrt{t_x},\sqrt{1-t_x})^T$ to probability error at most $g_*(N)/16$ using [F6]; square-root Cauchy evaluation, including zero endpoints, is supplied by the rounded Newton construction in [F2]. All branch and outcome bits are measured only at termination, with a polynomial-time final predicate. Apply the interpreter once to this complete input-generated circuit. Its energy-block error contributes at most $g_*/32$ after the half mixture, the second coin contributes at most $g_*/32$, and interpreter error contributes at most $g_*/16$, for total error at most $g_*/8$. Thus the length-only rational thresholds $c(N)=1/2+g_*(N)/8$ and $s(N)=1/2-g_*(N)/8$ apply to every promised length-$N$ input. Both lie in $[0,1]$ since $g_*\le1/4$, and their gap is inverse polynomial. Amplify this uniform verifier using [F4]; witness width, initialized workspace, size and generator time remain polynomial.

$$|\eta_\phi\rangle=N^{-1/2}\sum_{t=0}^T(U_t\cdots U_1\phi)\otimes|c_t\rangle,$$

where each clock ket is only on the displayed local window. For each local pre/post block, its quadratic form is one half the squared norm of the difference between the post component and $U_t$ applied to the pre component, so it is positive semidefinite. On legal clock words these patterns identify exactly the adjacent times $t-1,t$. Put $H_{prop}=\sum_tH_{prop,t}$. Define

Write a normalized initial computation vector as $\phi=\phi_c+\phi_d$, where $\phi_c$ has clean verifier ancillas and $\phi_d$ is orthogonal to that subspace; set $\alpha=\|\phi_c\|$ and $\beta=\|\phi_d\|$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=1$ and $p_{bad}=\beta^2$. Let $K$ be the verifier's accept Kraus map, which is a contraction. By [F3], $\|K\phi_c\|\le\sqrt{s}\alpha$; hence the triangle inequality gives $p_{acc}=\|K\phi\|^2\le(\sqrt{s}\alpha+\beta)^2$. Therefore $p_{bad}+p_{rej}=\beta^2+1-p_{acc}\ge1-s\alpha^2-2\sqrt{s}\alpha\beta.$ The symmetric matrix $\begin{pmatrix}s&\sqrt{s}\\\sqrt{s}&0\end{pmatrix}$ has largest eigenvalue $s/2+\sqrt{s+s^2/4}$; its Rayleigh quotient at $(\alpha,\beta)$ bounds the subtracted term. This eigenvalue is increasing for $s\ge0$, and at $s=1/8$ it is $(1+\sqrt{33})/16<1/2$ because $\sqrt{33}<7$. Thus $p_{bad}+p_{rej}\ge1/2$.

By [F2], every unit $v\in T_0$ has $\|P_Sv\|^2=1-(p_{bad}+p_{rej})/N\le1-1/(2N)$. Put $c=\|P_SP_{T_0}\|$; then $c^2\le1-1/(2N)$ and $1-c\ge1-\sqrt{1-1/(2N)}\ge1/(4N).$ For any two orthogonal projections $P,Q$, the map $v\mapsto(Pv,Qv)$ has squared norm operator $P+Q$. On $\operatorname{ran}(P)\oplus\operatorname{ran}(Q)$ its block matrix has diagonal $I$ and off-diagonal norm $\|PQ\|$, so $P+Q\le(1+\|PQ\|)I$. Taking $P=P_S,Q=P_{T_0}$ gives $P_{S^\perp}+P_{T_0^\perp}=2I-P_S-P_{T_0}\ge(1-c)I.$ By [F5], the input penalty has positive integer eigenvalues on the dirty-ancilla sector at time zero, while the output penalty has eigenvalue $N\ge1$ on the reject sector at time $T$; these clock sectors are orthogonal. $$\|P_Sv\|^2\le1-\frac1{2N}.$$
Consequently the least eigenvalue of $H_{in}+H_{out}+H_{prop}$ on legal clocks is at least $1/(2N^3)$. The proof allows arbitrary initial ancilla states in $T_0$; the QMA soundness premise is applied only to the clean-ancilla component.

derivations.claim: A binary word has no adjacent occurrence of $01$ exactly when its bits are nonincreasing from left to right: if a zero occurred before a later one, the first subsequent transition from zero to one would be adjacent; conversely a word $1^t0^{T-t}$ has no such transition. Thus the common zero space of all adjacent projectors is spanned by the legal unary words. On a basis word, $H_{clock}$ is diagonal with eigenvalue the number of forbidden adjacent pairs, so every illegal word has eigenvalue at least one.

The stated propagation windows contain three clock bits and at most two work bits; each input/output term couples one clock and one work bit, and each clock penalty couples two clock bits, proving the support bounds from [F1]. Let $S$ be the legal-clock subspace. Then $H_{clock}$ vanishes on $S$ and is at least $I$ on $S^\perp$. Applying [F2] with $H_1=H_0$, $H_2=J_{clock}H_{clock}$ gives additive error at most $K^2/(J_{clock}-2K)<g/4$. Since $K$ is polynomial in the circuit length and previously chosen weights and $g$ is inverse polynomial by [F3], this integer weight is polynomially bounded and preserves a positive gap.

For each fixed $k$, the encoded $k$-Local Hamiltonian promise problem of [[def-qa-33-k-local-hamiltonian-promise]] is in QMA. A verifier receives an $n$-qubit witness $\rho$, uses the $\ell=\lceil\log_2m\rceil$ address qubits to choose uniformly one of $d=2^\ell$ addresses, rejects addresses $j\ge m$, and for $j<m$ measures the locally synthesized effect $E_j=(I-H_j/B)/2$. Its ideal local-energy test has acceptance probability
$$p(\rho)=\frac{m}{2d}-\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(H\rho)}{2dB}.$$
The promised acceptance gap is $(b-a)/(2dB)\ge(b-a)/(4mB)$ (with $d=1$ when $m=1$). Synthesize each conditional test to effect error at most one eighth of this gap; then the implemented verifier retains an inverse-polynomial gap and is uniformly generated from the term encodings. An efficiently synthesized coin normalizes the instance-dependent acceptance midpoint to length-only QMA thresholds. The QMA amplifier of [[thm-qa-33-qma-amplification-entangled-witness-soundness]] then gives standard bounded error.

A promise problem is **QMA-hard** if every problem in QMA reduces to it by a deterministic polynomial-time many-one promise-preserving reduction. It is **QMA-complete** if it is QMA-hard and itself belongs to QMA. “Promise-preserving reduction” has the meaning of [[def-promise-preserving-reduction]]; no behavior is required off the source promise.

For $T$ clock qubits let $S_{legal}=\operatorname{span}\{|1^t0^{T-t}\rangle:0\le t\le T\}$ and
$$H_{clock}^{KKR}=\sum_{1\le i<j\le T}I\otimes|01\rangle\langle01|_{C_iC_j}.$$
Its kernel is $S_{legal}$ and every illegal computational-basis clock word has eigenvalue at least one. Let $H_0$ be the sum of the remaining weighted KKR terms, with $K\ge\|H_0\|$, and let $g>0$ be the soundness gap allocated before this restriction. Any integer
$$J_{clock}>2K+4K^2/g$$
makes the projection-lemma error strictly less than $g/4$. The clock penalty is 2-local even though it has $O(T^2)$ summands.

Fix $L\ge2$ and let $T_2$ be the number of controlled-$Z$ gates. Pad the verifier to $T=(T_2+1)L-1$ steps, with controlled-$Z$ gates exactly at times $t=lL$ for $1\le l\le T_2$ and exactly $L$ clock configurations in each block $[lL,(l+1)L-1]$. Every other $U_t$ is one-qubit. For each one-qubit gate time $t$, define the KKR local propagation term by
$$H_{prop,t}=\tfrac12(I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_tC_{t+1}}+I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_{t-1}C_t}-U_t\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_t}-U_t^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_t})$$
for $1<t<T$. When $T\ge2$, use the endpoint terms
$$H_{prop,1}=\tfrac12(I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_1C_2}+I\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_{C_1}-U_1\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_1}-U_1^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_1}),$$
$$H_{prop,T}=\tfrac12(I\otimes|1\rangle\langle1|_{C_T}+I\otimes|10\rangle\langle10|_{C_{T-1}C_T}-U_T\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_T}-U_T^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_T}).$$
For $T=1$ (necessarily $T_2=0,L=2$), use only $H_{prop,1}=\tfrac12(I\otimes I_{C_1}-U_1\otimes|1\rangle\langle0|_{C_1}-U_1^*\otimes|0\rangle\langle1|_{C_1})$. Each summand is at most 2-local. Put $H_{prop1}=\sum_{t:\,U_t\text{ is one-qubit}}H_{prop,t}$. On the legal clock space it is a direct sum of half-weight path Laplacians, and its kernel $S_{prop1}$ is spanned by block histories
$$|\eta_{l,i}\rangle=L^{-1/2}\sum_{t=lL}^{(l+1)L-1}U_t\cdots U_1|i\rangle\otimes|c_t\rangle,$$
where $i$ ranges over a computational basis of the work register and $l$ over the blocks. The nonzero gap is at least $g_1=1-\cos(\pi/L)\ge2/L^2$. If the remaining weighted terms have norm at most $K_1$, choose $J_1g_1>2K_1+K_1^2/\epsilon_1$; the projection lemma then incurs additive error below $\epsilon_1$ when restricting to $S_{prop1}$.

Assume the padded verifier has $T_2\ge1$ designated controlled-$Z$ gates and fixes an integer $L\ge5$, with $T=(T_2+1)L-1$ and those gates at times $t=lL$; if the source circuit has none, the hard-instance compiler can add a cancelling pair, after which this restriction applies. On $S_{prop1}$, let each designated controlled-$Z$ gate at time $t=lL$ be preceded at times $t-2,t-1$ by $Z$ on its first and second work wires, respectively, and followed at times $t+1,t+2$ by $Z$ on those wires. Since $L\ge5$, all clock indices $t-3,\ldots,t+3$ lie in $1,\ldots,T$. Each wire receives two $Z$ gates; they commute with controlled-$Z$ and square to identity, so the insertions preserve the verifier unitary. Write $P_a=|a\rangle\langle a|$, $P_{10}=|10\rangle\langle10|$, and $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$. Define
$$H_{qubit,t}=\tfrac12(-2P_0^{f_t}-2P_0^{s_t}+P_1^{f_t}+P_1^{s_t})\otimes X_{C_t},$$
$$\begin{aligned}8H_{time,t}=I\otimes[&P_{10}^{t,t+1}+6P_{10}^{t+1,t+2}+P_{10}^{t+2,t+3}+2|11\rangle\langle00|_{t+1,t+2}+2|00\rangle\langle11|_{t+1,t+2}+X_{t+1}+X_{t+2}\\&+P_{10}^{t-3,t-2}+6P_{10}^{t-2,t-1}+P_{10}^{t-1,t}+2|11\rangle\langle00|_{t-2,t-1}+2|00\rangle\langle11|_{t-2,t-1}+X_{t-2}+X_{t-1}].\end{aligned}$$
Put $H_{prop2}=\sum_{l=1}^{T_2}(H_{qubit,lL}+H_{time,lL})$. Each displayed summand is at most 2-local. On the four physical work sectors $00,01,10,11$, the legal-clock matrix on the adjacent coordinates $|c_{t-1}\rangle,|c_t\rangle$ is respectively $4D_-,D_-,D_-,2D_+$, where
$$D_-=\tfrac12(|c_{t-1}\rangle-|c_t\rangle)(\langle c_{t-1}|-\langle c_t|),\quad D_+=\tfrac12(|c_{t-1}\rangle+|c_t\rangle)(\langle c_{t-1}|+\langle c_t|).$$
In block-history coordinates the $CZ$ phase conjugates the $11$-sector $D_+$ to $D_-$. After the common $1/L$ normalization, every sector therefore dominates one copy of $D_-/L$. Summing these lower bounds over blocks and basis labels gives
$$H'=\frac1{2L}\sum_{l,i}(|\eta_{l-1,i}\rangle-|\eta_{l,i}\rangle)(\langle\eta_{l-1,i}|-\langle\eta_{l,i}|).$$
Its kernel is the full correct-propagation space $S_{prop}$ and its gap is at least $g_2=2/[L(T_2+1)^2]$. If the remaining terms have norm at most $K_2$, choosing $J_2g_2>2K_2+K_2^2/\epsilon_2$ makes the restriction error less than $\epsilon_2$.

Fix an input-specific verifier circuit with only its witness unrestricted initially and all other work qubits in the checked zero-initialized set $A$. Write $V=U_T\cdots U_1$ and identify each normalized history with its initial computation vector. On the correct-propagation history space $S_{prop}$ of [[lem-qa-33-kkr-two-qubit-propagation-restriction]], the compressed input term is
$$H_{in}|_{S_{prop}}=\frac1{T+1}\sum_{a\in A}|1\rangle\langle1|_a,$$
where $A$ is the initially clean ancilla set, and the compressed output term is the transported reject projector $V^*(|0\rangle\langle0|_{out}\otimes I)V$. Thus the kernel of $H_{in}|S_{prop}$ consists of histories initialized with clean ancillas. If $A\ne\varnothing$, its least positive eigenvalue is at least $1/(T+1)$; if $A=\varnothing$, the input term is zero and the restriction is immediate. If $K_{in}$ bounds the norm of the remaining output term, choose
$$J_{in}/(T+1)>2K_{in}+K_{in}^2/\epsilon_{in}.$$
Then the final projection-lemma error is below $\epsilon_{in}$. For an amplified verifier with YES acceptance at least $3/4$ and NO acceptance at most $1/4$, the compressed output energy is at most $1/4$ on YES and at least $3/4$ on NO.

Fix $k$ and let $H=\sum_{j=1}^mH_j$ be an encoded $k$-local Hamiltonian with $m=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, local dimension at most $D=2^k$, and algebraic entries supplied by polynomial-time Cauchy procedures. For every rational $\tau>0$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm outputs rational Hermitian local matrices $\widetilde H_j$ with $\sum_j\|H_j-\widetilde H_j\|\le\tau$. Consequently $|\lambda_{\min}(H)-\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H)|\le\tau$. If the original promise thresholds are $a<b$ with gap $\Delta=b-a$, choose $\tau\le\Delta/8$ and output thresholds $a+\tau,b-\tau$; the mapped YES and NO instances remain on their respective promise sides with gap at least $3\Delta/4$. A concrete polynomial running-time conclusion requires the stated polynomial-time Cauchy bounds for each algebraic entry encoding.

Let a QMA verifier have completeness $c$ and soundness $s$ with $0\le s<c\le1$, and put $\gamma=c-s$. For $0<\delta<1$, choose an integer

$$r\ge 2\gamma^{-2}\ln(1/\delta).$$

Then the parallel verifier of [[alg-qa-33-qma-parallel-majority-amplification]] has completeness at least $1-\delta$ and soundness at most $\delta$. On a NO input its soundness bound holds for every joint $r$-block witness state, including entangled states. The repetition uses $r$ witness blocks and $r$ verifier copies, so choosing the least integer $r$ satisfying the bound gives polynomial size when $\gamma^{-1}$ and $\ln(1/\delta)$ are polynomially bounded. The probability bounds hold for every larger $r$ as well.

Use the fixed QC14 alphabet $\{H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}\}$. Let $M$ be one fixed deterministic polynomial-time classical machine that, on each binary input $x$ of length $n$, outputs a valid circuit description $P_x$ of at most $L(n)$ gate records on at most $W(n)$ data wires, where $L,W$ are fixed polynomials. Encode the output as exactly $L(n)$ fixed-width records: each record is either blank, a one-qubit label $H,T,T^\dagger$ with one wire address, or a CNOT label with an ordered pair of distinct wire addresses; unused address fields are zero. Let $\delta(n)$ be any inverse-polynomial rational tolerance produced by a fixed polynomial-time machine from $1^n$, with polynomial bit length. There is a full-list uniform QC14 family generated from $1^n$ which on classical basis input $x$ and data state $|\psi\rangle$ outputs a state within operator error $\delta(n)$, up to a global scalar, of
$$|x\rangle\otimes P_x|\psi\rangle\otimes|M(x)\rangle\otimes|0^w\rangle$$
for a polynomially bounded work width $w(n)$. Its size and generator time are polynomial in $n$ and $1/\delta(n)$. The program and arithmetic registers are terminal unmeasured wires; their presence changes the data-register outcome law from executing $P_x$ by at most $2\delta(n)$. This lemma converts a polynomial-time input-dependent compiler into the input-length-uniform verifier model.

For promise problems $(Y,N)$ and $(Y',N')$ in [[def-promise-problem]], a polynomial-time many-one promise reduction is a total polynomial-time function $f$ satisfying $f(Y)\subseteq Y'$ and $f(N)\subseteq N'$. There is no condition on $f$ outside $Y\cup N$.

A polynomial-time oracle promise reduction is a polynomially clocked deterministic oracle machine $M$ which solves $(Y,N)$ for **every** total language $B$ satisfying $Y'\subseteq B$ and $B\cap N'=\varnothing$. This uses binary, consistent membership completions: an off-promise word may have either bit, but repeated queries to that word receive the same bit. The clock is uniform over all completions.

For a finite QMA verifier with witness acceptance effect $E_x$, if a witness density operator $\rho$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)\ge c$, then some pure-state density operator $|u\rangle\langle u|$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(E_x|u\rangle\langle u|)\ge c$. Thus allowing mixed witnesses does not increase the completeness threshold.

derivations.claim: By [F8], amplify the verifier to completeness at least $3/4$ and soundness at most $1/4$ using polynomially many repetitions. On each YES input, [F11] lets the amplified verifier attain its completeness threshold with a pure witness. For each source input $x$, make the amplified circuit input-specific: replace its classical input register and every parallel-copy input register by fresh zero-initialized scratch wires, count all of them among the clean ancillas $A$, and prefix the circuit with $X=HT^4H$ on each root input bit where $x_i=1$. Then use the CNOT fanout prescribed by [F8] to load the same basis string $x$ into each separate copy register. Use [F9] to compile each copy's terminal predicate and the final majority predicate, specialized to $x$, reversibly into one output qubit; count their zero-initialized work wires in $A$ as well. Thus the input-penalized history starts with all input scratch registers zero, and the prefix and fanout set every verifier input to this particular $x$ before verification. Replace each CNOT by the exact identity $CNOT=(I\otimes H)CZ(I\otimes H)$; $Z=T^4$, and $CZ$ has exact matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,-1)$. If there are no controlled-$Z$ gates, add two cancelling $CZ$ gates on two fresh clean work qubits; their product is identity. For each designated $CZ$ on wires $f,s$ at time $t$, insert $Z_f,Z_s$ at times $t-2,t-1$ before it and $Z_f,Z_s$ at $t+1,t+2$ after it. These commute with $CZ$ and each wire has two $Z$ factors, so the computation is unchanged. Let $T_2\ge1$ count the resulting controlled-$Z$ gates; choose polynomial $L\ge5$ larger than every one-qubit segment plus its four inserted $Z$ steps, including the input-loading prefix, pad each segment with exact idle identity matrices on a fixed work wire to length $L$, and set $T=(T_2+1)L-1$. Thus controlled-$Z$ gates occur at $lL$, every other step is a one-qubit unitary, and all clock indices required by the KKR terms exist. The identities are matrix entries of the reduction's finite Hamiltonian list and do not alter the verifier computation. The padded length remains polynomial. [F8, F9, F11, given, algebra]

Set $\epsilon_0=\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_{in}=1/64$. First choose $J_{in}$ with effective gap $J_{in}/(T+1)>2K_{in}+K_{in}^2/\epsilon_{in}$, where $K_{in}$ bounds the compressed output term. Next choose $J_2$ so $J_2g_2>2K_2+K_2^2/\epsilon_2$, with $K_2$ bounding $H_{out}+J_{in}H_{in}$. Then choose $J_1$ so $J_1g_1>2K_1+K_1^2/\epsilon_1$, where $K_1$ bounds $H_{out}+J_{in}H_{in}+J_2H_{prop2}$. Finally choose $J_{clock}>2K_{clock}+K_{clock}^2/\epsilon_0$, where $K_{clock}$ bounds all preceding weighted terms. The gaps $g_1,g_2$ are inverse polynomial by [F4]–[F5]; each $K_i$ is polynomial in the verifier length and earlier weights. Choose each next integer also larger than $T^2$ times the previous weight. All four remain polynomial and satisfy $J_{in}\ll J_2\ll J_1\ll J_{clock}$.

Apply the four restrictions in order. The illegal-clock term, one-qubit edge terms, KKR controlled-phase checks, and input penalty each lose less than $1/64$ from the least eigenvalue by [F3]–[F6]. On YES the valid clean history has energy equal to rejection probability, at most $1/4$, so the full Hamiltonian has least eigenvalue at most $1/4$ by the projection-lemma upper bounds. On NO the final clean-history subspace has least output energy at least $3/4$; the four lower-bound errors sum to less than $4/64$, so the full least eigenvalue is greater than $11/16$.

All terms of $H_{clock}$ are pair projectors. A one-qubit propagation check couples one work qubit and a clock projector. Each $H_{qubit,t}$ summand couples one work qubit and one clock bit, and each $H_{time,t}$ summand acts on one or two clock bits. Input and output terms couple one work and one clock qubit. Thus every summand is at most 2-local, and the number and norms are polynomial because there are polynomially many clock pairs and all four weights are polynomial. Choose rational thresholds $a=1/4$, $b=11/16$; the strict bound in step 1.3 places every NO instance above $b$. Apply [F7] with $\tau\le(b-a)/8$ and shifted thresholds; this preserves at least $3(b-a)/4>0$ gap and gives a polynomial-time rational encoding. The verifier generator and all arithmetic are deterministic polynomial time, so [F10] makes this a promise-preserving reduction from every QMA problem. Membership is [F1].
